author: tsavo
body: ## Summary Finish the #6447 consumer arm: when a managed generator terminates before the first yield, `GeneratorWithSugar` now emits the **observed** manager-protocol raise as a `Halted(RaiseEffect)` ExitSet arm (projected as `Incomplete` in the block), instead of `SugarNotWritten` ("terminated before first yield"). Observation remains sole-sourced in `generator_entry_refusal.observed_entry_refusal()` — no vendor module name in the consumer (`generator_construction_law` stays R=0). ## Gate - Real reproducers: `return` before yield; `if False: yield` - Truthful: exception name + message match observed vendor conversion - Lying: wrong spellings still fail observation twins; opaque branch still loud - Focused: 28 tests green; R_generator_construction = 0 ## Not - No census / scoreboard / pin-only - Does not invent a second raise spelling Follow-on to #6447 observation-only land. > [!NOTE] > ### Fix generator never-yield enter to return an ExitSet raise instead of a refusal > - When a generator manager terminates at first resume (never-yield/premature return), `GeneratorWithSugar.desugar()` previously raised `SugarNotWritten`; it now returns a `Complete` outcome containing an `Incomplete` arm with a `RaiseEffect` (RuntimeError). > - A new static helper `_entry_refusal_exit()` converts enter-time `GeneratorTerminationV1` into an `ExitSet` with a single `Halted` arm, using `observed_entry_refusal()` to retrieve the vendor-observed exception name and message. > - Tests in [`test_generator_context_manager_construction.py`](https://github.com/TSavo/sugar/pull/6449/files#diff-94e55387dc77922abd716e297c564377f0ce63e91fa8966cbf7a8c9c13e83402) and [`test_generator_entry_refusal.py`](https://github.com/TSavo/sugar/pull/6449/files#diff-5ead9f42f001b8e0b7ce1d44ac5e2e155509d87311db3ffec69c272774d28346) are updated to assert the new `RaiseEffect` outcome rather than expecting a panic. > - Behavioral Change: callers that previously caught `SugarNotWritten` on never-yield generators will no longer see that exception; they will instead receive a structured `Halted` outcome carrying a RuntimeError raise. > > > > Macroscope summarized aacbf5d. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Generator-based context managers that return or never yield now complete desugaring while surfacing the observed runtime refusal as a raised effect. * Replaced the previous diagnostic failure with consistent handling of generator-entry refusals. * **Tests** * Added coverage for immediate returns, unreachable yields, and consumer behavior when generators fail to yield.

author: dginev
body:
> **Stacked on #405** — the first commit here is that PR's. Merge #405 first;
> this rebases onto it and its diff then reduces to the `&` half.

**Diagnostic.** Seven arXiv/2605 papers report `Error:unexpected:&` at
`Anonymous String` — the recursive BibTeX session. The `&` is real `.bib`
content: `publisher = {Taylor & Francis}`, `journal = {Infrared Physics &
Technology}`, `booktitle = {… Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining}`, `author = {…
Daishi Kuroiwa & Matteo Rocca}`, `copyright = {… Lippincott Williams &
Wilkins}`. BibTeX's lexer has no alignment, so that `&` is a character in a
name; TeX reads catcode 4, errors, and **drops** it — the entry printed "Taylor
Francis". This is *not* a Rust-only defect: same-host `latexmlc` raised the
identical per-`&` count on all six re-measured witnesses (1/1, 3/3, 1/1, 1/1,
1/1, 1/1), and `bibtex` 0.99d + pdflatex agree — under `plain` and under
natbib's `abbrvnat` the bare `&` is copied into the `.bbl` and pdflatex stops
with `! Misplaced alignment tab character &`, printing "Taylor Francis". Rust
already beat Perl on these overall (2605.01936: 13 errors and a complete
bibliography vs Perl's 101 + a Fatal + none at all).

A second, unrelated ampersand bug turned up in the same sweep: `\&` — an
HTML entity that survived into the `.bib` and was TeX-escaped a second time.
That one raises no error anywhere (Perl and pdflatex both print "&"), so the
catcode work does not reach it.

**Approach.** A `.bib` field's content is **data, not TeX** (maintainer policy)
— authorized surpass-Perl and surpass-pdflatex, because LaTeXML reads `.bib`
directly, with no `.bst` and no `bibtex(1)`, and so decides what reaches the
tokenizer. `&` is regime A, beside #405's `%`: it derails alignment in *any*
field, and these fields have no Perl `Semiverbatim` precedent to follow (unlike
`doi`/`isbn`/… which `eprint` joins in #403). Both of #405's seams are extended,
and both are needed — the per-entry Mouth (`Mouth::with_align_as_other`) and
`mouth::tokenize_bib_literal` for the handlers that re-tokenize a stored raw
field and never pass through it (`\bib@@title` recasing, name/date/pages
assembly, MR/Zbl). Per-Mouth, not a State catcode, so a `.sty` raw-loaded from
inside a field handler — and the document — keep TeX's alignment tab.
`undouble_escaped_ampersand` handles the `\&` family separately, at the
entry-assembly seam and again in `\bib@@title`. `OXIDIZED_DESIGN #75`.

**Validation.** Per-witness `Error:` totals, debug profile with dumps, baseline
= #405 tip:

| witness | before | after | `unexpected:&` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2605.06249 | 3 | **0** | 3 → 0 |
| 2605.03054 | 1 | **0** | 1 → 0 |
| 2605.00462 | 1 | **0** | 1 → 0 |
| 2605.08753 | 1 | **0** | 1 → 0 |
| 2605.10409 | 1 | **0** | 1 → 0 |
| 2605.01936 | 13 | **6** | 7 → 0 |
| 2605.06624 | 4 | **3** | 1 → 0 |

No `unexpected:&` remains on any of the seven; the two residuals are unrelated
`undefined:` errors. #405's own canaries are unaffected (2605.02131 and
2605.01196: 0 errors both before and after this change). Entity witness
2605.00833 renders "Computer Engineering, & Applied Computing" (was `&`),
0 errors.

Guards, each RED-verified by reverting the relevant hunk (`git diff` +
`git checkout`, never `git stash` — that stack is shared across worktrees on
this box and it swapped two agents' trees today):
`06_cluster_bibliography::bib_bare_ampersand_is_literal_data` (5 post-stage
errors → 0, and "Taylor & Francis" instead of "Taylor Francis"),
`::bib_bare_ampersand_leaves_live_markup_alone`, and
`::bib_escaped_amp_entity_decodes_to_one_ampersand` (`&amp;` → `&`).
All three gate the POST stage with `convert_and_post_clean`. Clippy and fmt
clean; full suite green apart from the known
`latexml_post graphics::tests::process_coalesces_only_matching_conversion_options`
(issue 401, fails on clean main on this host).

## Decisions & open questions

1. **Where to neutralize `&` — per-Mouth (regime A) vs per-field `Semiverbatim`
   (regime B).** Chose regime A, per the blast-radius rule: `&` is destructive
   in any field, and `publisher`/`journal`/`booktitle` have no Perl per-field
   idiom to mirror. Regime B would have meant inventing `Semiverbatim` for five
   ordinary rendered fields, which also suppresses `~ $ ^ _ '` in them — far
   more than the evidence supports. *What would settle it:* a witness needing
   `&` literal but something else in the SPECIALS set live.
2. **Both seams, or just the mouth.** Both. The `%` agent measured 2605.02131
   getting *worse* (28 → 37) with the mouth alone, because `\bib@@title` re-reads
   the raw field. Confirmed directly here: with only the mouth covered, `\&`
   in a `title` stayed broken while the same shape in a `booktitle` was fixed.
3. **`#` deliberately not included.** Checked rather than assumed: exactly one
   bare `#` across all seven witnesses, in 2605.00462's JabRef `file` path, and
   that field is already covered (unknown field → `Verbatim Verbatim`).
   *Settles it:* a witness with a bare `#` in a rendered field.
4. **`\&` — repair, or render faithfully?** Chose repair. pdflatex is the
   named tiebreaker and pdflatex prints `&`, but it has no way to know
   better; reading the `.bib` we can see one file mixing two escaping
   conventions, and the entity is unambiguous — no author writes `\&`
   meaning six characters. The alternative ("garbage in, garbage out") is
   defensible; it just means every reader of that paper sees `&`. Scoped
   tightly: only `amp;` DIRECTLY after an ampersand, so "amplitude" and a lone
   `\&` are untouched, with a near-miss case in the fixture.
5. **Known cost of `&`-as-data.** A `.bib` field containing a real `tabular`
   would no longer align. Judged acceptable — no such witness in the 6000-source
   scan — but it is the honest price of regime A.
6. **A `copyright`-specific fix was implemented, then withdrawn.** Before the
   policy call, `copyright` was the one field in the cluster with a #73-style
   argument (no `.bst` emits it; no `FMT_SPEC` queries
   `ltx:bib-date[@role='copyright']`), and reading it `Verbatim` took 2605.01936
   7 → 6. Dropped once `&` became data everywhere — it would be a second
   overlapping mechanism in a file four agents are editing. *Reopen if:* a
   non-`&` special in `copyright` shows up in a sweep.
7. **`latexml_core/src/mouth.rs` is shared machinery.** The change is additive —
   one `bool`, one builder method, one arm in `catcode_of` — and inert unless a
   caller opts in; the only opt-in is the BibTeX path. Flagged because it is not
   my own binding.
8. **Renamed #405's `mouth::tokenize_percent_literal` → `tokenize_bib_literal`**
   (one call site). It now neutralizes `%` *and* `&`, so the old name would
   mislead. Trivial to revert if #405's author prefers the original name.

author: dfattal
body:
Editorial (class-B) follow-up to the auto-synced mechanical data — authored by
`/sync-website` from the July release wave plus the notes gathered in
`#tmp-dxr-website-sync`. Mechanical facts (versions, demo cards, repo list,
extension names) are handled separately by `sync-org.yml`; **this PR is prose
only** — no `lib/data/generated/*` or `public/*` changes.

`tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, and `next build` all green.

## What changed

### Linux — the site was two releases behind
The July wave took Linux from "hand-unpacked tarball, cube renders" to full
demo parity, transparent desktop overlays, and a one-command bundle. The site
still described the old state, and the architecture page didn't mention Linux
at all.

- **`lib/data/roadmap.ts`** — rewrote the *Linux runtime (Preview)* item: all
  five demos are native window-owning Linux apps, the transparent avatar
  reaches platform parity with live desktop content composited under the weave,
  Wayland joins X11, and every component ships a `.deb` with a one-command
  bundle install. Kept it in **Now**, not **Done** — M8 is still open and the
  service-side render path, windowed-3D phase origin, and Intel Arc target are
  in flight. Also corrected the extensions item, which listed only three
  platforms for window binding.
- **`lib/data/compatibility.ts`** — Linux row: X11 *or* Wayland, both surface
  bindings, transparency, tri-LTS validation, `.deb` + bundle distribution.
- **`app/architecture/page.tsx`** — Linux was absent from the platform story.
  Added it to the Stack Overview line and wrote a Platforms paragraph beside
  the Windows/macOS/Android ones. "Three platforms" → "four".
- **`app/download/page.tsx`** — Linux had **no presence** here despite
  `DisplayXRBundle-*-linux-amd64.tar.gz` and per-component `.deb`s shipping.
  Added Linux to the runtime card, the bundle blurb, and a Linux footnote
  paired with the existing macOS one.
- **`app/demos/page.tsx`** — the authored platform-tag overlay was stale
  (gaussiansplat said "Windows, macOS" only) and `avatar` / `earthview` had no
  entries at all, so they rendered untagged. All five now ship all four
  platforms; verified against each demo's release assets.
- **`lib/data/ecosystem.ts`** — same staleness in the repo descriptions.

### New architecture section — *Compositing on a Woven Surface*
The rule that overlay exclusion handles partial regions but a **full-surface
effect cannot be layered over a woven window at all** — the overlay shares the
window's rect, the weave-match goes ambiguous, and the window falls back to
presenting raw side-by-side. The fix is to change *what gets woven*, not to
draw over it.

Worth the space because it's the thing every inline-3D author gets wrong first
and it fails as a *rendering artefact* rather than an error, so nobody debugs
their way to it. Closes with the 2D-fallback paragraph, which makes the
existing "progressive enhancement, never a hard dependency" claim concrete.

**Placement note:** the draft proposed this after *Native Compositor Model*; I
put it after *One Model for 2D and 3D Regions* instead, so the region /
compositing material stays contiguous and the reader already has the zone
vocabulary. Easy to move if you disagree.

### Ecosystem — the gallery was missing entirely
- **`lib/data/ecosystem.ts`** — `displayxr-gallery` was not in the repo list, so
  it appeared on neither the homepage ecosystem map nor `/contribute`. Added
  under `demos`.
- **`components/home/EcosystemMap.tsx`** — a short *See it running* block. Prose
  rather than another card, because the point is that it's **live**, not that
  it's one more repository.
- **`lib/constants.ts`** — `REPO_URLS.gallery` + `GALLERY_URL` (verified 200).

### Extensions
- **`app/extensions/page.tsx`** — added `XR_DXR_wayland_surface_binding`
  (shipped in runtime v2.1.2, gated on `XRT_HAVE_WAYLAND`), status `early`.
  Description written from the header comment, including the detail that
  transparency is native on Wayland and needs none of the ARGB-visual work X11
  requires.

## Deliberately not published
- **The depth model is never named.** The neural stereo depth comes from a
  non-commercial-licensed model with only a verbal interim OK. Naming it on a
  public commercial site is licensing exposure, not a style question. Copy says
  "per-eye depth" and stops. Changing that needs sign-off first, not a copy edit.
- **No display-vendor names in any new copy**, per the standing rule — "vendor
  display-processor plug-in", "3D display". (The one `Leia` string in the diff is
  the pre-existing *Leia Image Format* file-format reference on a line where I
  only appended "Linux".)
- **Public mirror only** for the gallery; the source repo is private and is not
  referenced.
- **No infrastructure detail** — no GPU workers, hosting, or database.

## Detected but intentionally skipped
- **New ADRs: none.** The reviewed baseline already covers all 35 signals, so
  `editorial-baseline.json` is untouched by this PR.
- **Closed milestones: none new.** M8 (Linux Support) is still open with 6 open
  issues — which is exactly why the Linux roadmap item stayed in **Now**.
- **`.github`, `displayxr-website`** — flagged as missing from the ecosystem
  grid; neither should be featured.
- **iOS tilt parallax and the full-frame depth reprocess** — real work, but
  changelog material; neither changes what the site claims.
- **Demo-in-roadmap check** — flags all five demos every run because
  `roadmap.ts` describes demos generically rather than by repo name. Noise, not
  a gap.

## For the reviewer
- **Any existing gallery screenshot on the site is now stale** — the curated set
  replaced the old seed content on 26 Jul, and the content is materially better.
  Re-capturing is an asset task, not copy, so it's not in this PR.
- **Open question carried over from the draft:** the content-swap rule may belong
  in the `displayxr-web` SDK authoring notes with the site linking to it, rather
  than being restated here. Worth deciding before it exists in two places and
  drifts.
- PR #15 (`chore/editorial-sync`, ADR-026 on `/contribute`) is still open. This
  PR is on a separate branch and touches no file in common with it.

🤖 Authored by /sync-website (displayxr-runtime hub). Review the prose and merge to publish.

author: lannguyensi
body:
Closes task `be55cf5f`.

Node 22.4+ ships a global `localStorage` that is non-functional without
`--localstorage-file`, and vitest's jsdom environment does not replace it. On
Node 26 that shadowed jsdom's Storage and failed 19 tests across three files
with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'clear')`. CI
pins Node 22 and was green, so this only ever bit locally.

Applies the capability-guarded `--no-experimental-webstorage` recipe already
proven in `clawd-monitor` (fdf5fde) and deploy-panel.

## Verification

The reviewer reproduced this independently rather than re-reading the
implementer's log, using a scratch harness outside the repo with two configs
differing by exactly one line:

| | Node 20.20.2 | Node 22.23.1 (CI) | Node 26.5.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| flag available | no | yes | yes |
| `localStorage` global present | no | no | **yes** |
| suite, with guard | n/a | 358/358 | **358/358** |
| suite, without guard | n/a | 358/358 | **19 failed / 339 passed** |

So the guard is causal, not incidental, and it degrades to an inert empty
`execArgv` on Node 20 rather than crashing with `bad option`.

## Also in this PR

- The inert postcss override in `cli/package.json` is annotated rather than
  deleted, since `cli/` predates joining this workspace and could be installed
  standalone again. npm reads `overrides` only from an install's root manifest,
  so it does nothing here or for consumers of the published package. The note
  uses the conventional `//overrides` comment key, not a bespoke field that
  reads like a real npm field in the published tarball.
- The root `test` script now covers the frontend workspace, ordered
  frontend → cli → backend. Backend needs Postgres and several env vars, so
  putting it first made the new leg unreachable on exactly the machines this
  change serves.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` no longer claims the root `npm test` fans out across all
  workspaces. It didn't before this change and still doesn't: mcp-server and
  mcp-bridge stay out, because adding them needs a build-ordering step.

## Known gap, filed as `12029b3d`

**Nothing in CI protects this guard.** On Node 22 the suite is green with or
without it (measured, not assumed), so deleting the `execArgv` line would show
every check passing and the failure would only resurface on a developer's newer
local Node. Closing that needs a Node 26 CI matrix entry, which this task
explicitly put out of scope.

## Not verified

The root `npm test` chain was not run end to end; the backend leg needs a
Postgres instance and env vars unavailable here, a dependency that predates
this branch. The frontend and cli legs were run directly.

author: kaihao-zhao
body:
## Overview

Adds a `device_limit` config option under `[auth.anonymous]` that caps how many distinct anonymous devices can be tracked. Once the limit is reached, new unrecognized devices are rejected (`ErrDeviceLimitReached`) rather than registered, and this error now propagates synchronously through authentication (the previous fire-and-forget goroutine is replaced with a blocking call). The limit is also exposed to the frontend via `anonymousDeviceLimit` in the bootstrap config.

author: orchestratedchaos
body:
## Summary
- Single-user runs (python3 recommenders/movie.py alice, or any web-UI-triggered per-user job) fed a one-user resolved_usernames set into the unconditional cache-orphan prune added in 2.10.31, misclassifying every OTHER configured user's cache as orphaned.
- Under the dry_run: true default this only logged false "would remove" candidates, but flipping general.cache_prune.dry_run to false (a reasonable next step) would delete every other user's cache on the next single-user run, forcing a full Plex re-scan.
- Fix scopes pruning to full runs only (no username arg), the only case where resolved_usernames actually reflects every currently-configured user. A user genuinely removed from config is still pruned on the next full run (cron / web UI's "full" engine).

## Test plan
- [x] test_single_user_run_does_not_orphan_other_configured_users - proven to fail against pre-fix code (deletes alice's cache), passes against the fix
- [x] test_full_run_still_prunes_a_user_removed_from_config - full-run pruning still works for the legitimate removed-user case
- [x] test_full_run_prunes_by_resolved_not_raw_admin_username - locks in that pruning classifies by resolved username, not raw config string, so this can't invert into deleting a live cache
- [x] Full suite: 2465 passed, 1 skipped (baseline 2462/1 + 3 new tests)
- [x] ruff check / ruff format --check clean
- [x] tests/harness.py byte-identical

author: chiradip
body:
## What

Binder leg of full `IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM` support — completes the feature end-to-end (parser #47, analyzer #59, this).

- `map_binary_op` maps the operator texts `"IS DISTINCT FROM"` / `"IS NOT DISTINCT FROM"` to the parser's new `ast::BinaryOp::IsDistinctFrom` / `IsNotDistinctFrom`, so the predicate lowers to a `BinaryOp` `Expr` instead of failing "unlowerable". `fold_binary` already returns `nullopt` for these (no const-fold), so they flow through the optimizer as opaque comparisons.
- The IR dump spells them: the parser's `binary_op_to_string` returns `"Unknown"` for the new enum values, so a small local `binop_text()` in `expr_ir.cpp` names them and delegates everything else to the parser helper, keeping plan dumps correct.

## Submodule pins

- analyzer `63e0a90 → b323e55` (picks up the analyzer leg #59)

author: 0xaslan
body:
Stacked on #1163 (which is itself stacked on #1162) — this PR's diff is the last commit only. It should merge together with #1163.

## Summary
- `mintExactAmount` takes a required `maxCostRaw` and passes it as the contract's new `max_cost` argument, taking the builder from 12 to 13 `moveCall` arguments.
- The friendly `PredictClient.tx.mintAmount` takes a required `maxCost` in USDC and converts it to raw quote units.
- Both are required rather than optional-with-a-default, mirroring the contract.

## Why
- The SDK builds `expiry_market::mint_exact_amount` as a positional argument list. #1163 makes that entrypoint take a required all-in cost cap, so an unchanged SDK would emit a call one argument short and every budget mint it produced would abort on landing.
- The SDK test suite is not part of CI, so nothing else would catch the mismatch before the package publishes.

## Key decisions
- **`maxCostRaw` is required, not optional with a `U64_MAX` default.** `mintExactQuantity` defaults its two guards that way because the contract accepts `u64::MAX` as "uncapped". The budget mint has no disabling value — the contract aborts on zero — so offering a default here would only produce calls the chain rejects.
- The friendly layer takes USDC and converts with `usdcToRaw`, matching how `mint`'s optional `maxCost` is already handled.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm test` in `packages/predict/sdk` — `Test Files 12 passed (12)`, `Tests 115 passed (115)`
- [x] `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — exit 0
- [x] `tx-trade.test.ts` asserts the cap is serialized at the argument index the contract reads it from and is never the uncapped sentinel; `client.test.ts` asserts a $10.50 ceiling converts to `10_500_000` at USDC's six decimals
- [x] Before the client fix, `client.test.ts` failed with `Cannot convert undefined to a BigInt` at the new argument — the required type caught the second call site rather than shipping a silently short call

## Risk / rollout
- Breaking change for SDK consumers of `mintAmount` / `mintExactAmount`: they must supply a ceiling. The published SDK must not ship ahead of the contract that takes the argument.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Addresses post-merge review findings on the stablecoin payment rail.

Key fixes:
- **Payment Hub state machine** — `approved` can now transition to `orchestrating`, so `executeStablecoinConnector` can move stablecoin intents through `approved → orchestrating → settled` without the previously invalid `approved → orchestrating` jump. `readiness` is checked before the transition and any settlement failure flows through `orchestrating → failed`.
- **Treasury atomicity** — `TreasuryEngine.hold/release/post` now run their `BEGIN ... FOR UPDATE ... COMMIT` sequences on a single pooled `Client` (`pool.connect()`), so the row lock and rollback actually protect concurrent operations instead of being silently released between individual `pool.query` calls.
- **Fee accounting** — `settlePayment` now transfers only `payment.amount_cents` on-chain and calls `TreasuryEngine.post(reserveId, txHash, { settledAmountCents })`. `post` debits the sent amount from the balance and releases the hold for the full reserve; the gateway fee stays in the treasury.
- **Failed settlement reserve release** — `settlePayment` catches `blockchain.settle` errors, calls `failPayment` to release the treasury reserve, and rethrows so the Payment Hub can mark the intent failed.
- **WSO2 proxy security** — `/api/stablecoin/wso2/*` now requires an `admin` role and validates that the method is in `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE` and the path matches `^/[A-Za-z0-9_\-./]+$` with no `..` traversal.
- **Public health redaction** — `GET /api/stablecoin/health` now returns only `ready`, `mode`, `network`, and `assetCode`. Full readiness details (Horizon URL, distributor public key, Magic/WSO2 endpoints) are still available through the existing authenticated operator routes.
- **Payment asset/network validation** — `StablecoinGateway.createPayment` and `createFromIntent` reject payments whose asset or network does not match the configured engine, preventing silent settlement mismatches.

author: lgritz
body:
Converting an image whose channels have differing native integer depths (e.g. a Softimage PIC with a 16-bit R and an 8-bit G channel) to OpenEXR produced garbage pixels: the uint16/uint8 bytes were copied straight into the half channels and reinterpreted rather than rescaled. Three coupled issues, all rooted in treating "output supports channelformats" as "output stores these exact per-channel formats":

- exroutput: spec_to_header forced spec.format to one of EXR's three stored types but left spec.channelformats naming the original (uint16/uint8) types, so the post-open spec misdescribed what was actually stored. Remap channelformats through the same mapping (and drop the list when all channels collapse to one type) so the spec is consistent with the half/float/uint the file really holds.

- ImageOutput::copy_image: the native (no-conversion) fast path was taken whenever the input had channelformats. Only take it when the output will store each channel in the input's native format; otherwise fall back to the converting path.

- iconvert: its by-hand copy path (used whenever the input has mixed channel formats) requested a native per-channel transfer unconditionally. Apply the same check against the opened output's stored formats and, when they differ, transfer through the output's format so values are rescaled.

Regression test added to testsuite/softimage: converting the mixed 16/8-bit file to EXR now yields correctly normalized values.

Assisted-by: Claude Code / Opus 4.8

author: grimicorn-agent
body:
## What changed and why

`fetchOnThisDayEntries` (`server/utils/on-this-day-helpers.ts`) issued 2 relation queries per matching entry, calling `loadEntryRelations` per row inside `Promise.all`. A user with several years of app usage hitting the same day would see photo/tag loading scale linearly with entry count.

Added `loadRelationsForEntries(database, entryIds)` to `server/utils/entry-helpers.ts`: a batched counterpart to the existing single-entry `loadEntryRelations`, mirroring the `inArray` pattern already used in `server/api/entries/index.get.ts`. It:
- Seeds every requested `entryId` with `{ photos: [], tags: [] }` up front, so callers never need a fallback default.
- Issues exactly 2 queries total (photos, tags) regardless of match count, via the existing private `fetchPhotosForEntries`/`fetchTagsForEntries` helpers.
- Merges rows into the seeded map by `entryId`.

`fetchOnThisDayEntries` now: fetches the matching rows, guards the empty-rows case (returns `[]` without calling the relations loader at all — avoids an `inArray` against an empty array), then calls `loadRelationsForEntries` once with all matching entry IDs and maps each row to `{ ...row, ...relations }`, throwing loudly if the map is ever missing an id (defense-in-depth; unreachable through the real implementation since the map is seeded from the same `entryIds` list).

`loadEntryRelations` (single-entry) now delegates to `loadRelationsForEntries` so the two can't drift on how a tag row becomes `{ id, name }`. Its 5 existing callers (`[id].get.ts`, `[id].patch.ts` incl. transaction client, `[id]/like.delete.ts`, `[id]/like.post.ts`, `index.post.ts`) are unaffected — same signature, same return shape.

## How output was verified unchanged

- New unit tests in `tests/server/entries/on-this-day-helpers.test.ts` assert: empty-rows case returns `[]` and calls no relation queries; user scoping reaches the actual `.where()` call (not just filter construction); result order follows row order (`occurred_at DESC`), independent of relations-map insertion order; photos/tags are correctly associated per entry when relations are interleaved across entries; entries with no relations still return empty arrays; a missing map entry throws loudly.
- New unit tests in `tests/server/entries/entry-helpers.test.ts` directly exercise `loadRelationsForEntries`: empty `entryIds` short-circuits with no query; every requested id is seeded; photos/tags map to the correct entry (not just the first); rows for entries outside the requested set are ignored; the batched photo query still sorts by `sortOrder` (batching moved this from a per-entry to a single global `ORDER BY`); `loadEntryRelations` delegation returns the same shape as before.
- Full existing suite (112 files, 1344 tests) passes unchanged.
- Ran `npm run e2e` twice against fresh Neon branches (once after the initial refactor, once after the final round of review fixes that touched `loadEntryRelations`) — all 14 e2e specs passed both times, including the entry-creation flow that exercises `loadEntryRelations`.

## Before/after query count

For N matching entries: **before** = 1 (entries) + 2N (relations, 2 per entry) queries. **After** = 1 (entries) + 2 (relations, batched) queries — constant regardless of N.

## Implementation decisions

- Centralized the batched grouping logic in `entry-helpers.ts` as `loadRelationsForEntries` rather than duplicating grouping helpers locally in `on-this-day-helpers.ts` (caught in code review round 1 as a rule-of-three violation — the `{ id, name }` tag reshape would otherwise have existed in 3 places).
- Kept `fetchPhotosForEntries`/`fetchTagsForEntries`/`TagRow` module-private in `entry-helpers.ts` — they were briefly exported in an earlier revision but nothing outside the module needs them once `loadRelationsForEntries` centralizes the batching.
- Did not touch `server/api/entries/index.get.ts`, which has its own pre-existing (and now duplicate) local `fetchEntryPhotos`/`fetchEntryTags`/`groupByEntryId`. Consolidating that is out of scope for this fix — kept the diff scoped to the on-this-day path per the task brief, and that file wasn't part of this issue.

No new environment variables, external services, or migrations required.

Closes #92

author: afloresescarcega
body:
Closes #2.

## What changed

This branch takes the Helmod → blueprint converter from "places machines with broken inserters" to a working end-to-end pipeline with routed supply lines, and replaces the old Python/Deno experiments with a single React app in `frontend/`.

- **Pipeline fixes**: rewrote the Lua table parser (the old one mistracked consumed characters and crashed on Helmod's nested exports), removed a stray NUL byte in the encoded blueprint string that made Factorio reject every import, and switched extraction to read recipe entries with their factory counts instead of harvesting every item block. Works with both Helmod 1.x (gzip) and 2.x (zlib) exports.
- **Layout**: machines in wrapped columns (15 per column), inserters outside the 3x3 footprints, medium poles on the column centerline so both input and output inserters have power, input/output belt lanes on each side.
- **Routing** (the project's namesake): one bus line per consumed item in reserved rows above the grid. External inputs flow east from labeled feed points (constant combinators signal the expected item); intermediates are collected north from their producer columns and flow west to consumers. Splitter taps drop into column lanes, hopping lower bus rows with underground belts. Second/third ingredients get extra lanes served by long-handed inserters, using the vanilla recipe graph vendored from factorio-blueprint-editor. Columns are topologically sorted so producers sit east of their consumers.
- **Validation**: `frontend/validator/validate.mjs` mirrors factorio-blueprint-editor's decode + Ajv schema + entity/recipe-name validation; the CLI (`node frontend/cli.mjs < input.txt`) refuses to emit strings that fail it.
- **Deploy**: GitHub Actions workflow publishes the CRA build to GitHub Pages on pushes to main (enable Pages with source "GitHub Actions" in repo settings after merging).

## Verified

- A 150-machine plan (60x electronic circuit + 90x copper cable, Helmod 2.2.11) generates 2300+ entities with zero overlapping tiles, passes the editor-schema validator, imports into factorio-blueprint-editor, and renders correctly.
- Frontend tests pass and `react-scripts build` compiles clean with CI=true.

## For a reviewer

- Inserter directions follow the "blueprint direction points at the pickup tile" convention; splitter side-load behavior is standard but hasn't been verified in a live game yet.
- Known limits (warned, not fatal): max 3 bussed items, max 3 item ingredients per recipe, no fluid handling. Yellow-belt throughput is far below Helmod's full-speed machine counts — machines will run starved on big plans; belt tiers/multi-lane buses are future work.

author: maisiebird2
body:
### Root cause

The orchestrator run died every time at the same spot with `TypeError: fetch failed`. This wasn't a transient network blip: PostgREST echoes the full request URL back in a `Content-Location` response header, and the bulk `.in()` queries (500 UUIDs, ~18 KB of query string) make that one header ~20 KB. Since #38 forced all script traffic onto HTTP/1.1, every response goes through undici's h1 parser, whose default header budget is 16 KiB total — so every such request failed deterministically with `UND_ERR_HEADERS_OVERFLOW`, surfaced only as "fetch failed" (probed: overflow starts at ~400 UUIDs; the server itself answers 200 even at 500). The same query shape worked fine over HTTP/2, which is why this only appeared now.

### Changes

- **`scripts/lib/http-dispatcher.mjs`** — raise the shared Agent's `maxHeaderSize` to 256 KiB. Fixes every bulk script at the transport layer where #38 introduced the limit, with plenty of headroom for the largest chunked query.
- **`scripts/lib/supabase-retry.mjs`** (new) — `runWithNetworkRetry()`: re-runs a Supabase query with short backoff only when the failure is network-shaped (response status 0 / connectivity-looking message, i.e. supabase-js's wrapping of a fetch rejection). HTTP-level errors (4xx/5xx) still surface on the first attempt. Covered by 11 vitest tests.
- **`scripts/sync-soundcloud.mjs`** — wrap the five bulk read loaders in the retry helper; per-artist writes stay un-retried by design (their failure handling defers to the next run). The fatal handler now prints the error's `cause`/`details`, so the next failure names its real reason instead of just "fetch failed" — this is exactly what exposed the root cause above.
- **`scripts/lib/harvest-failures.mjs`** — same retry wrapping for `loadFailureUrls`, which runs in callers' bootstrap path.

### Verification

- `npx vitest run scripts/lib` — 197 tests pass (186 existing + 11 new).
- `DRY_RUN=1 npx tsx scripts/sync-soundcloud.mjs --limit 1` — previously crashed 100% of the time on the `artist_enrichment` chunk query; now runs clean through it and processes artists normally.

body:
## Summary

Right-drag on the top-down office view already **orbited** (yaw) horizontally. Now vertical right-drag also **tilts** the pitch — from a near-straight-down overhead to a low oblique angle — so you can rotate *and* tilt the view with the same gesture.

## How it works

- Implemented in the map's **axonometric projection engine**, not as a CSS 3D transform, so **hit-testing stays exact**. `TILT` drives the depth-foreshortening (`UY`) and height scale (`VZ`); `worldFrom` already uses `UY`, so clicks/selection remain accurate at any tilt.
- The office centre is **re-anchored vertically** as tilt changes, so tilting never drifts the view off-screen.
- Horizontal drag = rotate (existing), vertical drag = tilt (new); a plain right-click still opens the context menu.
- **View reset** (the ⤢ button and right-click → Reset) now levels the tilt back to default alongside zoom/pan/rotation.

## Testing

Rendered the static map with headless Chromium at several pitch/yaw values (near-top-down, default, oblique, and a combined 30° rotate + oblique tilt) — geometry stays consistent, room labels stay upright, and the default (no-tilt) view is visually unchanged from before.

author: skleinjung-agent[bot]
body:
## The input changes

One requirement added, one retired.

```yaml
- id: specification-stands-alone-at-build-time
  statement: |
    the specification states every value the build turns on — a path, a filename, a literal
    spelling, a format, a default — rather than leaving it to a citation to fetch, so a builder
    reading the document with its citation tokens stripped can still produce the artifact.
```

`r:specification-does-not-restate-entries` is **retired**, superseded by it. That rule barred a sentence whose whole content restates an extracted entry — which is exactly the sentence the new rule requires, since a value a token would have fetched has to appear in the prose instead. What it cut beyond that case was already cut by the minimum-sufficient bar, so it fired on almost nothing while pulling authors the wrong way.

A first attempt kept both and carved an exception into the old rule. That was refereeing, not integration: the carve-out swallowed the rule's central case and still left reviewers reconciling two pulls sentence by sentence. One rule in one direction is the whole point.

## What prompted it

The third `minecraft/dev-kit` draft never named `behavior_pack/manifest.json`, `resource_pack/manifest.json`, or `dist/` anywhere. It said "two `stat` calls per package, at fixed relative paths" and "probe each package's two fixed source-manifest paths", each with a citation. A builder holding only `spec.md` could not construct a path.

That was not carelessness — it is what the checklist rewarded. Every prose test on it cut: one removes surplus *why*, the other asked whether striking a restating sentence left the specification whole. Naming a path a requirement also names reads as restatement under that test, so the safe move was to put it behind a token. Nothing on the list asked whether what remained could be acted on.

## Changes to `authoring`'s spec

- **`## Saying it once` is gone**, along with the "whole content" argument that existed only to serve the retired rule. The one thing it carried that nothing else did — the definition of "the specification", meaning everything after the Summary that is not the Open questions or Components block — moved into the opening of the build-document section, where the stripped-document read is stated.
- **The build-document section now argues two edges** rather than one: length, governed by `d:minimum-sufficient-specification` and the evidence on over- and under-specification, and values, governed by the new rule. It was subtractive throughout before.
- **Checklist**: the restatement row is removed and the new test takes its place as row 3 — a peer of the build-content test, not a qualifier on it. "Strike every citation token: does the specification still say what to build, with every path, literal, format, and default present in the prose or a component?"
- **The rule applied to this spec itself**, which failed it in five places: the citation token form `[[<kind>:<id>]]` was never spelled; the two source locator forms and their field names (`url` / `where` / `quote`, and `description`) were left to a fact citation; the cross-design source pointed at "the upstream's requirement" without naming `requirements.yaml`; "the field is filled" never named `falsifiers`; and "the specification" was used without its section boundaries.

## Worth a look

**The retirement records its reason in `rationale`, not in a `reason` field.** I asked for `reason` / `superseded_by`; those are fact-only fields, and `r:entry-schemas-are-closed` makes a field outside a requirement's schema an error. The rationale names both the reason and the replacement, matching the one existing retired requirement in the repo (`design/minecraft/dev-server/requirements.yaml`). If you would rather requirements carry retirement metadata as structured fields like facts do, that is a `doc-structure` change, not this one.

## Prompt changes that enforce it

The rule only bites if the agents applying it changed too. Three did:

- **`review-spec.md` dimension 6** told the panel that "a sentence whose whole content restates an entry it cites should cut without loss" — the retired rule, and precisely the sentence the new one requires. Left alone, the panel would have flagged every literal the next spec states. It now covers minimum-*why* only, and says outright that stating a value an entry fixes is never a finding there.
- **`review-spec.md` dimension 7** and **`capstone-review.md`'s first question** now read the spec the way the builder receives it, every citation token struck out, and check that each path, filename, literal spelling, format, and default is present in the prose or a component. Both previously asked "could a builder build from this alone?" while reading the annotated document, which is the version that always looks complete.
- **`write-design-doc.md`** summarises the authoring rules for the writer; its line about not re-narrating the extracted lists described the retired rule and now describes the new one.

`CLAUDE.md` needs nothing. Its retirement guidance uses `reason` and `superseded_by`, which are fact fields, and it is about facts.

## Related, not in this PR

The intent behind reviewing foundations rather than prose has a second half no rule states: prose must be *faithful* to what it cites, not merely carry a token. Today a spec can cite a requirement and overstate it, and the citation-presence check passes. Coming separately as `prose-matches-what-it-cites`.

## Not done here

The builder's artifact — stripped spec plus an appendix of requirement statements — is a format concern belonging to `doc-structure`. This PR assumes it; it does not specify it, and no build step emits it yet.

`npm run check` is green. `how-to-plan/authoring` remains `draft`; no decisions were added and no other design was touched.

author: zackees
body:
## Problem

`pip install ~/dev/clud` failed intermittently on Windows while another process was reinstalling `soldr`. Builds died with crates failing at random, `exit code: 1`, and **no compiler diagnostics at all**:

```
error: could not compile `litrs` (lib)
Caused by:
  process didn't exit successfully: `...\shims\rustc.exe ...` (exit code: 1)
```

## Root cause

The compiler shims under `~/.soldr*/v<version>/shims/` are hardlinks to the `soldr` binary, re-materialized whenever that binary changes. `materialize_executable`'s publish loop handled a stale target with `remove_file(target)` and left republication to a later retry.

That is wrong in two ways on Windows:

1. **It cannot replace a running shim.** Windows refuses to delete or overwrite a mapped executable image, so with a live compiler-wrapper process holding the shim, `remove_file` failed on all 20 attempts and materialization returned `Access is denied` (os error 5).
2. **It left a hole.** Between the delete and the next retry's rename, the shim path did not exist. A concurrent cargo spawning it in that window failed with a bare "cannot find the path specified" — which is exactly the diagnostic-free failure above, because the process that died was the wrapper, not the compiler.

## Fix

Rename the stale shim aside, then publish immediately:

- A running image **can** always be renamed even when it cannot be deleted, so the previously fatal case now succeeds.
- Two back-to-back renames keep the shim path continuously occupied.
- If publication still fails, the displaced file is renamed **back** — a failed attempt never leaves the shim missing.
- Displaced files are deleted best-effort and swept later, **scoped to this process's own PID** so a concurrent swap's restore target is never deleted out from under it.

The old `remove_file` remains as a fallback when the rename-aside itself fails, so same-volume stale files still get replaced rather than failing publication outright.

## Validation

- New Windows regression test `replaces_a_shim_whose_image_is_currently_running` spawns a real executable from the shim path and replaces it while the image is mapped. Verified it **fails against the pre-fix implementation** with the same `Access is denied` seen in the wild, and passes with the fix.
- `soldr cargo test -p soldr-cli --lib shim_materialize` — 11/11 pass.
- `soldr cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- Full `soldr cargo test -p soldr-cli --lib` — 875 pass, 1 failure in `cargo_front_door::tests::diagnostic_capture_does_not_wait_for_leaked_stderr_handle_after_cargo_exits`, which is **pre-existing**: it fails 3/3 on this tree with the change stashed. Untouched by this PR.
- `pip install ~/dev/clud` now succeeds repeatedly once the shim binary is not being rewritten mid-build.

author: quentinivankic
body:
Closes the defect the 2026-07-27 national roll exposed (task #40).

## What happened

The roll deleted **Kootenai National Forest's 50 USFS trailheads**, Frank
Church-River of No Return's 3, Aldo Leopold's 3, and 7 more across 8 areas —
while logging `federal usfs: 0 features in bbox` and exiting 0. No step failed.
The `cleared 10` in the summary was accurate and read as ordinary churn.

`federal usfs: 0 features` appeared for **23 of 50 states**, including Arizona
(93 features from the homelab minutes earlier) and New Mexico (155). A targeted
re-run recovered Idaho, which returned 362 that time, and New Mexico returned 0
*again* — so retrying is a coin flip, and every real attempt risks clearing more.

## Root cause — two independent holes in the same call

**1. An error is not an empty result.** ArcGIS answers a throttled, rejected or
over-limit query with **HTTP 200** and a body of `{"error": {...}}` — no
`features` key. The code did:

```python
feats = data.get("features") or []
if not feats:
    break
```

so a failure was indistinguishable from an empty layer. A genuine empty result is
a well-formed FeatureCollection with `"features": []`, so the key being *present*
is the signal that the query actually ran. `_features_or_raise` now raises
`ArcGISUnavailable` for an error body or an unexpected shape, and returns `[]`
only for a real empty collection.

**2. No retry at all** — alone among the remote calls in this script. Now on the
shared 30/90/300 ladder, but only for failures worth retrying: a rejected query
(`error 400`) answers the same every time, and burning the ladder on it would
repeat the missing-`shapely` mistake of retrying a deterministic failure and then
blaming the remote service.

## Fail closed

`fetch_federal` returns `(lots, failed_source_keys)`. When a source could not be
read, `process` carries that source's **existing** pins forward for any area
still blank in this run, so pass 3 sees no change and clears nothing. A stale
trailhead beats no trailhead — and `publish_areas.py` already does exactly this
carry-forward for parking across a republish, so the federal path was the
outlier.

- Carried pins are counted separately from the fill, so `federal fill added N`
  stays an honest count of NEW pins.
- A `::warning::` names the state and the source, so the log says which states
  need a re-run instead of that surfacing weeks later.

**Deliberately unchanged:** if OSM now maps parking for an area, the area is not
blank, OSM is authoritative, and its old federal pins are still meant to go. And
a source that answers *honestly empty* still clears — there is a test pinning
that specifically, because that signal is the one worth keeping.

## Verified three ways

1. **24 unit tests pass** (was 22). New cases cover all five failure shapes
   ArcGIS can return, and which of them deserve a retry.
2. **End-to-end with no network:** an area shipping two USFS trailheads keeps
   both when the layer 429s, and loses both when the layer answers empty.
   ```
   ::warning::NM: federal source(s) ['usfs'] unavailable — kept 2 existing pin(s)
   across 1 area(s) rather than clearing them. RE-RUN THIS STATE
   USFS unavailable -> parking = 2 pin(s)   OK: carried forward, nothing cleared
   USFS answers empty -> parking = 0 pin(s) OK: a real empty answer still clears
   ```
3. **Live `--state nm --dry-run`** against the real endpoints: NPS 152 features,
   USFS 155, parsed by the new path.

## Next, not in this PR

Re-run the 22 states where USFS returned 0. They hold **82 parking-blank federal
areas that have boundaries** — Sandia Mountain Wilderness (108 trails), Boundary
Waters Canoe Area Wilderness (100), Chiricahua (64), Aldo Leopold (43),
Pemigewasset (23). None of them got a working USFS pass in the roll. That re-run
is only safe once this is in, because today it can clear more than it adds.

author: dungle-scrubs
body:
**Plan:** `00-e2e-coverage` · **Milestone:** M0.2 - Build gate and clean slate

`src/server/client-bundle.generated.ts` is gitignored, and the suite drives the shell that bundle **is**. So a green run has always been able to be a green run against whatever the last build left on disk - which is indistinguishable, from the outside, from a green run against the code in the commit. #54 made the suite run somewhere other than a laptop; this makes its result mean something.

## The build gate

`globalSetup` compares the bundle's mtime against everything under `client/` and against `scripts/build-client.ts` (a change to *how* the bundle is made stales it as surely as a change to what goes in it), rebuilds when it is behind, and then **checks again**.

The second check is the point. "The build script exited 0" and "the artifact on disk is newer" are different claims, and they have not always agreed. If the bundle is still stale afterwards the run is refused rather than reported.

The logic lives in `test/e2e/gate.ts` with the build **injected**, which is what makes any of it testable - a gate written as four lines inside a Playwright hook can only ever be verified by hand, once, and then never again.

## Verification

**17 unit tests** over `gate.ts` (`test/e2e-gate.test.ts`), including the case the gate exists for: a build that exits 0 and changes nothing. Also live, in both directions:

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| source touched now, bundle older | `bundle is older than client/chrome/Shell.tsx - rebuilding` → run proceeds |
| source dated 2030 | **refused** - no build can ever catch up |

That second row was an accident while testing (`touch -t 203001010000`) and it produced a correct refusal with a *misleading message* - it blamed the build. A future-dated source is a clock or a restored-mtime problem, so it now gets its own diagnosis and tells you to `touch` the file.

Full suite: **74 passed, 1 skipped**, 2.6m. `typecheck`, `lint`, `bun test` (374 pass, up from 358) green.

## The teardown, and what it must not kill

`globalTeardown` kills what the suite left running. Scoping mattered more than reaping here: **you run Lucid from this same checkout**, so matching every process running `src/cli/main.ts` would reap your own hub.

A match needs a second signature only the harness produces - a path under `lucid-e2e-*`/`lucid-hub-e2e-*`, or `hub --port 0`, which is not something a human types. There is a test named for the case that must not happen (*LEAVES the developer's own hub from this same checkout*), covering a real hub, a real `open`, and a real `__serve` on a real file.

Verified against an actual leak rather than a mock: spawn a detached `__serve` holding a harness temp path, confirm it is alive, sweep, confirm it is not.

```
leaked pid: 55929 alive before sweep: true
  1 process outlived the suite - killing:
    55929  …/bun …/src/cli/main.ts __serve /var/folders/…/lucid-e2e-yY0daR/plan.html
killed count: 1 | alive after sweep: false
```

Every kill is **reported**, not tidied away. A survivor is a bug in whichever fixture should have stopped it, and M3.1's `use()` teardown is what should make this find nothing - a sweep that cleans up in silence hides the leak it exists to reveal. On a clean run it prints nothing, which is what it did on the full suite above.

## One claim weaker than the others

The run-root sweep is verified only against a synthetic tree. Nothing writes `~/.lucid-e2e/` until M5.5 builds the durable-path fixture, so unlike the rest of this milestone it is not exercised by a real run. That is the plan's sequencing rather than a gap introduced here, but it is worth saying rather than letting a green checkbox imply otherwise.

## Note on `dist/lucid`

Built once per run as specified, but nothing under `test/` runs it yet - every harness spawn goes through `bun run src/cli/main.ts`. Today a green job proves the binary *compiles* from this commit and nothing more; the compiled-binary scenario is Phase 5's. The comment in `global-setup.ts` says so rather than implying coverage that does not exist.

Preserves the single piece of unique work on `docs/board-ops-m2-verification` so that branch can be deleted without losing anything.

## What was actually unique

That branch (PR #26, closed as superseded by #28) is 108 commits behind `main` and holds one commit touching only `KANZ_TASKS.md`. Almost all of it is OPS-M2 status rows, replaced by #28's stronger per-workflow live evidence — that's why #26 was closed.

But one clause never reached `main`: the standing rule's second sentence, **"Nor is a working transport."**

`main` has *"a document, a roadmap, a comment, or a DONE line is not evidence."* It did not have the transport clause — which is a principle, not a status, and was earned the hard way: OPS-M2c authenticated the TUI to the gateway with no kubeconfig, rendered a real node, and was written up as the milestone being verified, when only the transport had been proven.

## Extended, because the pattern kept recurring

Two more instances this session paid for:

- **`kanz-build` was green on pull requests while every push to `main` failed** — PRs build without pushing, so the visible signal came from a path that never exercised the failing one.
- **`golangci-lint` sat `SKIPPED` for weeks** behind an earlier failing step. Its findings were invisible, not absent, and appeared the moment the step ahead of it went green.

## Method

Cherry-picked **as prose, not as a merge**. The branch's remaining content is stale by design and merging it would reintroduce superseded status claims. Board validator: 62 rows, exit 0.

Once this lands, `docs/board-ops-m2-verification` can be deleted with nothing lost.

**`composer verify:sources` is red on `main`** — `AGENTS.md` cites `GB-CORE-UPDATE-SINK`, but that row lives on the unmerged #378 branch, so `main` carries a reference with no row. Caught by the dangling-ID scan, which is exactly the guard for this.

Reported by the Coordination session, verified on a clean `main` at `ed4d902`.

**Fix:** describe the note instead of naming the ID. Adding the row here would duplicate #378's and conflict on merge, and the sentence never needed a specific citation — it illustrates a *class* of claim rather than resting on that row.

The irony is worth stating rather than stepping around: **the PR that introduced "verify the question, not the claim" is the one that broke the verification gate.** Same shape as the failure it documents — I checked the ID was correct, not that it resolved in the tree I was committing to.

**Also adds a better worked example** (supplied by Coordination): `git branch -a --sort=-committerdate | head -20` sorts by the date of the **commit a branch points at**, not branch creation — so a branch cut minutes ago from an older commit sorts by that older date and drops off the list. It exits 0, prints a plausible answer, and omits precisely the case it's run to catch. A silent failure, which is worse than a loud one.

`verify-sources`: 33 citations, green. Docs-only.

author: frikkern
body:
Registry parity read 66/66 while **20 blocks in live production papers** carried types that NO renderer on ANY surface knew — `h2`×12, `h3`×5, `h1`×1, `ordered-list`×2 — so they drew the unknown-block box on web, TUI and mobile simultaneously. Same bug class as the `bulletList` alias family already fixed for 77 blocks. Task: mob-zb-bl-heading-alias-drift ## The ruling (criterion 0, charter D57) **Aliases only, at read time, on all four render surfaces. No data migration, and none filed as owed.** Three independent grounds: a per-row migration is priced out by the recorded ~25-minute 500-serving incident; raw mutate can re-introduce these spellings the day after any migration, so the alias is required *anyway* and a migration would be a one-shot that leaves the hole open; and the identical bug class was fixed alias-only and held. ## The load-bearing finding **The level comes from the TYPE, not from `level`.** A census re-run over all 553 published papers found **6 of the 18 drifted headings** (1 `h2` + all 5 `h3`s) carry **no `level` key at all** — so a naive `h3: heading` alias would have shipped a silent defect, rendering them at every surface's `headingLevel` default of 2. The type overwrites a contradicting stored level (0 live blocks contradict). Pinned by test on all four surfaces. ## Surfaces changed | Surface | Change | |---|---| | `compose.ex` | `@heading_aliases` + `ordered-list` clauses (View + Email) | | react `core.ts` | `headingAtLevel` + `'ordered-list': numberedList` | | `pdrender` | `headingAtLevel` struct + `ordered-list` (TUI) | | mobile `core-prose.tsx` | `headingAtLevel(n)` + `'ordered-list': numberedList` | `tiers.ex` is **deliberately untouched** — existing aliases are absent from it by design, and the VARIABLE-guard form is reused so these spellings stay out of the tiers-completeness and pd-parity extractors. Re-proven: `scripts/pd-parity-completeness.sh` still reports 60 in-scope types. `from_markdown.ex` needed nothing — it is a *producer* that already emits canonical `heading`/`list` shapes and can never emit an h-tag. ## Per-surface before/after, on the REAL live blocks | | before | after | |---|---|---| | react/web | `
Unsupported block: h3
` | `

Shipped

`, `
  1. Count a criterion…` | | Elixir View+Email | `%{"kind" => "_raw", "html" => "…Unsupported block: h3…"}` | `%{"kind" => "PdHeading", "level" => 3}` | | Go TUI | `╭───╮ │ unknown block: h3 │ ╰───╯` | `Shipped` at the level-3 style; `1. 2. 3.` | | mobile | 5/5 new tests FAILED, `console.warn` unsupported | 5/5 pass, correct level per type | ## Honest residual — not fixed here On **Elixir and Go** the 2 `ordered-list` blocks now render correct ordering and correct arity but **blank item text**, because their items are map-shaped (`{content:[…]}`). Run-proven orthogonal: the *canonical* `list` with the same items is equally blank, so this is the pre-existing list-item normalization defect (charter D38, `task-993d136b0fbf2fd1`), not an alias defect. react and mobile already normalize map items and show full text. The alias is a strict improvement everywhere and regresses nothing. **Recorded ceiling:** `h4`/`h5`/`h6` stay unaliased — zero in the corpus, and `PdHeading` models only levels 1-3. An `h4` keeps degrading honestly, pinned by test. **Coverage gap named, not closed:** the four pre-existing alias spellings have zero Elixir test anywhere in `api/test`. This slice tests only the D57 family it ships. ## Mutation proofs Every new test carries a guard proving it can fail: - **Go** — the vacuity guard *fired on first run*: heading levels 2 and 3 are byte-identical under `NoColor` (they differ only by foreground color), which would have made every "renders at level N" assertion vacuous. The test now forces `TrueColor`. Explicit mutation: stripping `attrs["level"] = h.level` reds with `h3` painting the level-2 accent `38;2;63;207;142` instead of the level-3 dim `38;2;81;81;91`. - **mobile** — 5/5 tests fail on unmodified source; a level-less `heading` must NOT match the h3 size. - **Elixir** — asserts levels 2 and 3 actually differ in the composed node. ## Gates - mobile `pnpm test` **37 suites / 684 tests**, `typecheck`, `lint` — all green on the rebased tree - react vitest **15 files / 326 tests**, `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` — green - Go `go test ./internal/pdrender/`, `go vet`, `gofmt` — green - `scripts/pd-parity-completeness.sh` 60 in-scope, `docs-anchors-check.sh` PASS, `check-doc-budgets.sh` PASS - **Elixir: `compose.ex` IS touched**, so the Elixir Test CI gate must be green before merge. The new `heading_alias_drift_test.exs` is 7/7 locally and `mix format --check-formatted` is clean; the full local suite was still running at hand-off. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
## Summary Implements an OTLP metrics pipeline (11 named metrics), an optional Prometheus `GET /metrics` scrape endpoint, `#[tracing::instrument]` spans on PR-validation rules and GitHub API calls, and a structured, dependency-aware `GET /health` endpoint — gated by two new opt-in env vars (`MERGE_WARDEN_METRICS_ENDPOINT`, `MERGE_WARDEN_HEALTH_CHECKS`). Built via the full Tech Lead TDD pipeline (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR → AUDIT + SECURITY → DOCUMENT → VERIFY). All phases passed; see `.llm/workflow-state.md` for the complete audit trail. references #334 ## What changed (operator-facing) - 11 OTLP metrics exported whenever `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set (same var traces already use). 3 of the 11 (`ingress.queue.enqueue_duration_ms`, `ingress.queue.depth`, `ingress.queue.age_oldest_message_secs`) are defined for forward-compatibility but have no call site yet in this binary — queue-mode enqueueing happens in a separate out-of-repo service, and `queue-runtime` 0.2.1 has no depth-query API. Documented, not a defect. - `GET /metrics` (Prometheus text format), opt-in via `MERGE_WARDEN_METRICS_ENDPOINT=prometheus`; 404 otherwise. - `GET /health` now returns structured JSON (`status`, `checks.{github_api,config,queue}`) with HTTP 200/207/503 for healthy/degraded/unhealthy. Default `basic` mode is unchanged (fast, no dependency calls). Opt-in `MERGE_WARDEN_HEALTH_CHECKS=full` actually probes GitHub reachability (via an authenticated `get_app()` call) and queue connectivity. - `rule_name`, `endpoint`, and `status` span attributes added across PR-validation rules (`crates/core`) and ~22 GitHub API call sites (`crates/developer_platforms`). See `.changeset/observability-metrics-health.md` and `docs/user/reference/environment-variables.md` / `http-endpoints.md` for full operator-facing detail. ## Audit summary (QA Engineer — verdict CLEAR) Found and fixed 3 real bugs, each with a regression test verified red→green: 1. `opentelemetry-prometheus` double-appended `_total` to already-`_total`-suffixed counter names (would have rendered `ingress_webhook_requests_total_total` on `/metrics`) — fixed via `.without_counter_suffixes()`. 2. Test-infra bug: health-check "unreachable GitHub" tests were silently hitting real `api.github.com` instead of the intended mock, because the test client didn't override the SDK's base URL — fixed, plus a genuine hung-connection timeout regression test added. 3. Zero test coverage existed for the `MetricsRecorder` bridge (`pr.validation.duration_ms` / `pr.bypass.activations_total`) — 5 tests added proving correct once-only recording on all exit paths (success, error, early-return, multi-bypass). 15 new tests added during audit. Full workspace: **1324 passed, 4 ignored (pre-existing, credential-gated), 0 failed.** Non-blocking observations: no `# HELP` description text on the 11 metrics (cosmetic); the Prometheus registry is a process-wide `OnceLock` (architectural, out of audit scope). ## Security summary (Security Reviewer — no critical/high, no hard blockers) Highest-priority check — whether the authenticated GitHub health probe (`get_app()`) could leak App credentials/JWTs into the public, unauthenticated `/health` response on failure — verified **clean**: all error paths discard the underlying error and substitute static generic messages, backed by adversarial tests (`full_mode_error_message_does_not_leak_private_key_material`, `..._does_not_contain_rust_backtrace_markers`). `cargo audit` clean for the new dependencies (`opentelemetry-prometheus 0.32.0`, `prometheus 0.14.0`). Full findings below (Medium/Low, all non-blocking):
Full contents of .llm/findings/observability.md $(cat .llm/findings/observability.md)
## Verification (Verifier — verdict PASS) All 9 acceptance criteria from `.llm/task.md` verified pass, with evidence (file/line/test). Catalog (`docs/catalog.md`) confirmed current against every new abstraction. Doc-vs-code drift check found no new discrepancies beyond the one already honestly disclosed in `http-endpoints.md` (the `/metrics` `Content-Type` header is axum's default `text/plain; charset=utf-8` rather than the Prometheus-conventional `text/plain; version=0.0.4` — flagged as a maintainer decision, not a functional defect). ## Test plan - [x] `cargo test --workspace` — 1324 passed, 4 ignored, 0 failed - [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` — clean (pre-existing, unrelated findings only) - [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean - [x] `cargo audit` — clean for new dependencies 🤖 Generated with the Tech Lead multi-agent TDD pipeline (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR → AUDIT + SECURITY → DOCUMENT → VERIFY)

## 解决的问题

多 Agent 编排链路存在三类闭环缺陷：

1. Planner 产出的计划转 TaskGraph 时**步骤间依赖丢失**，导致下游步骤在上游未完成时被提前调度；
2. Scheduler 在部分分支失败/跳过时**终态语义不明确**，独立分支可能被错误终止，`final_result` 与实际执行情况不一致；
3. TaskLogger、SSE 事件流与前端展示的 `step_result` / `final_result` **口径不一致**，无法从 UI 还原真实执行结果。

## 本层新增内容

- **TaskGraph 依赖恢复**：`src/orchestration/plan_to_task_graph.py` 补齐 Planner 计划到 TaskGraph 的依赖推导与校验；`src/prompts/planner.md` 同步补充依赖描述约束。
- **Scheduler 终态闭环**：`src/orchestration/runtime.py`（+217）、`scheduler.py` 完善工作流终态语义；分支失败只影响其依赖闭包，不再错误终止独立分支；`providers.py` 支持 provider 优先路由。
- **TaskLogger / SSE / 前端结果展示**：`src/robust/task_logger.py` 补充终态记录；`src/service/web_app.py` 与 `web/app.js`（+236）对齐 `step_result` / `final_result` 结果契约与分支反馈展示。
- **调度及远程链路回归**：新增 `test_scheduler_multi_agent_closure.py`、`test_scheduler_runtime.py`、`test_task_logger_terminal.py`、`test_routing_provider_preferred.py`、`test_web_scheduler_result_contract.py`、`tests/integration/test_wangqiang_scheduler.py` 等 10+ 个测试文件；`remote_agents/hr_assistant_agent.py` 远程链路配套增强。

## 明确不包含的范围

- 不包含 Agent Contract / Result Envelope 模型（见上层 PR feat: 引入 Agent Contract 与三 Agent 契约）；
- 不包含 Agent 结果归一化与 Artifact fan-in；
- 不包含结构化错误协议（FailureDescriptor）与前端错误展示。

## 测试命令和结果

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -o addopts= `
  tests/test_scheduler_runtime.py `
  tests/test_scheduler_gate_routing.py `
  tests/test_web_scheduler_entry.py `
  tests/test_task_logger_terminal.py -q
```

结果：**36 passed** (6.09s)。

栈顶分支 211 项扩展回归：**209 passed, 2 skipped**（2 项 skip 为需要真实远程环境的集成用例，按设计跳过）。

## 依赖的下层 PR

无（本 PR 为分支栈最底层，base 为 `main`）。

## 安全边界及兼容策略

- 分支失败传播遵循 fail-closed：失败仅沿依赖闭包传播，未受影响分支正常收尾，不放行未验证结果；
- `.env.example` 新增配置项均带默认值，未配置时行为与现状一致；
- `src/workflow/process.py` / `cache.py` 改动保持既有工作流入口兼容，旧调用路径不受影响。

author: ayasukaran
body:
## Why

Majsoul logins kept dying with server error `151` (`ERR_CLIENT_VERSION`) on every game release, because the client code version sent at login was a hardcoded constant with no discoverable source.

## What the server actually checks

Measured against the live CN server with a real account:

| Sent | Result |
|---|---|
| `client_version_string = WebGL_2022-0.16.257` (current) | OK |
| `WebGL_2022-0.16.254` | OK |
| `WebGL_2022-0.16.253` | **151** |
| `WebGL_2022-0.17.0`, `WebGL_2022-0.16.999`, `WebGL_2022-99.99.999` | OK |
| `0.16.257` (no prefix), `WebGL_2019-0.16.257` | **151** |
| `client_version { resource = 0.10.0 }` with a current version string | OK |
| `client_version { package = 9.9.99 }` | OK |

Conclusions:

* Only `client_version_string` is validated. The `client_version { resource, package }` message is **not checked at all**.
* The check is a **lower bound**, not equality: everything from about `current - 3` patches upward is accepted, including arbitrarily future values.
* The `WebGL_2022-` prefix is required.
* `fetchGameLiveList` and `fetchGameRecord` behave identically whether the version is exact or inflated, so the choice has no downstream effect.
* A nonexistent account returns `1002` regardless of version, i.e. the account check runs before the version check — so the version cannot be probed without real credentials.

## The change

Since the accepted set is upward-closed, the version does not need to be *known*, only bracketed. On error `151` the collector searches for the lowest version the server still accepts and adopts it:

* escalate `+4, +16, +64, …` until one is accepted, then binary-search back to the boundary — about six logins for the usual few-patch gap;
* probes are paced five seconds apart, because a burst of failed logins is itself worth not doing;
* the result is persisted under the watch cache, so a restart does not repeat the search, and is ignored once a code update pins something newer;
* the configured `client_version` still wins under normal operation.

Reporting the floor rather than something comfortably above it is deliberate. An arbitrarily high version is accepted but is a trivially detectable fingerprint; the floor sits three patches under the live client, which is exactly what a browser tab that has not been reloaded reports.

A Majsoul release now costs a short search instead of an outage until someone edits a constant.

## Scope notes

* This relies on the check remaining a lower bound. If Majsoul ever adds an upper bound the search still terminates — it just fails and logs, rather than silently logging in with a wrong version.
* `discover_package_version` is left in place. It is now known not to be load-bearing for login, but it keeps the frame faithful to a real client and never blocks login.

## Test

`cargo test --lib`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo fmt --check` all clean.

`search_version_floor` takes its probe as a closure, so the boundary logic is unit-tested offline: it finds the exact floor for near, far and adjacent cases, and gives up rather than climbing forever. The six-login figure and the floor `0.16.254` were both measured against the live server before the code was written.

body:
## Summary

Introduces a pre-match lobby screen that all players see on load instead of dropping directly into gameplay. Players can either start a solo match against bots of chosen difficulty, or wait for other players to join and ready up before a synchronized countdown begins. The relay now owns match-start state (ready flags, deployment status) to coordinate the start signal across clients.

## Key Changes

- **New Match Start UI** (`src/match/ui.js`): Self-contained view with two panels — Bots (pick garrison size and deploy immediately) and Multiplayer (share room link, both players ready up, relay fires start signal). Includes room code display, player roster with ready status, and countdown display.

- **Match System** (`src/match/index.js`): State machine managing setup → countdown → live transitions. Defers garrison spawning until match start (respecting player's bot choice or none for players-only matches). Handles ready toggling, deployment, and countdown timing. Emits `match:start` and `match:countdown` events.

- **Relay match-start logic** (`server/index.mjs`, `worker/room.js`): Added `ready` and `deployed` flags per peer. `maybeStart()` fires the start signal when all players in a not-yet-live room have readied up. Live rooms (anyone deployed) skip the ready flow so late joiners drop straight in. Broadcasts lobby state and countdown duration.

- **Net System updates** (`src/net/index.js`): Carries match-start lobby state (`live`, `players` with ready/deployed status). Emits `net:lobby`, `net:countdown`, `net:join`, `net:leave` events for the match system to consume. Added `setReady()`, `deploy()`, `copyInvite()` methods and `everConnected` flag to distinguish "connecting" from "dropped out".

- **Audio cues** (`src/audio/foley.js`): New synthesized UI sounds — rising chirp on join, mechanical click on ready, square-wave tick per countdown second, low horn on deployment.

- **AI deferred garrison** (`src/ai/index.js`): Added `deferGarrison` config flag. When set, garrison doesn't spawn during boot; the match system calls `ai.populate()` with the chosen size at match start.

- **Documentation**: Updated MULTIPLAYER.md with match-start flow, bot presets, and relay coordination details. Updated README and ARCHITECTURE.md to reflect the new subsystem.

## Implementation Details

- The Match Start UI is self-contained (CSS + DOM) following the pattern of `src/net/ui.js`, so it doesn't reach into the HUD stylesheet.
- Ready state and the "is live" flag live on the relay because two clients cannot each independently decide when "everyone is ready" became true.
- Countdown is wall-clock based (not frame-time) so dropped frames don't stretch one player's countdown relative to the other.
- The deployment horn is the only UI sound that rings past a second; its audio slot is held that long so the tail doesn't get stolen mid-swell.
- Players-only matches spawn zero bots; bot garrison is per-client and spawned at deploy time.
- Late joiners to a live room see "match in progress" and a **Deploy now** button instead of the ready flow.

author: im-ian
body:
Supersedes #716, which bundled these same 11 bumps but could not merge: `react-resizable-panels` 3.0.6 → 4.12.2 is a breaking major and the type check failed on 12 errors. This branch carries the bumps plus the migration.

## Dependency bumps

Ten are patch or minor and need no code changes: `@tanstack/react-virtual` 3.14.8, `lucide-react` 1.27.0, `react` / `react-dom` 19.2.8, `@playwright/test` 1.62.0, `@storybook/*` + `storybook` 10.5.4, `@vitejs/plugin-react` 6.0.4, `postcss` 8.5.23.

## react-resizable-panels v4

The renames are the visible half of the change:

| v3 | v4 |
| --- | --- |
| `PanelGroup` | `Group` |
| `PanelResizeHandle` | `Separator` |
| `direction` | `orientation` |
| `autoSaveId="x"` | `useDefaultLayout({ id: "x", storage })` |
| `ref` + `ImperativePanelHandle` | `panelRef` + `usePanelRef()` |
| `order={n}` | derived from JSX position |
| `defaultSize={30}` | `defaultSize="30%"` |

That last row is the one that fails quietly rather than loudly: v4 reads bare numbers as **pixels**, so every size prop had to gain a unit. The `SIDEBAR_*` / `RIGHT_PANEL_*` constants in `App.tsx` are now percent strings, which keeps them usable both as props and as arguments to the imperative `resize()`.

`useDefaultLayout` has to run at the top level of a component, so `PersistentGroup` wraps it once rather than threading `defaultLayout` / `onLayoutChanged` through all nine groups. Persistence also moves onto `onLayoutChanged`, which fires when a pointer drag ends instead of on every pointer move, so a resize now writes to `localStorage` once.

Group layouts are `{ panelId: weight }` maps in v4, not positional arrays. `LayoutRenderer` converts at the boundary. Only the ratio matters and `normalizeSplitSizes` already rescales to sum 100, so persisted pane splits round-trip and the store needs no migration.

## ResizeHandle

This is the part renames did not cover. The component drives its hover, drag, and collapsed-neighbour visuals off DOM attributes that v4 stopped emitting — v4 ships only `data-group`, `data-panel`, `data-separator`, `data-disabled`, and `data-testid`.

- `data-resize-handle-state` → `data-separator`, whose `active` value also replaces the removed `onDragging` callback.
- `data-panel-size` / `data-panel-collapsible` are gone, so a collapsed neighbour is now detected from the inline flex-grow the library writes. Every Acorn panel declares a `minSize`, so only a genuinely collapsed panel reaches zero.
- Adjacent panels are found by sibling walk instead of `aria-controls`, which covers both sides with one code path.
- Per-handle `hitAreaMargins` is replaced by the Group-level `resizeTargetMinimumSize`. The default is 20px coarse / 10px fine — at least as forgiving as the old 12/6 values, so no explicit prop is set.
- v4 added a built-in double-click that resets a panel to `defaultSize`. Acorn binds double-click to re-expanding a collapsed panel, so `disableDoubleClick` turns the built-in off and the existing handler stays.

## Verification

Every CI step was run locally against this branch:

- `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate` — no known vulnerabilities
- `pnpm run typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm run test` — 1180 passed / 103 files
- `pnpm run build:frontend` — built

`src/test/setup.ts` gains a no-op `ResizeObserver`. jsdom does not implement one and v4 constructs one whenever a Group mounts, which crashed 13 tests across `RightPanel` and `PullRequestDetailModal` on mount alone.

## What still needs a human

The `ResizeHandle` rewrite is the risk in this PR and it is not the kind of thing the test suite covers — jsdom reports zero-size elements, so hover, drag, and collapse behaviour cannot be asserted there. Worth a pass in the running app before or after merge:

- [ ] Drag each divider; confirm the accent line appears while dragging
- [ ] Collapse the sidebar and the right panel to the edge; confirm the white grip pill appears
- [ ] Hover a collapsed divider; confirm the "Double-click to expand" tooltip
- [ ] Double-click it; confirm the panel re-expands rather than resetting
- [ ] Restart; confirm panel sizes and pane splits were restored

Closes #716
