author: weiqingy
body:
Part of the FLIP-497 implementation stack under umbrella [FLINK-36953](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-36953). Landing order:

| Step | Sub-task | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PR-1a | [FLINK-40167](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40167) | EARLY_FIRE hint surface + option validation (#28353, merged) |
| PR-1b | [FLINK-40168](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40168) | Thread the hint into the interval join (#28796, merged) |
| **PR-2 (this PR)** | [FLINK-40169](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40169) | `target` option |
| PR-3 | [FLINK-40170](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40170) | Update-producing changelog mode + insert-only guard |
| PR-4 | [FLINK-40171](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40171) | Runtime early-fire emit + retraction |
| PR-5 | [FLINK-40172](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40172) | Processing-time early fire on an event-time join |
| PR-6 | [FLINK-40173](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40173) | State restore coverage |
| PR-7 | [FLINK-40174](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/FLINK-40174) | User-facing documentation |

## What is the purpose of the change

Adds an optional `target` option to the `EARLY_FIRE` hint so a hint can be explicitly scoped to a single operator kind. Only `interval_join` is accepted today, and an omitted `target` means `interval_join`, so existing hints keep their meaning. This is a forward-compatibility guard: it keeps a bare `EARLY_FIRE` hint from silently expanding its scope if other operators honor the hint in the future.

## Brief change log

  - Add `EarlyFireJoinHintOptions.TARGET` (optional `stringType`) and the `INTERVAL_JOIN` constant.
  - The `EARLY_FIRE` KV option checker validates `target` against the supported set. Any other value fails planning.
  - `StreamPhysicalIntervalJoinRule` applies the hint only when it targets the interval join, and leaves a hint aimed at another operator kind untouched. That rule-level check is redundant with validation today, since an unsupported value already fails planning. It is there so that a hint aimed at a future operator kind is ignored by this rule rather than misapplied.

## Verifying this change

This change added tests and can be verified as follows:

  - `EarlyFireJoinHintTest`: an explicit `target='interval_join'` still threads `earlyFireDelay`/`earlyFireTimeMode` into the exec plan, and an unsupported `target` value fails planning with a message naming the supported set.

## Does this pull request potentially affect one of the following parts:

  - Dependencies (does it add or upgrade a dependency): no
  - The public API, i.e., is any changed class annotated with `@Public(Evolving)`: yes (a new option on the `@PublicEvolving` `EarlyFireJoinHintOptions`)
  - The serializers: no
  - The runtime per-record code paths (performance sensitive): no
  - Anything that affects deployment or recovery: no
  - The S3 file system connector: no

## Documentation

  - Does this pull request introduce a new feature? yes (an option on the FLIP-497 hint)
  - If yes, how is the feature documented? in the documentation PR at the end of this stack (PR-7)

author: kerem-ersoz
body:
## Why

The unofficial `garminconnect` integration has no push/webhook, so workouts only reach the local library when someone runs `fetch garmin` by hand. This adds a background job that polls Garmin roughly every 15 minutes and exports new activities automatically, shortly after they sync.

## What it does

Near-real-time (poll-based, not instant) export driven by Docker + launchd on macOS. Two changes to the fetch path make frequent polling safe and cheap:

- **Session reuse (token cache).** The first login caches the garth session tokens; every later run resumes from that cache instead of logging in fresh. Fresh logins every 15 minutes quickly trip Garmin CAPTCHA / rate limiting (429s). Configurable via `GARMINTOKENS` or `--token-dir`, default `~/.garminconnect`.
- **Incremental downloads.** With a persistent `--raw-dir`, any activity whose `.fit` already exists is skipped (matched by activityId), so each poll only fetches what is new. Skipped/new counts are logged.

New `fetch garmin` options: `--token-dir` and `--json-dir` (writes one JSON per new activity, named to match the raw `.fit`).

## Scheduling layer

- `scripts/garmin-export.sh` - Docker wrapper: builds the library tree, checks the Docker daemon is up (logs and exits 0 if not, so launchd does not retry-spam), archives raw `.fit` plus per-activity JSON, appends to `~/.fit2json/logs`.
- `deploy/com.fit2json.garmin-export.plist` - launchd template (`StartInterval` 900; injects a PATH so `docker` resolves under launchd's minimal environment).
- `scripts/install-launchd.sh` / `scripts/uninstall-launchd.sh` - install/remove via `launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID` (interval overridable with `INTERVAL`).
- `scripts/seed-garmin-login.sh` - one-time interactive login to seed the token cache (handles 2FA/MFA).

## Notes for reviewers

- **Version tolerance.** The published image installs garminconnect 0.3.x while local dev may have 0.2.x, and they differ: the garth client is exposed as `.client` (0.3.x) vs `.garth` (0.2.x), and 0.3.x adds a `prompt_mfa` callback. Persistence dumps via whichever attribute exists, and MFA is wired only when supported (interactive prompt, or a clean error when unattended). Without this, token persistence silently no-ops on 0.3.x and every poll re-logs in.
- **Backward compatible.** Token caching is additive; email/password still work as before.
- **Tested for real.** Ran the full flow end to end against a live account: fetched 80 activities (raw + JSON), then a second run resumed from the cached token (no login) and skipped all existing activities. Network-free unit tests (mocked client) cover token resume, credential fallback + persistence on both attribute names, and skip-existing dedup; the full suite passes.
- **Follow-up:** consider pinning `garminconnect` (for example `==0.3.7`) for reproducibility; the code handles both versions either way.

README has a new "Automatic / continuous export (macOS, Docker + launchd)" section covering setup, the one-time seed, changing the interval, logs, and uninstall.

author: tfcollins
body:
Follow-up to #98.

The shared release concurrency group was also applied to pull-request and branch runs. GitHub keeps only one pending run per concurrency group, so the Debian workflow was cancelled while the native-system workflow ran. This keeps the shared group for tag finalizers but isolates non-tag runs by workflow and ref.

It also builds fpm packages from a disposable source copy so root-running Linux containers cannot leave generated, root-owned egg-info in the checkout.

Verification:
- `pytest -q test/test_release_preflight.py` (9 passed)
- Bash syntax and workflow YAML parsing
- #98 hosted native build/install/smoke jobs passed on Debian 12, Fedora 42, and macOS 14; this PR reruns those jobs with the isolation fix.

author: jiangzhuo
body:
`ggml/` is now upstream's tree verbatim. The `conv_transpose_1d` CUDA kernel was the last local patch, and it is gone because the operator it patched is gone. ## Why the patch existed Two reasons, only one of them recorded: - Upstream's `supports_op` accepts `CONV_TRANSPOSE_1D` only when both operands are F32, so with halved weights those four decoder nodes fell back to the CPU **silently** — the undeclared placement `docs/port-validation.md` calls a hard failure. - Upstream's kernel scales quadratically in input length. `ljs-long` took over 240 s against 1.48 s patched — on the **F32** profile, which carries no halved weights and by the recorded description should have been unaffected. ## What replaces it `transpose_conv1d_without_bias` expresses the operation as a column matrix multiply followed by `ggml_col2im_1d` — what the fused op decomposes into, and upstream already, with CPU, CUDA **and Vulkan** kernels. `ggml_mul_mat` takes an F16 `src0` on the ordinary weight path, so the `supports_op` widening is unnecessary; the quadratic kernel is never reached. The layout recipe is [qwentts.cpp](https://github.com/ServeurpersoCom/qwentts.cpp)'s, from its `ARCHITECTURE.md`: merge the kernel's leading `[kernel, out_channels]` pair so `k` varies faster than `oc`, then transpose so the multiply reduces over the input channels. Faster than the **patched** kernel, not merely than upstream's — four `upsample` stages at `ljs-long` shapes on GB10: | | fused op, patched | mul_mat + col2im_1d | | --- | --- | --- | | CPU, four stages | 204 ms | 130 ms | | CUDA, four stages | 33.8 ms | 4.9 ms | Agreement with the fused op is exact on a small case and 5e-7 relative at real F32 shapes. ## What it cost Transposed-convolution weights now stay F32 in every profile. CUDA's F16 matrix multiply accumulates in half precision where the templated kernel had upconverted and accumulated in F32, so halving these eight tensors would have taken CUDA from bit-exact agreement with the F32 reference to ~3e-3 relative, to save 5.32 MB. All four packages were re-cut (byte-identical across two quantizer runs); a package built earlier is refused by tensor type at load rather than run at reduced accuracy. **The published Hugging Face weights are therefore stale and will not load.** Re-uploading is not part of this PR. ## Also fixed, incidentally Vulkan rejects `CONV_TRANSPOSE_1D` with an F16 `src0` exactly as CUDA did, and the patch only ever touched CUDA — so VITS's F16 decoder had been falling back to the CPU on Vulkan the whole time, undetected. And Qwen3-TTS's intake expected to need a 1-D column scatter-add operator; it does not. Kokoro is untouched: it never used the fused operator, and keeps F16 weights with the tolerances measured for them. ## Coverage `transpose_conv1d` is exercised with several channels in both directions, on every registered backend, against the transposed convolution written out from its definition. The single-channel cases that preceded it cannot see a channel-ordering mistake — verified by making one, which they pass and the new cases fail. The helper's rejection contract is covered too: null operands, non-positive stride, negative padding, channel mismatch, a batched kernel, and cropping at or past the whole signal. Verified by removing the `ne[3]` guard, which makes the batched-kernel case reach a GGML assertion and abort. ## Measurement **Corrected after review.** `tests/tolerances/vits.json` holds **84** stage entries, not 42: CUDA under `profiles/

/backends/CUDA/stages`, CPU under a sibling `stages` key on the profile itself. The first pass here probed the shape with `profiles[*].backends`, saw only `{'CUDA'}`, and re-measured one branch — so 42 CPU entries survived the operator change still describing the operator they were measured against, and the card metadata disagreed with them. All 84 are now measured from the same runs. Twelve entries moved, the six CPU and six CUDA `waveform-decoder` probes. **Every structural probe on both backends is still exact on every case.** The CUDA half returned identical values across two independent runs. All twelve card figures match the registry to the digit. Waveform drift moved under 1% except vctk F16 on CUDA (0.1957 → 0.2166); the decoder's PCM drift is dominated by TF32 and by the weights that are still halved, so that is noise rather than the transposed convolution. Honest caveats: - The model cards **drop** their RTX 4070 SUPER column — that host was not available, and carrying the figure forward would describe packages that no longer exist. - The GB10 column in `docs/models/vits-ljspeech.md` was **replaced rather than updated**: its F32 and F16 entries disagreed by an order of magnitude with the same stage's record in `tests/tolerances/vits.json`. That discrepancy predates this change and was not reconstructed. ## Commits 1. `Take the Kokoro LSTM's cross-backend bound per device` — a **pre-existing** failure, not caused by this work. Its `1e-4` bound was measured under the strict-FP32 gate; commit `9959795` removed that gate and re-measured `tests/tolerances/` but not this file. It kept passing only because a stale build directory still set `GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_TF32=ON`, an option that commit deleted — so that directory cannot be reconfigured and its binaries answer a question nobody is asking. Built clean it reports 7.06e-4 on CUDA at length 37 against 1.79e-7 on the CPU. 2. `Replace VITS's fused transposed convolution, emptying ggml-patches` — the change above. Its message claims a "42-entry CUDA grid"; see commit 3. 3. `Re-measure the CPU half of the VITS grid, and fix the docs it contradicted` — the review response: the grid correction above, plus documentation that still described transpose-convolution weights as F16 in `docs/quantization.md` and in `docs/porting/families/vits.md`'s VCTK section, either of which would have led a reader to build a package the loader refuses. ## Follow-up, deliberately not here With no local modification left, `ggml/` could become a submodule at the same SHA, dropping 1,992 files and ~19.5 MB. That changes cloning, sdist packaging and re-vendoring, and should be its own change. ## Gates - unit 59/59, integration 27/27 (all 14 VITS golden stages), `clang-format` clean - CUDA 13.3 / GB10 / sm_121a, built against **verbatim upstream ggml** 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: streamentry
body:
## What changed

- add `book/edition.json` as the sole schema-v1 authority for title, credit, language, output identity, source binding, cover copy, shared labels, accessibility text, and validation scope
- make Typst, the EPUB builder, release verification, frozen-candidate checks, and Publication CI consume that contract
- fail closed on duplicate or unknown keys, malformed locale and paths, unsafe identifiers, timestamp drift, metadata drift, and cross-format identity mismatches
- validate contract-bound XHTML head metadata, OPF metadata, navigation, cover alt text, and future-edition artifact paths
- document the evidence that must remain separate for any future locale and refresh the deterministic EPUB and release record

## Why

The prior publication identity was repeated across Typst, Python, and CI. That made a future translation or filename change capable of producing internally inconsistent PDF, EPUB, release evidence, or external-gate checks. One strict contract makes those disagreements observable and testable.

## Reader and maintainer impact

The current Vietnamese PDF is byte-identical to the previously verified PDF. The reflowable EPUB remains deterministic and structurally equivalent while its publication data now has one authority. A future locale still requires translated content, rights, doctrinal and safety review, novice evidence, and reader-app evidence; Vietnamese results do not transfer.

## Validation

- 123/123 `unittest` tests passed
- 123 `pytest` tests plus 37 subtests passed
- two consecutive builds produced identical PDF and EPUB hashes
- release verifier passed: 149 PDF pages, 155 EPUB content entries, hashes and metadata match
- EPUBCheck 5.3.0: 0 fatals, errors, warnings, or infos
- DAISY Ace 1.4.6: no issues in cover, navigation, book XHTML, or OPF
- Ruff, Python compilation, workflow YAML parsing, and `git diff --check` passed
- two independent post-change reviewers returned PASS

External rights, independent review, novice-cohort, and human reader-app gates remain OPEN.

author: kujoumolean
body: Previously the download wrote directly to the target JAR file. If the server restarted or crashed during the download, the plugin would be corrupted (half-written JAR). Now we write to a .tmp file first, and only after a successful download do an atomic move to the target path. On failure the temp file is cleaned up, leaving the original plugin intact.

## DT5 — multi-line canonical pricing (auto BI / GL / EPLI absorbed)

Successor to DT4 (#126). All four contract lines now price from their **own** NCSC CLCM stage-share vectors and median hours — and mapping the lines surfaced and fixed a real contract bug (auto trial double-count).

### Invariant impact statement (required)

**Contract v1.1.0-candidate** (authored in the substrate; re-vendored via the deliberate digest re-pin path, `4fd1f971… → 587e3b92…`, third exercise): `phase_baseline` restructured to per-case-type vectors from CLCM Table 4 (malpractice 14/11/25/43/7 · auto 14/10/21/47/8 · premises 17/14/19/42/8 · employment 18/15/21/39/7; rounding residuals to L400, recorded per vector; every vector sums to 1.00, asserted at authoring). **Bug fix:** the auto line's `trial_likelihood`/`appeal_likelihood` are now `universal_overrides` — universal `trial_posture` can no longer double-count trial for auto matters (tested: neither `trial_posture` nor `appeal` appears in auto's driver ids). **Capped composite exercised for real:** EPLI's correlated group prices L100 at 6.0×√4.5×√2.5×1.65 ≈ 33.2 → **cap 10.0**; a single group member applies largest-in-full (6.0); a partial group is exact and uncapped (1.9×1.5 = 2.85) — all test-pinned. **Med-mal regression pinned unchanged** (2.325 / 3.47375 / base 202.96). The stratified corpus embeds contract digest + plan ids, so it is regenerated and re-frozen against v1.1 (same 174 matters and split; new digests; frozen↔regenerated match tested).

### Trust zone declaration (required)

Candidate-only, synthetic-only, `downstream_control`, `reference_class_only`. Dollars deterministic; no ML; no promotion. CLCM category labels are not line-exact (e.g. "employment" vs EPLI defense) — confidence stays sourced_medium and the labels record it. The pipeline's canonical stage still prices only med-mal (legacy elicitation); other lines price via explicit profiles; line-specific pipeline elicitation is future work. No real data; no cross-repo write.

### Provenance note update (required)

Engine change is a lookup extension only (`LINE_TO_CLCM_CASE_TYPE` + `by_case_type` fractions) — every number remains governed contract data. Mirror updated with the DT5 note + pointers. Decision trace: `docs/ai-handoff/decision-traces/DT5-multi-line-pricing.md`. DAD loop recorded.

## Drift check (required)

### Old rule preserved
Med-mal pricing byte-identical in outcome (regression-pinned); DT1 adapter, conformance gate, DT3 stage, DT4 generator logic unchanged; all five DT suites green together (45).

### Intentional change
Contract v1.1 (vendored) + digest re-pin; engine per-case-type baseline lookup; regenerated frozen stratified corpus; six failing-test-first tests.

### Unchanged surface
Every connector / Lake / SQLite / submission / matter-opening boundary unchanged. No schema shape changes (`export_schemas` idempotent at 530).

## Prohibited actions checked
No canonical taxonomy promotion; no real data or rates; no ML; no invented dollars; no connector, Lake/SQLite, budget approval or submission, matter opening, docketing, external write, conflict conclusion, or silent learning. `main` not pushed directly.

## Validation
`tests/test_multi_line_pricing.py`: 6 passed; DT suites together: 45. Conformance gate green; ruff check + format clean; `export_schemas` idempotent. Full local CI reproduction run bare on the committed tree, marker-verified, before merge.

## Human gate
Owner pre-authorized squash-merge on green local CI for this slice sequence. Substrate contract promotion remains open.

Cross-vendor review: no — single-vendor session; flagged per docs/CROSS_VENDOR_REVIEW_POLICY.md for reviewer discretion.

author: chisanan232
body:
## Description

Two Costs-surface defects from the 2026-07-26 dashboard design-QA re-audit.

**AAASM-5185 — the KPI strip reported `0` for what it never measured.**
`deriveCostKpis` skipped every team row with a null spend or ceiling, so a
Blocked-by-budget count of `0` conflated *"measured every team, none is over"*
with *"could not measure a single team"*, and `CostsPage` captioned it with the
unconditional `no teams over the daily limit`.

This was never outage-specific. On a **successful** `/costs` carrying spend but
no `daily_limit_usd`, the strip read `BUDGET UTILISATION N/A · no daily budget
limit set` immediately beside `BLOCKED BY BUDGET 0 · no teams over the daily
limit` — two KPIs on one strip disagreeing about whether a daily limit exists.
`certainFromQuery` alone cannot fix that, because the query succeeded; only the
derivation knows its own coverage. So the fix is two steps:

1. `KpiCardProps.value` / `sub` become `Certain<ReactNode>` rather than `string`,
   so an absence has somewhere to live and renders as `NO_DATA` with its
   `TRUTH_STATE_META` tone. The severity colour is applied only to a *known*
   figure.
2. `blockedByBudget` becomes a `MeasuredCount` — a `Certain<number>` plus the
   measured/total split — absent when no row was measurable, and stating its
   coverage (`1 of 2 teams measured · 1 unmeasured`) when only some were.
   `agentsTracked` / `teamsTracked` get the same treatment, their
   `0 across 0 teams` being the identical false negative. A genuinely empty
   `[]` breakdown still reads `0`: a measured zero is a fact, only an
   *unmeasured* one was the bug.

The Utilisation card's locally-invented `N/A` goes with it — `lib/truthfulness`
names `—` as the single affordance for "no production value" and explicitly
forbids the ad-hoc variants. The two `N/A` assertions in the AAASM-5126 review
spec are retargeted at the shared marker; the guarantee they carry is
strengthened, not relaxed.

`costKpis.test.ts:88` was titled *"never counts a team whose ceiling is unknown
as either blocked or safe"* while the rendering layer did exactly that, so the
suite certified a guarantee the UI broke. It is now an explicit coverage
assertion rather than a title.

**AAASM-5160 — the per-team Agents and Monthly-spend columns.**
The Per-team tab was a flat list of `TeamBudgetBar` showing team plus burn only,
so team size was invisible on the only per-team cost surface and no per-team
monthly figure existed anywhere in the product — despite
`TeamCostEntry.monthly_spend_usd` and `TeamSummary.agent_count` both already
being on the wire. Restored as the mock's table
(`design/v1/hi-fi/costs.jsx:428-478`, `design/v2/hi-fi/costs.jsx:410-460`, v2
authoritative per ADR-0025): **Team | Agents | Daily spend | vs daily limit |
Monthly spend**, with `TeamBudgetBar` kept verbatim as the "vs daily limit" cell
so its AAASM-5135 absence handling holds unchanged.

**Both data sources confirmed on the wire** — `TeamSummary.agent_count`
(non-nullable, `GET /api/v1/topology/overview`) and

author: zqchris
body:
## 意图契约

- 目标：加固现有域名分流 DNS proxy 的配置、响应和路由信任边界。
- 非目标：本 PR 不加入“全局模式排除域名”UI、物理 DNS 直连或 TTL 路由租约。
- 行为契约：合法的现有分流规则保持原行为；非法配置整体拒绝；只接受匹配当前查询的上游回复；只有成功安装的路由才进入本次进程所有权。
- 验收：新增正常与主要错误路径测试，Debug/Release 均可构建；真实 root 路由与 resolver 联调明确留作有授权的中断性测试。

## 根因

`xdvpn-dns-proxy` 以 root 运行，但此前直接信任用户可写的 `/tmp/xdvpn-split-domains.conf`，并把配置行拼入 `/etc/resolver/<suffix>`。同时，上游 UDP socket 未连接到指定 DNS，也没有核对 transaction ID 和 question；收到的任意 A 记录都会触发 host route。路由命令的退出状态也被忽略，失败的安装仍会进入缓存且不再重试。

## 改动

- 把域名后缀规范化提取到 `XDVPNCore.DomainRules`，App 与 root proxy 共用同一套规则；特权边界遇到任意非法活动行时 fail closed。
- 将上游 UDP socket 连接到配置的 DNS peer，并校验 response 方向、opcode、transaction ID 以及规范化后的 question。
- 让 route 安装返回真实结果，通过 `RouteOwnershipTracker` 仅记录确认成功的路由；失败项可在后续 DNS 回复中重试。
- 为路径穿越输入、DNS 错配/畸形响应、路由失败与重复安装补回归测试。

## 自测

- ✅ `swift build -c debug`
- ✅ `swift build -c release`
- ✅ 独立纯 Swift harness 覆盖域名拒绝、DNS ID/question 匹配、路由失败重试与去重
- ✅ `git diff --check`
- ⚠️ `swift test` 在当前机器被 Command Line Tools 缺少 `XCTest` 阻断：`no such module 'XCTest'`；测试源码已加入，需在完整 Xcode 环境执行
- ⏭️ 未启动 XDVPN、未中断当前 VPN，也未执行真实 root route／`/etc/resolver` 联调

author: d3vi1
body:
## What

Adds the `features/executor` boundary for one exact-address, exact-function, typed full SPINE READ or WRITE. Dispatch is performed only through a runtime-owned atomic `RoundTripIfCurrent` operation.

Closes #19.

## Contract

- Resolves exactly one local source feature and one remote device/entity/feature by complete SPINE address, feature type, role, and function.
- Requires the remote declared full READ or full WRITE operation before contact.
- READ uses the typed SPINE function factory and full `ReadCmdType(nil, nil)` only.
- WRITE accepts exactly one complete matching typed command.
- Rejects filters, selectors, partial/delete operations, invoke/call, wrong function, cross-family function, multi-command input, missing target, missing runtime, stale identity, stale generation, and dispatch substitution before an underlying send.
- Final dispatch binds exact device address, opaque remote identity, and positive connection generation inside `ExactRemoteRuntime.RoundTripIfCurrent`.
- The executor never calls `Device.Sender` and exposes no independently substitutable `RoundTripper` capability.
- Returns typed request/response commands, correlation key, remote/protocol errors, and request/response timestamps while preserving legal opaque command extensions.

## Strict TDD evidence

It does not touch transport, wire, protocol, opcode, mux, or gateway retry/reconnect paths. The correlated wire primitive was gated separately in spine-go #9.

author: joshbotts
body:
**Stacked on #526** (which records the trace that prompted this) — review that first, or read this against it. Base will retarget to `v2` once #526 lands.

## Why

`UILaunchScreen: {}` drew a **blank white screen** for the entire pre-render window. #526 measured that window: 158 ms in `FRUSExplorerApp.init()` alone, 137 ms of it `makeFRUSContainer()` — a synchronous SwiftData store open with nothing in it to delete. It is real, it is not shrinking, and **no SwiftUI overlay can reach it**, because it is before the first frame. A launch screen is the only thing that can draw there.

That is what overturned the plan's original "we'll address it by removing work instead" — removing work addresses 5% of it.

## What it looks like

The 1a identity block: gradient app tile, wordmark, caption, on an asset-catalog ground with light **and** dark variants.

Verified in the simulator on a **clean install** — launch screens are cached aggressively, so an in-place reinstall proves nothing — in both appearances, and through the hand-off to the onboarding Welcome step. It does not stick.

## Constraints, all inherent

A launch screen runs **no code**. So:

- The gradient can't be drawn → the tile is a pre-rendered **vector PDF** (`LaunchAppTile.pdf`, 88pt, r20, the hand-off's 160° `#2B8CFF → #0055D4`).
- The SF Symbol can't be tinted at runtime → the white glyph is baked into that PDF. Generated by filling white and compositing `.destinationIn` against the template image; drawing the symbol and compositing `.sourceAtop` over it instead fills the entire bounding box, which it did twice before I stopped trusting `sips` to rasterise my preview.
- No Dynamic Type, no localization.

**Identity only.** The animated cloud belongs to `LaunchSplashView` in O-3, which takes over once SwiftUI is up. The two compositions are meant to read as one moment — that is the entire argument for option (a) having two halves — so **keep them in step** when O-3 builds the splash.

## Two traps, recorded at the sites that would repeat them

1. **`UILaunchScreen` and `UILaunchStoryboardName` are mutually exclusive.** iOS 14+ prefers the dictionary when both are present, which would silently ignore the storyboard and leave the screen blank with no error anywhere. The empty dictionary is **removed**, not left alongside.
2. **The macOS target globs the same `FRUSExplorer/` directory**, and `ibtool --target-device mac` **hard-errors** on an iOS storyboard rather than skipping it — `"iOS storyboards do not support target device type 'mac'"`. Without the exclusion in the macOS target's `sources`, the macOS build breaks outright. It did.

## Verification

- iOS and macOS both **BUILD SUCCEEDED**. `xcodegen generate` run; schemes restored per CLAUDE.md.
- Simulator, clean install, light **and** dark: launch screen renders, then hands off to onboarding.
- No Swift code changed — no tests are implicated, and none were added; a launch screen has no testable surface short of a screenshot test, which the repo does not do.

**Visual review, iPhone (the thing to actually check):** delete the app first — a reinstall over the top will show you the cached blank screen and you will think this doesn't work. Then launch in both appearances. On your device the launch screen should be up appreciably longer than in the simulator, since your store is large; that is the 137 ms (plus dyld and runtime init) becoming visible, and it is exactly the window this fills.

author: ahngbeom
body:
## Summary

Each chapter ends with a `## 체크리스트` of competency statements, but readers had no active way to check whether they actually learned the material. This adds `./exam`, a terminal quiz that asks concepts as multiple choice, commands as short answer, and judgement calls as essay.

Standard-library-only Python3, matching the existing `scripts/` convention — no pip, no build step, no CI.

## What's included

**Runner** (`exam`, `scripts/exam.py`)
- `./exam` with no arguments picks DBMS → tier → chapter interactively; a bank path, `--dbms`, and `--shuffle` still work and skip the matching screen.
- Shuffles multiple-choice options, offers a per-question hint (`h`), and locks each question on first submission so revealing the answer can't be used to inflate the score.
- Free navigation with `←`/`→`, live score and A–F grade in the header, feedback events with a streak counter, and a post-exam menu to continue into another chapter without restarting.
- Falls back to a line-mode runner when stdout is not a tty.
- `--keydebug` prints what the terminal actually sends, for diagnosing Option/Alt key differences across terminals.

**Authoring** (`scripts/seed_exam.py`)
- Drafts a question bank from a chapter, reusing `filter_dbms.py`'s marker/code-fence parsing so each question inherits the right `dbms` tag.

**Question banks** (`exams/`) — 216 questions across all 23 chapters:

| Tier | Chapters | Questions | mcq / short / essay |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01-beginner | 6 | 50 | 23 / 16 / 11 |
| 02-intermediate | 8 | 76 | 34 / 26 / 16 |
| 03-advanced | 9 | 90 | 28 / 26 / 36 |

Higher tiers weight judgement over recall — the advanced tier asks what design to choose and why (partitioning trade-offs, sync vs async RPO, shard key evaluation, managed-vs-Operator).

Vendor coverage follows each chapter rather than being forced: chapters with little vendor-specific content stay neutral, and every chapter keeps enough neutral questions that picking any DBMS leaves a viable exam.

**Results** are appended to `.exam-results/results.jsonl` (gitignored — personal study records) and the chapter picker shows each chapter's previous best.

## Notes

- `exams/**/*.json` is not vendor-filtered when generating single-vendor branches; the JSON stays a neutral superset and `--dbms` filters at runtime. Documented in `docs/dbms-branch-strategy.md`.
- `docs/exam-authoring.md` covers the schema, question types, grading, key bindings, and the seed → refine workflow.

## Test plan

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` — 71 tests covering grading, choice shuffling, streak idempotency, terminal key-sequence decoding, cursor motion, and lints that hold every bank to the same bar (schema, no answer leaked into the question text, hint on every question).
- Round-trip check: all 68 short answers grade themselves correct, and all 85 multiple-choice answers survive 20 shuffle seeds.
- `scripts/seed_exam.py` runs without crashing on all 23 chapters, including the two with embedded Runbooks/templates.
- Manual: ran the TUI end to end in a real terminal — tier/chapter selection, answering each question type, navigation, hints, results, and continuing into another chapter.

author: sgentzen
body:
## What

Adds `.app > * { min-width: 0 }` to `src/App.css`, plus a deterministic e2e regression test.

This fixes the consistently failing e2e test `Board view > drags a task card to the In Progress column`, which timed out waiting for a PATCH to `/api/tasks/` after `dragTo`.

## Why

The drag handlers were never broken. The drop target was off-screen.

`.app` is a grid with `grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto` and a single implicit `auto` column. Its children are the header, `.main-content` and `AlertBanner`. `.main-content` and its own children already carried `min-width: 0`, but `.app`'s children did not, so a grid child with `min-width: auto` set the floor for that column.

`AlertBanner`'s message span is `white-space: nowrap`, so its min-content width is the full untruncated message. Its own `overflow: hidden` zeroes its automatic minimum size but does not reduce its min-content *contribution* to the parent's intrinsic sizing, so the banner div's `min-width: auto` still resolved to the full message width.

Measured on a real page load with a long blocker in the database:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `.app` column track | 3521px | 1280px |
| `.main-content` `1fr` track | 3081px | 840px |
| PLANNED / IN PROGRESS / DONE column x | 200 / 1227 / 2254 | 200 / 480 / 760 |

With `.app { overflow: hidden }`, everything past 1280px was silently clipped. **Any unresolved blocker with a long reason made the In Progress and Done columns invisible and unreachable for real users**, not just for the test.

The test failure follows from that: Playwright still treats a clipped column as visible (non-empty bounding box, not `visibility: hidden`), so `dragTo` aimed at coordinates outside the viewport, no `drop` event fired, and no PATCH was issued. It only reproduces against a database that happens to hold such a blocker, which is why CI stayed green and it failed locally.

## How

One rule, mirroring the existing `.main-content > *` rule directly below it:

```css
.app > * {
  min-width: 0;
}
```

Scoped to the horizontal axis only, since the defect is purely horizontal. `min-height: 0` was deliberately left out to avoid making the `auto` header row squashable, which is unrelated to this bug.

The new regression test stubs `/api/blockers` with `page.route` rather than creating a real blocker. The banner is global state in a shared SQLite database, so a real blocker would leak into every spec running in a parallel worker, and would survive a timeout or a cancelled run in the developer's own working database, leaving behind the exact state that causes this bug.

## Testing

- [x] Tests pass (`npm test`) — 418 passed across 45 files
- [x] New tests added for new functionality
- [x] Manually verified in the dashboard

Details:

- `npx playwright test`: **15 passed**, up from 13 passed / 1 failed. Both the previously failing drag test and the new regression test are green.
- The regression test was confirmed red without the fix (`Expected: <= 1280, Received: 4792.03`) by stashing `src/App.css`, and green with it.
- `npm run lint`: clean.
- `semgrep --config=auto --error` on the changed files: 0 findings. `jscpd`: the 5 clones reported are all pre-existing (`board.spec.ts:18-71`, `App.css:18-24`); none in the new code.
- Live dev server against a real database containing a long blocker: `.app` track is 1280px and the three columns measure x=200/480/760 at 280px each, all inside the viewport. The banner truncates with an ellipsis as it was always meant to. No console errors.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows existing patterns
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) — not applicable
- [x] No hardcoded paths or credentials

## Notes for the reviewer

- The fix is at the layout level rather than in `AlertBanner` on purpose: it protects every `.app` child, including future ones, and matches the convention already established by `.main-content > *`. A reviewer suggested also adding `minWidth: 0` to the `AlertBanner` root for component self-containment; I left it out to keep the regression test tied to the single rule under test. Happy to add it if preferred.
- Found while reviewing, pre-existing and **not** addressed here: `src/App.tsx:341` guards the banner with `blockers.length > 0 || fileConflicts.length > 0`, but `AlertBanner` only reads `blockers`, so a file-conflict-only state renders nothing. Tracked separately.

author: probepark
body:
## Summary

- **Session hosts leaked forever.** A broker-spawned session host is detached and outlives the client that created it, which is what lets a client reconnect with `session/load`. Nothing ever reclaimed one: clients do not send `session/close` on exit, so hosts accumulated across restarts — over a hundred on a development machine, some days old. A host now reclaims itself after a grace period during which its launching client's pid is dead, no client connection is negotiated, and no turn is in flight. Connection-close callbacks do not arrive when a client is killed rather than closed, so pid liveness is the authoritative signal for the launcher, while any live connection keeps a reattached session alive. Expiry routes through the lifecycle owner's shutdown path so the session is disposed and persisted; exiting from inside the extension would skip job drain and MCP/LSP teardown. `GJC_SDK_HOST_IDLE_REAP_MS` overrides the 30-minute default.
- **A prompt aborted before `agent_start` pinned the session busy forever.** `turn.abort` left its correlation in `pendingPromptCorrelations`. Since `isBusy()` reads that array, the session reported busy permanently and every later prompt was refused. Those correlations are now terminalized through the failure path so reconciliation does not keep them `accepted`.

## Verification

- `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/sdk-host-wiring.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/notifications-session-switch.test.ts` (91 pass), plus `sdk-host-reaper.test.ts` (26 pass) and `sdk-broker.test.ts` (53 pass) — 170 across the four files
- `bun x tsc --noEmit -p packages/coding-agent/tsconfig.json` (0 errors)
- `bun x biome check` on the five changed TypeScript files
- `git diff --check origin/dev..HEAD`

Following review, `awaitAbortReady` now also drains unstarted correlations. It previously looped on `isSessionBusy()` — which counts `pendingPromptCorrelations` — without discarding them, so `turn.abort_and_prompt` could wait forever on a prompt that was accepted but never started: the same busy-pin this change set fixes for `turn.abort`. Two regressions drive the real WebSocket SDK host and deliberately never emit `agent_start`, covering both abort paths; the `abort_and_prompt` case races its replacement response against a bounded timeout so a regression surfaces as a failure rather than a hang.

Reclamation was also exercised manually end to end: with an 8s window the host was reclaimed after its client was killed, and with the default window the host survived and a subsequent `session/load` reconnect succeeded.

## Relation to #3240

Supersedes #3240, which was closed at `f846bae6` under the coherent-feature bar. That review's five open findings are addressed here rather than deferred.

**P2 — pid-only identity.** A pid is not an identity: once the client exits the OS can reuse that number, and the host would read the stranger as a live launcher and never reclaim itself. The initiator now records the process incarnation alongside the pid and carries both through the lifecycle request; the host compares observed against expected. Built on the existing `processIncarnation`/`isProcessIncarnation` house pattern rather than a new reader.

**P3 — propagation and stale ambient env.** Only the per-request identity is trusted now; the ambient `GJC_SDK_CLIENT_PID` is no longer forwarded, so a pre-existing detached broker cannot aim a new host at an unrelated client. ACP publishes identity at the initiator.

**P4 — zero reaper tests.** The ownership rules lived inside a closure, which is exactly why nothing could test them. `parseLauncherIdentity`, `isLauncherAlive`, and `shouldReclaimHost` are now small exported functions that the running host calls, with the liveness probe injected. 26 tests cover identity parsing (10 malformed shapes), liveness including EPERM, and the reclaim matrix.

**P5 — grace-boundary race.** Connections count from their first frame until they negotiate or close, so a client reconnecting at the boundary is no longer reaped mid-handshake.

**P6 — swallowed dispose errors.** A `session.dispose()` rejection no longer exits 0 as clean success; it is logged durably and exits non-zero on both the idle-reap and signal stop paths.

Sensitivity checked by reverting each guard: removing the incarnation comparison fails `treats a reused pid as dead even though signalling it succeeds`, and removing the handshake guard fails `never reclaims while a client is still handshaking`. Both pass again with the source restored.

**Still fail-open, deliberately.** Non-ACP session-launch paths do not yet publish initiator identity, so hosts they spawn report their launcher alive and are never reclaimed. That is the safe direction — leaking a host is recoverable, reclaiming a live session is not — but it does mean the reaper is still ACP-scoped in practice. Handshake tracking also starts at the first SDK frame rather than TCP accept, because `NotificationServer` exposes no connection-open hook today. Say the word if you want either closed here rather than as follow-ups.

author: jbreezyasf
body:
Issue #016 is done and its links are live. This makes the remaining fifteen possible — starting with a check that costs nothing.

## Why a survey comes first

Backfilling the earlier issues depends on something the repo cannot tell us: **whether those weeks have message ids at all.**

`setup_scraper_schema.sql` adds `message_id` via `ALTER TABLE`, which means `telegram_messages` predates the Telethon scraper. Rows written before that column existed have `message_id = NULL` and nothing to link to. Issue #016's week was 204/204, but that is the most recent week and says nothing about issue 003.

`--survey` answers it for free: every issue with its week, message count, how many carry ids, whether it is already linked, and a verdict. **No model calls, no writes.** Running it first avoids spending fifteen model calls to discover half the weeks are unlinkable.

## Batch mode

`--issue` now accepts `16`, `1-15`, `3,7,9`, or `all`.

Behaviour chosen for a batch that touches published content:

- **Independent issues.** A failure is recorded and the run continues — nothing was written for the failed issue, and the others are unaffected.
- **The content guard raises instead of exiting**, so one odd issue cannot abort fourteen good ones.
- **One deploy at the end**, not one per commit.
- **Summary lists every outcome** and prints the exact command to retry only the failures.
- **Idempotent**, so partial progress is safe to keep.

## Known risk, not mitigated in code

Older issues were rendered from **older versions of the template**, and re-rendering pulls today's. For #016 that was harmless — the diff was purely links plus CSS. If the design changed between issue 001 and now, re-rendering those pages could restyle them beyond adding links.

The dry run is the protection: it prints `+N / -M` per issue. `+29/-3` is links; `+400/-380` is a redesign and should be skipped. I have deliberately not added an automatic threshold — the right cutoff depends on how the template actually drifted, which the dry run will reveal.

## Verification

- Range parsing: single, range, single-element range, comma list, comma dedupe, whitespace.
- The content guard now raises `ValueError` rather than calling `sys.exit`, confirmed by test, so a batch survives it; additive merges still pass.
- All four workflows parse; every shell block passes `bash -n`.

**Not verified:** the survey and batch paths have never run against the live database. The survey makes no writes and no model calls, so it is the safe thing to run first.

## Suggested order

1. **Survey** — tick `survey`, leave `issue_number` empty. ~30 seconds, free.
2. **Dry run the ready ones** — e.g. `1-15` with `dry_run` checked. Check the diff sizes.
3. **Apply.**

## Resumen
Este Pull Request consolida la integración definitiva del motor de recomendaciones basado en el **Patrón Strategy** con el servicio de orquestación (`PredictionServiceImpl`), desacoplando la lógica del backend y delegando la internacionalización al frontend.

---

### 📋 Principales Cambios e Hitos del Desarrollo:

1. **Integración en Orquestación (`PredictionServiceImpl`):**
   - Se inyectó `RecommendationService` para procesar automáticamente las reglas tras recibir la inferencia del modelo de Machine Learning.
   - Recopilación de variables del request (tipo de inmueble, horas de climatización, hábitos en horario pico) para construir un contrato de recomendación enriquecido.

2. **Refactorización a Enum Enriquecido (`ConsumptionCategory`):**
   - Se eliminaron las constantes planas y las sentencias `switch` imperativas.
   - Se introdujo un Enum con la clase anidada `ModelValues` que centraliza los valores esperados de la IA (`ALTO`, `MODERADO`, `BAJO`) y los mapea con las claves visuales del frontend (`efficient`, `moderate`, `inefficient`).

3. **Evolución del Patrón Strategy (`RecommendationRule`):**
   - Implementación de reglas base por categoría y reglas granulares/estructurales (`CommercialOptimizationRule`, `PeakHourUsageRule`, etc.).
   - Migración de `MessageSource` a claves cortas (`TipKey`), liberando al backend de la responsabilidad de traducir oraciones.

4. **Documentación Técnica:**

body:
## Exact stack

- Base branch: `main`
- Exact base commit: `ccaebcbee74cf0fa01af59d11b16b736ddb19791`
- Exact head commit: `749bbbd6953982bd641fab2b38dcd498acc234fa`

## Scope

This bounded package extends generated ordinary Rust adapters with exact closed-schema reconstruction and a root-only schema-bound envelope smart constructor. It also compiles the generated output under `no_std + alloc`, records the boundary in the README and design documents, and adds a permanent read-only workflow.

It does not implement catalog/profile construction, transition execution, shell publication, or adjacent project-specific profiles.

## Public API changes

Every generated Rust root type now exposes:

```rust
Root::zfcis_schema() -> Result<Schema, SchemaError>

root.to_root_envelope::<H>(limits)
    -> Result<SchemaAdmittedEnvelope, AdapterError>
```

Generated `AdapterError` additionally exposes `Schema`, `SchemaEnvelope`, and `SchemaHashMismatch` cases. Generated owned `Box` references are fully qualified through `alloc` so the compiled fixture remains `no_std + alloc` compatible.

## Dependency changes

No new external dependency and no lockfile change. The compiled fixture adds an existing workspace `zeno-fcis-crypto` dev dependency with the already pinned RustCrypto feature so tests can exercise the generation-time provider.

## Authority boundary

Schema authors and reviewers retain authority over the schema, stable identifiers, profile, version, and bounds. The generator only renders the accepted schema. The caller supplies runtime `ValidationLimits` and `CommitmentHasher`. `SchemaAdmittedEnvelope` remains responsible for schema validation, structural admission, canonical envelope admission, and retained metrics. The generated helper fails closed unless the runtime provider produces the exact schema commitment embedded at generation.

No schema, stable identifier, provider, protocol version, generator identity, formatter identity, migration, proof, or promotion status is selected by this package.

## Deterministic resource bounds

- Exact generated `SchemaLimits` bind the schema type count and maximum record-field, enum/sum-variant, and tuple cardinalities.
- Caller-supplied `ValidationLimits` bind recursive root validation.
- Existing default structural value limits and the 64 MiB complete-envelope limit remain in force.
- Each call reconstructs one finite owned schema, value, and envelope without cache, I/O, clocks, randomness, threads, async, or global mutable state.

## Laws and negative tests

- Generated reconstruction equals the exact source `Schema` across the fixture's complete type-kind graph.
- Expected-provider schema commitment equals embedded `SCHEMA_HASH_HEX`.
- Successful root admission binds exact root type, schema hash, value, and validation metrics.
- Caller validation budget is enforced at the generated API boundary.
- A mismatched provider is rejected with `SchemaHashMismatch`.
- Invalid typed data rejects before a later provider mismatch.
- Repeated generation remains byte-identical and generated-file manifests bind the changed output.

## Validation and toolchain

Local exact-head validation used Rust `1.97.1`:

body:
Closes #44

사이트에 처음 들어온 사람이 "무슨 개발자인지"와 "주력 스택이 뭔지"를 알 수 없던 문제. 이력서에는 둘 다 명시돼 있는데 사이트에만 없던 구멍이다.

## 1. Hero — 직군 표기

`GEON` + `Adaptability` 뿐이라 **첫 화면에서 프론트엔드 개발자라는 사실조차 드러나지 않았다.** `Adaptability` 아래에 `Frontend Engineer`를 추가했다.

비디오 블렌드(`mixBlendMode: screen`) 연출은 기존 두 요소에만 두고 직군 표기는 평문으로 뒀다 — 작은 글자에 영상이 비치면 읽기 어렵고, 이 줄은 장식이 아니라 정보이기 때문이다.

## 2. Skills 섹션 신설

주력 스택을 알려면 프로젝트 카드 7개의 배지를 전부 훑어야 했고, 경력 카드의 `techStack`도 회사별로 흩어져 있었다.

- `src/data/skills.ts` + `src/components/sections/Skills.tsx` 신설
- 섹션 순서: **Hero → About → Skills → Career → Projects → Contact**
- `Header` `navItems`에 `SKILLS` 추가 (4개 → 5개)
- 기존 `SectionTitle` · `TechBadge` 재사용, 카드 스타일은 Career 섹션과 맞춤

### 이력서와의 정합성

사이트 Skills가 이력서보다 넓으면 그 자체로 새 불일치가 된다. 두 장치로 막았다.

| 그룹 | 처리 |
| --- | --- |
| Front-End · State & Data | 이력서 Skills에 있는 그룹 → `core: true`, `CORE` 배지 + 전체 폭으로 시각 구분 |
| Design System · Backend & Infra · AI & DX | 사이트에만 노출 → `context`에 근거 프로젝트 명시 |

`context` 덕분에 "Supabase는 왜 이력서에 없냐"가 아니라 "JobLog에서 쓴 거구나"로 읽힌다.

﻿## Summary
Redesigns the skeleton drawn in the Body Cultivation Chamber's Bones tab so it is anatomically true to life and actually fits the silhouette. The old layout had 27 paths whose ribs and arm bones sat outside the body outline (they were being clipped by the silhouette mask).

The new layout is 111 paths measured against the silhouette's real proportions (shoulders at y=40, costal margin 76, iliac crest 90, hip joint 106, knee 151, ankle 190):

- **Skull** — cranial vault, orbits, nasal aperture, zygomatic arches, mandible with jaw rami
- **Spine** — 5 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar vertebral bodies that widen downward, plus sacrum and coccyx
- **Ribs** — 12 pairs sloping inferiorly as they run forward, sternum (manubrium/body/xiphoid), costal margin, floating ribs 11-12
- **Arms** — clavicle, scapula, humerus with head, elbow, paired radius and ulna
- **Hands / feet** — carpals, 5 metacarpals, phalanges; tarsals, metatarsals, toes
- **Legs** — pelvis (iliac blade, acetabulum, obturator foramen), femur with head and neck, condyles, patella, tibia and fibula
- **Marrow** — now glows at the real red-marrow sites (vertebral column, ilia, femoral and humeral heads) instead of one chest blob

Implementation notes:
- Viewer-left bones are authored once and mirrored about the centre line by `mirrorBoneD`, so the two halves cannot drift apart.
- `BODY_BONE_ACTION_PARTS` is derived from the defs instead of hand-maintained, and lookups in the render loop use a Map.
- New `--bone-weight` per bone kind so ribs and fingers render finer than femurs.
- Fixed a pre-existing CSS bug: the generic `.body-sil-overlay path` rule was overriding `fill: none` on bones, so open curves like ribs and the mandible were being filled and the marrow rendered bone-coloured instead of red. Bones are now excluded from that rule.

## Test plan
- Verified all 111 path strings parse in a real browser (`getTotalLength` finite and > 0 for every bone).
- Rendered the bones overlay in-page with the real CSS at full refinement and confirmed every bone sits inside the silhouette (no mask clipping) and the marrow reads red.
- Confirmed the eight bone actions (skull, spine, ribs, arms, hands, legs, feet, marrow) each map to parts for pulse feedback.

author: orangepeachpink
body:
Closes #1668.

**Stacked on #1685 (CP3)** — it imports `verify`/`contract` for `--verify`, exactly as the issue predicted ("genuinely easier to write once those exist, because it can call them in `--check` mode"). Merge CP3 first; this diff is then just `state.py` + its tests + one recipe.

## The rule did the work

> *Never infer phase from anything but observed state. `unknown` is acceptable where `probably §5` is not.*

That caught **two falsehoods in my own first draft**, which is the strongest argument for the rule I can offer.

### The frozen candidate

#1657 has no store yet. The obvious move is to show the draft's target instead — and it's wrong. *"What was agreed"* and *"what the draft points at"* are **different claims**, and #1657 exists precisely because they can differ. Substituting one would invent the agreement. It reports absent, and says why.

### The signer run — this one shipped in my first version

A signer run records **no tag**. `displayTitle` is just the workflow name and the dispatch input isn't exposed by `gh run list`:

```
30182168038 title=sign release firmware (#302) sha=c959ba7f66be
```

So my first draft printed the repo-wide latest run under whatever tag you asked about — `release-state v0.8.2` confidently displayed **v0.8.1's** run. The only observable link is whether the run built the draft's target commit, so now:

```
v0.8.1  → built c959ba7f66be — THIS draft's target
v0.8.2  → built c959ba7f66be — cannot be attributed to v0.8.2: a signer run
          records no tag and there is no draft target to match it against
```

Found by running it against a tag with no draft. A fixture would not have shown it.

## Verified live, three genuinely different states

| tag | phase | next |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.8.1` | §6 done | published, assets sealed — a correction needs a new tag (#1438) |
| `v0.8.2` | §1 / §1.1 | milestone open, 54 issues → `just release-preflight v0.8.2` |
| `v9.9.9` | before §2 | no milestone, no draft → create it, then preflight |

`unknown` appears honestly in each — that's the feature.

## Tests

9, driven from fact dicts rather than the network. Two of them read the source, because **a behavioural test cannot distinguish a field that was queried from one that was assumed** — and that distinction is the entire specification here.

The signed-draft branch asserts the next action says `release-verify` and **"publish only if it exits 0"**, never "publish": `assets > 0` is not evidence a release is correct, and this tool must not shortcut #1662.

`just check` green.

— DX

author: guangyuxu
body:
Both CI jobs fail at `npm ci` on Linux, while the same command succeeds on macOS:

    npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json
    and package-lock.json ... are in sync.
    npm error Missing: @emnapi/core@1.11.3 from lock file
    npm error Missing: @emnapi/runtime@1.11.3 from lock file

Cause: `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` (new in the Tailwind 4 bump) pulls `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime@1.1.6`, which npm hoisted to the top level. Its own deps -- @emnapi/core and @emnapi/runtime at 1.11.3 -- were never recorded there. The only @emnapi/core and @emnapi/runtime entries in the tree were nested under @rolldown/binding-wasm32-wasi at 1.11.1, so the top-level requirement was unsatisfiable.

It passes on macOS because that whole subtree is an OPTIONAL dependency that darwin-arm64 never needs, so npm's `ci` consistency check skips it. That is also why regenerating the lockfile on macOS does not fix it: `npm install --package-lock-only` there leaves both entries absent. The lockfile had to be regenerated on Linux, where npm actually resolves that subtree.

The change is purely additive -- 8 entries added, 0 removed, and every darwin/win32 binary variant is still present, so the lockfile remains cross-platform.

Verified: `npm ci` now succeeds on node:26-alpine (the Dockerfile build stage) and node:22 glibc (the runner via .nvmrc), and still on macOS. `docker build --platform=linux/amd64` completes, and `npm ci && make ci` is green inside linux/amd64 node:22 -- the checks job end to end.

author: zesanrahim
body:
Removes both front-ends and leaves one: a CLI over the existing trigram engine.

## Why

The Bubbletea TUI had accumulated layering problems that were invisible while it
was the only consumer of the engine, but would have torn as soon as a second one
existed. Rather than refactor a UI that was going to be replaced, this removes it
and keeps the fixes it needed — in places a web surface can also use them.

## What changed

**`internal/paths`** — clones, corpus files, and index caches now resolve under
`os.UserCacheDir()` rather than seven hardcoded `/tmp/codesearch` literals spread
across the TUI and the indexing pipeline. `/tmp` is tmpfs on many systems, so
nothing survived a reboot. `CODESEARCH_CACHE_DIR` relocates it, which is also what
makes the new tests hermetic.

**Repository identity** — `Repo` carries `Org`, and `NewRepo` derives identity from
a clone URL. Index cache paths are keyed on organization as well as name, so
`facebook/react` and `myfork/react` no longer overwrite each other. That was real
content mixing, and would be a cross-repo leak in any hosted version.

**`ParseRepoURL`** replaces two inconsistent URL parsers that disagreed on edge
cases. **`ListCachedRepos`** reads identity from the cache layout instead of
stripping `.gob` off a filename and splitting a remote URL to recover the org.

**Error handling** — search collected per-repository errors and dropped every one
of them, while `SearchResultMsg.Err` and `SearchMultiLineResultMsg.Err` were
declared and never assigned. An unreadable repository was indistinguishable from
one with no matches. The CLI reports failures on stderr and still prints the
matches it did find.

**Progress reporting** — the TUI shared one package-level channel buffered at 100
across all indexing operations. Nothing drained it once the TUI moved on, so a
large enough run filled the buffer and blocked the indexer permanently. Gone with
the TUI; the CLI writes progress to stderr on one rewritten line so stdout stays
pipeable.

**`desktop/`** — an Electron + React Hello World with no IPC bridge and no Go
integration, plus a committed `package-lock.json` for dependencies nothing used.

**`web/theme.css`** — the project colour scheme, five hues forming a severity ramp
with semantic aliases. Nothing consumes it yet.

`go mod tidy` drops bubbletea, bubbles, and lipgloss.

## Verification

`make check` (gofmt, `go vet`, `go test -race`) passes. New tests cover
`ParseRepoURL` (HTTPS/SSH, `.git` suffixes, trailing slashes, rejection of
unparseable input) and `ListCachedRepos` (identity from layout, forks staying
distinct, corrupt caches skipped rather than fatal). `help` and `list`
smoke-tested.

## Found but deliberately not fixed here

Recorded so they aren't lost:

- **The index cache has never worked.** `service.go` deletes the corpus via
  `defer os.Remove(tempFile)`, but `LoadIndex` re-mmaps the stored `CorpusPath` —
  that same deleted path. Every run fails the cache check and re-indexes from
  scratch. In-session search survives only because Unix keeps an unlinked file
  alive while mapped. Fixing it needs a disk cap in the same change, since
  persisting corpora removes the accidental bound `os.Remove` currently provides.
- **`shouldIgnore` matches ignore patterns by substring against the whole path**,
  so `internal/builder/`, `internal/distributor/` and everything under `.github/`
  are silently dropped from the corpus. Wants segment comparison.
- **`loadGitignore` reads a single shared file above all clones**, not the
  `.gitignore` of the repository being indexed. The path moved; the behaviour did
  not.
- **`GetRepo` is dead and broken** — nothing calls it, and its `repoPath` and
  `cloneURL` are declared and never assigned, so it returns a `Repo` with empty
  paths. It is also the only caller of `database.GetClient`, so removing it drops
  the last use of the stubbed Supabase client.
- **`filepath.Walk` runs twice** per index, once to count for progress and once
  for real.
- **`module codesearch`** is a bare module name, which blocks `go install`.
- `GetFileFromOffset` linear-scans every file boundary per result, and line
  resolution re-reads whole files from disk to count newlines from byte zero.

author: btontoh1
body:
Terminating an employee only ever flipped employmentStatus - the linked User account (their login) stayed fully active, so a terminated employee could still use every self-service page (attendance, leave, payslips, payment details). Nothing in the codebase checked employmentStatus outside the Employee module itself.

EmployeeService.updateStatus now deactivates the linked User (isActive = false) when the transition is to TERMINATED, via a new UserAccessRepository in employee-data-access - reaches into the shared "users" table directly since scope:employee can't depend on scope:iam, same pattern as PayrollEmployeeRepository/AttendanceEmployeeRepository etc. TERMINATED has no outgoing transitions in the status state machine, so this only ever needs to deactivate, never reactivate.

Note: this blocks future logins immediately but doesn't revoke an already-issued access token, which remains valid until it naturally expires (~15 min) - there's no token blacklist in this codebase.

author: huangmj0
body:
# Entry

Framework — not a log-driven entry. Nothing under `src/` is touched, so no rebuild and no byte-budget movement.

## What changed

**`/drain` — one loop tick that reads almost nothing.**

`/loop` fires into the *same* session, so everything an iteration reads stays in context for every iteration after it. Worked inline, one entry costs tens of thousands of tokens — `src/app.js` alone is 78 KB — and a handful exhaust the window. That is the same rot the split test suites and split archive addressed, arriving by a different route.

`/drain` runs `npm run queue`, branches on the exit code, and hands the entry to a subagent that starts cold and dies when it finishes, reporting six fixed lines (entry, PR, CI, bytes, deviations, status). Those six lines are all the orchestrator keeps. It is told explicitly not to read `src/`, run the build, or write a PR body.

On exit 3 it runs `/refill` the same way — but only after checking no queue proposal is already open, since a refill PR needs a human merge and two open proposals cannot both land. It notifies once, then idles on a long interval and resumes on its own once you merge. It never proposes a second queue.

It delegates by **naming** the `entry` and `refill` skills rather than restating them, so the loop body still lives in exactly one place.

**A hazard fix this loop would otherwise have hit.**

The exit-4 guard read the log in the working tree, so it only saw an in-flight entry while the tree was still on that entry's branch — an assumption a long-running loop breaks on any container restart, resumed session, or subagent worktree.

Reproduced before fixing: from a checkout of `origin/main` with entry 43 `Done` on an unmerged branch, `npm run queue` returned **exit 0 and named 43 as next** — the loop would have redone it and opened a duplicate PR.

`queue-status.mjs` now also asks the remote: any branch not merged into `origin/main` whose log marks an entry `Done` that main still shows as `Todo` is work someone already holds. Content-based like the existing check, so it depends on no branch-naming convention — the same reasoning that made the current guard better than the branch-prefix check it replaced. Reuses `parseEntries()` from `scripts/log-model.mjs` rather than adding a second parser.

## Tests

`npm test` — 5/5 suites pass.

New assertions in `tests/docs-check.mjs`, none weakened: `drain.md` exists, branches on `npm run queue`, and names **both** the `entry` and `refill` skills — so it cannot quietly start carrying its own copy of the loop body.

Verified by hand:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Hazard: tree on `main`, entry 43 `Done` on unmerged branch | **exit 4**, naming entry and branch (was exit 0) |
| Clean: nothing in flight, main's log | exit 0, `next: 43` — unchanged |
| That branch merged/removed | back to exit 0 — no sticky false positive |
| Fixtures `clear` / `unmerged` / `stale` | 0 / 4 / 5 — unchanged |
| Delegation assertion, with `` `entry` skill `` removed | fails as intended |

## Byte budget

Unchanged — `index.html` stays at 144,032 bytes, 89.5% of the 161,000-byte budget.

## Deviations

- **Not yet exercised end to end.** `/drain` has not been run, by hand or under `/loop`. The plan's next step is one supervised tick before starting the loop, which would take entry 43.
- **The context saving is a soft guarantee.** It depends on subagents honouring the six-line report format. If one pastes a diff into its reply the saving evaporates — the prompt states the constraint and the reason, but nothing enforces it mechanically. Worth watching on the first few iterations.
- Subagents run without worktree isolation, so iterations serialise on one working tree. The stateless guard makes worktree isolation safe to add later if parallelism is ever wanted, but entries overlap in the files they touch, so serialising is the correct default.

## Summary
- Adds `packages/engine/discovery/pcfg.js`: a probabilistic-context-free-grammar equation-discovery engine over the system's own fold/operator primitives (fold amplitude variables, arithmetic ops, unary ops, and EO primitives like `gaussianKernel`), inspired by arXiv 2012.00428 ("Probabilistic Grammars for Equation Discovery"). Grammar rule probabilities are weighted toward shallow/simple trees, acting as a parsimony (Occam) prior; `discoverEquation` runs Monte Carlo sampling over the grammar and ranks candidates by fit error combined with the prior.
- Adds `test-equation-discovery.mjs`: sanity-check harness that seeds known target formulas (a `gaussianKernel` combination and a plain arithmetic difference) and confirms the search recovers them as the top-ranked candidates.

This complements the existing `derivation-map.md` work (in `eoreader-proxy`), which verifies known equations against these same primitives — this module instead searches for previously-unspecified equations that fit given data.

author: ernisch
body:
Der PR enthält jetzt **zwei** Teile. Teil 2 ist der wichtigere: er behebt einen Defekt aus #143, der in Production aktiv Vorgänge korrumpiert.

Details: [`befund-csd-2026-vorgangsverlust.md`](docs/befund-csd-2026-vorgangsverlust.md) §12a (Korrekturen), §12b (Befund), §12c (Behebung).

---

# Teil 2 · Resolver gegen Magnet-Vorgänge (B4-2)

## Ursache — eindeutig nachgewiesen

`sameVorgang()` fragte: *„gibt es **irgendein** Dokumentpaar, das dasselbe Ereignis beschreibt?"* — ein **Existenzquantor**. Damit wächst die Trefferwahrscheinlichkeit **linear mit der Bestandsgröße**, und **jede Aufnahme macht einen Vorgang anziehender**. Selbstverstärkend.

**Production-Beleg:** `vg-zeitung-20260428-f362cc` wuchs in **einem einzigen Lauf von 13 auf 65 Dokumente** und enthielt am Ende Armutsbericht, Sportfördergesetz, Pflegereform, den Rücktritt des Verkehrsministers, eine vietnamesische Gewerkschaftswahl **und den Anschlag auf den Berliner CSD**.

**Isoliert, nicht vermutet:** dieselben 65 Dokumente ergeben durch die aktuelle Clusterfunktion **16 getrennte Cluster**. Die Clusterregel ist gesund — der Resolver war es nicht. Alle 65 Dokumente hatten eine Veröffentlichungszeit; fehlende Zeitstempel scheiden als Ursache aus.

## Magnet-Analyse — objektive Definition statt Bauchgefühl

Neues Werkzeug `scripts/vorgangs-magnet-analyse.js`, **rein lesend, bereinigt nichts**. Man gibt die Dokumente eines Vorgangs erneut in die Clusterfunktion: ein echtes Ereignis bleibt **ein** Cluster, ein Magnet zerfällt.

> **Kohärenz** = größtes Cluster / alle Dokumente · **Magnet** = ≥ 10 Dokumente **und** Kohärenz < 0,6

| | Magnete (12) | gesunde Vorgänge (24) |
|---|---|---|
| Kohärenz | **0,07 – 0,55** | **0,67 – 1,00** |
| Kernanker | **0 – 2, überwiegend 0** | **2 – 8** |
| Dokumente (Mittel) | 71,3 | 17,6 |
| Themenvielfalt (Mittel) | 31,2 Cluster | 2,8 Cluster |
| größter | **400** (`vg-regierung`) | — |

Zwischen 0,55 und 0,67 liegt **kein einziger** Vorgang — die Schwelle trennt in einer echten Lücke der Verteilung, nicht an einem geratenen Punkt. **Jeder** Magnet hat **keinen Kern**.

## Lösung — die kleinste, die die Fehlerklasse schließt

> **Verglichen wird Kern gegen Kern, nicht Dokument gegen Dokument.**
> Ein Vorgang, dessen Dokumente nichts gemeinsam haben, **hat keinen Kern** — und kann strukturell nichts mehr anziehen. **Der Magnet wird durch seine eigene Heterogenität unschädlich.**

Fünf Riegel, jeder mit eigenem Ablehnungsgrund: `vorgang-voll` (≥ 60 Dokumente) · `bestand-ohne-kern` · `cluster-ohne-kern` · `vorgang-zu-alt` (14-Tage-Fortschreibungsfenster) / `jahreskonflikt` · `kernueberdeckung-zu-schwach`.

Die Anforderung in Schritt 5 **skaliert mit der Kerngröße** (`min(2, ⌈Kern/2⌉)`). Ein fester Wert wäre in beide Richtungen falsch: bei zwei Kernankern würde jede echte Fortschreibung abgelehnt, bei sechs würde ein einziger Treffer („berlin") jedes Berliner Thema anziehen.

**Verworfen** (im Code dokumentiert): Mehrheitsentscheidung über Dokumentpaare (zu streng für laufende Ereignisse — späte Reaktionen passen sprachlich nicht zu frühen Tatmeldungen) · reine Größenobergrenze (begrenzt den Schaden, behebt die Ursache nicht) · Embeddings (teuer, nicht deterministisch, nicht offline testbar).

## Nachvollziehbarkeit

Jede Entscheidung liefert eine **vollständige, reproduzierbare Spur**: verglichene Dokumente, beide Kerne, Überdeckung mit Gewicht und geforderter Schwelle, erfüllte und fehlende Kriterien. Auch **Ablehnungen** werden je geprüftem Kandidaten protokolliert.

## Production-Validierung (read-only)

Der echte CSD-Cluster (16 Dokumente) gegen die 25 größten Vorgänge:

| | |
|---|---|
| Magnete geprüft | **12** |
| davon blockiert | **12 von 12** |
| Vorgänge, die den CSD-Cluster aufnehmen würden | **keiner** |
| unter dem ALTEN Resolver hätten ihn gezogen | **3** |

Beide Riegel greifen unabhängig: alle 12 Magnete haben Kernanker = 0, elf zusätzlich ≥ 60 Dokumente. Die gesunden Vorgänge lehnen mit `kein-spezifischer-kerntreffer` ab — inhaltlich korrekt.

**Keine Bereinigung bestehender Magnete.** Sie bleiben, wie sie sind — sie können nur nichts mehr anziehen. Eine Bereinigung wäre ein Production-Schreibzugriff mit KI-Kosten und eine eigene Freigabe.

---

# Teil 1 · Drei Qualitätskorrekturen

**K-1 · `--karenz=<stunden>`** im Nachhol-Werkzeug. Standard bleibt 24 h, wirkt ausschließlich dort. Ohne die Option blockierte die Karenz 16 von 20 CSD-Dokumenten.

**K-2 · Prompt-Auswahl.** Bisher nach Dokumentkennung (faktisch zufällig). Gemessen am echten CSD-Stapel:

| Strategie | Schlüsselfakten | Anker |
|---|---|---|
| alt (Dokumentkennung) | 5/6 — ohne Terror-Einordnung | 59 |
| neueste zuerst | 5/6 — ohne Landesreaktion | 58 |
| älteste zuerst | 5/6 — ohne „Täter erschossen" | 66 |
| **neu: Faktenabdeckung + feste Endpunkte** | **6/6** | **69** |

„Neueste zuerst" ist damit **nicht** optimal. Eine zusätzliche zeitliche Streuung wurde gebaut, gemessen und **verworfen** (5/6 statt 6/6).

**K-3 · Telemetrie.** Gemeldet war eine Inkonsistenz, gefunden wurden **drei**: Filter auf `understanding-lagecheck` statt `understanding-lage` (+ fehlendes `understanding-nachhol`) · `ERGEBNISGRUPPEN` ohne die zwei Pending-Ergebnisse · `verarbeitet = counts.saved` ohne `updated`/`merged`. Namensliste durch **Präfix** ersetzt. Weitere Inkonsistenzen dieser Art gesucht und **nicht gefunden**. Zwei **Strukturtests** prüfen künftig den Quelltext gegen die Zuordnungstabellen.

---

## Merge-Konflikt

Der Konflikt mit #144 lag ausschließlich im Kopf von `CURRENT_STATE.md` (beide Sprints änderten die Aktualisierungszeile). Aufgelöst **ohne Informationsverlust**: die Zeile nennt jetzt beide Sprintreihen, der Incident-Banner aus #144 bleibt vollständig; `main`-HEAD und Banner-Stand nachgezogen.

## Tests · CI

Offline-Suite **162/162** · Browser-Smoke **32/32** · neu `vorgangs-resolver-test.js` **54/54** · `vorgangsidentitaet-test.js` **67/67** · `vorgangs-lebenszyklus-test.js` **81/81**. **CI grün**, beide Pflicht-Checks, Run `30244383597`.

## Risiko · Rollback

Keine Migration, kein Flag, kein Cron, keine Datenänderung. Der Resolver ist **strenger** als vorher — im Zweifel entsteht ein eigener Vorgang statt einer falschen Zusammenführung. Das kostet mehr KI-Aufrufe (mehr neue Vorgänge), verliert aber nichts: jedes Dokument bleibt verknüpft und hat einen Endzustand. Rollback: Vercel-Redeploy des Vorgängers.

**Nicht selbst gemergt, nicht selbst deployt.**

author: kkoshin
body:
## Problem

In SSH (remote project) mode, clicking a branch in the branch picker switches the branch successfully (verified in the terminal), but the branch name shown in the UI never updates. Local mode works fine.

## Root cause

`Repository::change_branch` relied entirely on the worktree file watcher noticing the `.git/HEAD` change to re-scan and propagate the new branch. On a remote (SSH) host that watcher round-trip is unreliable: the `git switch` runs on the server, but the downstream `UpdateRepository` carrying the new `branch_summary` never reaches the client, so `apply_remote_update` on the client never emits `HeadChanged` and the UI stays stale. Local mode only worked because the local watcher reliably observes `.git/HEAD`.

This is inconsistent with the sibling mutating operations, both of which explicitly refresh git state after the mutation rather than trusting the watcher:

- `Repository::reset` calls `schedule_scan(updates_tx, cx)` after the job.
- `Repository::fetch` calls `refresh_branch_list(...)` after a successful fetch.

`change_branch` did neither — it just ran `backend.change_branch()` (local) or sent a `GitChangeBranch` RPC (remote) and returned.

## Fix

Mirror `reset`: make `Repository::change_branch` call `schedule_scan(updates_tx, cx)` after the change job.

- **Local repo:** `schedule_scan(None)` → `compute_snapshot` reads the new branch, emits `HeadChanged` locally.
- **SSH server:** `schedule_scan(Some(tx))` → `compute_snapshot` reads the new branch, sends `DownstreamUpdate::UpdateRepository` over the downstream channel → the client's `apply_remote_update` sees the new `branch_summary` and emits `HeadChanged`.
- **SSH client:** its own git store is `GitStoreState::Remote`, so no local scan runs; the server does it.

`schedule_scan` is keyed by `GitJobKey::ReloadGitState`, so any scan additionally triggered by the watcher is deduped.

`change_branch` needed `cx: &mut Context<Self>` for the scan (matching `reset`'s signature); updated the branch picker, the server-side `handle_change_branch`, the agent worktree archive caller, and the collab/remote_server integration tests. Added assertions in `test_remote_git_branches` that the downstream client repository observes the new branch after a remote switch.

## Note

The same watcher-reliance gap likely affects `delete_branch`, `create_branch`, `rename_branch`, `create_remote`, and `checkout_files` (they would also fail to refresh the branch list / HEAD over SSH). Left untouched here to keep this scoped to the reported bug; a follow-up can apply the same `schedule_scan` / `refresh_branch_list` pattern to them.

Release Notes:

- Fixed branch name in the UI not updating after switching branches in a remote (SSH) project, even though the switch succeeded.

author: just-tobi

author: chriswong6031-creator
body:
> ⚠️ **Stacked on #3798** (batch B). Its commit is included in this diff until #3798 merges; I rebase and force-push this branch once it does. **Merge #3798 first.** Review only the top commit (`test(unrun): fix + wire the two PIT/tape reds`).

Batch C of the red-on-arrival sweep (A: #3791 merged, B: #3798). Full method: `docs/UNRUN_TEST_CENSUS.md` §"Red on arrival — the P4/P5 sweep".

## One root cause, two suites

Both were red because **the fixture encoded a moment rather than a contract**.

### `test_setup_tier` — a relationship about a live tape is still a claim about the market

The probe class read the **live** `data/china_search/closes.parquet` and asserted relationships about three real tickers ("`300725` must be in 2W stoch washout (<= 35)"). Its own docstring claimed these "pass on any panel update that keeps the same structural setup story" — but the structural story is the market's to change, not the repo's:

- `300725`'s 2W stoch had recovered out of the washout band (**24 → 45**)
- `688306`'s 2W MACD was no longer approaching up

Two of six probes red, the other four passing on borrowed time. Scanning cutoffs showed all six hold together **only up to 2026-07-03** — the tape they were authored against — so the class now reads a committed **33 KB** three-ticker slice frozen at that date, with the regeneration recipe in the docstring. It now tests the *engine*, which is what it was always for, and cannot decay again.

Its `skip_if_no_data` guard is deleted along with the live read: **a skip that fires in CI is a pass you cannot see** — the class `scripts/check_skip_only_suites.py` (#3768) exists to catch. The orphaned `_data_available()` helper goes with it.

### `test_stock_personality_wiring` — a fixture below a producer's floor

It dated its fires `2024-06-03`. The stamper clamps its scan to `max(build_date - 30d, "2026-07-06")` — the ledger wire-in date, before which it never backfills. The fixture matched no fires, the writer returned early, and the test failed on a **missing parquet** — which presents as a broken writer, not a stale date.

> When a producer grows a floor, every fixture below it stops exercising the producer and starts failing for an unrelated-looking reason.

The dates now **straddle** the floor on purpose, so the no-backfill rule is *asserted* rather than tripped over.

That suite also carried the mirror of batch B's vacuous green: its "wrong date" row sat one day before `build_date`, from when the filter was same-day. The filter later became a 30-day lookback (fires land in `track_record` retroactively, so a same-day filter would match nothing, ever) — making that row legitimately **in** window and proving nothing. It is now genuinely pre-floor.

Both suites were also worse than the sweep reported: `-x` had hidden two extra failures in `test_stock_personality_wiring` and one in `test_setup_tier`.

## Wiring

Per #3488: new `unrun-pit-probes` lane, plus both test files in `ci.yml` `paths` — **and the frozen fixture itself**, because it *is* the input under test, so re-freezing the tape must retrigger the suite that reads it. Subjects are `engine/setup_tier.py` and `scripts/build_stock_library.py`, already covered by the `engine/**` and `scripts/*.py` catch-alls. Byte-identical dependency install so the pack keeps one shared venv. 2 suites / 90 tests / ~1.4s.

## Verification

- 90 tests green, run as the lane invokes them
- `run_ci_pack.py --validate-only` green
- rebased onto merged `main` (post-#3791/#3788/#3790)
