author: georgesleen
body:
After a reset the heading anchor (#65/#66) falls back to the static `offset_seed_deg` (Vancouver declination), losing the boat iron and frame-constant terms GNSS had learned. This persists the GNSS-refined `mag_offset` to flash and restores it at boot, so a reset recovers the full learned offset immediately instead of coasting to the rough guess. GNSS still owns absolute heading and refines it further, so a stale value is self-correcting and always at least as good as the static seed.

## Host-testable core (Arduino-free)
- `lib/fusion/offset_store.h`: a 16-byte flash record (magic + version + offset + CRC-32) with `encode`/`validate`, and `OffsetPersistPolicy`, which writes only when the offset is GNSS-validated (variance below a gate the mag alone can't reach), changed past a threshold, and a minimum interval has elapsed. Time is injected; unit-tested in `test_offset_store` (round-trip, erased/foreign/corrupt/out-of-range rejection, the three-way write gate).

## Firmware wiring (`#ifdef ARDUINO`)
- `offset_store_eeprom`: load/save over the earlephilhower EEPROM emulation (one flash sector).
- A low-priority `persist_task` takes the latest offset from a 1-slot mailbox the fusion task publishes and commits it when the policy says so, keeping the few-ms, core-idling flash write off the 100 Hz fusion loop.
- `main.cpp` loads a valid blob at boot and overrides `mti_yaw.offset_seed_deg`; a missing/invalid blob keeps the tuning value. Emits `# persist: loaded/saved <deg>`.

## Verification
210 native + 212 sim tests green; `pico2` builds (EEPROM auto-linked, RAM 17%).

**Not yet hardware-validated:** the load-bearing risk is `EEPROM.commit()` calling `rp2040.idleOtherCore()` under FreeRTOS SMP. Needs an on-hardware run (write, power-cycle, confirm load + no hang) before this is trusted; if `idleOtherCore` misbehaves, fall back to suspending the scheduler around the commit.

author: witbrock
body:
## What changed

- Removed the replay sampler's Python semantic verdict, required-tool/effect tables, selector/certification logic, automatic action classifier, model probing, and premium-model gate. Collection status now means only that evidence was captured; unscored observations are `inconclusive`.
- Replaced read-named local adaptive tools with capability-neutral discovery/invocation and delegated exactly three existing additive representation effects: `create_concepts`, `upsert_text_relation`, and `add_relationship`.
- Bound actor, namespace, creation scope, and provenance outside model arguments; authorised existing subjects by exact actor identity or canonical actor/organisation scope; denied only the evidenced visibility-widening predicate family.
- Preserved model call order for batches containing effects and propagated succeeded/partial/failed/indeterminate effect evidence through persisted telemetry.
- Made commit-before-error paths truthful, while keeping pre-dispatch and typed validation failures definite.
- Kept the intentionally read-only stdio `von_chat_run` surface honest by filtering write effects from its advertised catalogue.
- Added telemetry-driven model-choice doctrine: compare a stronger model before durable semantic code when capability is plausibly the cause; compare a faster/cheaper model when adequate behaviour is too slow or costly.
- Defined read-only as a semantic-effect boundary rather than a zero-write storage guarantee.

## Why

The preceding architecture accumulated Python-side guesses about intent and success. Those guesses blocked alternative model strategies, confused evidence collection with evaluation, and encouraged more case-shaped control code after each miss. This candidate subtracts that controller policy while retaining deterministic authority and effect truthfulness only where concrete harm or ambiguity was demonstrated.

## Impact and boundary

Ordinary authenticated turns can now choose among broad delegated reads and a small generic representation aperture. No request classifier, domain resolver, prompt patch, automatic model router, merge, cutover, or production activation is included.

This is a stacked draft on PR #309 and is frozen at commit `51ccd68cff41519a0a4741f9ee7cd5fde4174a7b` for a bounded fresh-case experiment. Do not merge independently or before the human evidence gate.

## Validation

- Shared affected-surface suite: 181 passed, 5 skipped (before the final narrow review corrections).
- Final effect/authority/stdio/telemetry suite: 84 passed, 5 skipped.
- Pruned sampler/report suite: 37 passed.
- Focused sub-suites during review: 41 sampler tests, 23 catalogue tests, and authority/privacy checks all passed.
- Ruff on every changed Python file, `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Live represented prompt read-back confirmed it contains no retired or new local adaptive tool names; no prompt mutation was required.

## Frozen live evidence

The bounded round is complete; there were no post-reveal code or prompt changes.

- Exact read-only case: Terra and Luna both gave honest grounded non-answers with no effects. Luna was 127.2 s versus Terra's 184.9 s (31.2% faster), supporting a bounded faster-profile experiment rather than a universal model switch.
- Factual ecology case 1 (`arXiv:2408.02603`): the paper type, paper, and qualified source record committed after effect timeouts, but final synthesis timed out and the fallback falsely said nothing changed.
- Factual ecology case 2 (`arXiv:2506.03346`): the paper and an analyst-inference predicate committed; the requested cross-paper relation did not. Final synthesis again timed out and the fallback falsely said nothing changed.
- Counterfactual Harry Q. Bovik case: the counterfactual-scenario and fictional-persona types plus their instances committed. No unqualified lab membership or paper authorship was created, but the scenario role/relationships were incomplete and the fallback omitted the committed concepts.
- All three effect turns spent about 150–153 s in adaptive research, with 62–76 s measured LLM time and 102–117 s adaptive non-LLM time. Their final Terra calls then expired inside the shared turn envelope.

General judgement: the model demonstrated useful cross-domain semantic judgement without case-specific controller code. The merge blocker is a general effect-completion/terminal-reconciliation defect: late commits remain indeterminate to the turn, and a final-model timeout can produce a false no-change narration. The evidence does not justify ecology/arXiv/Harry-specific Python, required predicate lists, or a stronger-model arm.

Recommended bounded successor: persist late completion against the existing `effect_id`; reconcile fallbacks with effect/canonical evidence; reserve or route a measured final-response budget; and remove measured synchronous Atlas/index work that is not needed for the committed fact. Keep identity and authority checks. Then use known cases as regressions and fresh cross-domain ecology/deontology cases as unseen evaluation.

Full evidence judgement SHA-256: `0b87dea4793acaf8eae25c187d5e723a55cde6f73c543d63243e2e51e7f13b17`.

PR remains draft and unmerged.

## Atlas/handler diagnostic addendum

Independent log analysis found negligible MCP queue time (about 0.2–3.1 ms) but handler/database dominance: eight create deadlines at 8.7–20.0 s, seven late completions at 19.8–44.3 s, broad legacy-name scans returning 101 + 899 concepts, visibility reads over about 1,617 IDs, and relationship-extent refreshes of 1.0–3.9 s. A stronger model would not remove this cost.

The smallest measured performance candidates are to coalesce a whole logical create batch inside the existing deferred relationship-extent synchronisation scope; batch name/content/note enrichment into one existing text fetch; and avoid launching a successor mutation while the first non-cancellable handler remains live. Tightening legacy name search is separate because it changes compatibility behaviour.

The redacted Mongo diagnostic entry point itself failed with `NameError: _mongo_query_diagnostics_report`, and the profiler fallback had no samples. Therefore no missing-index or winning-plan claim is made.

Diagnostics addendum SHA-256: `e3c227e110ee7b8a259c560aeebc076404750a797d116347603e1a0b0688c622`.

author: jeroendk
body:
Stacked on #119 (which is stacked on #117) — merge those first. This PR's own diff is the two `go.mod`/`go.sum` pairs below.

Closes the last two open alerts of any severity: `golang.org/x/net` `< 0.55.0` (GHSA-5cv4-jp36-h3mw, DoS in the `net/html` parser) in `services/bsnk-mock` (#22) and `services/consent-portal-backend` (#31).

## Why these two needed a hand

`golang.org/x/net` appears in **neither `go.mod` nor `go.sum`** for these services. No package from it is imported, so Go's module graph pruning leaves it out of the recorded requirements — but MVS still selected **v0.53.0** from the dependency graph, and that is what Dependabot flags.

The fix is an explicit `// indirect` requirement at v0.55.0, which `go mod tidy` retains. It also pulls `golang.org/x/sys` to v0.45.0 and `golang.org/x/text` to v0.37.0.

I checked all 13 services: these two were the only ones below v0.55.0. The other seven that pull x/net were already at v0.55.0, so no further changes were needed.

## The other six medium alerts

Alerts #9, #17, #18, #24, #25 and #27 (`golang.org/x/net` at older ranges, `google.golang.org/protobuf` `< 1.33.0`) are **already closed** — the `go mod tidy` runs in #117 carried protobuf to v1.36.11 and x/net past those ranges.

## Verification

Per service: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` — all pass.

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session and transcript operations contained competing SQLite mutation implementations, duplicated transcript projection builders, and whole-store deserialization for a single-session lookup. These paths could disagree about aliases, cross-process conflict checks, session identity, active-branch visibility, and timestamps. A malformed unrelated row could break a valid session, and deleting a wrapper without preserving its wider public contract could break cron.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one existing per-agent SQLite transaction owner for exact and alias-target patches, one deterministic transcript projection for both rebuild paths, and direct keyed session reads. Preserve synchronous transaction commits, public lifecycle compatibility, opaque aliases, external Pi-owned transcripts, current-main gateway list projections, and inherited model routes. Tighten the canonical accessor-debt ratchet from two obsolete transcript reads to zero.

## User Impact

No new config, provider, plugin SDK, database schema, database version, or gateway protocol. Existing session identity, transcript history, migration, active branches, gateway listing, and provider-owned transcript behavior are preserved. Large session catalogs no longer parse unrelated entries to answer one-session queries.

## Correctness Fixes

- A planted malformed unrelated SQLite row no longer breaks the requested session, catalog candidate, or transcript.
- Exact-key and opaque-alias writes share snapshot revalidation, identity publication, maintenance, and synchronous commit ownership.
- The public delete lifecycle retains the broader cron `requireWriteSuccess` contract.
- Synchronous and worker transcript rebuilds share visible-branch selection, source timestamps, watermark, active rows, and rewind identity.
- Rebased main's gateway list projection and inherited model route remain intact and have direct gateway regressions.
- The stale allowance for two removed legacy transcript reads is deleted; the strict accessor guard remains enabled.

## Exact-Head Runtime Proof

Reviewed head: `7d75234d07ab5327639effb805548c0ae882c1ad`. Rebase parent: `054495d16dd6c161a3afc1429d299b060dc1676d`. Fresh isolated run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/30243550259.

```text
session accessor boundary guard passed
SQLite transaction boundary guard passed
check-session-accessor-boundary.test.ts: 36 passed
check-sqlite-transaction-boundary.test.ts: 5 passed
session-accessor.test.ts: 82 passed
session-accessor.conformance.test.ts: 51 passed
session-transcript-projection-rebuild.test.ts: 4 passed
server.sessions.list-store-materialization.test.ts: 2 passed
embedded-gateway-stub.test.ts: 19 passed
26 files / 8 shards / 429 tests passed
full production build: passed
```

The malformed-row regression, 100,000-message transcript rebuild, opaque Matrix aliases, cross-process cleanup, parent forks, read-only recovery, timestamp preservation, public session SDK, gateway projection, and Pi catalog/adoption are included.

## Full Validation

- Exact-head required `openclaw/ci-gate`: passed.
- Exact-head session-accessor and SQLite transaction boundary checks: passed.
- Exact-head precise OpenGrep security scan: passed. Its first runner encountered a base-fetch network timeout; the unchanged-head retry completed without findings or a scan exemption.
- Four complete core/plugin production and test typecheck lanes: passed.
- Both production boundary guards and all 41 guard regressions: passed.
- All 429 regression tests: passed.
- All three production, full-tree, and script dead-code gates: zero findings.
- Full CLI, bundled-plugin, 142-entrypoint SDK, Control UI, assets, and performance build: passed.
- Fresh high-reasoning autoreview and secret scan: clean.
- Net production reduction: 293 lines.

## Summary

author: ferraroroberto
body:
## Summary

The bot could act (#14: chat, select_slot, break_block, place_block, use_item) but couldn't move. `move_to(x, y, z)` and `look_at(x, y, z)` (`src/movement.js`) add that, through the **same `performAction` gate as #14** — no exceptions, no separate movement-only path.

`player_auth_input` was split into its own issue (#17) rather than squeezed into #14 because it is a fundamentally different shape of problem: every other action is one packet (or a short fixed sequence) the caller fires and verifies once. Bedrock's `player_auth_input` is the client's continuous, per-tick assertion of its own position — sent every tick the client is connected, not a one-shot command. BedrockX has **zero** implementation of it (confirmed by grep across its source — only the wire shape exists in the pinned `protocol.json`); this sender is built from the protocol definition alone, nothing to mirror.

### The key design point — stated explicitly, not buried

Every other action in this vocabulary follows "never treat a written packet as success" by waiting for an observable world-state change. Movement doesn't get one on the happy path, and that's not a gap — it's how the protocol is designed. The packet is literally named `player_auth_input` because the **client asserts** its position each tick; the server only replies (`correct_player_move_prediction`) when it **disagrees**. So for `move_to`, "we sent the planned ticks and nothing corrected us" *is* the intended positive result — applied to the world model via a new `applySelfMove` helper (`src/world.js`), separate from `reduce()`'s inbound-packet dispatch since it isn't a real inbound packet. A real correction always overrides it; a correction that lands far from the requested target is reported as **failure**, with the server's actual position in the reason, never silently accepted.

### How the #14 envelope governs movement, unchanged

`move_to`/`look_at` are wired into `perform-action.js` as a new "streaming" action kind (`stream: true`) — a per-tick loop instead of a fixed packet list — but go through the identical gate: dry-run by default (reports an estimated tick count, writes nothing), the bounded-region check refuses out-of-range targets rather than clamping them, and each call consumes exactly **one** rate-limit slot regardless of how many ticks it sends internally (verified by test — a multi-tick `move_to` doesn't starve the limiter for the next caller). `look_at` is the one exception to the spatial check: it only rotates the bot, so a look target outside the operating region isn't a movement-safety concern the way an actual `move_to` target is — called out explicitly in the code, not silently diverging from the pattern.

### Two explicitly unverified assumptions

- **Tick cadence: 50ms/20Hz**, the standard Minecraft simulation tick rate. Nothing in the pin states the client's expected *send* rate for `player_auth_input` specifically — conventional, not measured.
- **Walk speed: ~0.2154 blocks/tick** (Minecraft's normal walking speed), used only to size the naive step and tick budget, not a claim about what the server will accept.

Naive straight-line movement only, per #14's own out-of-scope carve-out — no pathfinding, no obstacle avoidance. LLM wiring stays a separate future layer (#15), deliberately not started here.

## Validation

- `npm run verify` green, 142/142, on the Windows tower. Not re-run on the Mac Mini this session.
- Fully offline: a fake client/world pair drives the tick loop in `test/movement.test.js` (packet shape, stepping math, silent-success, server-correction-accepted, server-correction-rejected, look_at) and `test/perform-action.test.js` (dry-run writes zero packets, region refusal names the region, one rate-limit slot per call, end-to-end armed move via the shared gate).
- `test/world.test.js` covers the new `correct_player_move_prediction` reducer (player vs. vehicle prediction type) and `applySelfMove`'s malformed-input no-op contract.
- No live Realm connection made or attempted for this issue — offline research + implementation only, per the standing rule.

Closes #17

body:
## 요약
- 근본원인(curl로 dev 백엔드 직접 재현해 확定): `proxy.ts`에서 sp_at이 없거나 무효라 refresh를 타는 두 분기가, 새 토큰을 정상 발급받고도 **원 pathname을 그냥 통과**시켰다. bare 레거시 링크(`/board` 등)는 그 pathname에 대응 페이지가 없어(오직 `/{ws}/{proj}/board`) Next 라우터가 즉시 404 — 다음 요청부턴 sp_at이 유효해 정상 경로를 타므로 "재로그인 직후 첫 진입만 404, 재진입은 정상"이었다.
- `resolveAndRespond()`로 해소 로직(legacy-redirect/rename-redirect/workspace-resolve)을 하나로 모아, 정상 경로와 refresh-직후 경로 **둘 다** 동일하게 타도록 리팩터.
- AC3(본체): 프로젝트를 못 정했을 때(`!projectId`)나 BE 단건조회 실패(`!slugs`)도 404 대신 `/org-briefing?next=<원경로>`로 302 — org는 확定됐으니 프로젝트 불필요 페이지로 보내고 원 목적지를 보존("고르면 여기로 돌아온다").
- `use-unified-switcher.ts`가 `?next=`을 읽어 프로젝트 선택 직후 원래 목적지로 복귀.
- open-redirect 방지(생성 쪽 proxy.ts + 소비 쪽 switcher 양쪽) + 되돌이 방지 마커(`_prRetry`)로, next로 복귀해도 다시 실패하면 무한 왕복 대신 정직하게 멈춤(Next 404).

## 재현 (dev 백엔드, curl)
```
① sp_at 고의 손상(서명무효)+sp_rt 유효 → bare GET /board → 404 (새 sp_at은 org/project 다 정상으로 발급됨)
② 그 새 sp_at으로 같은 bare /board 재요청 → 301 정상
```
선생님 재현("같은 브라우저·같은 탭, 로그인 풀린 채 재로그인하면 첫 진입만 404, 재진입은 정상")과 일치.

## 테스트
- `proxy.test.ts`: 회귀가드 4건 신설(토큰-refresh-우회 2건 + dead-end→302 전환 2건 + 되돌이 방지 1건) — mutation 확認(되돌리면 RED).
- `use-unified-switcher.test.tsx`: next-복귀 1건 + open-redirect 방지 3건(protocol-relative/절대URL/백슬래시).
- `org-briefing-shell.test.tsx`: 기존 테스트에 `next/navigation` mock 보강(회귀 없음).
- 전체 vitest: 312 files / 2079 passed.
- `pnpm build`: 성공(exit 0).

## Test plan
- [ ] dev 배포 후 라이브 puppeteer로 동일 curl 시나리오 재현 확認(첫 진입 301/무배너, 프로젝트 미확定 시 org-briefing 배너+스위처로 복귀)

author: ryanbr
body:
Follow-up to #872, from its review. **Comments only, no behaviour change.**

Both allowlist comments claimed:

> allowed ONLY while a probe is actually in flight, so a default install can never form these bytes

That is true on 5/MG and **only** there. The whole `send()` allowlist sits inside the
`deviceFamily == .whoop5` branch, and WHOOP 4.0 has no send allowlist at all — so on a 4.0 the only
thing keeping `START_FF_KEY_EXCHANGE`(117) and `SEND_NEXT_FF`(118) off the wire is
`probeFeatureFlags()`'s own Test Centre gate.

Same practical outcome, and it matches how every other 4.0 command already works, so this is **not a
hole**. But the 4.0 is the family with a published key dump to reproduce, which makes it the likely
first runner — and someone auditing the safety story of an opcode nobody has validated on hardware
should not have to discover that the reassuring sentence only covers the other family.

Also adds a line on the Test Centre guard itself: for 4.0 it is not belt-and-braces, it is the belt.
That guard doing its job is load-bearing on that family, and the comment now says so.

Both platforms, both comment sites. `doc_comment_lint` and `i18n_audit.py --ci` green.

Originally offered as a patch on #872, but the push to the fork was refused (`maintainerCanModify`
is on, the token is not), so it lands here instead. Applies unchanged on top of the merge.

author: yballul-bytedance
body:
## Summary

Improves the `lark-drive +search` reference documentation with two new guidance sections:

1. **Title + body joint search**: When the user provides both a title keyword and a body keyword and requires both to match the same resource, the agent should issue a single combined `--query "title-word body-word"` search with scope filters (`--folder-tokens`, `--doc-types`), rather than splitting into a title-only and body-only search and intersecting results client-side. `--only-title` / `intitle:` are reserved for cases where the user explicitly wants title-only matching.

2. **Top N result cap with bounded pagination**: When the user asks for at most N results, N is an output upper bound — not a `--page-size` value. The agent should page through results (up to 3 pages), retain only candidates that satisfy both conditions based on `title` and `summary_highlighted`, read the body sequentially only for title-matched candidates when the summary is insufficient, and stop as soon as N confirmed results are collected. If 3 pages are exhausted without N results, the agent returns what it found and suggests the user narrow their keywords or scope.

The pagination strategy decision rule is also updated to reflect the new 3-page cap for joint searches alongside the existing 5-page limit for other scenarios.

## Changes

- `skills/lark-drive/references/lark-drive-search.md`
  - Added blockquote: — single `--query` approach for combined title+body searches; avoid splitting into two searches
  - Added blockquote: **Top N result cap** — pagination rules (up to 3 pages), sequential body reading, bounded scan termination
  - Added quick-reference table row: folder-scoped title+body search example
  - Updated **分页策略** decision rule to include the 3-page cap for joint searches

## Test Plan

- [ ] Documentation-only change; no executable code modified.
- [ ] Verify the new blockquotes render correctly in the Markdown preview.
- [ ] Manually validate the quick-reference table row for the joint title+body search command is consistent with the guidance text.
- [ ] Confirm the updated pagination strategy rule is internally consistent with the new Top N pagination section.

body:
## Summary

The TUI now takes control of its own background instead of inheriting the terminal's: every screen paints a dark tint of its mode's accent colour, so all users get the same visual experience regardless of their terminal theme. Analysis is deep green (`rgb(9,23,19)`), Planning deep blue, Standup deep magenta, Retro deep teal, Poker deep gold, Performance deep rust, Reporting deep violet, Usage deep amber. Home, splash, provider select, settings, changelog, and feedback screens use a neutral dark base (`rgb(16,16,20)`). Tints are deliberately dark (channel values ≤ 40) because the existing foreground palette is designed for dark backgrounds.

How it works:

- `Theme` gains a `bg` field, and a new `build_page_panel()` helper in `ui/shared/_components.py` builds the full-screen root Panel with `style="on {theme.bg}"`. Rich cascades that style onto every child segment — content rows, spacers, scroll filler, padding — the mechanism already proven by the analysis results screen's card background. All ~55 full-screen Panel sites now route through it.
- `MusicLive._stamp` back-fills the neutral base on any Panel that slips through unstyled (Rich's default Panel style is the string `"none"`, not empty). The screensaver and splash, which bypass that path, style themselves.
- The analysis results page keeps its original `rgb(13,31,27)` (now `_ANALYSIS_CARD_BG_RGB`) as a slightly-lighter elevated surface over the darker analysis page tint.
- The shared loading screen (`_build_standup_progress_screen`) and the generic run hub take the calling mode's theme, so poker/retro/reporting/performance reuse renders with the right tint.
- An AST-scan test (`tests/unit/test_screen_backgrounds.py`) fails the build if a raw full-screen `Panel(` reappears under `ui/`, plus truecolor render tests assert the background SGR escape per mode and for representative screens. The `tui-standards` skill documents `build_page_panel` as the mandatory page root.

Notes: an independent review flagged (and this branch fixes) the shared loading screen hardcoding the standup theme and the analysis roster-retry dialog bleeding terminal background around its popup. One deliberate small visual change: the feedback draft-guard popup page now has the standard white rounded border like every other page. Accepted limitation: a single refresh-tick flash of the terminal's own background when the alt screen first opens (fixing it would require OSC 11, which mutates the user's terminal).

## Test plan

- `make test` — full suite, 5786 passed / 16 skipped
- `make lint` — clean
- New tests: `tests/unit/test_screen_backgrounds.py` (per-mode tint rendering, distinctness + darkness invariants, representative screens incl. splash/screensaver/run-hub, AST guard), `test_music_bar.py` safety-net cases, `test_shared_components.py` `Theme.bg` + `build_page_panel` cases

author: youknowone
body:
Follow-up to #820. That PR took the `pyre-jit-trace` prepass from 15.5 GB / 13m46s to 8.95 GB / 5m24s. This takes the remaining peak down further, in the Charon LLBC front-end — which #820's phase map showed is now 99.7 % of the footprint.

## What was wrong

`Llbc::from_slice` materialised every inline `"HashConsedValue":[id, body]` occurrence as a `serde_json::Value`. Across the three pyre artefacts that is **207,783 bodies: 66.0 MB of JSON text held as 1602.7 MB of `Value` trees** (21.4×, measured malloc-exact, not RSS).

Only **55,428 of them (26.7 %) are ever reached** — the consumers in `front::mir` / `front::result_exc` / `front::option_try` only project the ids their lowered functions mention.

## The change

`struct DedupBody { raw: Box<RawValue>, parsed: OnceLock<Value> }`, exploded on the first `dedup_body(id)` call.

The accessor still returns `Option<&serde_json::Value>`, so **the ~45 call sites are untouched** — that is why this is a one-file change. `adt_def_id_from_ty_body` now reads the raw text through a typed projection instead of navigating a `Value`.

## Measured

`PYRE_PROFILE_PIPELINE=1` on the `pyre-jit-trace` prepass:

| phase | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| load 3 `.ullbc` | 3.27 GB / 2.48 s | **1.81 GB / 1.40 s** |
| after lowering | 8.92 GB / 44.6 s | **7.70 GB / 27.5 s** |
| build-script peak | 8.95 GB / 57.1 s | **7.74 GB / 36.3 s** |

## Verification

Generated output byte-identical: `819 all_jitcodes (555669 bytes bincode), generated 25254 bytes`.

Gate: `python3 ./pyre/check.py --backend dynasm,cranelift,wasm` → dynasm 329/329, cranelift 329/329, wasm 326/326.

## Note for reviewers

`majit-charon-reader/src` *is* listed by `scripts/extract-llbc.py --list-inputs` for pyre-interpreter and pyre-jit, so this edit re-keys the LLBC fingerprint. It does not change the artefacts: `rg -c charon_reader` on both `.ullbc` returns 0 — Charon does not extract this crate's items. `pyre/check.py` does not re-extract.

## What this does not do

The front-end still eagerly lowers all 14,998 functions. Instrumenting `GraphStore::get`/`get_mut` shows only **2,133 graphs / 62,343 of 380,868 blocks (16.4 %)** are ever fetched, so on-demand graph construction (RPython `bookkeeper.getdesc(func).cachedgraph`) is the remaining lever — worth an estimated further ~5 GB. That is its own change.

## 배경
실제 회의 녹음 테스트에서 재현된 `contradiction_detect.py`의 두 이슈 수정:
- "WAV로 저장하는 게 낫지 않을까요" 발화 1개 → 모순 카드 2개(중간/높음) 중복 저장
- "굳이 지금 바꿀 필요 있을까요? 기존 방식대로 가시죠"(새 주장 없는 단순 동의) → 오탐

## 변경 내용
1. **발언당 카드 1개 저장** — top-5 후보를 각각 판정해 통과분을 전부 저장하던 것을, 판정을 모은 뒤 `confidence` 최고 1개만 저장하도록 변경. `dedup_key`도 `(source_type, source_id, reference_file_id, reference_file_id)` 즉 **(발언, 근거 파일) 단위**로 만들어 청크가 달라도 같은 발언·문서면 중복 저장/알림을 막음.
2. **관련도 필터** — `search_hybrid` 후보 중 유사도 `< RELEVANCE_THRESHOLD(0.4)`인 청크는 LLM 판정 전에 제거. 무관 조각이 어쩌다 confidence threshold를 넘겨 오탐 나던 것 차단 (AI Chat 노드의 `filter_by_relevance`와 동일 기준).
3. **프롬프트 강화** — 새 사실·수치·방침 주장이 없는 단순 찬반/제안거절/동의는 모순 아님 명시. severity(high=사실 직접충돌 / medium=방침 상충 / low=뉘앙스) 기준 프롬프트에 명시.

## 참고
- 승주/지수가 임시로 WS push는 최고 1개만 보내도록 해뒀는데, 이 PR로 **DB 저장 단계에서부터** 1개만 남게 되어 목록/대시보드 조회의 중복도 해소됩니다.
- 검색 결과 병합/필터 로직만 바뀌어 기존 반환 형식(`detected_contradictions`, `saved_contradiction_ids`)은 그대로. WS push(`_detect_and_push_contradiction`)와 호환.

author: raymondkrahwinkel
body:
Implements `[e]` of the screenshot epic, on top of `[d]`'s selection surface.

## What changes for the operator

Press W on the selection surface and the window under the pointer lights up; the one on top wins where they overlap. Since the capture already holds every pixel on the desktop, taking a window is a crop to its rectangle — nothing is asked of the window itself, and it is never raised or focused.

## The mode that cannot exist everywhere

- **Windows** — `EnumWindows` walks top-level windows in z-order already, so the stacking comes free. Bounds from `DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS`, not `GetWindowRect`: the latter includes the invisible resize border, which would put a band of whatever is behind the window into every window shot. Cloaked windows are skipped — a window on another virtual desktop still enumerates and still reports a rectangle.
- **macOS** — `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo`, which reports bounds and layer without Screen Recording permission, because geometry is not pixels.
- **Linux, genuine X11** — `_NET_CLIENT_LIST_STACKING`, bottom-to-top, reversed.
- **Linux, Wayland** — **not available, and the surface says so.** Telling one client where another's windows are is what Wayland was designed not to do, and this app is an XWayland client on Plasma 6, so the X11 property lists only other XWayland windows — a fraction of what the operator can see. KWin's `org.kde.KWin.ScreenShot2` remains the one candidate, and the two things the ticket wants proven about it (whether `CaptureInteractive` shows KWin's own picker; whether access is declarative through an installed `.desktop` entry, which would make one a packaging requirement) need a spike on a real Plasma session. Until then the mode does not exist there and explains itself, rather than being a key that quietly does nothing.

## Verification

- Build clean with `-warnaserror`; Core 2501, ViewTests 144, Infrastructure 363 — all green.
- The picking arithmetic is tested against a stubbed window list on a 150% display, so window bounds arriving in desktop space and being used in image space is exercised rather than assumed.
- The Windows enumeration was run against the real desktop on a Windows machine.
- Guards mutation-proven. **Two are honestly not covered and say so in the code**: which DWM attribute is asked for, and the cloaked filter. Neither can be distinguished from a desktop whose real window edges are unknown; both are readings of the documentation, and `[g]` is where a maximised window with a band of wallpaper around it would show up.

author: wilshi
body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw devices list` rendered the paired-device table without a `deviceId` column, but `openclaw devices remove <deviceId>` requires one. When several paired devices share a display name, the rows are indistinguishable and the only way to learn the actionable identifier is to discover `--json` independently.

Fixes #114279.

## Why This Change Was Made

The human-readable list now keeps the friendly `Device` label, adds a sanitized `Device ID` column for scanning, and prints a compact `Full device IDs` index after the table. Real device IDs are 64-character SHA-256 fingerprints, so the index deliberately emits each full ID and matching friendly label on one logical output line instead of relying on a table cell that can hard-wrap the token.

The gateway response and `--json` output already contain `deviceId` and are unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish devices with identical display names and copy the complete identifier required by `devices remove`, `devices rename`, `devices rotate`, and `devices revoke` directly from ordinary list output.

## Evidence

- Current-main repro at `95a1420d978f673af14d7a6665ff2430baba846e`: a focused duplicate-name test failed because the paired table contained neither `Device ID` nor the two IDs.
- Exact-head focused suite: `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/devices-cli.test.ts` — 52/52 tests passed.
- The regression uses two distinct 64-character fingerprints and requires each exact `<full-id>  OpenClaw Desktop` mapping to occupy one newline-delimited output line.
- Source-blind behavior checks covered duplicate display names, the unchanged JSON payload, and terminal-control sanitization.
- `oxfmt --check src/cli/devices-cli.runtime.ts src/cli/devices-cli.test.ts` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent adversarial refutation: `NO-ACTIONABLE-OBJECTION` after the long-ID repair.
- Codex autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings.

## Changes

- `src/cli/devices-cli.runtime.ts` adds the sanitized table column and a copyable full-ID index derived from the same ordered row projection.
- `src/cli/devices-cli.test.ts` proves two devices with identical friendly names remain distinguishable with realistic full-length IDs.

## Notes

- Pending approvals and other device subcommands are untouched.
- Full IDs are shown only after the existing operator-authorized pairing-list RPC succeeds; no new authorization or data surface is added.

author: yohamta0
body: ## Problem `dagu validate` reports every preserved value reference at the same level, so these three are indistinguishable in its output: | Reference | Resolves at run time? | |---|---| | `${steps.build.outputs.undeclared}` | never, the output is not declared | | `${context.paths.artifacts_dir}` | always | | `${env.API_TOKEN}` | yes, the operator supplies it | Only the first is a defect. The other two are reported because validation evaluates a spec outside a run, where a synthetic scope holds almost nothing: `noticeBuiltinContext` models 3 of the 22 supported `context.*` bindings, and the env scope is deliberately built with `includeOS=false` so validation does not depend on the shell it runs in. The noise is not harmless. A correct workflow was deleted on the strength of a `reason=namespace_unavailable` line that was a false alarm. Dagu's own bundled examples trip it too, since `dagu example 12` uses `${context.paths.artifacts_dir}`. The true positives are worth keeping. The undeclared-output check is what caught a wrong cursor example in the docs (dagucloud/docs#24). ## Approach Classify instead of suppress. Resolution semantics are unchanged. They already carried the needed distinction: `namespace_unavailable` means "well formed, absent from this scope", while a name the spec does not define already produced `unknown_context_field`. So no resolver behaviour moves, and the tests that pin it (`builtin_context_test.go`, `value_notices_test.go`) needed no edits. - **defect** — `unknown_step_id`, `unknown_output_name`, `missing_dependency`, `self_reference`, `unknown_context_field`, `unknown_const_name`. Reported by default, now at warning level. - **runtime_only** — `namespace_unavailable`, `unknown_env_binding`. Kept out of the default output; `--show-unresolved` prints them. `noticeBuiltinContext` is deliberately **not** extended to cover all 22 keys. That would silence the symptom while duplicating the runtime list in `internal/runtime/eval.go`, so every new context key would reintroduce the bug. ## Two reasons that had no code `bindingEnvValue` and the `consts` branch of `bindingMapValue` returned bare `fmt.Errorf`, so their notices arrived with an empty reason and could not be classified. They now report `unknown_env_binding` and `unknown_const_name`. The split matters: a const is declared in the spec, so an unknown one can never resolve and is a defect. A param is not, and neither is an environment variable. Verified rather than assumed: ``` $ dagu start undeclared-param.yaml -- UNDECLARED=supplied value=[supplied] ``` so `params` stays runtime-only. ## Unrelated false positive fixed alongside A step's `with:` was resolved against the DAG-level env scope, so referencing the step's own `env:` was reported as unresolved. `reportSingleStepEnvValueReferenceNotices` already built the step scope and threw it away; it is now returned and threaded into the field walk via a new `ReferenceField.OwnerStepPath`. ## Verification ``` $ dagu validate defects.yaml level=WARN ${steps.producer.outputs.undeclared} ... the referenced output name is not declared level=WARN ${context.paths.typo_dir} ... unknown context field # ${context.paths.artifacts_dir} and ${env.OPERATOR_SUPPLIED}: silent $ dagu validate --show-unresolved defects.yaml # ... plus both runtime-only references at INFO $ dagu validate dbt-nightly.yaml # the workflow that was deleted $ dagu example 12 > ex.yaml && dagu validate ex.yaml # both clean ``` Green: `make lint` (0 issues, both GOOS), and `internal/cmn/value`, `internal/core`, `internal/core/spec`, `internal/cmd`, `internal/service/frontend/api/v1`, plus the `spec007` and `spec017` conformance packages. Note the defect subtests in `spec007` passed untouched; only the two `namespace_unavailable` cases needed `--show-unresolved`, which is a good sign the split lands where intended. ## Notes for review - `api/v1/api.gen.go` is hand-edited (13 lines) rather than regenerated. `go.mod` pins oapi-codegen v2.7.1 but the checked-in file was produced by v2.5.1, so a real regeneration produces a 12,298-line diff unrelated to this change. That drift is pre-existing and worth a separate PR. - `make api` cannot run on main at all: `api-validate` fails with `schema "DAG": extra sibling fields: [description]`. Confirmed present before this change. - `class` is an optional API field and the UI falls back to deriving it from `reason`, so an older server keeps working. --- ## Summary by cubic Make `dagu validate` separate real spec defects from values that only exist during a run. Adds context-aware classification, warns on defects by default, and hides runtime-only references unless you pass `--show-unresolved`. - **New Features** - Classified notices: `defect` vs `runtime_only`, with context-aware handling (step-output refs in fields without lookup scope are defects; runtime context misses stay runtime-only). - New flag `--show-unresolved` to print runtime-only notices; defects log at warn, runtime-only at info. - API: added optional `ValueReferenceNotice.class` and reasons `unknown_env_binding` and `unknown_const_name`; responses include the computed class. UI groups notices into “Needs a fix” vs “Resolved during a run,” adds a label for `unknown_const_name`, and classifies old responses correctly (treats `${steps.*}` `namespace_unavailable` as defects), with tests. - **Bug Fixes** - Step fields resolve against the step’s own `env:` (including `foreach` bodies and handlers), removing false positives. - Conformance and CLI tests updated to assert hidden-by-default behavior and `--show-unresolved` output. Written for commit a98306780a14657d875d6f0fe65ff3df85d95044. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added `--show-unresolved` to optionally display references resolved only during workflow execution. * Validation now distinguishes actionable defects from runtime-only unresolved references. * Inspection views categorize notices into “Needs a fix” and “Resolved during a run,” with clearer reason labels. * Added support for identifying unresolved environment bindings and constant names. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved environment scoping so step-level variables resolve correctly within the same step. * Unsupported context references are reported by default, while supported runtime context remains hidden unless requested.

author: nazt
body:
Fixes #709 (the "warn" half -- see below for what's scoped out).

`maw hey <session>` resolves a bare session to window index 0 with no check that anything agent-shaped is there. Caught live by m5: sending farewell/merge messages into a bash shell after the receiving window had been torn down into a viewer console -- `delivered`, exit 0, every time.

**Root bug this surfaced, caught by this fix's own test before it shipped:** `resolve_route_target` returns `session:windowINDEX`; `TmuxPane::target` (from `list_panes`) reports panes by window NAME. A naive string match between the two silently never finds anything. My first draft made exactly this mistake -- `serve_window_name_for_resolved_target` resolves the index against the session/window list before any pane lookup can work.

**What ships** (warn, not refuse -- the issue explicitly offered either, and a hard block risks breaking an intentional send to a shell):
- Same keyword + semver-command heuristic as #699/#690's `agents_is_agent_pane`, kept local since the two callers sit in different module trees
- Wired into both delivery paths: the receiving serve (`serve_deliver_local`, the exact shape m5 hit, cross-node) and the local CLI (`send_local_message_with_audit`)
- Warning threaded through `PeerSendWireResponse` -> `PeerSendResponse` so the cross-node CLI path prints it too, not just local
- Names exactly what was reached -- the issue's third ask ("delivered should name what it delivered to")

**Scoped out** (separate, larger asks from the same issue): resolving by name instead of index at all is a `maw-routing`/`maw-crates` change, outside this repo. Warning is not upgraded to a hard refusal.

Verified red-then-green on the index-vs-name gap specifically, plus a live false-positive check against a real agent pane on this machine.

author: pachaninm-lab
body:
## Проблема

`Production Hosting Authority` красная на `main` и падает на каждом PR, который задевает её trigger paths:

```
Production web hardening check failed:
- apps/web/app/api/health/ready/route.ts: missing "'Cache-Control': 'no-store, max-age=0'"
```

Заголовок при этом **присутствует и строже требуемого**:

| | |
|---|---|
| Проверка требует | `'Cache-Control': 'no-store, max-age=0'` |
| Роут отдаёт | `'Cache-Control': 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0'` |

Коммит `90e52a9e8` («Align robots policy with live SEO acceptance», 2026-07-26) **усилил** политику кэширования; литерал в `scripts/check-production-web-hardening.mjs` остался с `ed86674ae` и продолжал требовать прежнее, более слабое написание. Гейт падает ровно потому, что политику ужесточили.

Воспроизведено на чистом worktree `origin/main` (`b1d89f737`) — байт в байт тот же вывод. Дефект предсуществующий, не связан ни с удалением Netlify, ни с TAI, ни с зеркалированием образов PostgreSQL.

## Почему исправлен не литерал

Вернуть в проверку новое написание — значит «починить» гейт и **взвести ту же ловушку заново**: следующий коммит, ужесточающий заголовок, снова уронит сборку. Проверка должна утверждать свойство, а не орфографию.

Свойство: **readiness-проба не кэшируется нигде.** Связывающих директив две — `no-store` и `max-age=0`; обе остаются обязательными, порядок и наличие дополнительных — нет.

```js
requirePattern('route', [
  {
    pattern: /'Cache-Control':\s*'(?=[^']*\bno-store\b)(?=[^']*\bmax-age=0(?[\d.]))[^']*'/,
    describe: "a Cache-Control header carrying both 'no-store' and 'max-age=0'",
  },
]);
```

## Это не ослабление — проверено по кейсам

| Заголовок | Ожидание | Факт |
|---|---|---|
| `no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0` (текущий) | accept | accept |
| `no-store, max-age=0` (прежний литерал) | accept | accept |
| `max-age=0, no-store` (другой порядок) | accept | accept |
| `no-cache, max-age=0` — нет `no-store` | **reject** | reject |

author: jrhubott
body:
## Summary

Adds a **History card** — standalone, and openable as an overlay from the tile, root and decision cards (all three render the same `acp-history-view`, so the entry points cannot drift).

**Timeline** — one shared time axis with a hover readout across the whole stack:
- ACP target vs. recorded actual position, plus per-cover lines when an entry manages several (the aggregate mean hides a single stuck cover)
- a tilt track for venetian entries
- who-won bands from `decision_trace`, and control status from `control_status`
- HA-style labeled state bars: Integration, Automatic control, Sun in SAA, Glare, Manual override, Position mismatch
- night dimmed and sun-in-SAA spans highlighted behind the curves
- a stats line: moves, travel, manual-override time, time-per-handler

**Activity** — HA's logbook merged with ACP's command events, day-grouped with attribution. Neither source alone works: the logbook records the resulting state change but never the service arguments; the buffer records the commanded position but has no user attribution. Merged, an ACP move reads `cover.set_cover_position · position 45%`, a human move reads `Open — Jason`.

**Advanced** — the rolling diagnostic event buffer over `adaptive_cover_pro.get_diagnostics`, filterable, with a *Copy diagnostics* button. Each section maximizes to the full dialog.

## Design notes

- **`decision_trace`, not `control_status`, is the winning handler.** `control_status` is the integration's `ControlStatus` enum (`const.py` §23) — a different question. An early draft read the wrong one, which collapsed every band to the generic "Auto" badge since no status value is a handler name. The harness mock had the same assumption baked in and hid it; both are fixed, and the mock now gives the two sensors genuinely different values.
- **Bands are HTML, not SVG.** `preserveAspectRatio="none"` stretches glyphs horizontally, so in-band state labels were only possible outside SVG.
- **Logbook attribution resolves through `person.*` entities.** HA's own frontend reads the admin-only user list, so a non-admin viewer gets a nameless avatar; `person.user_id` is readable by everyone and needs no extra round-trip.
- **Frames.** Position and tilt normalize independently (`inverse_state` / `inverse_tilt`, #234 / #236); `linear_position` is already logical and is never re-inverted.
- **`mdi:chart-box`** — verified from `homeassistant/components/history/__init__.py`, not guessed.

## Also in scope

Tile editor: `cover` no longer pre-fills for single-cover entries — it pinned an `entity_id` discovery already resolves, against CLAUDE.md's "entity binding goes through discovery" rule, and it contradicted the editor's own "leave blank" hint. The picker is hidden unless the entry manages more than one cover or a value is already configured.

## Testing

- ✅ `npm run test` — **1724 passing** (149 new), 67 files
- ✅ `npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit`, reproducible `dist/`
- ✅ Built and loaded against a live HA config entry across nine deploy iterations
- Harness: History tab, five scenarios (`history-card`, `history-no-diagnostics`, `history-empty-buffer`, `history-multi-cover`, `history-venetian-tilt`), plus mocked `logbook/get_events`, `get_diagnostics`, per-cover divergence and tilt series
- i18n: en/fr/de complete; new tests assert every History key resolves in all three locales and that placeholder tokens match

## Related Issues

Refs #245

author: chriswong6031-creator
body:
Batch D of the red-on-arrival sweep — A: #3791, B: #3798, C: #3799, all merged. This one is rebased straight onto `main`, so the diff is a single commit.

## Two suites arrived strictly-dark in one day

Re-running `scripts/audit_unrun_tests.py` after the three fix batches turned up a **strictly-dark** suite — unrun and, per the auditor, untriggerable. Re-running it one batch later turned up a **second**. Both landed today, hours apart, named by no workflow:

| PR | suite | what it guards |
|---|---|---|
| #3776 | `tests/test_signup_email_validation.py` | the public account-creation email gate — pins the format validator **and** that the check runs *before* `sb.auth.signUp(` |
| #3797 | `tests/test_gh_quota_guard.py` (36 tests) | the shared-GitHub-quota hook — itself written because two watchers on one endpoint drained the 5,000/hr REST pool to zero and 403'd every session |

The first is the **highest-risk shape the census tracks**: a security-adjacent guard on the signup path, run by nothing. Both pass, so nothing would ever have complained.

#3636 emptied the strictly-dark set; #3645 emptied it again the same day. **Two more arriving in a single day** is the strongest available evidence that this is a *standing leak*, not a backlog to be drained once. The count is a snapshot, not a state — re-run the auditor rather than trusting any number written down, including the ones in this PR.

Strictly dark is back to **0**.

## A fourth measurement trap — this one produces false positives

The three traps already in the census doc all cause **under**-counting. This one runs the other way, and both suites here are instances of it:

> `audit_unrun_tests.py` derives a suite's subjects from its **imports** — and *neither* of these suites imports its subject. `test_signup_email_validation` reads `templates/onboard.js` as **text** and regexes it; `test_gh_quota_guard` invokes `.claude/hooks/gh_quota_guard.py` as a **subprocess**. So the auditor reports `subjects: []` and labels both untriggerable, when `templates/**` and `.claude/**` already match their subjects.

Only the **unrun** half of each verdict was real. Guards that reach their subject by path string or subprocess are a blind spot in the auditor, not a dark corner of `ci.yml`. **Check how a suite reaches its subject before believing a dark verdict.** Recorded in the doc.

## Wiring

New `unrun-dark-guards` lane. **Every half** pinned in `ci.yml` `paths` per #3488 — both suites *and* the two files they inspect — so neither a guard nor its subject can drift out of coverage. Neither needs third-party deps, but the lane repeats the shared install byte-for-byte so `run_ci_pack.py` keeps one venv rather than building a second for 38 tests.

## Verification

- 38 tests green; `run_ci_pack.py --validate-only` green (**133 jobs**); `check_workflow_yaml` green
- `audit_unrun_tests.py`: strictly dark **1 → 0**, unrun 858 → 857

author: rileytheriler
body:
🚨 Severity: MEDIUM

💡 Vulnerability: The `/api/login` endpoint was vulnerable to user enumeration via timing attacks. If a user was not found, the endpoint returned early. The expensive `check_password_hash` computation was only executed when a user existed. An attacker could use the time difference to enumerate valid usernames.

🎯 Impact: Attackers could automate requests to determine which users exist on the system, which is a prerequisite for targeted credential stuffing or brute-force attacks.

🔧 Fix: Implemented a dummy `check_password_hash` check when a user is not found using a perfectly valid `scrypt` hash (`scrypt:32768:8:1$5Bxpg4JHLUZVBGkq$1c0a5b635e1cd6c97e176d9e39783f48a8da0804a9f59d9e240c1cdd3e1544157ca5ace162677fe15517c9ac731232178f17bb1d9d75d4c8a3b36928b7b01582`). This forces the server to incur a delay computationally indistinguishable from an actual password check. I also cleaned up syntactically broken code in `backend/app/routes/community.py` caused by earlier duplicate merge conflicts, and fixed a logical error where `audio_file.save` executed *after* a `finally` block that deleted the source file, which would have leaked raw files to disk.

✅ Verification: 
- `pytest backend/tests/` was run to ensure no regressions were introduced to the backend (with known baseline issues acknowledged).
- Scrutinized the `scrypt` dummy hash structure in `test_hash.py` (since deleted) to ensure it executes `check_password_hash` without erroring out to normalize latency times.

author: ferraroroberto
body:
## Summary

The Board reported "chief: not running" next to a live, working chief because `label="chief"` was only ever applied by `ensure_chief`'s own spawn path. A chief started any other way — a manually typed `/chief` in the Coding tab, or (the case actually observed live) a session-host restart killing the PTY and Roberto reattaching the same underlying Claude Code conversation via Resume — stayed unlabelled forever. That silently broke `chief_ops.py`'s `chief-sid` lookup (fleet-config#443's escalation routing went dead) and the worker-cap count (an unlabelled chief consumed one of its own dispatch slots).

`_reconcile_chief_label` (`app/webapp/routers/board.py`) self-heals `label` read-time from either of two independent, narrow signals, either sufficient on its own:

- **`prompt_title`** (#266) — the session-host's own capture of a PTY's first *submitted* line. Exact for a freshly typed `/chief`.
- **`shared_name`** (fleet-config#302) — Claude Code's own persisted *conversation* identity, joined from the hook state file via the same agent-aware claim walk every other cross-tab title uses.

**Why both, and why the distinction matters:** my first attempt at this fix used only `prompt_title` and shipped with a fully green gate and full test coverage — and still didn't fix the reported bug. The actual observed case is a Resume into a *new* PTY after a session-host restart: the underlying Claude Code conversation continues, but the PTY's own "first submitted line" is whatever the human types next (a status check, a question — anything but `/chief`, since the conversation is already past that point). `prompt_title` is a **process**-identity signal; it cannot see past a Resume. `shared_name` is a **conversation**-identity signal — it belongs to the transcript, not whichever PTY is currently attached to it, so it survives the Resume. Reach for `shared_name` first if you're ever debugging a "chief looks unlabelled" report again; `prompt_title` alone will look right in tests and still miss the live case.

Both signals are scoped to a live PTY cwd'd in the fleet-config checkout — a directory name alone proves nothing, which is exactly why the **pre-existing `name == "chief"` fallback in `_find_chief` was already dead** and never caught this: `name` is the *launcher's* session name, which is the project name (`"fleet-config"`) for a Resume-launched session, never `"chief"`. A fallback that never fires is worse than no fallback — it reads as coverage in review but provides none. Left in place (still correct for its narrow original case — a legacy session-host that predates the `label` field) but now documented as dead for this scenario, in `docs/board.md`.

**Validated against the live failing session, not only synthetic tests** — re-confirmed after the fix:
- Board card for session `1c8e6dde84c441299c2dbe11068a262d`: `label: "chief"` ✅
- `chief_ops.py chief-sid` → `CHIEF_SID=1c8e6dde84c441299c2dbe11068a262d` (exact match) ✅

Also adds an explicit **Restart** control next to Start on the Board's chief row (shown/hidden by actual alive state), wired to `ensure_chief`'s existing `fresh=true` graceful stop-then-respawn — letting the fleet-config#442 handover log carry context forward. Never touches the session-host (`:8446`), which would kill every other PTY.

A residual piece of the "unlabelled chief" acceptance criterion — a log breadcrumb in fleet-config's `notify_on_idle.py` for the case where chief-routing silently falls back to Slack — lives outside this repo's reach: filed as `ferraroroberto/fleet-config#456`.

## Changes

- `app/webapp/routers/board.py` — `_reconcile_chief_label`/`_reconcile_chief_labels`/`_live_sessions_with_chief_label`; wired into `get_board` and `ensure_chief`.
- `app/webapp/static/{board.js,dom-utils.js,index.html,state.js}` — explicit Restart control.
- `tests/test_chief_ensure.py` — unit coverage for both healing signals plus an integration test reproducing the live Resume scenario exactly (`test_alive_chief_via_resumed_shared_name_is_kept`).
- `tests/e2e/test_board_chief.py` — Restart-button e2e coverage.
- `README.md`, `docs/board.md` — documented the fourth chief-lifecycle trigger (Resume), the self-heal mechanism, the dead fallback, and the Restart control.

## Validation

- `scripts/verify-before-ship.ps1`: green — byte-compile, 1298 non-e2e tests, full dual-projection e2e suite (383 passed, 17 skipped).
- UX-conformance gate (`ux_surface.py`): `TOUCHED=yes` — no new CSS tokens (Restart reuses the existing `.board-chief-start` class); visual check via the `verify` skill against both light and dark themes — Restart renders identically to Start's existing style/placement, nav pill and palette conform, no layout break.
- Live-verified against the real failing session (see above) — CI not awaited, local e2e + pytest green this session.

Closes #617

author: g10g11g12
body:
Closes the last open item from the HANDOFF.md accessibility section, which flagged contrast as **unchecked**.

## Method

A Playwright sweep over 12 routes × light/dark. For every visible element that owns text, it resolves the true background by climbing ancestors, then applies the AA thresholds (4.5:1 normal; 3:1 for large ≥24px or ≥18.66px bold). Two details mattered:

- **Colors are rasterized through a canvas.** Tailwind v4 emits `oklch()`, which `getComputedStyle` returns verbatim — regex parsing silently fails and falls through to a white default, which produces a page full of bogus "ratio 1.0" results. My first two runs were exactly that; the canvas approach measures what actually paints.
- **Gradient-backed nodes are skipped**, not measured against a distant ancestor — that was reporting the Compare "VS" badge as a 1.05 failure when it's fine.

## Findings and fixes

| Finding | Measured | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `text-slate-400` metadata on light surfaces | 2.5–2.63 | → `slate-500`; `slate-600` on slate-100 chips (4.35) |
| `dark:text-zinc-500` throughout dark mode | 4.12 | → `zinc-400` |
| AccessBadge E/C/F glyphs (`-500` fill, tinted text) | 2.35 | deeper fills, pure white |
| Star rating "4.8/5" — **worst in the app** | 2.04 | → `amber-700`; glyphs `amber-600` (3:1 non-text) |
| White-on-emerald CTAs | 2.47 / 3.65 | → `emerald-700` (5.5:1) |
| Comms own-message bubble + `opacity-70` metadata | 2.53 | → `emerald-700`, `opacity-90` |
| Notification/nav count badges | 3.65–3.81 | → `red-600` / `emerald-700` |

229 token occurrences swept across 41 files, plus targeted component work.

## One judgment call worth your review

**The action green is now `emerald-700` everywhere** — button fills and link text alike. Previously three shades (500/600/700) were doing the same job, and neither 500 (2.47) nor 600 (3.65) clears AA for the small text that sits on them.

This is a deliberate, visible brand shift — two steps deeper. I screenshot-checked Square, Substance, and Library in both themes before keeping it; it reads as a rich intentional green rather than washed out. **If you prefer the lighter green**, the accessible alternative is keeping `emerald-500` only behind text ≥18.66px bold — say the word and I'll rework it that way.

## Verification

- Contrast sweep: **0 failures** (from 100+).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean · `npm run lint` **0 errors** · `vitest` **67/67** · smoke **15/15** · `npm run build` clean.

Note: the sweep script is intentionally not committed — it's a one-shot instrument, not a test. Its method is documented in HANDOFF.md so it can be reconstructed if the palette changes.

Also worth knowing: Vercel's free-tier daily deploy cap was hit yesterday (~10:30 UTC), so the preview check on this PR may fail or be absent. GitHub Actions `build` is the real gate.

author: dniminenn
body:
Runs sharkfin in a Chromium browser over WebHID, at app.getsharkfin.com.

`app/src-web` is a wasm crate that includes `protocol.rs` and `registry.rs`
from `src-tauri` **by path** rather than copying them, so the wire format
cannot drift between the two builds. It replaces only the two things that
are platform-specific: the hidapi transport becomes WebHID, and the Tauri
command layer becomes wasm-bindgen exports. Pacing and the flash cooldowns
are ported with their values and reasoning intact, and live in the core
because a browser has no backend to put them behind.

The frontend is unchanged. Every Tauri call already went through one file,
so the web build aliases `@/lib/backend` to `src/web/backend.ts` and shims
the two plugins (file dialogs become a download and a file picker, the
opener becomes `window.open`). The only added UI is a connect button, since
WebHID needs a user gesture before a page may see the device.

Chrome hands the page only the vendor collection (usage page `0xFFFF`,
usage 2) and withholds the keyboard's own collections, so the page cannot
see keystrokes.

Verified on an Attack Shark X86 (Chrome 149, Linux): identify, profile,
settings, both keymap layers, macro read, and a lighting write round-trip
that was read back and restored.

author: gsapify
body:
## What

`fingerprint/chromaprint.py:14-29` builds a genuinely correct, locality-preserving
spectral-band bitstring, then line 29 throws that structure away by returning
`hashlib.sha256(bitstring.encode()).hexdigest()`. `similarity()` (`:32-36`) then
compares hex digests character-by-character, which is meaningless: SHA-256 is
designed so a single flipped input bit randomizes the entire output.

**Fix:** return `bitstring` directly instead of its digest. One line, plus
dropping the now-unused `hashlib` import.

## Why it matters

Before the fix, `similarity()` only worked on byte-identical input. Any
near-duplicate — a re-encode, a clip starting at a different offset, a mic
recording of the same source — collapsed straight from 1.0 to the random
floor. There was no graded similarity at all.

Measured on a 3-second two-tone reference (envelope + noise floor, not a pure
tone) with the fix applied:

| Perturbation      | Similarity |
|--------------------|-----------:|
| +0.5% gain         | 1.000      |
| 1-sample shift     | 0.977      |
| 20ms trimmed       | 0.908      |
| mild noise         | 0.968      |
| unrelated audio    | 0.525      |

All perturbations land well above unrelated audio, which is the property the
SHA-256 digest destroyed. These numbers are pinned in a new regression test.

## Persistence check

`AudioFingerprinter`/`AudioDeduplicator` are only referenced within
`fingerprint/dedup.py`. `AudioDeduplicator` keeps fingerprints in an in-memory
dict (`self._hashes`) that is never serialized to disk or a DB, so there is no
stored fingerprint format to migrate. The returned string also stops being a
fixed 64-char hex digest (length now depends on audio duration/frame count) —
worth flagging in case any future caller assumed a fixed-length hash.

## Scope

`fingerprint/shazam_like.py` and `fingerprint/matcher.py` (the constellation
matcher) are a separate, sound implementation and untouched by this change.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/fingerprint/` — 16 passed
- [x] Full suite: `pytest -o addopts="" -p no:warnings --tb=short` — 1668 passed (baseline 1667 + 1 new test)

author: hiosdra
body:
## Summary

Swaps the Miniflux REST client for a FreshRSS client speaking the Google Reader compatible API that FreshRSS exposes at `/api/greader.php`. Cloudflare Access authentication is dropped, as requested.

FreshRSS does not implement the Miniflux API, so the whole `data/remote` layer was rewritten rather than re-pointed.

## Endpoint mapping

| Previous Miniflux call | FreshRSS replacement |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/entries` | `GET /reader/api/0/stream/contents/user/-/state/com.google/reading-list` with `xt` (exclude read) and `r=o` |
| `GET /v1/entries?changed_after=` | same, with `ot=<unix seconds>` |
| `GET /v1/feeds` | `GET /reader/api/0/subscription/list` |
| `GET /v1/feeds/counters` | `GET /reader/api/0/unread-count` |
| `POST /v1/feeds` | `POST /reader/api/0/subscription/quickadd` |
| `PUT /v1/entries` | `POST /reader/api/0/edit-tag` with `a`/`r` = `user/-/state/com.google/read` |
| `GET /v1/entries/{id}/fetch-content` | local readability extraction from the article URL, falling back to the feed content already stored |
| `POST /v1/discover` | local `<link rel="alternate">` discovery with Jsoup |

## Notable changes

- **Authentication** — `GoogleReaderAuthenticator` performs `ClientLogin` and caches the token; `GoogleReaderAuthInterceptor` adds `Authorization: GoogleLogin auth=…` and retries once after invalidating the token on a 401. The cache is keyed by a credentials fingerprint, so editing credentials forces a re-login.
- **Runtime server address** — Retrofit is pinned to a placeholder host and `FreshRssUrlInterceptor` rewrites each request onto the configured server. This keeps Retrofit/OkHttp as Koin singletons while the address stays editable at runtime. Requests to other hosts (OpenRouter, article scraping) pass through untouched — previously the auth interceptor attached backend credentials to OpenRouter calls too.
- **Pagination** — the Google Reader API has no offset, so `ArticleRepository.refreshArticles` now follows `continuation` tokens.
- **Feed metadata** — stream items only carry `origin.streamId`, with no feed URL, so the subscription list is merged over the entry-derived feeds during sync.
- **Reading time** — not provided by the Google Reader API; estimated from the content word count so the reader chip keeps working.

## Configuration

Server address, username and API password moved out of `BuildConfig` into `PreferencesManager`:

- New **FreshRSS Server** section in Settings with a *Test connection* button.
- A setup screen is shown on first launch when no credentials are stored, and is skipped afterwards.
- Default address is `https://rss.hiosdra.com`; the API password comes from FreshRSS under *Profile → API management*.

The hardcoded Miniflux API key and Cloudflare Access client secret were removed from `app/build.gradle.kts`. **They should be treated as leaked and revoked** — they are still in the git history.

## Removed

`docs/API Reference.html` (a saved copy of the Miniflux API docs) is deleted, as it no longer describes the backend this app talks to.

## Testing

- `./gradlew lint test assembleDebug` — all green.
- 17 new unit tests: `StreamContentsMappingTest` (item ID hex decoding, read-state mapping, timestamp formatting, enclosure and continuation handling) and `FreshRssServerConfigTest` (base URL normalisation, subdirectory installs, credential fingerprinting).
- Not exercised against a live FreshRSS instance — the request/response shapes were verified against the FreshRSS `greader.php` and `Entry::toGReader()` sources.

author: chaowao
body:
## Summary

`docs/` is written almost entirely for people changing simpler's internals. Classified by use, roughly **18 of the 46 pages** under `docs/` and `docs/dfx/` serve someone *building on* simpler and **28** serve someone *modifying* it — and the user-serving pages are all reference material, with no task-oriented layer above them.

There was also **no API reference of any kind**. The repo has no doc generator (no sphinx/mkdocs/doxygen), and `simpler.__all__` exports only the logging helpers, so even the entry point — `from simpler.worker import Worker` — was undocumented anywhere.

This PR adds `docs/user/`, routed by the reader's task rather than by subsystem:

| Page | Covers |
| ---- | ------ |
| `user/README.md` | install → prove the setup works → write a kernel → multiple chips → profile → debug |
| `how-to/write-and-run-a-kernel.md` | the `@scene_test` path and the direct `Worker` path side by side |
| `how-to/profile-a-kernel.md` | question→flag table over the existing `dfx/` references, and which CLI reads which artifact |
| `how-to/run-on-multiple-chips.md` | L3 lifecycle, communication domains, and the real scope limits |
| `how-to/debug-a-failed-run.md` | classify the symptom before theorizing; getting a private device log |
| `reference/python-api.md`, `reference/cli.md` | the API surface and the flags/tools, hand-maintained |

## Design choices worth reviewing

**It links the examples instead of duplicating them.** `examples/workers/**/README.md` is already the tutorial layer, and `hello_worker/README.md` is genuinely good ("what it does" / "why each line matters" / expected output). The user pages route there rather than re-teaching, per `doc-consistency.md` §2.

**The reference is hand-written, not generated.** Docstring coverage on the user API is **54% (`worker.py`) / 57% (`task_interface.py`)**, so a generated reference would be mostly holes today. Raising docstring coverage and then adding a generator is the better sequencing, and is not attempted here.

**The `simpler` / `simpler_setup` boundary is documented as it actually is.** `.claude/rules/project-layout.md` calls `simpler` the "stable user API" and `simpler_setup` an internal test framework, but the examples import `simpler_setup` *more* than `simpler` (`KernelCompiler` ×15, `pto_isa` ×15, `torch_interop` ×11, `SceneTestCase` group ×7) — you cannot compile a kernel without it. The user pages say so plainly. **Aligning the packages themselves is a code change and is deliberately not in this documentation-only PR**; happy to follow up if maintainers want `python/simpler/__init__.py` to export the real surface.

## Every fact was read from the source

Not recalled. Three cases where checking changed the text:

- `Worker.__init__(self, level, **config)` — only `level` is declared; the reference lists the 9 keys actually read from `**config`.
- `ArgDirection` has **four** values (`SCALAR`, `IN`, `OUT`, `INOUT`) — an earlier draft said two.
- `Orchestrator.malloc(worker_id, size)` takes its arguments in the **opposite order** to `Worker.malloc(size, worker_id=0)`. Documented explicitly as a footgun.

## Testing

Documentation only (`.md`); no code, build, or config files changed, so the sim/hardware suites do not apply per the git-commit skill's test matrix.

- [x] `markdownlint-cli2` clean on all 9 touched files, using **v0.20.0** — the version `.pre-commit-config.yaml:83` pins, i.e. what CI runs
- [x] Repo-wide relative-link validation: **no new broken links** (5 pre-existing remain, all in files this PR does not touch)
- [x] All 23 API names cited in the new pages verified to exist in `python/`, `simpler_setup/`, or `src/common/task_interface/`
- [ ] Simulation tests — not applicable (no code changed)
- [ ] Hardware tests — not applicable (no code changed)

author: tktonny
body:
## Problem
Talk-over never fired — even when the debug HUD showed mic peaks clearing the floor, the barge-in count stayed 0 and Aria was never interrupted.

## Root cause
The barge-in energy VAD required **700ms of *continuous* ≥0.06 RMS** and **hard-reset** its pre-speech accumulator on any single sub-threshold frame. Real speech dips between syllables, so the accumulator was zeroed every gap and the confirmation window was never reached — barge-in was effectively dead. (Arming is fine: `assistantOwnsAudio` spans response-created → playback-drain, and the mic un-mutes on Aria's first audio delta.)

## Fix
- Add an opt-in **leaky accumulator** to `energyVad` (`leakyStart`): a sub-threshold frame *decays* the accumulator by one frame instead of zeroing it, so genuine gappy speech still reaches the window while transient echo blips decay away. Ordinary turn VAD is unchanged (`leakyStart` off).
- Lower the barge-in defaults **0.06 → 0.04** and **700ms → 300ms**.
- The start-of-utterance **grace window (900ms)** still eats the loudest echo onset, and every knob stays env-tunable (`EXPO_PUBLIC_BARGEIN_*`) so a bad-AEC room can raise the floor back up.

Mirror `tsc --noEmit` clean. Verify on-device via the debug HUD: speak over Aria and watch `b` increment / Aria pause.

body:
## Summary

- add the authenticated local `/recording` workspace with Nuxt UI `UFileUpload`
- stream server-advertised parts with receipt-confirmed progress, pause, retry, abort, and explicit ephemeral/retained selection
- persist only an opaque upload ID and require complete hash-verified file re-selection after refresh
- continuously enforce server-owned media expiry with a lifecycle-owned Nitro janitor
- disclose private local storage and the later Gemini Files transfer before staging
- keep the complete local UI/client/media implementation out of Cloudflare artifacts
- complete Conductor Task 3.5 and advance the active pointer to Task 3.6

## Privacy and architecture

- the selected browser `File` remains component-local and is never placed in SSR state, SQLite, cookies, or browser storage
- recording paths and names never cross the media API boundary
- session storage contains only the validated opaque media-session ID
- progress advances only from validated server receipts
- refresh-resume verifies a bounded-memory fingerprint over every ordered part before sending missing bytes
- every media mode has server-owned expiry independent of browser state
- startup reconciliation plus a non-overlapping one-minute sweep enforce expiry while Studio stays open
- expiry, write, seal, lifecycle transition, and delete share per-session ownership; busy sessions wait for the next sweep
- cleanup failures remain durable, are retried, and emit only sanitized code/count diagnostics
- dropping or selecting a file does not contact Gemini
- analysis execution remains intentionally deferred

## Verification

- `bun run check` — 65 CLI tests and 86 web tests passed; both production builds, local HTTP contract, and 32 MiB streaming probe passed
- `bun run test:e2e:ci` — 9 passed with no retries or flakes
- focused expiry/media suite — 28 passed
- `bun audit --production --audit-level=high` — no vulnerabilities
- Cloudflare boundary gate — 24 forbidden local markers absent
- tracked-file and staged-diff secret/media checks — clean
- three adversarial review rounds — no remaining BLOCKER or SHOULD_FIX findings

## Browser coverage

- production-built authenticated stage, seal, and delete of a synthetic MP4
- real 8 MiB confirmed-part receipt, refresh, reselect-required, complete hash verification, missing-part resume, seal, and delete
- actual drag/drop, keyboard selection, session denial/replay, temporary-key nonreflection, and mobile overflow
- unexpected browser console/page errors and flaky retries fail CI

## Scope

This PR completes Task 3.5 and hardens Task 3.4 retention enforcement. Task 3.6 (bounded local context-file ingestion) remains active. The Studio analysis composer and durable job execution remain later phases.

author: stormer78
body:
Closes the testability half of what OpenVTC/openvtc#185 needed. Additive; no signature changes.

## The problem

`resolve_vta_endpoint` builds its `DIDCacheClient` from the environment, so a consumer has **no way to point discovery at a fixture**: seeding a document into its own cache does nothing, because the function never sees that cache.

The practical effect is that *"does this VTA advertise `#tsp`"* — the question #765 and #810 made answerable — can still only be **asserted** against a live deployment. OpenVTC hit this covering its TSP-enablement path and had to leave the assertion unmade, with the wiring verified by construction rather than execution.

## This started as a MockVta fixture, which was the wrong layer

The obvious fix looked like "give `MockVta` a TSP-advertising variant". It cannot work: `preseed_did_docs` seeds the **VTA's own** resolver, and an external consumer resolves through its own. No fixture on the VTA side can reach a consumer's discovery call while that call constructs its resolver internally.

The blocker was never the fixture. It was the missing seam.

## The change

- **`resolve_vta_endpoint_with_resolver(vta_did, &DIDCacheClient)`** and **`provision_client::resolve_vta_with_resolver(...)`** run the same discovery over a caller-supplied resolver. The env-configured entry points delegate to them, so behaviour is unchanged and no caller has to move.
- Follows the pattern **`resolve_mediator_did_with_resolver` already set in the same module**, for the same two reasons: reuse (no second cache per resolve) and testability.
- `provision_client`'s two entry points now share one `flatten`, so they cannot disagree about what an endpoint shape means — the split that keeps "what is advertised" separate from "what we connected over".

## Tests — the assertions that were previously impossible

Four, seeding a document and asserting what discovery makes of it, in-process with no network:

- a dual `#tsp` + `#vta-didcomm` VTA (**the reference deployment's shape**) reports both, in preference order
- a DIDComm-only VTA reports no TSP
- a TSP-only VTA does **not** fall back to a REST URL synthesized from its own domain — the bug `resolve_vta_endpoint`'s own doc calls out, now covered
- a `#tsp` entry carrying a URL instead of a mediator DID is ignored rather than routed through

## Verification

- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --features session,client,didcomm,provision-client` — 462 + 16 + 78 + … all green, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` (CI's invocation) — clean
- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `scripts/check-version-bumps.sh` — `ok vta-sdk: 0.20.2 -> 0.20.3`
- `scripts/check-changelogs.sh` — `ok vta-sdk: 0.20.2 -> 0.20.3 (documented)`

## Two things flagged, not fixed

**Pre-existing clippy errors.** `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk --features session,client,didcomm,provision-client --all-targets` reports 3 errors (`didcomm_session.rs:673` "this loop never actually loops", and two others). **Same count on a clean `origin/main`**, none in files this change touches, and CI's own invocation is clean — so unrelated to this PR, but worth someone's attention since that feature combination is what consumers build with.

**A guard blind spot.** Both release guards resolve `$ROOT` via `pwd`, while `cargo metadata` reports the symlink-resolved path. On macOS, running from a worktree under `/tmp` (→ `/private/tmp`) makes the paths mismatch, every crate fails attribution, and both guards **pass vacuously** with "nothing to check". They behave correctly from the canonical path, and CI checks out normally so it is unaffected — but a guard that silently passes when it cannot attribute anything is worth hardening, given these exist precisely to catch what authors forget.

## Problem
On a device without Google Play Services (many Android emulators, some Huawei / China-ROM phones), "Register this phone" fails and showed the raw Java exception to the caregiver:

`Fetching the token failed: java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException: java.io.IOException: MISSING_INSTANCEID_SERVICE`

This is a **device limitation, not a build bug** — the FCM config is correct; the device just can't mint an FCM token.

## Fix
`getPushNotificationDeviceRegistration` now maps the known GMS-missing errors (`MISSING_INSTANCEID_SERVICE` / `SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE` / play-services) to a plain, reassuring line:

> This device doesn't have Google Play Services, so push can't be enabled here. Your alerts still appear in the Notifications tab.

No behaviour change otherwise — alerts already land in the Notifications tab regardless of push registration. Production Singapore phones have GMS, so push works there; this only improves the message on GMS-less devices.
