body:
## 📌 개요
RN 앱 2바퀴 — 홈 목록에서 카드를 누르면 열리는 **상품 상세 화면**을 구현합니다. 그 과정에서 웹·앱이 같은 공유 패키지(`@cuddle/shared`)를 보도록 모노레포 배관을 뚫고, 실기기 확인을 거치며 웹·앱 디자인을 하나로 정렬했습니다. 상세는 이번 바퀴에서 **읽기 전용**입니다(찜·채팅은 로그인 루프에서).

## 🔧 작업 내용

### 모노레포 배관 + 공유 로직 (`@cuddle/shared`)
- 웹이 `@cuddle/shared`를 참조하도록 배관(`transpilePackages`, tsconfig exclude 조정)
- `formatPrice` 시맨틱을 '숫자만'으로 통일하고 웹은 재수출 껍데기로 전환(호출부 무변경)
- 상대시간·상품 라벨·펫 라벨·거래상태 순수 로직을 shared로 이관, 앱 중복 함수 제거
- 상세 응답 타입(`ProductDetailItem`) 정의, `fetchProductDetail`(404 → `ProductNotFoundError` 구분)

### 상품 상세 화면 (앱)
- 홈 탭 안에 스택을 중첩(`(home)` 라우트 그룹)해 **상세로 이동해도 하단 탭바 유지**
- safe area 고려한 자체 헤더(네이티브 스택 헤더는 상단 인셋 옵션이 없어 직접 구현)
- 브레드크럼 · 이미지 캐러셀 · 요약 · 판매자 카드 · 로딩/오류/404 상태
- TanStack Query 단건 조회 + 목록 캐시 placeholder(`isPlaceholderData`)

### 웹·앱 디자인 정렬 (실기기 확인 반영)
- 판매/판매요청 뱃지를 알약으로 통일하고 웹 뱃지 색을 `badge-*` **디자인 토큰으로 승격**
- 강조색 정리: 가격은 제목과 같은 검정, 브레드크럼·링크는 브랜드 브라운(#633F00)
- **접근성**: 안 읽히던 골드(#E2A958, 대비 2.09) 강조 텍스트를 대비 통과 색으로 교체
- 조회·찜을 아이콘 대신 글자로("아이콘은 누를 수 있는 것에만")
- 판매자 아바타를 회색 → 디자인 시스템 크림(`primary-50`)
- 홈 카드 상품명 크기·여백, 찜 버튼 위치 등 미세 조정

## 📎 관련 이슈
- 계획 문서 기반 작업(연결 이슈 없음). 설계: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-rn-product-detail-design.md`, 계획: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-23-rn-product-detail-impl.md`

## 💬 리뷰어 참고 사항
- **웹 무손상**: 웹 관련 변경마다 `pnpm build` 게이트 통과. shared 타입이 웹 타입체크 대상임을 마커로 검증.
- **웹 `Product.isFavorite`는 여전히 `boolean`**(shared는 실측대로 `boolean|null`) — 두 타입이 분리돼 있어 이번엔 안 건드림. **다음 바퀴 정리 대상.**

This PR integrates `RPG` (Generating Long Semantic IDs in Parallel for
Recommendation) into `cornac`. `RPG` scales up to 16-64 unordered codes for Semantic IDs (`TIGER` uses 4 hierarchical codes).

### Key changes

author: wolfganggross
body:
## What this is

A small authoring convenience: note and hub pages get an **Edit locally** button that opens the underlying `.mdx` in whatever app the OS has registered for the type. Spot a typo while reading the rendered page, click, fix — no hunting for the filename.

This code was already sitting uncommitted in the working tree. The 2026-07-27 `/ingest` run deliberately left it out of its own commit and filed `tasks/2026-07-27-uncommitted-edit-in-editor-feature.md` to decide what to do with it. This PR is that decision, put up for review rather than pushed straight to `main` with the notebook content.

## Why it is safe to deploy

Gated in both halves, independently:

| Half | Gate |
|---|---|
| `app/api/open-in-editor/route.ts` | returns 404 unless `NODE_ENV === 'development'` |
| `components/edit-in-editor-button.tsx` | returns `null` under the same check — and `NODE_ENV` is inlined at build time, so the button is absent from the production bundle entirely |

Vercel builds preview deployments with `NODE_ENV=production` as well as production ones, so neither half is reachable on any deployed target. The route still appears in build output as `ƒ /api/open-in-editor` because it is dynamic — that is the 404 responder, not a live endpoint.

Path handling, for the dev case: the request path is validated against the same per-segment slug regex `velite.config.ts` uses, the candidate is joined onto `content/`, and the resolved file must still start with `CONTENT_ROOT + path.sep` before anything is opened. Only `.mdx` and `.md` are tried.

## A correction carried in this PR

The task file's first version — written by the ingest agent and already on `main` — claimed this feature *"becomes a live production endpoint if pushed"* and framed it as a security question. **That was wrong.** It was written without reading the route. The task file is rewritten here to say so and to scope down to what is actually left.

## What is actually left, and is not fixed here

The one real issue is the only warning `npm run build` emits:

```
Turbopack build encountered 1 warnings:
./next.config.mjs
Encountered unexpected file in NFT list — the whole project was traced unintentionally
Import trace: App Route: ./next.config.mjs → ./app/api/open-in-editor/route.ts
```

The likely cause is the module-scope `path.join(process.cwd(), 'content')` on line 13 — the warning text names exactly that pattern as the trigger, after which tracing can't bound the file set and the deployed function bundle inflates.

**Left unfixed deliberately**, so this diff stays the original author's work rather than an agent's rewrite of it. The rewritten task now scopes it narrowly with two candidate fixes (move the computation into the handler, or mark it `/*turbopackIgnore: true*/`). Happy to do it in this PR if preferred.

## Verification

- `npm run build` passes; static generation unchanged at 9 pages; the warning above is the only one.
- No content, schema or `lib/` changes — nothing here touches the wiki or its build contract.

## Reviewer note

`main` moved during this session (the `/ingest` commit `f4f8625`, plus concurrent content edits). This branch touches only `app/`, `components/` and one task file, so it does not overlap with any of that.

## What broke

North West Leicestershire's ModGov endpoint (`minutes-1.nwleics.gov.uk`) is now HTTPS-only. The `base_url` in `metadata.json` still used `http://`, causing Lambda to time out — the server silently drops HTTP connections rather than redirecting. This was confirmed by the error in the failing feed: `is_timeout error: … uri: http://minutes-1.nwleics.gov.uk/mgWebService.asmx/GetCouncillorsByWard, source: TimedOut`.

The HTTPS endpoint (`https://minutes-1.nwleics.gov.uk/mgWebService.asmx/GetCouncillorsByWard`) returns HTTP 200 with valid councillor XML (confirmed via curl).

A previous PR (#369) containing this fix was closed on 2026-06-26 without merging. The scraper has continued to fail since then with the same HTTP timeout.

## What was fixed

- `metadata.json`: changed `base_url` from `http://minutes-1.nwleics.gov.uk` to `https://minutes-1.nwleics.gov.uk`

## Scrape results

Confirmed via direct HTTPS fetch of the ModGov XML endpoint:

| Metric | Count |
|--------|-------|
| Councillors found | 38 |
| With email address | 0 |
| With photo | 38 |

Note: emails are not published in the NWL ModGov XML (the `<email>` field is empty for all councillors). All 38 councillors have photo URLs. This is consistent with the council's own privacy settings rather than a scraper issue.

author: tanakakao
body:
## Summary

- disable MLP internal early stopping only when the MLP is used as a bagging base estimator
- keep early stopping enabled for standalone MLP models and other ensemble types
- preserve the caller-provided `base_model_params` without mutating it
- add regression tests for the bagging-specific behavior

## Root cause

The default MLP configuration uses `early_stopping=True`. In recent scikit-learn versions, `BaggingRegressor` passes bootstrap sample counts to base estimators through `sample_weight`. MLP then splits those weighted rows into an internal validation set for early stopping. For some bootstrap samples, every row selected for that validation set has weight zero, and the validation R² calculation raises:

`ValueError: Sample weights must contain at least one non-zero number.`

## Fix

A dedicated bagging base-estimator builder creates the requested model and disables `early_stopping` only for `MLPRegressor` and `MLPClassifier`. This avoids the invalid internal validation score while retaining the MLP defaults for standalone use.

## Validation

- focused predictor-pipeline tests: 3 passed
- smoke-fitted a bagged MLP with the adjusted estimator
- confirmed the input parameter dictionary remains unchanged

# Commission: the-evidence/bert

## Subject and angle
Read **BERT** — Devlin, Chang, Lee & Toutanova, *"BERT: Pre-training of Deep
Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding"* (Google, arXiv:1810.04805,
Oct 2018; published NAACL 2019). This is a document the field cites to settle
arguments, which is exactly The Evidence's beat.

The angle: BERT is the paper that made "pre-train once, fine-tune per task" the
default, and its GLUE/SQuAD numbers are quoted as if they proved a machine
"understands language." Say what the document actually did — the masked-language-
model + next-sentence-prediction pre-training objective, the corpus, the parameter
counts, the exact benchmark deltas — and show the size of the foundation under the
claim. Then bring it to the present: whether the findings held (RoBERTa showed BERT
was badly under-trained; the generative GPT lineage took the spotlight) and where
BERT-style encoders still quietly run production systems (search ranking, embeddings,
retrieval, classification) even though BERT is not a chatbot.

## Duty assignment and mode
Duty (2026-07-27) lists `the-evidence` as **due**, mode **open**, empty commission
queue: invent tonight's subject within the beat. Chosen subject: BERT. Slug: `bert`.

## Recent catalog — do not repeat, and tonight's neighbors

if useful): attention-is-all-you-need, chain-of-thought, chinchilla,
emergent-abilities, gpt-3-few-shot, illusion-of-thinking, instructgpt,
scaling-laws-kaplan, sparks-of-agi. BERT sits directly downstream of
`attention-is-all-you-need` (the Transformer) and beside `gpt-3-few-shot` as the
other branch of the 2018–2020 pretraining story — reference, don't re-explain the
Transformer. Tonight's other Working-Knowledge pieces: the-instruments/gsm8k,
the-mechanics/knowledge-cutoff, what-could-go-wrong/gradual-disempowerment,
when-ai-breaks/ibm-watson-oncology. Avoid colliding framings with those.

- BERT paper, arXiv:1810.04805 — PRIMARY (owns every claim about method and numbers).
- GLUE benchmark paper, Wang et al., arXiv:1804.07461 — PRIMARY (owns what the GLUE
  score is).
- SQuAD papers (Rajpurkar et al. 1.1 arXiv:1606.05250, 2.0 arXiv:1806.03822) — PRIMARY.
- RoBERTa, Liu et al., arXiv:1907.11692 — PRIMARY (owns the "BERT was undertrained"
  correction).

author: ieyoukan
body:
## 背景 / なぜ
ワールドは mod を `modId:componentName` から算出し、URL から**無検証で fetch した生JSを Worker 実行**していた。完全性検証は皆無で、manifest の `capabilities` も配布者の自己申告をそのまま権限層へ渡していた。つまり **mod 公開者が同一 version のままバンドルを差し替えれば、承認済みワールドに任意コード注入・権限昇格ができる**。

このPRは **ワールド URL の provenance を信頼根**とし、mod 公開者を信頼しなくてよい状態にする（Subresource Integrity 相当）。

## やったこと（4コミット）

### 1. mod 完全性ロック（hash固定＋権限天井）
- `@ubichill/shared`: `ModLock` スキーマ（`sha256-<base64>` SRI で version/コードhash/capability天井を宣言）＋純粋ロジック `resolveLockedMod`/`requiresLock`（fetch/crypto 非依存＝Node単体テスト可能）。
- `scripts/build-workers.mjs`: 各 mod version に `lock.json` 断片（コードhash + manifest hash + 検出 capability）を出力。
- ロード時: version を lock で固定（最新ポインタを信頼しない）→ manifest/worker の生バイト列 hash を `crypto.subtle` で照合。**外部 provenance の不一致/lock欠落は実行拒否、local は寛容**。capability は verified 時のみ **lock 天井**を採用（manifest 申告を無視＝配布者による昇格を封殺）。

### 2. lock をワールドYAMLから分離（可読性）
人間が書く scene 定義と機械生成の hash を1ファイルに混ぜない。
- ubichillワールド: `worlds.lock` **DB別カラム**（migration 0003）→ 兄弟エンドポイント `GET /worlds/:id/lock` で配信。配信YAMLはクリーン。
- GitHub由来: 兄弟 `.lock.json`（`lockUrlFor` が導出、resolver が best-effort 取得）。
- 任意URL: `spec.lock` 埋め込みフォールバック。

### 3. `@ubichill/loader` 新設（frontend からロジック分離）
- ビルドレス・**React/DOM 非依存・browser+Node 両対応**・依存は `@ubichill/shared` のみ。`acquireMod`/`buildWorldLock`/`sriOf`（baseUrl・fetch 注入）。
- frontend の `modLoader`/`buildWorldLock` は薄いアダプタに縮小。`@ubichill/sandbox` は無改修（入力契約＝検証済み workerCode + capability 天井のみ）。

### 4. 汎用ロック生成CLI
- `pnpm gen:lock <world.yaml>` → 兄弟 `<world>.lock.json` 生成（fs / `--base-url` 切替）。GitHub 手書き作者も lock を作れる。`worlds/default.lock.json` 生成済み。
- ついでに pen の tsconfig paths から Host 内部を除去（mod は `@ubichill/sdk` のみ依存の原則を tsconfig でも担保）。

## 責務4層
知識=`shared` / 取得+検証+lock構築=`loader` / 状態+env解決=`frontend` / 隔離実行=`sandbox`。

## 検証
- 全パッケージ typecheck・`pnpm lint` クリーン、**205 tests（200 pass / 5 skip）**。
- frontend vite build 成功（loader をソース消費）。
- **ライブE2E**: `gen:lock` で default.lock.json 生成 → `/worlds/default/lock` 200・配信YAMLクリーン → 公式ワールド入室で pen×3・video-player×4 全 worker が初期化・lock拒否ゼロ（verified パス）。改竄バンドルは外部 provenance で拒否、manifest の権限過剰申告は lock 天井で無視——を Node harness と実ファイルで実証。

## 非対象（将来）
- assets（`Ubi.modBase` 遅延ロード）の hash 固定・lock 署名（作者鍵）・`ubi` CLI 統合。

| --- | --- |
| `contract.py` | **New.** `ExtractionRequest`, `TextPrompt`/`VisionPrompt` (discriminated), `PageImage`, caps, and `audit_view()` — the only representation permitted to reach a sink. |
| `app.py` | `POST /v1/extract` (validate → record → 501) and a `RequestValidationError` handler that reports field locations instead of echoing input. |
| `tests/test_contract.py` | 9 tests over the model. |
| `tests/test_extract_endpoint.py` | 5 tests over the running app, including the log-stream assertions. |

## The two requirements this implements

Both are already merged under `openspec/changes/qwen-vlm-consolidation`; neither is invented here.

**Exactly one tenant per request** — `tenant-access-control`, "Tenant Isolation At The Shared Inference Service":

> the worker calls the LiteLLM gateway directly, so none of the schema-per-tenant isolation, `documents.transition` claim enforcement, or per-call audit that Go applies on the worker's behalf is present at this boundary. Tenant isolation MUST therefore be enforced explicitly at the inference boundary itself rather than inherited.

So `tenant_id` is required, non-blank, and has nothing to fall back to.

**For images the control is exclusion, not transformation** — `audit-compliance-retention`:

> Non-textual inference payloads … MUST NOT be emitted to any log sink, trace exporter, or Temporal payload in any form, whole or partial, at any log level. For these payloads the control is exclusion, not transformation: only an opaque reference (the object-storage URI and content hash of the page render) MAY be recorded. Attempting to redact a page image in place MUST NOT be treated as satisfying this requirement…

That sentence is what shapes `PageImage`. If a request carried only bytes, `audit_view()` would have nothing safe to say, and a call with no audit line is untraceable. The reference travels **with** the payload so the log can name the render without holding it — and both reference fields are mandatory, so a page that cannot be audited cannot be submitted.

`audit_view()` is built **by construction, not by filtering**: it names what goes in. A field added to a model later is absent from the log until someone adds it here deliberately. A blocklist defaults the other way, and this codebase has already paid for a blocklist that did not match what the model actually emitted (#285's `\b` against snake_case keys).

## Two places the leak would have been invisible

**FastAPI's default 422 echoes the offending input.** For a vision request that input is a page image, so a malformed request would have written document content into a response body — and through the access log into a sink — with nobody having written a log line for it. Replaced with field locations, which is what a caller needs anyway. `test_a_rejected_request_does_not_echo_the_payload_in_its_error` covers it.

**The endpoint answers `501` rather than returning a stub extraction.** A fake success is indistinguishable from a real one to the caller, and the synthetic-only gate exists precisely so that an unproven path cannot be mistaken for a working one.

## Verification

- [x] Unit tests: `uv run --frozen --extra dev python -m pytest` — **21 passed**.
- [x] Typecheck/build: `mypy .` — clean (7 source files); `ruff check .` — clean.
- [x] **Runtime**: real uvicorn process, real `POST /v1/extract` carrying a page image whose bytes spell a NIF and an amount.
- [ ] Integration tests: N/A — nothing to integrate with until slice 3.
- [ ] OpenSpec validation: N/A — no spec delta; this implements merged requirements.

What the running server logged, in full:

```json
{"event": "extraction_requested", "modality": "vision", "tenant_id": "tenant-a",
 "document_id": "doc-1",
 "pages": [{"content_hash": "sha256:aaa", "storage_uri": "s3://processing/tenant-a/abc/pages/1.png"}],
 "level": "info", "timestamp": "..."}
{"event": "127.0.0.1 - \"POST /v1/extract HTTP/1.1\" 501", "logger": "uvicorn.access", ...}
```

Grepping the **entire** captured stream for the base64 payload, the NIF and the amount returns nothing.

Strict TDD evidence: `tests/test_contract.py` was written first and failed at import (`ModuleNotFoundError: contract`); the five endpoint tests then failed against the app before `/v1/extract` existed.

| Check | Status | Reason if not run |

| Docker-backed tests | N/A | No image in this slice; container is slice 5. |
| Browser E2E | N/A | No web surface. |
| Local API/runtime stack | **Run locally** | Real uvicorn process, see above. |

- Tasks complete: no — slice 2 of 5.
- Strict TDD evidence included: yes

- Estimated changed lines: 447 (446 insertions, 1 deletion) across 4 files, of which **271 are tests**.
- If over 400 changed lines, explain the chained PR plan or size exception:

Over by 47. The delivery is already sliced five ways, and the two halves here cannot land separately: a contract with no endpoint cannot be shown to exclude anything from a log, and an endpoint with no contract has nothing to validate. The excluded-bytes property is only meaningful when asserted over a running app, which is why the tests are the larger half.

author: iamharrie-labs
body:
## Summary

Closes #20.

The issue asks for something Solidity-specific: inherit `ERC20Snapshot`, integrate with OpenZeppelin's `Governor`. Neither exists here — this repo is a Soroban contract, not an EVM one, and there's no governance token or Governor contract in it at all yet. So this PR reimplements the actual problem the issue is describing rather than the literal ask.

The problem: if voting power comes from an account's *current* balance at the moment a vote is read, a flash-loaned balance can vote and then leave in the same transaction, since nothing pins what the balance "should have been."

The fix is the same idea as OpenZeppelin's checkpoint-based `ERC20Votes`, adapted to Soroban:

- Each account gets a history of `(ledger_sequence, balance)` checkpoints (`ledger_sequence` is Soroban's equivalent of a block number)
- `create_voting_proposal` pins a ledger sequence as that proposal's voting snapshot
- `get_votes` / `get_votes_for_proposal` binary-search that account's checkpoint history for the balance as of the snapshot, so a later balance change can't retroactively change it

This is implemented as free functions in a new `governance` module, called from `GrantRoundContract`'s existing `#[contractimpl]` block (new entrypoints: `set_voting_balance`, `get_votes`, `create_voting_proposal`, `get_votes_for_proposal`) — not as a second `#[contract]`. A second contract in this crate does compile, but running the full test suite with it in place blows past this repo's Windows/gnu toolchain's PE export-ordinal limit. Not something you'd catch reading the diff; only running `cargo test` without a filter surfaces it.

## A bug the tests caught

My first pass pinned the *current* ledger sequence as the proposal snapshot. A test simulating the exact attack this issue describes — mint 0, create a proposal, then mint 1,000,000 in that same ledger sequence — failed, because `set_balance` overwrites (rather than appends) a checkpoint for whatever sequence is still open. So a same-ledger mint after proposal creation could still poison the snapshot that was supposed to freeze it.

Fixed by pinning `current - 1` instead of `current`, which is the same trick Governor's `proposalSnapshot()` uses for the same reason. Left both the original failing scenario and its fix as a test (`later_balance_change_cannot_alter_a_pinned_proposal_snapshot`), since it's exactly the case a reviewer would want proof against.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo +stable-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu test --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu governance` — 3/3 passing
- [x] `cargo +stable-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu test --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu test_grant_round_flow` — existing test still passes, no regression
- [x] `cargo +stable-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release` — deployable artifact builds clean

(Filtered test runs rather than a bare `cargo test`, per the PE export-ordinal issue above — this is a pre-existing toolchain limitation, not something introduced here; it reproduces on `main` with zero changes applied.)

## Note on stacking

Based on `security/storage-layout-guard` (#37), so this diff includes that PR's changes until it merges. Review the top commit ("Add checkpoint-based voting power...") on its own.

body:
## 背景

実機 kbx-001 が「疲れやすい」— 満充電から 4〜10 時間で energy が枯渇し、1 日 2〜4 回の分割睡眠（充電）で継ぎ足す生活になっていた。

1 週間分の inner_state_history + appraisal_log の実測（覚醒 104.4h）:

| 要因 | レート |
|---|---|
| ルール減衰（decayInnerState、概日込み） | -0.029/h |
| appraisal イベント消耗（グロス） | -0.066/h |

時間経過の疲労はルール側が既にモデル化しているのに、出来事由来の消耗（small_down -0.075 × 高頻度）がその 2 倍強積まれていた（idle イベント棄却ガードの対象外である通常行動の分）。

## 変更

- `maxEnergyExertionPerEvent = 0.15` を追加し、energy の**負方向 delta のみ**半分にスケールする `energyDeltaLevelToNumber` を導入（large_down -0.15 / down -0.075 / small_down -0.0375）
- hunger の `maxHungerRecoveryPerEvent` と同じ非対称クランプのパターン。回復方向（充電・休憩の up 系）は従来どおり `maxDeltaPerEvent = 0.3` で据え置き
- `LIFE_TUNING_VERSION` を `tuning-v4` へ（proc_version に反映、reprocessing で追跡可能）

## 期待収支

ルール減衰 0.03/h + 消耗半減後のイベント分 ≒ 0.06/h → 満タンから概ね **14〜16 時間**で「眠い」域に入る、人間相当の一日周期。

## テスト

- `energyDeltaLevelToNumber` の非対称スケールのユニットテストを追加
- `npm run typecheck` / `npm test` 全 895 件パス

## Проблема

На `/payment-instruction.html` («Как оплатить») и `/partner-presentation.html` («Партнёрская программа») вместо иллюстраций Оплатишки показывались иконки битых картинок.

## Причина

Страницы ссылаются на `/mascot/*.png`, а файлы стали `.webp` ещё в PR #90 (19 июля). Ссылки тогда не обновили — 9 штук в двух файлах.

**Почему прожило больше недели:** обе страницы — статический HTML в `public/`, мимо сборки Next.js. Пути внутри не проверяет ни `typecheck`, ни линтер, ни билд. Заметить можно было только открыв страницу глазами.

## Что сделано

- 9 ссылок переведены на `.webp`;
- регресс-тест `lib/static-pages.test.ts`: каждая локальная ссылка из `public/*.html` обязана вести на существующий файл. Проверен намеренной подменой — ловит.

Тест лежит в `lib/`, а не рядом со страницами: всё в `public/` раздаётся по HTTP, тест-файл там стал бы публично скачиваемым.

author: printshop39-byte
body:
Follow-up to [#32](https://github.com/printshop39-byte/drucka/pull/32), which carried the Grid photos into Pro. This fixes the other half: work done **inside** Pro was lost on the way back.

## Cause

The Grid editor was deliberately kept mounted behind Pro. Pro was not — it unmounted the moment the view left it, taking the whole Fabric canvas with it. Crops, effects, pen strokes and text: gone, with no warning.

Pro now stays mounted too, hidden behind Grid, exactly as Grid is hidden behind Pro. Still lazy — nothing is downloaded or mounted until the customer asks for Pro once.

## Three things that needed fixing to allow it

**`fitCanvas` on a hidden host.** With `display:none` the host measures 0×0 and the `ResizeObserver` still fires. `Math.min((0 - 24) / w, …)` is negative, so `setDimensions` got a negative size and the artboard was destroyed. It now bails below the padding and refits on becoming visible.

**The photo handover was in the mount effect**, which now runs only once. Moved to an effect keyed on becoming visible, with an `importedRef` of placed photo ids. So: photos added on the grid side while Pro was hidden **do** come across, already-imported ones **don't** stack, and a photo deleted inside Pro **stays** deleted.

**Closing the Collage Maker** now unmounts Pro and clears the handed-over photos — otherwise reopening would show the previous artboard.

## Verified in the browser

Read off the live Fabric canvas via the editor's dev-only `window.__fc` hook.

| step | canvas contents |
|---|---|
| Grid: upload 2 photos → Pro | `2` — `[image, image]` |
| add text in Pro | `3` — `[image, image, text]` |
| → Grid → back to Pro | **`3` — `[image, image, text]`** (was: everything lost) |
| → Grid, upload a 3rd photo → Pro | **`4` — `[image, image, text, image]`** |

The last row is the one that covers all three concerns at once: the new photo arrived, the two already-imported ones did not duplicate, and the text survived.

`npm run build` passes.

author: superplane-gh-integration-9000[bot]
body:
fixes #6369

### Summary

The "Human review requested" checkbox in the Software Factory PR description is never checked because two progress-update runs fire in parallel and each rewrites the whole PR body from a stale copy. The "Mark CI Done" and "Mark Human Review Requested" nodes both trigger off the Babysit node's `passed` channel, do a read-modify-write of the PR description, and the last write wins, so the "Confirmed CI passes" write clobbers the "Human review requested" write.

Fix: serialize the two body-writing updates so "Mark Human Review Requested" runs after "Mark CI Done" completes, instead of running concurrently with it.

<details>
<summary>Implementation plan</summary>

## Where the bug lives

Everything is in the factory canvas definition:
`web_src/src/pages/home/factories/software-factory/canvas.yaml`

Key nodes:
- `onrun-onrun-2nvcpr` ("Update Progress") - a reusable onRun sub-app. It runs:
  - `component-node-t3n3jn` ("Get Pull Request Description", github.getIssue) - reads the current PR body
  - then `mark-implementation-done-mark-implementation-done-2-8ukxus` ("Mark Check as Done", github.updateIssue) with:
    `body: {{ replace($["Get Pull Request Description"].data.body, "- [ ] " + root().data.parameters.CheckName, "- [x] " + root().data.parameters.CheckName) }}`
  This is a full-body read-modify-write that flips exactly one `- [ ]` to `- [x]`.
- Four `runApp` callers invoke that sub-app with different `CheckName`:
  - `component-node-tfqihq` -> "Write implementation plan" (Mark Plan Done)
  - `mark-plan-done-mark-plan-done-2-9a4m74` -> "Complete implementation" (Mark Implementation Done)
  - `mark-implementation-done-mark-implementation-done-2-qpudc5` -> "Confirmed CI passes" (Mark CI Done)
  - `mark-ci-done-mark-ci-done-2-ru37ew` -> "Human review requested" (Mark Human Review Requested)
  (Note the node ids are historically mislabeled; trust the `name`/`CheckName`, not the id string.)

## Root cause (a lost-update race, not a text mismatch)

The checkbox text lines up exactly: the PR body seeds `- [x] Human review requested` (canvas.yaml ~line 954) and the caller passes `CheckName: Human review requested` (~line 581), so `replace(...)` would work.

The problem is concurrency. The "Babysit" node (`component-node-nbf347`) fans out on its `passed` channel to three nodes at once (edges ~lines 1370-1378):
- `github-markpullrequestreadyforreview-...-wie92w` (Mark PR Ready) - different API, harmless
- `mark-implementation-done-...-qpudc5` (Mark CI Done) - reads + rewrites PR body
- `mark-ci-done-...-ru37ew` (Mark Human Review Requested) - reads + rewrites PR body

Mark CI Done and Mark Human Review Requested run at the same time. Both call the same Update Progress sub-app, both `getIssue` the same starting body (plan + implementation already checked), both flip only their own box, then both `updateIssue` the entire body back. Whichever writes last wins; the other checkbox is lost. In practice "Confirmed CI passes" wins and "Human review requested" is dropped, exactly matching the screenshot in the issue (plan/implementation/CI checked, human review unchecked).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Babysit (passed)
    participant CI as Mark CI Done
    participant HR as Mark Human Review Requested
    participant GH as PR body
    B->>CI: run (parallel)
    B->>HR: run (parallel)
    CI->>GH: read body (plan+impl checked)
    HR->>GH: read body (plan+impl checked)
    CI->>GH: write body (+CI)
    HR->>GH: write body (+HumanReview)  %% overwrites CI... or vice versa
    Note over GH: last write wins -> one box lost
```

## Fix

Serialize the two body-writing updates so the human-review write happens after the CI write, reading an up-to-date body. Change the trigger of "Mark Human Review Requested" from the Babysit node to the "Mark CI Done" node.

In the `edges:` section of canvas.yaml, replace:

```yaml
    - sourceId: component-node-nbf347
      targetId: mark-ci-done-mark-ci-done-2-ru37ew
      channel: passed
```

with:

```yaml
    - sourceId: mark-implementation-done-mark-implementation-done-2-qpudc5
      targetId: mark-ci-done-mark-ci-done-2-ru37ew
      channel: passed
```

Result: Babysit passed -> Mark CI Done (checks "Confirmed CI passes"); Mark CI Done passed -> Mark Human Review Requested (reads the now-CI-checked body, then checks "Human review requested"). No concurrent read-modify-write on the PR body, so no lost update. Mark PR Ready still runs off Babysit in parallel (it touches a different API and is safe).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    B[Babysit passed] --> PR[Mark PR Ready]
    B --> CI[Mark CI Done]
    CI -- passed --> HR[Mark Human Review Requested]
```

Notes on the chosen approach:
- runApp nodes already emit a `passed` channel (Babysit itself is chained this way), so chaining "Mark CI Done" -> "Mark Human Review Requested" on `passed` is valid.
- Chaining to Mark CI Done (the other body-writer) rather than to Mark PR Ready is deliberate: Mark PR Ready is quick and does not write the body, so chaining there would still leave Human Review racing Mark CI Done. Chaining after the other writer guarantees serialization.
- The downstream nodes read `PullRequestNumber` from `$["Open Draft PR"].data.number`, which is main-workflow context available regardless of the immediate upstream node, so re-parenting the edge does not break parameter resolution.

## Optional hardening (not required for the fix, worth noting)

The same lost-update pattern could bite any two progress updates that ever run concurrently. Currently "Mark Plan Done" and "Mark Implementation Done" fire at different pipeline stages so they do not overlap, but to be fully race-proof the four progress updates could be chained into a single sequential path (Plan -> Implementation -> CI -> Human Review). That is a larger change and can delay early check-off feedback, so it is called out as a follow-up rather than part of this fix.

## Verification

- Manual/trace: confirm no two nodes calling `onrun-onrun-2nvcpr` share a source node + channel (i.e., never fan out to two Update Progress runs from the same edge). After the change, only Mark CI Done fans out to the human-review update.
- End-to-end (in a factory-enabled environment): trigger the factory on an issue, let it open the draft PR, run implementation and CI, and confirm all four boxes end checked, specifically "Human review requested".
- Sanity: the checkbox label in the seeded PR body (`- [x] Human review requested`) still matches the `CheckName` parameter exactly.

## Tradeoffs

- Pros: minimal, one-edge change; directly removes the concurrent write; keeps existing sub-app reusable and unchanged; preserves parallel Mark PR Ready.
- Cons: "Human review requested" is now checked slightly later (after the CI check-off) rather than simultaneously - negligible in practice and matches the intended ordering.

</details>

### Progress

- [x] Write implementation plan
- [x] Complete implementation
- [x] Confirmed CI passes
- [x] Human review requested

---

author: seiya1121
body:
Closes #81

## 概要

`SideNavAccountItem` に `href` / `external` を追加し、遷移する項目を `<a>` として描けるようにする。

```tsx
items={[
  { key: 'profile', icon: 'account_circle', label: 'マイプロフィール', href: '/users/me' },
  { key: 'help',    icon: 'help',           label: 'ヘルプ', href: 'https://…', external: true },
  { key: 'signout', icon: 'logout',         label: 'サインアウト', danger: true }, // href 無し＝操作
]}
```

## なぜ

`onSelect` の中で `navigate()` / `window.open()` を呼ぶ形だと、**リンクとして壊れる**:

- 中クリック / Cmd+クリックで別タブに開けない
- リンクのコピー・ホバー時の URL 表示ができない
- スクリーンリーダーが「リンク」と読み上げない

`Menu.Item` は Base UI 由来の `render` を透過するので、`href` のある項目だけ `<a>` に差し替えれば済む。

## 挙動

| 項目 | 描画 | 備考 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `href` あり | `<a href>` | `role="menuitem"` は保たれる |
| `href` + `external` | `<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">` | 行末に `open_in_new` |
| `href` なし | Base UI 既定（`<div role="menuitem">`） | 従来どおり `onSelect` のみ |
| `href` + `disabled` | `<a>` にしない | HTML の `<a>` に `disabled` は無く、`data-disabled` が付いても遷移が止まらないため（`UserLabel` が `href={disabled ? undefined : href}` で塞いでいるのと同じ理由） |

`href` 付きの項目でも `onSelect(key)` は従来どおり呼ぶ（遷移は `<a>` 自身が行うので、計測や後処理のフックとして残す）。ルーターには依存しない（素の `<a>`）。SPA 内リンクにしたい消費側は `items` を使わず `Menu` を直接組む。

## 検証

- `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm check` / `pnpm build` / `pnpm check:styles` すべて green
- Storybook で実ブラウザ確認。console error 0件
  - `href` 項目が `A` タグ・`role="menuitem"` で描かれ、`external` に `target="_blank"` / `rel="noopener noreferrer"` が付く
  - `href` + `disabled` の項目は `DIV` として描かれ `href` を持たない（遷移しない）
  - リンク項目のクリックで実際に遷移し（`location.hash` が変わる）、同時に `onSelect(key)` も呼ばれる
- `codex exec review --uncommitted`（medium）: 指摘0件

body: ## Summary - add a no_std + alloc mDNS codec and sans-I/O agent with a std-gated per-interface multicast socket driver - refactor discovery into a signed BeaconAgent and shared source-neutral PeerDiscoveryAgent with bounded storage, provenance, expiry, backoff, and dial budgets - integrate mDNS with Endpoint configuration, shared automatic dialing, interface refresh, shutdown goodbyes, feature matrices, documentation, and fuzz coverage ## Verification - just test - just clippy - just check-nostd - just docs - Rust 1.88 feature checks - ignored two-endpoint real multicast discovery test run manually - just fuzz 60: 39,019 executions with no crash - cargo fmt checks and git diff --check ## Known v1 limitations - no known-answer suppression or probing/conflict resolution - no receive-side hop-limit verification - IPv6 link-local advertisements are skipped until ip6zone support exists - no SRV, A, or AAAA record handling - macOS, BSD, and Android use an on-link prefix check as an ingress-interface attribution approximation --- ## Summary by cubic Adds libp2p‑compatible mDNS peer discovery, refactors discovery into a signed `BeaconAgent` plus a shared `PeerDiscoveryAgent`, integrates both with `Endpoint` and NAT, and hardens mDNS decoding/scheduling with strict bounds and rate limits. Docs now clearly separate signed-beacon wire config from the shared peer‑book/dial policy. - **New Features** - New crate `minip2p-mdns`: `no_std + alloc` mDNS codec and sans‑I/O agent, optional `std` per‑interface socket driver; feeds observations into the shared peer book; IPv6 optional; bounded decode size; per‑tick/action caps; strict DNS name handling; goodbye on shutdown. - Discovery refactor in `minip2p-discovery`: added `BeaconAgent` (validates/schedules beacons) and `PeerDiscoveryAgent` (bounded book, provenance, expiry, backoff, rate limits, dial budgets, tie‑break); `Multiaddr`/`Protocol` now `Ord` for stable merges. - Endpoint/drivers: new `.mdns()` builder; new `BeaconConfig` and `PeerDiscoveryConfig`; unified `DiscoveryEvent` with `DiscoverySource` and per‑source addrs; mDNS auto‑dials are direct‑only via `NatAgent::connect_direct`; docs/guides/feature matrix clarify `BeaconConfig` vs `PeerDiscoveryConfig`; examples, tests, CI, fuzz updated. - **Migration** - Replace `DiscoveryConfig` with `BeaconConfig` (beacon wire settings) and `PeerDiscoveryConfig` (shared book/dial policy): call `.discovery_config(BeaconConfig{...})` and `.peer_discovery_config(PeerDiscoveryConfig{...})`. - To enable LAN discovery without pubsub, enable the `mdns` feature and call `.mdns()` (optionally `.mdns_config(...)`). - `KnownPeer` now separates `beacon_addrs` and `mdns_addrs`; use `DiscoverySource` when handling events. - If using sans‑I/O directly, move from `DiscoveryAgent` to `BeaconAgent` + `PeerDiscoveryAgent`. Written for commit 067db1c29f3d450dde2302c45897f98ca3dd9798. Summary will update on new commits.

author: giviruk
body:
## Шаг CI: миграции на непустой базе

Юнит-тесты используют InMemory-провайдер и SQL миграций не выполняют, а E2E всегда стартует с пустой базы. Из-за этого дважды прошли зелёный CI и упали в проде миграции, ломающиеся именно на существующих строках.

Новая джоба воспроизводит продовый сценарий:

1. поднимает Postgres;
2. запускает приложение на ревизии **до** изменений — оно применяет миграции и сид, наполняя каталог;
3. проверяет, что база непустая (иначе проверка была бы холостой);
4. запускает приложение с текущей ревизии — то есть применяет новые миграции к реальным данным.

Падение процесса при старте валит шаг и печатает лог. Проверено с обеих сторон: на исправленных миграциях джоба зелёная, а с временно возвращённым дефектом падает ровно с `23502` из вчерашнего инцидента.

## Героическая способность — отдельная вкладка

Лист тонул в тексте: блок героики показывал описания всех улучшений, включая ещё не купленные, и весь список вторичных эффектов с полными правилами.

- Новая вкладка **«Героика»** (только Realms of Terrinoth) собрала выбор способности, личность (ROT-HA-01), параметр primary effect (ROT-HA-02) и покупку улучшений вместе с их полными описаниями.
- На листе осталась сводка: базовый эффект, строка активации и описания **только уже купленных** улучшений и вторичных эффектов, без кнопок покупки.
- `SheetTab` больше не принимает `reference` — он ему не нужен.

Проверено в живом приложении: на листе видно базовое описание и купленную «Улучшенную», непокупленной «Высшей» нет; на вкладке — всё целиком.

## Попутно

Создание персонажа падало в 500 (`ArgumentNullException` в `ToDictionary`), если в выборе стартовых навыков не указана группа. Теперь это ошибка валидации с машинным `reasonCode` до первой записи.

## Проверки

242 доменных + 420 API + 151 фронтовой тест зелёные, `tsc` и eslint чисты.

## Summary

- 在已落地的语言配置 Store / 迁移之上，实现 Issue #88 的 Service：P0 双语校验、幂等键、可选 `expected_version`、会话归属校验。
- `LanguageConfigReader` / `LanguageTargetResolver` 由 Service 实现；HTTP 四条 `/api/v1` 语言路由从空壳改为真实业务响应。
- `main` 在设置 `DATABASE_URL` 时启用 Postgres 语言服务并自动迁移；未设置时语言路由返回 `not_implemented`。
- 会话归属默认 `NotImplementedSessionOwner`（带 session 的接口 `501`）；本地可用 `LANGUAGE_SESSION_OWNER=trust-auth`（仅开发）。
- 复用当前控制面的 `authcontext` / `AccountIDFromContext`，并与 records 等既有 mux 接线共存。

## Base

本分支已 rebase 到 `feat/language-config-db`（含 advisory lock 与唯一约束按 `ConstraintName` 映射的修复）。  
相对 base 仅多 3 个提交：Service → HTTP → main 接线。

## Scope

**In**
- Service / validate / MemoryStore / SessionOwner 端口
- HTTP 错误码映射与鉴权上下文导出
- main 接线、单测与文档

author: jan-moravec
body:
Adds a **Go to Line** (`Ctrl+G`) and **Go to Timestamp** (`Ctrl+Shift+G`) pair of `Edit` menu entries that jump the table to a row by its 1-based line number or by a wall-clock time, closing item **8** of [`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md#8-goto-line--goto-timestamp) (crossed off in this PR, comparative feature matrix cell flipped to `✓`). `MainWindow` grows two `QInputDialog`-driven slots plus a static pure parser (`ParseGotoTimestampInput`) and a source-model search helper (`FindFirstRowAtOrAfter`) that all sit alongside the existing `SelectSourceRow` seam and reuse the anchor / find navigation plumbing verbatim. Timestamp parsing goes through a new library-side helper (`loglib::LocalMicrosecondsSinceEpochToUtc`) which does the local -> UTC shift required for naive user inputs (the table renders in the display TZ; user text without `%z` / `%Z` is a wall-clock in that TZ, not UTC).

`GotoLine` reads a 1-based row number, validates it against the *live* row count on both dialog-open (via `QIntValidator`) and dialog-close (`ExecuteGotoLine` re-reads `mModel->rowCount()` after `exec` returns to catch FIFO evictions that landed while the modal was open), probes filter visibility through the outer proxy chain, and hands off to `SelectSourceRow`. Line 1 is always the earliest retained row (newest-first display only affects paint, not the number the user types); streaming FIFO eviction may have dropped older rows so numbers need not match the source file's own numbering. Filtered-out targets surface a specific `Line N is currently filtered out.` message instead of the generic `Row is not currently visible.` fallback that `SelectSourceRow` prints for anchor jumps.

`GotoTimestamp` accepts every format the timestamp column already parses (via `Column::parseFormats`), two ISO 8601 fallbacks (`%FT%T`, `%F %T`, tried after the column formats so columns with an empty format list still accept typical inputs), and the relative shortcuts `-Nh` / `-Nm` (case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant; `+N` and bare `N` also mean "N units ago", matching lnav / less). Naive inputs (no `%z` / `%Ez` / `%Oz` / `%Z` in the winning format) are shifted from the display TZ (`loglib::CurrentZone()`) to UTC via `loglib::LocalMicrosecondsSinceEpochToUtc` before the search; zoned inputs bypass the shift so a pasted `2024-04-28T10:00:00Z` from the file is never double-shifted. The search picks one of three branches from `(userSortColumn, TimestampsAreMonotonic())`: an O(log N) binary search over source rows on the fast path, an O(N_visible) outer-proxy walk when monotonicity has broken, and an O(N_visible) display-order scan under a user sort so the "first" row honours the visible order the user is looking at.

## Why

The [comparative feature matrix](ROADMAP.md#comparative-feature-matrix) has "Goto line / Goto timestamp" as a Tier 1 v1 blocker — lnav, Klogg, LogExpert, LogViewPlus, OtrosLogViewer, QLogExplorer, LogSleuth, and Logan all ship one. `Ctrl+F` and column filters cover different workflows (find a needle / narrow the view), and none of the anchor navigation paths land on an *arbitrary* row: the user is triaging an incident that references `line 12345` in a bug report, or wants to jump to `-1h` from an ongoing stream to see what happened before the alert fired, and every existing seam either searches for a substring or requires an anchor pre-planted on the target row. A `Ctrl+G` / `Ctrl+Shift+G` pair is the smallest possible feature that closes both gaps.

The right shape is a *library-side TZ shift helper + Qt-side pure parser + Qt-side source-model search helper*. The TZ shift lives in `loglib` because DST edge cases (fall-back ambiguous hour, spring-forward gap) are load-bearing and every future TZ-shift caller (headless CLI's `--since`, saved views, time-gap detection) should route through the same `date::choose::earliest` policy rather than each reinventing it. The parser lives on `MainWindow` as a pure static helper (`ParseGotoTimestampInput`) so it drives from unit tests without an instance and stays free of Qt event-loop dependencies: the dispatch tries the relative shortcut regex first (`^[+-]?\s*(\d+)\s*([hm])\s*$`), then each entry of the column's `parseFormats` via `loglib::TryParseTimestamp`, then the two ISO fallbacks; it returns `GotoTimestampParse{micros, isNaive}` so the caller knows whether to shift, and the shortcut branch reports `isNaive == false` because `system_clock::now()` is already UTC. The search helper lives on `MainWindow` because it needs both proxies (source-row visibility through `mRowOrderProxyModel` + `mSortFilterProxyModel`) and the monotonicity flag off `LogModel`, all of which are Qt-side; `FindFirstRowAtOrAfter` is `[[nodiscard]] int` and public so tests can drive all three branches directly without a modal.

**Timestamp monotonicity is the load-bearing invariant of the fast path.** The naive fast path is `std::lower_bound` over source rows, but that assumes `ts[i] <= ts[i+1]` for every `i` — an invariant that a single-file static parse of a well-formed log holds, but multi-file `Append` opens with overlapping ranges, log rotation with a boundary flip, or multi-producer streams with clock skew can and do break. `LogModel::TimestampsAreMonotonic()` (backed by `mTimestampsMonotonic`, updated in-place by `UpdateTimestampMonotonicity` on every `AppendBatch` with an O(N_batch) running-max + boundary check) is what lets `FindFirstRowAtOrAfter` gate the binary search: on the first inversion the flag flips false irreversibly and the search degrades to a proxy walk that picks the chronologically earliest visible match. The flag is cheap enough (one comparison per batch boundary + running-max per row) that the streaming path pays essentially nothing. Missing-timestamp rows (unpromoted / null value) are skipped rather than treated as `-inf`: a `-inf` policy would break `lower_bound`'s monotonicity the moment one interleaved gap appeared in `[10, missing, 20, 30]` (the fast path would return the wrong row on `target = 5`). Every probe walks forward past missing rows, then the post-search walk skips filter-hidden rows through the outer proxy — worst case (all rows missing) is O(N), typical case (rare gaps) stays O(log N).

**Naive-vs-zoned dispatch on the parser side avoids a silent 2-hour miss.** The naive first cut treated every parse the same and returned UTC epoch micros, which was correct for `2024-04-28T10:00:00Z` (already UTC) but two hours off for `12:00:00` typed by a user in UTC+2. The table renders in the display TZ so `12:00:00` is what the user *sees*, and comparing the parser's "naive UTC" against the model's true UTC would jump them to a row two hours off the one they meant. `FormatHasZoneSpecifier` walks the format looking for `%z` / `%Ez` / `%Oz` / `%Z` (advancing one byte at a time on a no-match so a malformed `%E%z` still detects the inner `%z`; `%%` is a literal percent and does not register), which lets `ParseGotoTimestampInput` return `isNaive = !FormatHasZoneSpecifier(fmt)` from the winning branch. Naive results flow through `LocalMicrosecondsSinceEpochToUtc`; zoned results bypass it. Relative shortcuts derive from `system_clock::now()` which is already UTC, so they always report `isNaive == false` regardless of the display TZ.

**`LocalMicrosecondsSinceEpochToUtc` and the `date::choose::earliest` policy is the third correctness point.** The obvious wire-up is `date::zoned_time{tz, local_time}.get_sys_time()`, but that overload of `to_sys(local)` throws `nonexistent_local_time` on the spring-forward gap and `ambiguous_local_time` on the fall-back hour — neither of which are recoverable in the Goto Timestamp slot (the user typed a real string; we shouldn't refuse the jump). The `to_sys(local, choose)` overload handles both edge cases without throwing: ambiguous fall-back hour resolves to the earlier candidate; spring-forward gap snaps to the transition boundary (the first real instant after the gap). We deliberately do NOT catch `nonexiste

author: theolivenbaum
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes several issues in DateTime handling and Json.NET serialization:

1. **DateTime equality now compares values, not identity** — `DateTime` and `DateTime?` equality operators (`==`, `!=`) now correctly use value comparison instead of reference identity, fixing cases where two `DateTime` values constructed from the same instant compared as unequal.

2. **Json.NET camelCase conversion handles leading capital runs** — implements Json.NET's `StringUtils.ToCamelCase` logic to correctly convert names like `HTTPRequest` → `httpRequest` (not `hTTPRequest`) and `ALLCAPS` → `allcaps`.

3. **TypeNameHandling.None payloads with $type no longer fail** — when a client reads JSON with a `$type` field but has `TypeNameHandling.None`, the deserializer now ignores the type hint instead of throwing.

4. **System.Version serialization support** — `System.Version` now serializes as its string representation (e.g., `"1.2.3.4"`), matching Json.NET behavior.

5. **DefaultValueHandling logic corrected** — fixed the null-comparison logic for determining when to skip default values during serialization.

6. **DateTime fraction parsing** — corrected millisecond conversion from fractional seconds (e.g., `.25` → 250ms, not 25ms).

## Key Changes

- **Emitter.Expressions2.cs**: Extended `IsRuntimeObjectNullableValue()` to include `DateTime` so lifted equality operators use value comparison for `DateTime?`.
- **JsonConvert.js**: 
  - Added `camelCase()` function implementing Json.NET's leading-capital-run logic
  - Introduced `maybeBindToType()` for optional type resolution when `TypeNameHandling.None`
  - Added `System.Version` handling in the serialization contract walker
  - Fixed `DefaultValueHandling` null-comparison logic (both-null vs. one-null cases)
  - Updated all `TypeNameHandling.Auto` checks to use `declaredType` instead of `possibleType` (which is cleared when runtime type differs)
  - Updated camelCase calls to use the new function instead of inline first-character lowercase
- **Date.js**: Extracted fraction-to-milliseconds conversion into `System.DateTime.fractionToMilliseconds()` helper
- **Removed test infrastructure**: Deleted `NewtonsoftJsonTests.cs` and `NewtonsoftJsonRunner.cs` from the translator tests (test suite moved to dedicated `Transpose.Newtonsoft.Json.Tests` package)
- **Build configuration**: Updated `.devops/build-transpose-json.yml` to run the new dedicated test suite and updated SDK versions across all `.csproj` files

## Testing

The changes are validated by:
- New `DateTimeEqualityComparesTheInstant()` test in `DateAndTimeTests.cs`
- Dedicated `Transpose.Newtonsoft.Json.Tests` package (separate from translator tests) that runs snippets both natively and as translated JS, comparing output

author: clintropolis
body:
### Description
This PR improves catalog type validation to reject invalid complex types instead of silently being ignored. It also updates druid native type validation to perform case insensitive handling of `ARRAY` and `COMPLEX` type prefixes, to be more consistent with how primitive types are handled (case insensitive), and fixes bug with handling of malformed type strings without a closing `>`. Prior to this something like `long` was allowed, but `complex<json>` or `array<long>` was not allowed (while `ARRAY<long>` was since array parsing recurses after removing the prefix). Array and complex prefix handling is now case insensitive, but complex type name handling itself must still be exact, as the underlying complex type registry is still case sensitive.

author: mathiasbourgoin
body:
## What this closes

Backlog **#46** — generate the Rocq mirror from `PtxLayout.v` so drift is structurally impossible.

## The defect

`formal/codegen-ptx/test/test_layout_conformance.ml` opened with a module named `RocqMirror`: 130 lines of OCaml its own header described as

> *"a line-by-line OCaml transcription of the definitions in `theories/PtxLayout.v`"*

each function carrying a comment naming the `.v` definition it copied. The suite then checked the production layout module `Sarek_ir_layout` against that transcription.

So the chain from theory to test had a hand-maintained hop in it. Every theorem in `PtxLayout.v` — `record_leaf_nonoverlap`, `record_leaf_aligned`, `record_size_is_padded_end` — was proved about the Rocq definitions and then checked against a copy that **nothing compared to the original**. An edit to the theory nobody propagated left the suite green while it tested a model that had stopped being the model. The 2026-07-24 audit filed it as *"2 unlinked human-maintained hops OCaml ⇄ mirror ⇄ proof"*.

## The fix

`extraction/LayoutExtract.v` extracts the layout API to `extraction/sarek_ptx_layout_model.ml`; dune compiles it as a library; the suite links it. The whole change to the test body is `module Model = Sarek_ptx_layout_model` in place of the 130-line transcription — nothing else changed shape, because the transcription used the theory's own names. (That is also the evidence it was faithful when written: **all 11 tests pass against the extracted model unchanged**.)

### Why `Extraction "file.ml"` and not `Extraction Library`

`Extract.v` uses `Extraction Library`, and its five outputs begin `open Datatypes`, `open List`, `open Nat` — modules that exist only if the Stdlib is extracted alongside them. **Those files have never compiled.** They are committed, regenerated by every proof run, and linked by nothing; `test_codegen_ptx_conformance.ml` says as much in its header and hand-mirrors too. The monolithic form emits one self-contained pair of files — the difference between a generated artefact and a generated artefact that runs.

### Why the output is committed raw

Listed in `.ocamlformat-ignore`, deliberately. ocamlformat rewrites extraction output into semantically identical but differently formatted text, and once that has happened a regenerate-and-diff check cannot tell a changed definition from a reformat. It is exactly why `Extract.v`'s outputs are *restored* by `check-formal-proofs.sh` rather than *compared* — and why they are excluded from the new check rather than pretended to be covered by it.

## The gate

`scripts/check-formal-proofs.sh` byte-compares the regenerated model against the committed copy, after the from-scratch rebuild it already performs. Without it the chain is only as good as whoever last remembered to regenerate — the hand-mirror defect reappearing one level up.

## Red before green

**A generator nobody has seen react is not a generator.** `variant_payload_offset`'s alignment floor was changed from `4` to `8` in `theories/PtxLayout.v` — a mutation the proofs still admit, so the change had to be caught downstream or not at all.

**1. The extracted OCaml changed.**

```diff
 let variant_payload_offset ctors =
   fold_right (fun c acc -> Nat.max (ctor_align c) acc) (Stdlib.Int.succ
-    (Stdlib.Int.succ (Stdlib.Int.succ 0)))) ctors
+    (Stdlib.Int.succ (Stdlib.Int.succ (Stdlib.Int.succ (Stdlib.Int.succ
+    (Stdlib.Int.succ (Stdlib.Int.succ 0)))))))) ctors
```

**2. The conformance suite went red**, precisely:

```
[FAIL]  exhaustive  1  variants <=3 ctors x <=2 args
[FAIL]  host-pins   2  color
FAIL variant[C0()]: payload offset
2 failures! in 0.075s. 11 tests run.
```

**3. The drift gate went red** with the diff and an instruction:

```
::error::the extracted layout model differs from the committed copy.
theories/PtxLayout.v changed without extraction/sarek_ptx_layout_model.ml being
regenerated, so test_layout_conformance.ml is checking the production layout
against a stale model. Regenerate: cd formal/codegen-ptx && rocq makefile -f
_CoqProject -o CoqMakefile && make -f CoqMakefile, then commit both files.
```

The mutation was reverted and all three are green again.

An earlier attempt (`tag_offset := 0` → `4`) was rejected by the *proofs* rather than reaching the generator, which is why the payload-offset floor was used instead: it exercises the path this PR adds.

## Verified

- `dune build @install` — exit 0
- `dune build @fmt` — exit 0
- `dune exec .../test_layout_conformance.exe` — 11/11
- `scripts/check-test-alias-coverage.sh` — *all 82 e2e test executables are wired to an alias*
- `scripts/check-alcotest-registration.js` — *every `test_*` case registered*
- `scripts/check-formal-proofs.sh` — exit 0, including `extracted layout model matches theories/PtxLayout.v`

The extracted library is committed, so `dune runtest` in the `build` job needs no Rocq; the drift check runs in `formal-proofs`, which has it.


---

## Follow-up: the gate's first CI run was red, and it was the gate's fault

The whole diff was this:

```diff
-  { cl_tag = tag; cl_leaves = (flattens (tag :: []) payoff (number_args 0 c));
-    cl_payload_size =
+  { cl_tag = tag; cl_leaves =
+    (flattens (tag :: []) payoff (number_args 0 c)); cl_payload_size =
```

Identical tokens, different line breaks.

### It is not ocamlformat

That was the obvious suspect and it is wrong. The committed copy **is** raw and `.ocamlformat-ignore` holds — `dune build @fmt` does not touch it.

Rocq's extractor pretty-prints through OCaml's `Format`, and `Format`'s breaking decisions differ **between the OCaml the prover itself was built with**: 5.5.0 for the local distro install, 4.14.2 inside `rocq/rocq-prover:9.1.1`. Same Rocq version, same sources, same theorems — different wrapping. Confirmed directly by extracting inside the container and diffing against the local extraction:

```
=== raw byte diff ===
237,238c237,238   (the one hunk above)
=== whitespace-normalised diff ===
IDENTICAL after whitespace normalisation
```

So byte-comparing raw extractor output was never a drift check. It was a check on **which machine ran the extractor** — firing on every CI run forever, unable to distinguish that from the drift it exists to catch.

### Why not normalise through ocamlformat

It cannot run where it is needed. The extraction happens inside the Rocq image, which ships **no ocamlformat** (verified: `command -v ocamlformat` is empty). Moving the comparison to a job that has ocamlformat means moving the extraction to a job that has no Rocq.

`scripts/canonicalize-extraction.py` re-flows both sides identically and needs only `python3`, which that image does have. It **refuses** to run on a file containing a double quote — re-flowing whitespace is only safe while there are no string literals to re-flow across, and that is asserted rather than assumed. The committed copy goes through it too, so the comparison stays a byte-compare rather than becoming a fuzzy one. Verified byte-identical between the 4.14.2 and 5.5.0 extractions after canonicalisation.

### The check was also skipping itself

Running the gate in a container exposed a second defect, mine:

```bash
if [ -f extraction/… ] && git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree; then … fi
```

No `else`. Where git could not read the repository, **the entire check vanished without a word and the run reported OK having compared nothing.** That is the failure mode this script exists to remove, reintroduced by the check added to remove it. Both preconditions now fail loudly.

It stayed invisible because my first container run mounted a *linked worktree*, whose git directory is not inside the mount. Re-verification uses a real clone, which is what `actions/checkout` produces.

### Re-proved in the CI container, against a real clone

| | |
|---|---|
| **green** | gate passes **and prints** `extracted layout model matches theories/PtxLayout.v` — so it demonstrably ran |
| **red** | `variant_payload_offset

body:
## 요약

조커가 지시를 받아 문자를 보낼 수 있게 솔라피(Solapi) API를 연동합니다. 문자는 되돌릴 수 없으므로 **조커는 초안 카드만 만들고, 상준님이 카드에서 "전송"을 눌러야만 실제 발송**됩니다 (노션 삭제와 같은 확인 패턴).

## 흐름

1. "김실장한테 견적서 확인 문자 보내줘" → 조커가 `[[문자:수신번호|내용]]` 태그로 초안 작성
2. 채팅에 **💬 문자 전송 확인** 카드: 받는 번호 + 내용 미리보기 + [전송] [취소]
3. "전송" 클릭 → `POST /api/sms` → 솔라피 HMAC-SHA256 인증으로 1건 발송
4. 성공 시 "문자 전송됨", 실패 시 솔라피 사유(발신번호 미등록, 잔액 부족 등)를 카드에 표시

## 안전장치

- 채팅 스트림 핸들러는 절대 직접 발송하지 않음 — 발송 경로는 확인 카드 → `/api/sms` 하나뿐
- 호출당 수신자 1명 제한, 번호 형식 검증(0으로 시작 9~11자리), 내용 1000자 제한
- 번호를 모르면 조커가 태그 없이 먼저 되묻도록 프롬프트에 명시 (회사 메모리의 번호 활용)

author: jupiterv2
body:
## Problem

The streaming driver sends each binding to the processor over a pooled
`ProcessBindingsStream`, tagged with a `process_id`, and rejects any response
whose `process_id` doesn't match the task it's waiting on — ERR200
`unexpected ProcessID`.

`process_id` was taken from a **per-chain** counter (`TaskIndex.Global`,
`MainController.bindingIndex`), which starts at 0 in every chain. Multiple
chains in the same driver process therefore hand out the **same** `process_id`
values concurrently.

The processor SDK runtime keys a **single per-process context map by
`process_id` alone** (one map shared by every chain's stream). Colliding ids
across chains let one chain's context overwrite/close another's and misroute
db results, corrupting per-process stream bookkeeping. Combined with
stream-pool reuse, a stale/misrouted message lands on a reused stream and the
next task reads it → ERR200 → the run fails and crash-loops.

This is why the symptom only appears on **multi-chain** processors:
single-chain processors always have unique `process_id`s, so their context
map never collides.

## Fix

- Add a process-global `process_id` generator (`processIDGen`) and carry it as
  a separate `TaskIndex.ProcessID`, used **only** for the wire `process_id`
  (send + mismatch check). This guarantees uniqueness across all chains in the
  driver process, so the SDK's shared context map can no longer collide.
- `TaskIndex.Global` stays **per-chain** and keeps driving intra-chain ordering
  (the ready/finish waiters) and human-facing logging. The waiters are
  set/predicate based (`u < Global`), so the counter staying contiguous
  per-chain is preserved.
- Compare `process_id` on the `int32` wire type on both sides. `process_id` is
  an `int32` proto field; the previous `uint64(resp.GetProcessId())` comparison
  would sign-extend a wrapped (>2^31) id and report a spurious mismatch. A
  global counter reaches that range sooner, so this is fixed here too.

The task title / mismatch error now also include the `pid#` for easier triage.

## Notes / follow-ups

- Relies on the driver↔processor process pairing (a global-unique id per driver
  process makes every processor process it talks to see unique ids). This holds
  for the current topology.
- Defense-in-depth follow-ups worth doing separately: scope the SDK's context
  map per-stream instead of per-process, and drain a pooled stream to its
  terminal boundary on return / rebuild it on a mismatch instead of failing the
  whole run.

## Test

- Existing `driver/controller` tests updated/pass (`Test_main_failed`); the
  test's synthetic error now prints only the deterministic per-chain fields
  since `ProcessID` comes from a process-global counter.

body:
## Goal (RFC 0009 · G2-promote-predicate)

Narrow query→proactive promote eligibility to the **operational lane**.
Atomize-born knowledge claims (`domain=knowledge`, born-accepted, no `ac_status`)
are **no longer promote-eligible** — they reach the proactive/always tiers only
via **dream synthesis**, never the promote path. Operational claims still require
`ac_status: passed`.

The delta contract was authored, critic-accepted (default-deny envelope, no
waivers), and the goal converged with **contract PASS**.

## What changed

- **`claims_io.is_promote_eligible`** now delegates the domain gate to
  `store.is_accepted_operational_claim` (`domain=operational` + `ac_status=passed`)
  — reused, not re-stated, so "an accepted operational claim" has one definition
  across the engine. The domain-independent prerequisites (query tier + public)
  are factored into a new `is_promote_candidate`.
- **`metrics._tally_eligible`** keys `by_domain` off *candidates* and seeds each
  candidate domain at `0`, so a fully gated-out domain (`knowledge` → 0) stays
  **present as `0`** rather than dropping its key — an absent key is a hard raise
  in `contract._eval_intent`, not a satisfied zero. `total` stays
  `sum(by_domain.values())`.
- Tests updated across `test_promote_claims`, `test_metrics`, `test_goal_run`.

## Verified delta

| metric | from | to | bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| `promote_eligible.total` | 830 | 23 | `max: 30` ✓ |
| `promote_eligible.by_domain.knowledge` | 807 | 0 | `eq: 0` ✓ |
| `promote_eligible.by_domain.operational` | 23 | 23 | pinned by envelope ✓ |

Single-predicate edit; no vault content touched, so census/surfacing/eval and
`vault.content_fingerprint` stay unchanged under strict default-deny. No
invariant released (`supersedes: []`): the `promote_eligible` counter lives in
the metrics block, outside INV-1's census-only reach.

## Tests

Full suite green — **806 passed**.

author: spinkicks
body:
Documentation only. A recommendation for whoever owns the surface, not a decision I can make.

## The answer is neither option as framed

**Reject the recommendation-driven catalog. Do not defend the game either.**

The strongest study found is close to on-point: Brom et al. (2022), n = 11,949, randomised game versus plain quiz, same content, in genuine free-choice conditions on a public children's site competing against 200+ other games. The game **won** at catching interest (61.8% vs 53.6% past the first level) and **lost** at holding it (4.3% vs 6.0% completing), with fewer correct answers and more errors. The authors' framing: it "triggered situational interest but did not maintain it."

That is precisely backwards for us. A game shell is good at producing the signal our engine is required to **discount**, and no better at the cross-day return it **counts**.

I verified this against the paper directly, including its limits: the age band (~8-10) is the authors' own assumption rather than a measurement, the topic is one they describe as "difficult and boring", and the mechanic is a shooter rather than an exploratory world.

## But the browse direction is worse, and the deciding argument is ours

**Recommendation makes E4 non-identifiable.** A decline is only evidence if the alternatives were genuinely on offer. Once the offered set is a function of prior behaviour, *"this child rejected chemistry"* and *"the ranker stopped showing chemistry"* produce the same log — and more data tightens the feedback loop rather than breaking it. The counterfactual offered set is not recoverable after the fact.

This is a logical argument about identifiability, not an empirical finding, and the doc says so. The empirical case against children's filter bubbles is thin, and nobody should be sold the stronger version.

Separately, a video-first catalog collapses the depth channel back onto dwell — "chose harder work" and "unrequired revision" have no expression in a video card — which puts us back on the one signal we already ruled out (flat against learning, p = .80).

## We already satisfy most of the design requirements

| Requirement | Us |
|---|---|
| Normalise a decline by choice-set size | Done (E4) |
| Discount a fixed novelty window | Done |
| No reward external to the choice | Enforced (GC1/GC6) - and Patall makes this stronger than a style preference: an external reward **zeroes** the choice signal (d = −0.01 vs 0.35) |
| Log the offered set | Partly - `SurfacedRecord` lacks slate position, which a grid would need |
| Down-weight system-surfaced engagement | **E5, unbuilt. A recommender makes it mandatory, not deferred.** |
| Interleave a hold-out | **Missing entirely.** Without it any adaptive surface is unfalsifiable. Worth filing either way. |

All five claims about our own code were verified against it.

## Six evidence gaps, stated rather than filled

The two that matter most: **no study compares these two surfaces as interest-measurement instruments** — the question as asked is unstudied, and this is assembled from adjacent findings. And **no comparable product publishes evidence that it identifies genuine interest**. Khan Academy Kids has an RCT on literacy gains; Duolingo has published work on "goal drift", where engagement migrates from mastery to metric maintenance, which is exactly our failure mode. That is an open space, not a state of the art we have missed.

body:
…ry_table_after_syncd_orchagent (#25085)

### Description of PR

Summary:
This PR makes two related fixes to
`tests/lldp/test_lldp_syncd.py::test_lldp_entry_table_after_syncd_orchagent`, which deliberately restarts `swss`/`syncd` and cascades to a `bgp` container restart.

#### Commit 1 — Replace `time.sleep(60)` with a BGP convergence wait After restarting `swss`/`syncd`, the test currently waits a hardcoded `time.sleep(60)` before proceeding. On a DUT with many BGP neighbors (e.g., T1/T2 with 7050CX3), 60 seconds is **not enough** for bgpd to fully re-converge after the cascade restart.

This leaves bgpd in a warming-up state by the time the test ends. The **next test** (e.g. `test_lldp_entry_table_after_cont_flap`) then takes its memory baseline snapshot while bgpd RSS is still low. When bgpd subsequently reaches its normal post-init RSS during the next test, the framework's memory monitor reports a large increase (e.g. +139 MB > 128 MB threshold) and fails the next test with a **false-positive memory alarm**.

Replace `time.sleep(60)` with
`wait_until(duthost.check_bgp_session_state, ...)` so the test deterministically waits for all BGP sessions to reach `Established` state before exiting.

#### Commit 2 — Disable `memory_utilization` check for this test This test deliberately restarts swss/syncd, which cascades to a `bgp` container restart. The `memory_utilization` fixture takes before/after snapshots that become meaningless across such a restart (bgpd RSS drops to ~0 then warms back up over several minutes), so the in-test memory delta has no signal.

Add `@pytest.mark.disable_memory_utilization` to make the test intent explicit and prevent future framework changes (e.g. alarming on volatility or absolute decreases) from flagging this test on a meaningless measurement. This is consistent with other restart-style tests (e.g. `test_advanced_reboot`, `test_warm_reboot`, `test_container_autorestart`).

ADO: https://msazure.visualstudio.com/One/_workitems/edit/38230412

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement

### Back port request
- [ ] 202205
- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511

### Approach

#### What is the motivation for this PR?
Observed in plan `6a1b270895e3f84fd1e9ace9` (7050cx3.m1-128.202603 NightlyTest, branch `20260310.11`) on `testbed-bjw3-can-7050c-6`:

- `test_lldp_entry_table_after_syncd_orchagent` restarted swss/syncd (which cascades to bgp container)
- `time.sleep(60)` returned while bgpd RSS was still 67.9 MB (mid-convergence)
- Next test `test_lldp_entry_table_after_cont_flap` took its "before" snapshot: bgpd = 67.9 MB
- 16 minutes later, bgpd had warmed up to its normal 207.1 MB
- Framework reported `+139.2 MB > 128 MB threshold` → ALARM → next test FAILED

`vtysh show memory bgp` (FRR internal allocator counter) showed a consistent 204 MB both before and after the next test — proving bgpd did not actually leak memory. Only `top` RSS appeared to grow because the baseline was taken too early.

#### How did you do it?

**Commit 1 — wait for BGP convergence instead of sleep(60):**
```python
bgp_neighbors = list(duthost.get_bgp_neighbors().keys())
pytest_assert(
    wait_until(300, 10, 30, duthost.check_bgp_session_state, bgp_neighbors),
    "BGP sessions did not reach Established state after swss restart",
)
```
- Uses existing `duthost.get_bgp_neighbors()` to dynamically fetch the neighbor list (works on all topologies)
- Uses existing `duthost.check_bgp_session_state()` (default expected state = `"established"`)
- Parameters: `timeout=300s`, `interval=10s`, `delay=30s`

**Commit 2 — disable memory check on this test:**
```python
@pytest.mark.disable_loganalyzer
@pytest.mark.disable_memory_utilization     # NEW
def test_lldp_entry_table_after_syncd_orchagent(...):
```

The two changes are complementary:
- **Commit 1** prevents pollution of the next test (wait for BGP convergence before exit)
- **Commit 2** disables the meaningless measurement on this test itself

#### How did you verify/test it?
Logic review against existing helpers (`get_bgp_neighbors`, `check_bgp_session_state`, `wait_until`, `disable_memory_utilization` marker) — all are widely used elsewhere in sonic-mgmt.

Behavior change matrix for Commit 1:
- Healthy fast DUT (T0): exits in ~20–30 s (faster than old 60s sleep)
- Slow DUT (T1 with many neighbors): waits up to 300 s for actual convergence (vs. silently returning after insufficient 60s)

A real run on testbed-bjw3-can-7050c-7 / 7050c-6 will be needed to confirm the next-test memory alarm cascade no longer fires.

#### Any platform specific information?
None — both changes are platform-agnostic. The helpers used are standard sonic-mgmt helpers.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case? N/A — not a new test case. The existing test continues to run on all topologies where it currently runs.

N/A

- testbed-bjw3-can-7050c-11: https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6a20dc962296f2ad62e47dbc

body:
## Summary

- interpret `proc_pidfdinfo` file flags as Darwin `FREAD`/`FWRITE` capability bits
- retain session logs opened with `FWRITE` or `FREAD | FWRITE`
- exclude read-only session logs and unrelated files
- rename the predicate to describe that it checks how the Codex process opened the file

## Root cause

`vnode_fdinfowithpath.pfi.fi_openflags` reports kernel file capabilities. A real Codex Desktop rollout returned `FREAD | FWRITE` (access bits `3`), but the provider compared those bits with `O_WRONLY`/`O_RDWR`, incorrectly excluding read-write rollouts and accepting pure `FREAD` as writable. The app-server was discovered but had no associated session paths, so Desktop sessions displayed as zero.

## Verification

- TDD regression observed failing before the fix and passing after it
- full Swift suite: 159 tests, 0 failures
- release build, app packaging, and strict code-signature verification passed
- live Dashboard read included the current user Codex Desktop session
- live final build displayed the native Pet usage badge as an on-screen 48x28 layer-25 window

## Pet badge investigation

No Pet production change is included. Live diagnostics confirmed Locator, Tracker, Placement, Controller, and NSPanel all work with the current Codex Desktop window profile; the final clean build displays the badge. Temporary diagnostics were removed before commit.

author: gaoflow
body:
Round-tripping

```
k: >
  <TAB>
  detected
```

through `parseEvents` → `eventsToAst` → `present` emits a blank line before `detected`, so the value goes from `"\t\ndetected\n"` to `"\t\n\ndetected\n"`; with the tab line between two folded lines it costs two extra newlines. YAML 1.2.2 §8.1.3 defines a more-indented line by production [175] `s-nb-spaced-text`, whose leading [33] `s-white` is a space *or a tab*, and whose surrounding breaks are preserved ([177] `b-l-spaced`) rather than folded — `getBlockValue()` in the parser tests for both (`0x20 || 0x09`), but the presenter tested only for a space, at four sites in `foldBlockScalar`/`foldLine`, including the fold-point regexp `/ [^ ]/` which would break at the space in `aaa… \tzzz` and move the tab to the start of the next line. Enumerating every two-line block-scalar body over a 7-line alphabet in both block styles gave 84 parseable sources, of which 12 changed value through `present()` — all folded style, all involving a tab, literal style clean at 0/42; all 12 were confirmed against PyYAML 6.0.3 and ruamel.yaml 0.19.1 reading the emitted bytes, and all 12 round-trip after this change.

To be straight about the blast radius: `dump()` is not affected, since it routes tab-containing strings to double-quoted or literal style and never enters the folded path (0 of 41 distinct values from the same family broke either way), so this only reaches code that presents a parsed AST — exported and typed, but not documented in the README. I left `divergedFixtures` alone: R4YG's `dump` comparison still fails after the fix because the suite double-quotes that scalar while js-yaml faithfully keeps `>`, which is a genuine style divergence. (Its label there is "missing block scalar indent indicator", but a leading tab needs no indicator — indentation auto-detection only counts spaces — so R4YG was really this bug.) `npm test` goes from 1613 tests / 1600 pass / 0 fail to 1614 / 1601 / 0 fail with the added case, and reverting each of the four predicates on its own makes that case fail.

GitHub's macOS runner images ship a partially root-owned ~/.npm/_cacache, and npm refuses to use it, hard-failing with EACCES before doing any work — pack, publish, dry-run, and view all die on an otherwise healthy runner.
main now sets npm_config_cache to a runner-writable RUNNER_TEMP/silk-npm-cache directory at entry, only when unset, so every spawned npm inherits the redirect in all dispatch forms including the pnpm dlx npm executor.
The redirect existed pre-v4 in github-action-effects 2.2.1 but was lost in the kit migration; an upstream arg-splicing seam is filed as spencerbeggs/effected#198.
