author: fastner
body:
Implements `docs/plan/archive/2026-07-27-external-tracker-target.md`.

Until now, issue-shaped work had exactly two destinations: a local Markdown report, or issues in the Git forge behind `origin`. A team that keeps its issues in a project-management tool had no way to say so, and `apply-issues`/`plan-issue` were hard-wired to "the issue tracker of the `origin` remote".

## What changes

`tracker.mode` gains a third value `external`, and two new keys name the tool:

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `tracker.externalTool` | short identifier of the tool holding the issues; required when the mode is `external` |
| `tracker.externalToolHint` | free text — MCP server name, workspace, team or project key, identifier convention, state names |

Effective Flow ships **no adapter for any product** and keeps no whitelist. The hint is data the run-time agent uses to select an available MCP connection or an authenticated CLI, and every capability is established from that connection rather than inferred from the tool's name. `src/scripts/remote-tracker.mjs` is untouched — it stays the GitHub/Forgejo mechanism.

The new `src/shared/tracker-target.md` owns the external contract: connection discovery, the required capabilities, the write discipline that replaces the shipped helper's code guarantees (preview before mutation, verbatim fresh-read precondition, one canonical comment, byte-identical identity keys), the classification mapping, the container mechanism, and the reference syntax. It loads only when a run has actually resolved an external target.

## What stays put

- **Plan files.** `/effective-flow plan` still writes a committed Markdown file under `plan.dir` in every target. No target introduces an external publication path for plans.
- **Pull requests.** PRs, PR comments and review threads are code-host objects and stay with the forge behind `origin`. A forge auto-close keyword is never written for an external issue — that would close an unrelated forge issue on merge.
- **`local` and `remote`.** A project that does not opt in behaves byte-identically.

## Fail closed

Four failure classes each abort before the first write, with the workflow state preserved: missing tool identifier, no connection, ambiguous connection, missing capability. There is no silent fallback — publishing to the forge instead would scatter a team's issues across two systems, and degrading to a local report would hide work the user asked to publish.

The security disclosure gate now binds every publisher rather than only remote forge publishers: publishing a finding to a third-party tracker is a disclosure with the same consequences as publishing it to a public forge.

## Notes for review

- The plan predicted a single `lazy-include` fence inside `src/shared/issue-tracker.md`. That shipped a defective artifact: because `review.md` defers `issue-tracker` itself, the fragment also ships standalone through the eager-only path in `build.mjs`, where a raw fence survives verbatim into `dist/`. Build guard #99 stayed silent. The documented fallback was applied — the fence now sits in each of the six consuming tool sources, and the contract test derives that consumer set from the include closure so a seventh consumer cannot silently ship without the contract.
- `src/tools/apply-review.md` and `src/tools/plan-review.md` were not in the plan's affected-files table. Review found that the first gated its remote sub-file on the mode being `remote` — so the external contract could never load for an external epic or finding — and that the second's issue-mode comment update was written purely in forge-helper vocabulary. Both are minimal gap closures.
- Three review findings were deliberately not implemented; they are recorded with prompt suggestions in the local report rather than here.

## Verification

`pnpm agent:check`, `pnpm test` (354 pass, up from 346), `node build.mjs` and `pnpm test:distribution` all green. The always-loaded core stays under budget (review 601/700). `git diff --stat src/scripts/` is empty.

author: nmeji
body:
> **Scope note:** this PR opened as RI-1 and accumulated two Founder-approved additions (RI-2 delivery messaging, D7 discoverability). Retitled and rewritten so the description matches the contents — a reviewer should not approve changes they were not told about.

Six commits across three approved workstreams. **No page redesigned, no pricing changed, no product added, no analytics installed.** The site still cannot take money.

---

## RI-1 — Truthful Customer Communication (blocker B2)

`/contact` and `/book` ran a submit handler that awaited an 800 ms timer and then displayed **"Message received… we'll follow up within 1–2 business days."** Nothing was transmitted — the data lived in React state and was destroyed on navigation. Every CTA on the site terminated there.

This is a static export, so there is no server to post to. Rather than simulate a submission the system cannot perform, both pages now offer **direct email, pre-structured via `mailto`**. Both dropped `'use client'` and are static.

**D1** — `labs@terrapayx.com` is canonical: the only address with positive evidence of receiving mail. `contact@` is unverified and no longer published anywhere (it was in the **sitewide footer**, so the dead-alias risk existed independently of the forms).

**D3** — claims that could not be substantiated replaced with ones the record supports: *"active engagements"* → building and validating against production evidence; *"deployed for a technical operations team"* → capabilities Terra Pay X operates itself; *"Programs & Work / Representative programs"* → **"Capabilities"**. Also removed the unevidenced *"1–2 business days"* and *"scoped within one week"*.

**Legal entity** — `© 2026 Terra Pay X, Inc.` The wordmark remains the brand.

## RI-2 — delivery messaging

*"Delivered electronically after purchase — there is nothing to ship"* read as immediate; the FRPE-001 runbook sends after payment verification. Now: **"Digital delivery begins after payment verification."**

**States no timeframe, deliberately.** SPV-1 measured settlement once, at two days, and recorded that n = 1 is not an expectation. A service level is a *commitment*, not an *observation* (**D4**: no SLA yet).

## D7 — discoverability (RI-2 acceptance criterion)

The Starter Kit appeared in **0** navigation entries, **0** homepage sections, and **0** footer links — reachable only by typing the URL. D6 would have published a live offer nobody could find.

Exactly the four items RR-1 R1/R2 proposed: nav entry, hero CTA **added alongside** the advisory CTAs, footer link under Labs.

**No observation marker on the new CTA.** `engagement.cta.clicked` is unratified and the client validates before emission — a marker would look instrumented and retain nothing, which is the definition of E1. That is FOP-2, delivered by RI-3B after ratification.

**Not done:** Platform/Labs restructure, IA changes, marketing rewrite — all Terra Pay X 2.0.

---

## Inherited commit

`0f81c79` (`ci(deploy): inject NEXT_PUBLIC_STARTER_KIT_PAYMENT_URL at build`) predates this work — the branch was cut from `fix/website-inject-starter-kit-payment-url`, which was never merged. It is required by D6 and is included here rather than stranded. **Flagged because it is the only `.github/` change in the PR.**

## Verification (built output, not source)

- ✅ **0** `<form>` elements on `/contact` and `/book`
- ✅ **0** residual false claims
- ✅ `labs@` in footer and both pages; **0** rendered `contact@`
- ✅ Every page reaches the product via nav + footer; homepage also via hero CTA
- ✅ `Terra Pay X, Inc.` present; *"nothing to ship"* gone

## Risk

**L2.** Content and client behaviour. No payment, secret, or infrastructure surface touched — apart from the inherited deploy.yml commit above. Rollback is a revert.

## O que muda

Adiciona o **`CandlestickSeries`** do Lightweight Charts ao fluxo de caixa diário, alternável por um seletor **Barras | Velas** no cabeçalho do card.

## O problema: caixa não tem OHLC

Candlestick exige abertura/máxima/mínima/fechamento, e nossos dados são entradas/saídas/saldo. Em vez de inventar valores, derivamos um OHLC **financeiramente honesto**, encadeando o saldo:

| Campo | Derivação | Significado |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Abertura** | saldo no fim do dia anterior | onde o caixa começou |
| **Fechamento** | saldo no fim do dia | onde terminou |
| **Máxima** | abertura + entradas | pico, se tudo entrasse antes de sair |
| **Mínima** | abertura + saídas | fundo, se tudo saísse antes de entrar |

Resultado: **o corpo é o resultado do dia** (verde fechou acima, vermelho abaixo) e **os pavios são a faixa** que o caixa percorreria conforme a ordem dos lançamentos.

## Correção por construção

As invariantes do candle valem sempre, sem precisar de `clamp`: como `fechamento = abertura + entradas + saídas` (com saídas ≤ 0), segue que `máxima ≥ max(abertura, fechamento)` e `mínima ≤ min(abertura, fechamento)`.

Conferido em 5 cenários, incluindo os degenerados: **dia zerado**, **só saídas**, **só entradas** e **saldo negativo**.

## Legibilidade

A leitura de uma vela de caixa não é óbvia, então a **legenda** e o texto do botão **"i"** explicam o que corpo e pavio significam — em vez de deixar o usuário adivinhar. Dias previstos entram esmaecidos, igual às barras.

## Validação

- `npm test` ✅ **8/8 guardas** · `next lint` ✅ · `npm run build` ✅
- Invariantes do candlestick verificadas por script sobre 5 datasets

author: anneschuth
body:
Carries @bormog's #437 forward. Their 24 commits are preserved with authorship intact — this branch exists only because #437's head lives on a fork that this session cannot push to, so #437 itself could not be updated in place. **#437 should be closed as superseded, not as rejected** — the feature and nearly all of the code are theirs.

## 1. Rebased onto current main

#437 was based on `cb1fb50`, before the CI repairs, and had gone `dirty`. Merged onto current main (v1.18.4); only `CHANGELOG.md` conflicted, and both sections are kept.

**The knip check that #437 called out as red is now green.** Its description scoped that fix out because main was red too; main now pins knip and treats `src/**/index.ts` as entry points, so the new user-attribution barrel isn't flagged. Nothing about the feature had to change for it.

## 2. Default on, but only for shared threads

Per review feedback on #437, the default flips `false` → `true` — but a flat default-on would put `[@username]:` in front of every message in solo threads, where the prefix names the only person who could have spoken. So the prefix is gated on the session actually having more than one participant.

The signal is the existing session allowlist: seeded `new Set([owner])` and grown only by real collaboration events (`!invite`, or another user reviving a paused session). No new state. It's evaluated **per send**, not once at session start, so a thread that becomes shared mid-session starts attributing from that point on.

```ts
export function shouldAttribute(enabled: boolean, participantCount: number): boolean {
  return enabled && participantCount > 1;
}
```

Kept as a pure predicate over primitives so it stays trivially testable and pulls no `Session` import into the attribution module. All six send sites route through it; `formatUserTurn` itself is untouched.

Two details worth reviewing:

- **The system-prompt note keys off the config flag, not the live participant count** — so Claude is primed for a prefix that may only start arriving once someone is invited mid-session.
- **`pruneDefaultFalseFlags` no longer drops `userAttribution`.** With a `true` default, pruning an explicit `false` would silently re-enable the feature on the next start, making opt-out impossible. This is the one place the flipped default has a non-obvious consequence.

Resumed sessions keep the value they started with; sessions persisted before the flag existed stay unattributed.

## Verification

- 4 new tests for the gate, **verified RED before GREEN** — removing the participant check fails 2 of them, restoring it passes all 14.
- 8 existing tests updated for the new semantics: three asserted the old default, five enabled the flag on solo sessions the gate now correctly suppresses.
- Full suite green: **2650 pass / 0 fail**, plus typecheck, lint, knip, build and `bun audit`.

## Not addressed

The pre-existing deferred-context persistence limitation documented in #437 is still out of scope and unchanged here.

author: msywulak
body:
Two things, both from the README pass.

## 1. `/audit-*` rename

The `-audit` suffix scattered the family across four letters in the command list. Renamed so they group:

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| `/contracts-audit` | `/audit-contracts` |
| `/docs-audit` | `/audit-docs` |
| `/prod-audit` | `/audit-prod` |
| `/www-audit` | `/audit-www` |
| — | **`/audit-readme`** (new) |

Live cross-references updated: `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/agents/audits.md`, and the commands that reference each other (`blog.md`, `audit-docs.md`, `audit-prod.md`, `audit-contracts.md`). Verified zero stale names remain in live files.

Historical references in `.claude/research/` and `docs/adr/` **deliberately keep the old names** — they record what was run at the time, and rewriting them would falsify the record. Noted in `audits.md` so it doesn't read as an oversight.

## 2. `/audit-readme`

README.md was covered by neither `/audit-www` (scopes to `apps/www`) nor `/audit-docs` (`apps/docs`). It drifts by a mechanism those two don't share: **nothing in the shipping loop touches it.** No gate, no route, no test points at the README — so a milestone can add an entire pillar without it ever being opened. The drift is *omission-shaped*: what's written stays true while describing less and less of the product.

The command encodes three traps I hit auditing it by hand, so the next run doesn't re-hit them:

- **The plugin count looks wrong and isn't.** `ls plugins/` returns 25 against a stated 24 — but `check-plugin-count.sh` owns the counting rule and excludes one directory. Hand-counting manufactures a false finding. Part B is guard-first for exactly this reason.
- **Liveness claims look like drift and usually aren't.** "Google Chat coming soon" reads stale next to 8 adapter files, especially right after www was corrected. But `gchat` is the only `coming_soon` entry in the catalog, and GitHub/Linear are action targets rather than chat. Part C's rule: resolve against the install gate, never the file listing.
- **Positioning and accuracy need different permission.** Fix factual drift inline; only ever *propose* a re-positioning. An agent shouldn't quietly change what someone's front door leads with.

## Factual README fixes applied

- **Security table named Firecracker as an isolation tier.** It isn't one — it appears in the codebase only as a comment about Vercel Sandbox's underlying MMDS. The same row omitted `vercel-sandbox`, which is the actual SaaS default. Both corrected.
- **Architecture tree was missing 4 of 14 packages** — `webhook-publisher`, `oauth-helper`, `okf-bundle`, `fumadocs-okf`.

## Not fixed here

The README has **zero mentions** of Knowledge Base, dashboards, learned patterns, answer styles, or durable sessions — five shipped subsystems, two with their own ADRs. That's a positioning call, so it's reported and left for the maintainer.

Verified: `check-plugin-count.sh` still passes.

Found by the weekly overwatch sweep, Section 12.

`check-evolves-not-deprecates.sh` exited 1 (DRIFT) on one line: `Core/products/_intake/2026-07-19-signal-dirt-census/census.md:114`. That line is a census row whose subject is a malformed YAML `catch_mechanism` value. The string that tripped the matcher is a **filename in a data cell** — `SIG-EXEC-2026-06-05-ecosystem-deprecation-correction.md` — not an assertion about intent-site's lifecycle. Canon (evolves in place, deprecation gates on Phase 3) is not contradicted anywhere.

The script's printed remedy is actively wrong here: editing a census row to satisfy a grep would corrupt a record that accurately describes a real file with a real defect.

Why it matters beyond one line: this scan is the recurrence-prevention catch-net for SIG-EXEC-2026-06-05, so its exit code needs to mean something. Left as-is it flags the identical line every week, and the fail-closed discipline around exit 2 weakens when exit 1 is known noise.

Proposes extending the existing exclusion set (which already covers `.intent/` and `archive/`) to enumeration artifacts, with a narrower token-context alternative noted.

body:
## The problem with the green suite

Both suites passed — but an audit of today's fixes against the tests found **9 of them asserted nowhere**. A later change could silently undo any one. A green run on incomplete coverage is worse than no run, because it invites trust it hasn't earned.

The mail-pipeline text logic — where today's hardest bugs lived — had **no repo coverage at all**. It was only ever checked with throwaway scripts containing hand-copied logic, which can drift from the deployed code and produce a false green.

## Tests now exercise the real code

Extracted the pure helpers into shared plain-ESM modules that **both the Deno functions and the Node tests import**:

- `_shared/email-text.mjs` — MIME-tree body extraction, quoted-thread trimming, HTML entity decoding
- `_shared/mime-headers.mjs` — RFC 2047 header encoding (the garbled subject)

Dependency-free, using only `atob`/`TextEncoder`, so Deno and Node import them unchanged. `gmail-sync` and `gmail-send` now import rather than carry their own copies.

**`tests/email-text.test.mjs` — 35 assertions** covering the four bugs actually reported (garbled subject, snippet-instead-of-body, `'` leaking, quoted thread attached) plus the over-trimming guards that stop the fix eating real content.

## 11 new browser checks

`full-sweep.cjs` now covers fixes that had none: mobile Dashboard tab, admin password prompt, cross-sell draft target field, the auto-sync throttle (including that the repeat is blocked — that's what prevents a render→sync→render loop), and the clients table body id.

## Two of my own test bugs, fixed not papered over

1. A length assertion depended on how long the fixture happened to be, and broke when I shortened it. Now a ratio.
2. Teardown removed any fixed high-z-index layer — which deleted `#pw-ov`, the admin password overlay that **ships in index.html** — making `openAdmin()` throw on null. It now snapshots the page's own top-level elements after boot and removes only layers the run created.

## Totals

| Suite | Checks |
|---|---|
| `email-text.test.mjs` (unit, no browser) | 35 ✅ |
| `smoke.test.cjs` (merge gate) | 10 ✅ |
| `full-sweep.cjs` (broad) | 88 ✅ |

**133 checks, all passing.** CI runs all three, unit tests first since they fail fastest and localise best.

author: thiagoesteves
body:
## Summary
- `Appup.make/6` carried a `transforms` argument and `[module]` typespec straight over from Distillery's original `appups.ex`, where it fed a `Transform.up/down` plugin behaviour letting custom modules rewrite the generated instruction list (e.g. force `:soft_purge`). Jellyfish never ported that behaviour - the parameter was bound to `_transforms` and silently discarded, so passing anything there did nothing, with no error or warning.
- Confirmed with the maintainer this is intentional scope, not a gap to fill: Jellyfish's model is deliberately simpler than Distillery's - no per-app transform plugins, generation runs automatically as a release step, and the one supported way to hand-tweak an appup is `EDIT_APPUP` for local testing (not CI).
- So this drops the dead parameter and its redundant 6-arity `@spec` rather than implementing the missing behaviour. `Appup.make` is now `make/5`. The only internal caller (`GenAppup`) already always passed `[]`, so no runtime behavior changes.

## Risk assessment
- **Impact:** `Appup.make/6` no longer exists (`make/5` only). This is a public function in a published hex package, so technically a backwards-incompatible signature change for anyone calling `make/6` directly - though since the 6th argument never did anything, no caller's behavior could have depended on its value. Worth a line in the next version's CHANGELOG when cutting a release.
- **Blast radius:** two files; the only internal caller (`GenAppup`) updated in the same commit.
- **Regression risk:** low. Full suite passes unchanged; existing `Appup` tests already called the 5-arg form.
- **Rollback plan:** revert this commit.

## Test plan
- [x] `mix test --warnings-as-errors` - 49 tests, 0 failures
- [x] `mix format --check-formatted`
- [x] `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` - no warnings

author: rimgosu
body:
## 배경

이 레포의 `.claude/commands`, `.claude/skills` 를 `~/.claude` 로 옮기는 수단이 없어서 매번 수동 복붙이었다. readme의 다른 스크립트들처럼 **clone 없이 `curl | bash`** 로 되게 했다.

## 사용

```sh
# 설치
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rimgosu/script/refs/heads/main/install-claude-dir.sh | bash

# 무엇이 바뀌는지 먼저 확인 (권장)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rimgosu/script/refs/heads/main/install-claude-dir.sh | bash -s -- --dry-run --diff
```

## 설계

- **항목 단위 덮어쓰기** — 대상 디렉토리를 통째로 지우지 않는다. `~/.claude` 에는 이 레포에 없는 로컬 전용 커맨드/스킬이 많아서, 전체 동기화(rsync --delete 류)를 하면 그게 다 날아간다. 반대로 스킬은 **디렉토리째 교체**해서 레포에서 삭제된 파일이 남지 않게 했다
- **소스 결정 순서** — `--local` > 스크립트 옆의 `.claude`(= clone 상태) > 원격 tarball. `curl | bash` 면 `BASH_SOURCE` 가 실파일이 아니므로 자동으로 tarball 경로를 탄다 (public repo라 인증 불필요)
- **백업** — 덮어쓴 항목은 `~/.claude/.install-backup/<타임스탬프>/` 로. 개수를 세서 실제 백업이 있을 때만 안내한다
- **`SUBDIRS` 배열** — `hooks` 등도 이름만 추가하면 같은 방식으로 동기화된다

## `--dry-run --diff` 를 넣은 이유

동기화가 **레포 → `~/.claude` 한 방향뿐**이라, `~/.claude` 에서 직접 고친 게 있으면 레포의 구버전으로 덮인다. 실제로 이 작업 중 확인해보니 **`aws-quiz-rimnote` 가 로컬 쪽이 더 최신**이었다 (로컬에만 "원문 문단 구조 유지, 불릿화 금지" 지시가 추가돼 있음). 그래서 덮어쓰기 전에 diff를 볼 수단을 넣고, readme·`--help`에 방향이 한쪽뿐이라는 경고를 명시했다.

> 후속: 위 `aws-quiz-rimnote` 로컬 개선분은 아직 이 레포에 반영돼 있지 않다. 이 스크립트를 쓰기 전에 레포로 먼저 올려야 한다.

## 검증

- 3개 실행 경로 모두 확인: local(clone) / tarball(stdin으로 파이프해 `curl | bash` 재현) / `--help`
- `--dest` 로 임시 디렉토리에 **실제 쓰기** 후 확인:
  - 로컬 전용 `commands/local-only.md`, `skills/my-local-only/` 보존됨
  - 스킬 안에 심어둔 잔여파일 `STALE.md` 가 제거됨 (백업에는 남음)
  - 백업 내용 정확 (`.install-backup/<ts>/commands/worktree.md`, `.../skills/aws-quiz-rimnote/STALE.md`)
  - 2회차 실행 시 전부 `=` (멱등), 백업 줄 미출력
- `bash -n` 문법 검사, exit code 0 확인 (EXIT 트랩이 non-zero를 반환해 exit 1이 되던 문제 수정)

author: peace-cyber09
body:
# fix(#1079): Skeleton pills and clean fallback for CategorySection

## Summary

When category fetch requests failed or returned an empty array,
`CategorySection` had two distinct bugs:

1. **Wrong skeleton behaviour** — `categoriesToRender` fell back to
   `defaultCategories` while `isLoading` was still `true`, so
   `CategoryChips` rendered both the skeleton pills *and* the real pill
   buttons simultaneously (the `isLoading` / `!isLoading` branches inside
   `CategoryChips` are not mutually exclusive at the data level).

2. **Render-phase side-effect** — `onError(...)` was called directly in the
   render body, firing on every re-render, not once per error.

## Changes

**`apps/web/components/events/category-section.tsx`**

- Moved `onError` call into a `useEffect` (deps: `[error, onError]`) so it
  fires exactly once each time an error first appears.
- Decoupled the `categoriesToRender` derivation from the loading state:
  - While `isLoading === true` → pass an empty array to `CategoryChips`
    together with `isLoading={true}`, letting the existing skeleton branch
    in `CategoryChips` render 6 animated placeholder pills cleanly.
  - After load resolves → use API data if non-empty, otherwise fall back to
    `defaultCategories`, ensuring the section is never blank.
- Added a `hasCategories` guard that returns `null` for the entire section
  only if loading is complete *and* `categoriesToRender` is still empty
  (defensive; unreachable today given the fallback, but prevents a blank
  layout gap if `defaultCategories` is ever removed).
- Added a matching skeleton for the "Browse by Category" heading so the
  heading line doesn't float in empty space above the pill skeletons during
  load.
- Typed `defaultCategories` explicitly as `DiscoverCategory[]` and moved the
  stray `import { CategoryChips }` to the top of the import block.

## Acceptance Criteria

| Criterion | Status |
|-----------|--------|
| Skeleton pills render during the loading state | ✅ |
| Empty/failed fetch does not produce a blank layout gap | ✅ |
| Section is hidden cleanly if no categories are available | ✅ |

## How to Test

1. Throttle the network to Slow 3G in DevTools — confirm 6 animated skeleton
   pills and a skeleton heading appear while the request is in-flight.
2. Block the `/api/events/discover/categories` request in DevTools — confirm
   the section falls back to the 10 default category pills with no console
   errors and no blank gap.
3. Return an empty array `[]` from the API — same result as above.

## Related

Closes #1079

author: boseshittu2323-design
body:
subscribe() previously stored any Address as the token without verifying it implements SEP-41. An invalid token address would produce a subscription that always fails at payment time, wasting storage rent and returning an opaque error on execute_payment().

Changes:
- error.rs: add InvalidTokenAddress = 11 to ContractError enum.
- lib.rs (subscribe): add step 3 — token address validation: (a) Self-address guard: return InvalidTokenAddress if token equals the contract's own address (prevents re-entrancy risk). (b) SEP-41 liveness probe: call token.decimals() — a cheap, read-only cross-contract call. If the address is not a deployed contract or does not implement SEP-41, the invocation traps and the transaction reverts before any state is written. (c) Address tracking check: call token.balance(subscriber) to confirm the token contract tracks this address type.

Closes #343

## Operator feedback round 2 (attended, 2026-07-27 morning)

1. **Home default = pure closest-first.** The saved quiz profile no longer silently shapes the location results' order ("showing interesting ones, not near ones"). Default ranking = proximity among open bars, full stop. The profile MOVED, didn't vanish: it pre-fills the Tweak-the-vibe surface, and applying there (night-scoped, explicit) is now the only way vibes shape the home ranking. author: tannergooding
body:
Fixes #131390.

`Microsoft.Bcl.Memory.Tests` links `System.Memory/tests/AllocationHelper.cs` and targets `net481`, where `NativeMemory` doesn't exist. #131280 switched that helper from `Marshal.AllocHGlobal` to `NativeMemory` without accounting for the shared compile, breaking `windows-x64 Release Libraries_NET481`.

Rather than reverting to `Marshal.AllocHGlobal` -- which is `LocalAlloc` on Windows and would pessimize every modern .NET consumer to fix a `net481`-only compile error -- this adds a test-only `NativeMemory` polyfill under `Common/tests`, alongside the `RuntimeHelpers` polyfill already linked into the same `.NETFramework` `ItemGroup`.

`System.Memory.Tests` is `$(NetCoreAppCurrent)`-only, so `Microsoft.Bcl.Memory.Tests` is the only project that picks the polyfill up.

----------

The one unavoidable change in `AllocationHelper` itself is the argument cast:

```diff
-                memory = (IntPtr)NativeMemory.Alloc((nuint)size);
+                memory = (IntPtr)NativeMemory.Alloc((nuint)(void*)size);
```

`IntPtr`/`UIntPtr` aren't the numeric types on .NETFramework, so `(nuint)size` is `CS0030` there -- that's the second error in the issue, and it's independent of the polyfill. The pointer round-trip is legal on both and compiles to nothing.

----------

Validated locally on Windows x64:

| Leg | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `Microsoft.Bcl.Memory.Tests` `net481` innerloop | 548 passed |
| `Microsoft.Bcl.Memory.Tests` `net481` outerloop | 2 passed |
| `Microsoft.Bcl.Memory.Tests` netcoreapp innerloop | 548 passed |
| `System.Memory.Tests` innerloop | 52,929 passed |
| `System.Memory.Tests` outerloop | 31 passed |

The outerloop runs cover the remaining `AllocationHelper` consumers (`Overflow`, `Clear`, `BinarySearch`, `Base64`, `Base64Url`). Stashing the fix reproduces the exact `CS0103`/`CS0030` errors from the issue.

CC. @dotnet/area-system-memory

> [!NOTE]
> This PR description and the code changes were drafted with GitHub Copilot.

author: stonesthrows
body:
Below 769px the slide-out sidebar was the **only** navigation in the app — the top `.nav`/`.sub-nav` were `display:none`, and `.botnav` was `display:none` at *both* breakpoints, so the bottom tab bar in the markup never rendered at any width. But the sidebar was still styled and wired as the desktop rail.

Mobile now has three layers: **topbar → sub-nav strip → bottom tab bar**. The bar says which section you're in, the strip says which view within it, and the drawer is the escape hatch for everything else rather than the only route to anything.

Touched: `css/app.css`, `js/home.js`, `js/app.js`, `jewelry-workflow.html`. **The desktop rail is unchanged** — still 196px wide, still 33px rows, no strip, no bar, same 70px content offset. Verified, not assumed.

---

## 1 — Make the mobile sidebar behave like a real drawer

- Nav rows were ~33px tall (9px padding, 12.5px text), well under the 44px touch minimum; the hamburger was a 32px box. Rows are now 44px with 14px text, and the drawer widens from 196px to `min(280px, 82vw)` to give them room.
- The app is an installed PWA with `viewport-fit=cover`, but only the dead bottom nav consumed safe-area insets — on a notched phone the topbar and its title sat under the status bar. Topbar, sidebar brand, footer and landscape edge now all clear their insets, and sidebar height moves to `100dvh` so the last row isn't stranded behind Safari's collapsing URL bar.
- Added scroll lock (closing the drawer used to dump you at the top of the page), finger-tracking swipe-to-close with a 30% threshold and an axis lock so a vertical drag still scrolls the list, Escape, and teardown on resize so no stuck overlay survives a rotation.
- Rows were bare `<div onclick>`: not tabbable, no keyboard activation, and the off-canvas drawer stayed in the tab order so it swallowed every Tab press before page content got one. Rows are now `role="button" tabindex="0"` with Enter/Space, the active row carries `aria-current="page"`, a closed drawer is `visibility:hidden`, and an open one traps Tab. Focus only moves on open, so touch users never see a focus ring.

## 2 — Revive the bottom tab bar

Persistent 4-tab bar: **Orders / Inventory / Supplies / More**. Switching between the three highest-traffic sections no longer requires opening the drawer. More opens the same drawer, and the bar hides while it's open (higher z-index — it would otherwise float on top). Both drawer triggers stay in sync on `aria-expanded` and return focus to whichever one was used.

## 3 — Bring back the sub-nav strips, and give Gmail a sidebar row

The `.sub-nav` markup already existed with the right children and mobile-tuned styling (horizontal scroll, 44px targets); the redesign had killed it with a single `display:none`.

This also rescued three tab panels that had **no route from any visible navigation** — on desktop too, not just mobile. `print-bag` and `pj-ref` live in these strips; `gmail` doesn't, so it gets a sidebar row after Trips, matching the old top-nav order.

Chrome height is now derived rather than hardcoded. Four full-height panels (`.rq-page`, `.sot-layout`, `.notes-page`, the print-bag iframe) each subtracted a magic constant — 100px, 116px, 236px — predating both the strip and the bar. They now subtract `--m-chrome`, composed from real heights plus safe-area insets, with the strip's contribution driven by `:has(.sub-nav.active)` so direct tabs correctly get no offset.

## 4 — Auto-hide the strip on scroll-down

Slides up behind the topbar when you scroll down, returns on scroll-up or navigation, always shown near the top. Direction-driven, not position-driven. Content padding is deliberately untouched: the strip is always visible at scroll-top, and past that the padding is off-screen, so there's nothing to reflow and no gap. Only applies where the document scrolls — the full-height panels scroll internally and are sized to fit exactly, so the strip stays put there rather than opening a gap they can't fill.

## 5 — Merge `main`

`main` moved while this was open (ecom bag pricing, inside-stamp text, a component-local `--msg-tail-x` default, and `f300bc2` repairing 15 malformed cache-buster tags). Both conflicts were cache-buster tags in `jewelry-workflow.html`: took main's repairs for `tokens.css` and `customers.js`, and moved `css/app.css`, `js/app.js`, `js/home.js` to `20260727f` so the merged files sit ahead of both sides. No `$V` placeholders or malformed tags remain. `css/app.css` merged cleanly with both sides' changes intact.

All four suites were re-run against the merged tree, not just the pre-merge one — `main` also touched `js/orders.js` and `js/order-normalize.js`.

---

## Bugs found and fixed along the way

- **`.content` bottom padding was being reset.** The `padding: 12px 12px` shorthand in the 640px block overrides the bottom padding set earlier in the file. Harmless while the bar was hidden, but once it was visible the last ~44px of every scrolling page was trapped underneath, unreachable even scrolled to the end.
- **Strip taps left the topbar title and sidebar highlight stale.** The strip calls `switchSubTab()` directly and only `sbNav()` was wired to `_sbSetActive`. Every nav indicator now hangs off `_showPanel`, so all three follow the active panel from one place regardless of which control drove it.
- **Two competing sources of truth for the bottom bar.** A legacy sync in `_scrollActiveIntoView` re-derived the active tab from the old *hidden* top nav, which has no concept of `home` or the "More" grouping — it fought the new sync and left the bar unhighlighted on the landing page. Now one shared function keyed off the active panel.
- **`js/app.js` had a malformed cache-buster** (`?v="20260726e""` — stray quotes break the attribute), so bumps to it were silently not busting the cache. This turned out to be one instance of a broad problem; `main`'s `f300bc2` has since repaired the rest.
- **Designs rendered its raw lowercase id as the page title** (missing `SB_TITLES` entry).

## Verification

Headless Chromium with real CDP touch events at 390×844 and 1280×900, light and dark:

- **44/44** drawer — targets, insets, swipe (short drag snaps back, vertical drag scrolls instead of closing), keyboard, focus. Touch-vs-keyboard focus ring checked against `:focus-visible` rather than assumed.
- **18/18** bottom bar — navigation, highlighting, drawer sync, and a *returning* user's restored tab, not just the fresh-session default.
- **15/15** sub-nav across **all 21 destinations** — each reachable, correct strip (or none), strip flush under the topbar, and nothing trapped under the bar when scrolled to the bottom.
- **16/16** auto-hide — hide, reveal-while-still-scrolled, reveal at top, reset on navigation, no gap, desktop unaffected.

`tests/run.js` matches its pre-change baseline with no fingerprint drift, which matters here since `_showPanel` now fires on every panel change. Its two failures are pre-existing and were confirmed against unmodified `main`, not assumed: the service-worker cache assertion fails identically on `main`, and the `tvInit` page error is already recorded in `tests/fixtures/fingerprint.json`.

## Still open — flagging, not fixing

- **`js/triplog.js:522`** throws on every weekday load: `tvInit()` does `document.getElementById('tvWrap').style` but `#tvWrap` isn't in the markup. Triplog tab code, and CLAUDE.md says don't touch another tab while working on this one.
- **`bgab` is a dead entry** in `DIRECT_TABS` — no `#tab-bgab` panel exists anywhere in the markup.
- **Vertical chrome** is ~150px on a strip page before auto-hide kicks in. Looked fine in testing, but only real-device use will say whether the hide/reveal threshold feels right against iOS Safari's own collapsing URL bar doing the same dance.

author: alexey-pelykh
body:
## What & why

Fixes #745. Clicking **▶ Start daemon** could be a **silent no-op**: `LoginItemModel.startDaemon()` set `.idle` as soon as `SMAppService.register()` returned, then relied on a `watch` snapshot to leave `.notRunning`. But `register()` only means launchd *accepted the plist* — the plist's `RunAtLoad` still has to spawn the daemon, and that spawn can fail (bad launchd config, crash-loop, sandbox denial) while `register()` reports success. When it does, no daemon comes up, no snapshot arrives, and the card sits silent forever. This is the exact dead-end hit while validating #170 AC2 (the EX_CONFIG spawn failure, #744).

## The fix

After a successful register, `startDaemon()` now **waits for a daemon to actually take the single-instance lock** before resolving:

- reuses the same `daemonLockHeld` flock probe `canStartDaemon` already gates on (#742) — `canStartDaemon` guaranteed the lock was **free** at the click, so a lock that becomes held within the window is the daemon our register just started;
- lands `.idle` as soon as a daemon comes up (panel then leaves `.notRunning` on the next `watch` snapshot, as before);
- else lands `.failed` with an actionable **"The daemon was registered but didn't start. Check Console for details."** — a reason the `StartDaemonCard` **already** renders (red label), so no new UI;
- the `registering` spinner is held across the wait (button disabled — no double-click), and the failed state leaves `canStartDaemon` true so the user can retry.

Poll interval / timeout are **injectable** (prod: 500 ms / 8 s) so the timeout-path test runs in ~ms.

## Scope

- UI-model only. **No wire / schema change**; the app stays a pure IPC client (zero-egress guard passes).
- The reason copy lives in `LoginItemModel` (like the existing `startFailureReason`) — keeps the model ServiceManagement-free so it compiles into the headless `MenubarTests` bundle.

## Testing

`xcodebuild test -scheme Menubar` (Debug, unsigned) — **477 tests, 0 failures**. `LoginItemModelTests` now 16 tests:

- `testStartDaemonSuccessWhenDaemonComesUp` — register + daemon takes the lock → `.idle`.
- `testStartDaemonRegistersButDaemonNeverComesUpSurfacesFailure` (new) — register succeeds, daemon never comes up → `.failed` with the "registered but…" reason (the #745 regression guard).
- All existing start/two-owner/liveness-gate tests unchanged and green.

## Bug signale par Sebastien

`/{fr,en}/esn-paris-developpeurs-seniors` = **404** en prod. Impact : les posts LinkedIn Paris devaient pointer sur cette page, contournement obligatoire vers `consultant-informatique-paris`.

## Root cause

Landing bien creee dans le CMS Payload (id=7, timestamp 2026-07-27 09:47) MAIS le route handler `app/[lang]/[slug]/page.tsx` ne lit **que** `lib/landing-pages.ts` (statique) via `generateStaticParams()` + `dynamicParams=false`. Les entries CMS Payload landing-pages sont ignorees par le build Next.js.

Documente dans le skill `abbeal-cms` (correctif W29 2026-07-13) : "Collection landing-pages — draft/publish NON fiable via l'API REST".

## Fix

Copie de l'entry CMS vers le repo :

- `lib/landing-page-bodies.json` : +1 key `esn-paris-developpeurs-seniors` avec 17 body blocks + 6 FAQ items (fr)
- `lib/landing-pages.ts` : +1 entry (position 13), FR-only (comme `consultant-informatique-paris`) :

author: am225723
body:
## Summary
Next slice from the Advisor Dashboard feature audit: **#26 Reports**, flagged as "real PDF/HTML/CSV export exists elsewhere in the app but not surfaced in the Advisor Workspace."

- `TherapistDashboard.jsx` has real, working report generators (`handleExportCSV`, `handleExportReports`, `handleGenerateReport`) that pull live client data (assessments, journals, moods, activity) into CSV and printable-HTML reports — but they're entirely unreachable from the redesigned Advisor Workspace.
- The workspace's existing "reports" surface (`generateWorkspaceReport`/`loadWorkspaceReports`, the AI Snapshot/Change Summary features) is a *different* thing — AI-generated narrative text, not a structured export of the client's real record.
- New **Export report** action in the client detail header builds a printable HTML report — wound pattern assessment history, between-session mood/homework/journal activity, treatment goals, identified parts, and recent session notes — entirely from data the workspace has **already loaded** for the selected client (`assessmentHistory`, `betweenSession`, `goals`, `parts`, `savedNotes`). No new Supabase queries. Opens in a new window with a "Print / Save as PDF" button, the same mechanism `TherapistDashboard.jsx` already uses.
- Gated behind the same "claim this client first" (`canWrite`) pattern as other write-oriented actions in the client header, consistent with how detail loading itself depends on an active assignment.
- All interpolated fields (name, notes text, part descriptions, etc.) are HTML-escaped before being written into the report window, since this data can contain arbitrary client/therapist-entered text.

**Deliberately out of scope for this slice**: caseload-wide CSV export (`handleExportCSV`/`handleExportReports` in `TherapistDashboard.jsx`). Those operate on fields (progress %, modules completed, wound scores) that are only populated in the workspace once a client's detail has been individually loaded — the caseload list itself carries neutral placeholder values until then, so a bulk export today would either need a new "fetch every client's detail up front" pattern or would silently export garbage for anyone not yet opened. Left as a possible follow-up.

## Test plan
- [x] New tests in `advisorWorkspaceLoader.test.js`: `buildClientReportHtml` renders real data (assessment scores, mood entries, goals, parts, notes), degrades to neutral empty states when nothing real exists, and HTML-escapes injected content to prevent script injection.
- [x] New tests in `advisorWorkspaceView.test.js`: `onExportReport` is gated by `canWrite` (undefined for unclaimed clients, wired for claimed ones) and routes to the handler with the correct client id.
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 90/90 tests pass in the two touched test files
- [x] `npx eslint` on all changed files — clean, no new errors or warnings
- [x] `npm run build` — succeeds

author: mnews-mma
body:
## 結論: 停止条件に該当したため、修正(手順2以降)は実装していない

RIZIN.2/.5/.10/.21について、既存の`splitIntoBoutChunks`/`parseBoutChunk`(無改変)にresultsPageIdの取得HTMLを通して失敗箇所を特定した結果、**4件とも異なる原因**だった。指示書の停止条件「失敗原因が3種類以上に分かれた」に該当する。

| 大会 | 開催日 | 原因 |
|---|---|---|
| RIZIN.2 | 2016-09-25 | `<h2 class="article-heading">`自体が存在しない旧`#match-list`構造(RIZIN.1と同種の個別対応が必要) |
| RIZIN.5 | 2017-04-16 | フォーマットBの勝敗マーカーregexが半角`[WIN]/[LOSE]`前提だが実際は全角`［WIN］／［LOSE］` |
| RIZIN.10 | 2018-05-06 | フォーマットAのspan regexが`font-weight:bold`(スペースなし)前提だが実際は`font-weight: bold`(スペースあり) |
| RIZIN.21 | 2020-02-22 | フォーマットAの`raw-html` div抽出が非貪欲マッチのため、動画埋め込み用の1つ目のdivで打ち切られ結果本体の2つ目に届かない |

RIZIN.5・.10・.21は既存フォーマット関数への局所パッチで直りそうだが、RIZIN.2だけはRIZIN.1と同様「新規パーサーを書くか手動書き起こしするか」という設計判断が要る(かつ2015年の2大会など同種の旧テンプレート大会が他にもある可能性)。指示書は4大会の原因調査を一体のタスクとして依頼しており、停止条件が全体にかかるため、3件だけ先行実装することもしていない。

`data/`・`src/`・`scripts/`への変更なし(git diffゼロ)。取得したHTMLはリポジトリ外のスクラッチ領域に保存し、gitには含めていない。

## 停止条件の該非
- 失敗原因が3種類以上 → **該当(4種類)**
- 既存80大会の差分ゼロ / 必達不変条件 / ランキング順位移動20件以内 → 手順2以降を実施していないため評価対象外

出力: `out/rizin-parse-failures.md`

author: bits-bytes-nn
body:
## 무엇

`_posts/2026-07-27-ai-ready-data-semantic-layer-knowledge-graph.md` — Insights / Data-Architecture 카테고리의 14,671어절 심층 분석 글 1편과 자체 다이어그램 4개를 추가합니다.

**관통 논지**: AI-ready 데이터의 본질은 깨끗한 데이터가 아니라 맥락을 기계가 실행할 수 있는 형태로 새겨 넣은 데이터다. 출발점은 Sequeda et al. 2023의 16.7% → 54.2%(zero-shot text-to-SQL 대 온톨로지·매핑으로 감싼 지식 그래프)이고, 데이터 형태별로 맥락층이 셋(정형→시맨틱 레이어, 비정형→지식 그래프/GraphRAG, 메타데이터→카탈로그)이며 셋이 MCP 하나로 수렴한다는 지도를 세운 뒤 각 갈래를 해부합니다.

## 구성

| 절 | 내용 |
|----|------|
| §1 | Analytics-ready / ML-ready / AI-ready 구분 — 맥락이 어디 사는가 |
| §2 | 세 갈래 지형도, 그리고 종착점이 사람에서 에이전트로 바뀌며 가치가 오른 이유 |
| §3 | 택소노미→온톨로지→지식 그래프 사다리, RDF/OWL 대 프로퍼티 그래프, 2024~26년 움직인 표준(GQL ISO/IEC 39075, RDF 1.2 reification) |
| §4 | GraphRAG 구축 스펙트럼(관리형→오픈소스→자체구축)과 무너진 인덱싱 비용 |
| §5 | CQ에서 거꾸로 내려가는 시맨틱 레이어 구현, semantics-as-code |
| §6 | 이기종 통합, 에이전트 거버넌스(RFC 8693/8707, 혼동된 대리자), MCP 수렴 |
| §7 | 사례 3건(은행·BenevolentAI·Cerebras) + 실패 모드 3건 + 반면교사 셋 + 판단 프레임 |
| §8 | 손익분기선이 이동했다는 결론 회수 |

## 품질 게이트

`.claude/skills/write-post` 파이프라인으로 17라운드를 돌렸습니다.

- **루브릭 6축 최종**: accuracy 9 / faithfulness 9 / depth 9 / structure 9 / voice 9 / pedagogy 9 — `factual_errors` 0건, `unsupported_claims` 0건, `pass: true` (팩트 두 축 임계 9, 나머지 8)
- **결정적 검사**: 14,671어절, H2 9개, `~다:` 종결 0, 이모지 0, `§N` 상호참조 전부 실존, 참고문헌 73개, 외부 이미지 8개 HTTP 200, alt 텍스트 전부 존재
- **빌드**: `jekyll build --future` 무경고, `htmlproofer`(CI 동일 옵션) 통과

인용은 전부 1차 출처로 대조했고, 검증 과정에서 나온 주요 수정은 다음과 같습니다.

- RDF 1.2 `<< >>`를 "사실을 다른 사실의 주어로 삼는 문법"이라 잘못 쓴 것 → 명세 대조 후 reifier/triple term 구조로 재작성(Turtle 전개형 포함)
- dbt 벤치마크의 "전체 스키마를 컨텍스트로 밀어 넣었다" 단서가 표 전체에 걸린 것처럼 읽히던 것 → 원문대로 modeled project 비교 1건으로 범위 축소
- Cerebras 원문이 HTTP 500이라 아카이브 스냅샷 URL·날짜를 본문에 명시
- 접근이 막힌 인용(NeOn Springer 챕터, 스캔본 Grüninger & Fox 1995) → 저자 배포본 PDF와 DOI가 해소되는 자매 논문으로 대조 경로 병기

벤더 자체 측정치(LazyGraphRAG의 0.1%·700배, AWS·Databricks 제품 서술 등)는 모두 "자체 측정, 독립 재현 아님"으로 라벨링했습니다.

## 다이어그램

Excalidraw 4개(`.excalidraw` 소스 + PNG 함께 커밋):

- `ai-ready-convergence` — 세 데이터 형태 → 세 맥락층 → MCP 수렴
- `context-three-layers` — 온톨로지/지식 그래프는 스키마·인스턴스로 수직, 시맨틱 레이어는 직교하는 별개 축
- `vector-vs-graphrag` — 같은 두 홉 질문에서 벡터 RAG가 연결 고리 조각을 놓치고 GraphRAG가 경로로 답하는 대조
- `confused-deputy-defense` — 같은 질문이 서비스 계정 경로와 위임 신원 경로에서 어디서 멈추는가

`assets/images/render-diagrams.sh`도 함께 수정했습니다. 하드코딩된 macOS 절대경로를 리포 루트 기준으로 바꿔 다른 머신에서도 돌아가게 하고, 폰트를 Caveat에서 Excalifont로 바꿔 기존 다이어그램과 서체를 통일했습니다.

## 리뷰 시 봐 주실 것

게이트는 텍스트만 봅니다. 렌더 실물에서 다음을 확인해 주십시오.

- [ ] 라이트박스(glightbox) 개폐 — 앵커 12개(로컬 4 + 외부 8)
- [ ] 외부 hotlink 이미지 8개가 실제로 뜨는지 (htmlproofer는 외부 링크를 건너뜁니다)
- [ ] 본문 유일 수식 `$$\theta$$`의 MathJax 렌더

author: domains-sparstrow
body:
Promotion of `staging` (4 commits) to `main`.

## Merge with a merge commit — not squash

`main`'s ruleset now allows both. Use **"Create a merge commit."** Squashing two
permanent branches is what caused the 10 phantom conflicts on the last promotion:
it writes `main` a new commit holding staging's content with no ancestry link, so
the merge base freezes and every later promotion replays history `main` already
has. See CLAUDE.md → Git flow.

## What's in it

**`1dd31e8` — fix(chat): two user-facing bugs**

The `antigravity` provider invoked `agy --model X --print -`, treating `-` as a
stdin marker. `agy --print` takes the prompt as its *argument value*; there is no
stdin path. So the model received the literal prompt `"-"` every turn and replied
with a generic greeting, ignoring what was typed. Verified against agy v1.1.7:

| Invocation | Result |
|---|---|
| `agy --print -` + stdin | "How can I help you today?" ← the bug |
| `agy --print "<prompt>"` | correct answer |
| `agy --print` + stdin | usage error — no stdin path exists |

The prompt now goes in argv with a byte-budget guard on the transcript, so the
~32KB Windows command-line limit (the reason stdin was originally chosen) can't
be hit. Separately, the sent message rendered twice — the optimistic bubble
stayed mounted after the server round-trip returned the persisted copy; the
predicate is extracted to `lib/chat-pending.ts` and unit-tested.

**`ef82717` — ci(gate): tests now run, and staging is watched**

CI ran `pnpm typecheck` only, and only on `main`. Tests were never run anywhere
in CI, and `staging` — where every feature branch actually lands — had no trigger
at all. 500+ tests were enforced purely by an agent choosing to follow the
Definition of Done by hand.

`test` is a **separate job** from `typecheck` on purpose: `typecheck` is a
required check, and folding tests into it would let a single failure block every
PR to `main` before the job had proven itself.

**`a734204` — fix(core): a real race the first Linux CI run exposed**

That first `test` run failed. Not native modules — reproduced in a `node:24`
container to get actual evidence.

`wakeTask` sets a task `in_progress`, then spawns a real run. With no agent CLI
present the spawn fails, `finalize` marks the run failed, and the task follows to
`failed` — so a test asserting `in_progress` after a fixed 150ms sleep was always
racing that sequence. Windows won the race; `ENOENT` returns faster on Linux. The
spawn is now stubbed, which also satisfies CLAUDE.md's rule that tests never
execute real agent CLIs.

Six uncaught exceptions were the same race from the other side, and this half is
**production code, not a test artifact**: a child's `close` handler calls
`RunManager.finalize`, which called `getDb()` unguarded — throwing out of an
event handler with nothing to catch it. During core shutdown, any run whose child
closes after the DB is closed would throw identically. `finalize` now checks
`isDbOpen()` and logs. `isDbOpen()` was added test-first.

**`2eea7a7` — docs(specs): intake backlog triaged and sequenced**

All 7 open captures triaged against current code and the Phase 6 spec. 0005 was
already shipped (closed). 0007's data layer is already designed as Phase 6e §3.5.
0011 was invalidated by the Curator/intake deletion and needs re-design. Order:
0009 → 0008 → 6-pre → 6a–6f → 0007 → 0011 → 0010 → 0006.

6-pre is rescoped from a "focused pass" to a full frontend redesign, on a
measurement: the UI adopted the shadcn *look* without the shadcn *components* —
18 primitives against Multica's 60 + 12 on the same design system, with `empty`,
`alert`, `sonner` and `field` absent entirely, which makes the Definition of
Done's "all four states, always" currently unsatisfiable.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck` 6/6 clean · `pnpm test` **506 passed / 4 skipped**
(59 shared + 442 core + 5 ui), zero uncaught exceptions.

Verified on **both** platforms — Windows locally, and Linux in a `node:24`
container matching the CI runner. Both chat bugs and the delegation race were
reproduced first, then fixed, with tests written before the fix.

## After merging

1. The `test` job's first run failed and is fixed in `a734204` — a latent race
   Windows was masking, not a native-module problem. Confirm it's green on the
   staging run before promoting.

body:
## Summary
- The startup preflight wrote its only instruction into `briefing.md` while telling the spawned session to treat that same file as untrusted, delimited external data. A compliant model correctly refuses to act on a file it was told to distrust, so the probe reported `session auth: unknown` even when credentials were fine.
- The probe reads no external data by design, so it never needed a `briefing.md` in the first place.

## Changes
- `EphemeralSession` (`src/overseer/session.rs`) now takes its CLI prompt as a field instead of hardcoding it, so different callers can pass different framings.
- Extracted the existing "treat `briefing.md` as data only" instruction into `session::BRIEFING_PROMPT`, used unchanged by judgment (`judge.rs`), triage (`triage.rs`), review (`review.rs`), and ops (`discord/ops_session.rs`) sessions — all of which genuinely stage external/untrusted content in `briefing.md`.
- `session/preflight.rs` no longer writes `briefing.md` at all; it passes its self-contained instruction (write `result.json` with `{"ok":true}`) directly as the session prompt, so there is nothing left for the session to be told to distrust.
- Updated call sites and tests (`judge/tests.rs`, `triage/tests.rs`) to pass the new `prompt` field.

## Test Plan
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — pass
- `cargo test` — 1215 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — pass
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps` — pass
- Not performed: live daemon reload + `robco overseer status` check. That requires a release/install/service-restart cycle that is out of scope for this change; the existing `preflight::tests` (`only_an_auth_refusal_reports_a_broken_credential`, etc.) already cover that a broken-credential outcome (`AuthFailed`) stays distinguishable from a probe that ran and produced no result (`Unknown`), and that behavior is untouched by this change.

## Impact
- Preflight probes on a daemon with working credentials should now actually produce `result.json` and report `session auth: ok`, instead of falsely reporting `unknown` due to the self-contradictory prompt.
- No behavior change for judgment, triage, review, or ops sessions — they keep using the same briefing-fencing prompt as before.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added/updated where needed (call-site + fixture updates for the new `prompt` field)
- [x] `task check` equivalent (fmt + test + clippy + rustdoc) passes locally
- [ ] Live daemon verification (out of scope for this PR; see Test Plan)

author: phisch90
body:
Beide Grafiken kommen rein — aber nicht beide für denselben Zweck.

## Welche als Symbol

Als App-Symbol taugt nur das **Monogramm**: bis 40 px bleiben der d20 und die „35" erkennbar. Beim **Helden-Bild** zerfallen drei Gesichter und die Wortmarke schon bei 80 px. Ich habe beide in echten Symbolgrößen (180 / 120 / 80 / 60 / 40 px) nebeneinandergelegt und angesehen, statt es zu schätzen.

Das Helden-Bild ist deshalb nicht verschwendet: es sitzt jetzt als Kopfbild in den **Einstellungen**, wo es die Fläche hat, die es braucht.

## Der Satz

Erzeugt von `tools/brand/build-icons.py`, die Master liegen daneben in `tools/brand/`:

| Datei | Zweck |
| --- | --- |
| `icon-192/512.png` | Manifest, `purpose: "any"` — das Abzeichen, wie es gemeint ist |
| `icon-maskable-192/512.png` | Manifest, `purpose: "maskable"` — mit eigener Luft |
| `apple-touch-icon.png` (180) | iOS liest fürs Startbildschirm-Symbol **nur** diese Zeile im Kopf, nie das Manifest |
| `favicon-32.png` | Browser-Tab (vorher wurde das 192er heruntergerechnet) |
| `logo.png` (480) | Kopfbild in den Einstellungen |

**Der maskable-Punkt ist der eigentliche Fund.** Bisher stand `purpose: "any maskable"` an einem randvollen Abzeichen — eine Android-Maske (Kreis, Squircle, Tropfen) schneidet dabei den Goldrand rundherum ab. Ich habe alle drei Maskenformen simuliert: Vollformat zerlegt den Rahmen, die maskable-Fassung (Abzeichen auf 78 %) bleibt in jeder Form heil. Deshalb jetzt zwei getrennte Sätze statt einem doppelt belegten.

## Dateigröße

128 Farben statt volle Farbtiefe — bei dieser flächigen Grafik auch bei 4× Zoom nicht zu unterscheiden, halbiert aber die Größe. Der ganze Satz plus Kopfbild: **391 kB statt 1122 kB**. Das zählt hier, weil die App alle Dateien offline vorhält.

Die Master (2× ~1,9 MB) liegen bewusst in `tools/brand/` und nicht in `public/` — so wandern sie nicht in den Offline-Vorrat, bleiben aber im Repo, damit die Symbole reproduzierbar sind.

## Geprüft

Gegen den **echten Build**, nicht den Dev-Server (dort erzeugt das PWA-Plugin gar kein Manifest — mein erster Testlauf ist genau darüber gestolpert):

- jede im `<head>` und im Manifest genannte Datei antwortet mit 200
- das Manifest trennt `any` und `maskable`, und kein Eintrag ist doppelt belegt
- `apple-touch-icon.png` ist tatsächlich 180×180
- das Kopfbild rendert auf der Einstellungs-Seite (160×160)

Dazu `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm -r test` (252) und ein Build mit `PAGES_BASE=/Chardex35/`, in dem die Pfade korrekt auf `/Chardex35/…` zeigen.

body:
## Summary

Prevent interrupted downloads and failed writes from replacing valid files with partial content, and centralize the single-file replacement contract in a reusable workspace crate.

## Changes

- add `maa-atomic-fs` for same-directory staging, file synchronization, and atomic replacement of existing destinations
- preserve existing Unix permission bits and use normal umask-filtered creation permissions for new write-like files while keeping staging files private during writes
- migrate maa-cli configuration, import, migration, and Copilot cache writes to the shared helper
- commit ETag response bodies before updating validators, preserve the previous cache on transfer failure, and remove stale sidecars when a 200 response omits ETag
- keep 304 and check-interval behavior unchanged, including timestamp refresh handling on Windows
- atomically replace generated release JSON and shell metadata
- add regression coverage for failed transfers, ETag ordering and removal, conditional requests, freshness checks, permissions, and replacement behavior

The helper intentionally does not provide multi-file transactions, writer locking, metadata preservation beyond documented Unix permission bits, or parent-directory synchronization. Windows replacement uses the overwrite-capable persistence path from `tempfile`, covered by the Windows CI jobs.

## Validation

- `cargo +nightly fmt --check`
- affected crate Clippy checks with warnings denied
- `cargo test -p maa-atomic-fs` (9 passed)
- `cargo test -p maa-installer --features ureq/json` (65 passed)
- `cargo test -p xtask` (1 passed)
- `cargo x test --no-core-tests`
- design, adversarial, and patch reviews

author: supermo0
body:
## What

Swept `services/api` (95 Python files) and `supabase/` (12 migrations + seed) for comments and docstrings that restate what the code already says.

## Counts

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `#` comment lines | 313 | 41 |
| Docstring lines | 2,222 (550 docstrings) | 57 (57 docstrings, all single-line) |
| **Backend Python total** | **2,535** | **98** |
| SQL comment lines | 155 | 40 |

Diff: 108 files, +128 / −2,828.

## What was kept, and why

Three categories survive, because none of them can be recovered by reading the code:

**1. Docstrings that are not documentation.** FastAPI publishes a route handler's docstring as the OpenAPI `description`, and `tests/test_openapi.py` states that document is the contract `@sync/api-client` is generated from. Pydantic does the same for a model's docstring. And `sync_parsers/schema.py`'s docstrings are part of the structured-output JSON Schema sent to the extractor — they are prompt, not prose. All kept, all compressed to one line.

**2. About a dozen `#` comments marking a trap** — places where removing the comment invites a change that breaks something silently:

- the `sqlacodegen` flags in `scripts/generate_models.py` (`nojoined` because three tables share a PK with the table they reference and are queues, not subclasses)
- the Storage client's trailing slash, which the suite's warnings-as-errors setting depends on
- middleware add-order (Starlette treats last-added as outermost, so the access log must run inside the request id)
- the `numeric(4,1)` column behind `MAX_YEARS_EXPERIENCE`
- the test truncation that must skip `RESTART IDENTITY` on tables the `postgres` role does not own, and must delete Storage objects through Storage's API first
- the conftest URL that has to match `additional_redirect_urls` in `supabase/config.toml`

**3. SQL comments stating an invariant DDL cannot show:** the shared-PK candidate-XOR-recruiter construction, why RLS is `ENABLED` but deliberately not `FORCED` (FORCE would subject the `postgres` owner to RLS and block migration 11's own seed), why the RAG migration sets `search_path`, and the NULL semantics of the embedding-queue columns.

## Verification

- `ruff check` — clean
- `ruff format --check` — clean
- `mypy` (strict) — clean, 95 files
- `supabase db reset` — all 12 migrations replay
- `pytest` — 243 passed, 5 deselected

The OpenAPI document was diffed against `main`: all 24 operations and every published schema keep the descriptions they had.

## Note

Worth flagging, since it shaped the result: the `#` comments in this repo were overwhelmingly *why*-comments — ADR references, race-condition and constraint rationale — rather than restatements. The bulk of the 2,437-line reduction is therefore docstrings, per the scoping decision on this task, and a fair amount of design rationale went with them. It is all in `git log` if any of it is wanted back.

author: wertania
body: ## Problem A page reference written through the API or the MCP tools ended up as literal text with backslashes instead of a link. An agent writes `[[Target]]` into a page. On a block page that text lands inside an **html** block, and materializing that block runs it through Turndown — which escapes square brackets: `[[Target]]` → `\[\[Target\]\]`. Consequences: - the link extraction regex no longer matches → no link in the graph, no backlink - every `read_page_content` / search hit shows the backslashes - a follow-up edit using the string just read fails, because the block content and the materialized text disagree — surfacing as the misleading `oldString spans multiple blocks` ## Change - **`wikilinks.ts` (new)** — one place for the marker syntax and its three representations: the plain `[[Target]]` marker, the block editor's canonical `[[Target]]`, and the escaped variant Turndown produces. Target/alias are html-escaped; conversion skips `code`/`pre` and tag attributes and is idempotent. - **`materialize-blocks.ts`** — a canonical reference materializes back to a plain `[[Target]]` marker (Turndown rule instead of the default `` `[[Target]]` ``), and escaped markers are restored. The `text` cache, search, embeddings and the link graph therefore always see real references. - **`knowledge-text-edit.ts`** — an edit that writes `[[Target]]` into an html block stores it in the canonical form, so an agent-written reference is a clickable link exactly like one inserted in the editor. An `oldString` copied out of the materialized text (where the reference reads as the bare marker) is matched against the stored form, instead of failing as a cross-block match. - **`knowledge-text-links.ts`** — uses the shared pattern rather than its own copy. Markdown blocks and plain-text pages keep the bare marker; that already is their canonical form. ## Tests - `wikilinks.test.ts` (new, 12 cases): marker detection, conversion to/from html, idempotency, `code`/`pre` and attribute safety, html escaping, unescaping, plus materialization round-trips ending in extractable targets - `knowledge-text-edit.test.ts`: two DB-backed cases — writing references into an html block (stored canonically, clean materialized text, links in the graph) and editing over a reference read back as a plain marker - `bun run typecheck` clean; the wikilink-related suites pass. The remaining failures in `src/lib/knowledge` are the pre-existing embedding tests that need a provider/`MISTRAL_API_KEY` (no outbound API in this environment). Consumer side (editor lifting bare markers into references, MCP tool wording): symbiosika/wiki#125, which bumps the submodule to this commit. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01MntfhVLdgJDhGSGbVV62N4)_

author: rjmendez
body:
The context bridge is now scheduled on `hugbot5000-jetson`, but the units existed only in that box's `/etc/systemd/system` — unversioned, and reproducible only from memory. That is the same fragility the mesh audit flagged for the A2A container, whose `docker run` is likewise hand-typed and referenced by nothing.

## What the README carries

Two things that are not obvious from the unit files and that would hurt on a second node:

- **The local A2A server must support `store_local` (#144).** Against an older server the flag is silently ignored, `context_broadcast` stores before it fans out, and every run re-inserts a copy of the memory it just read — with a fresh id and `created_at`, so the copy looks new next tick and is relayed again. Unbounded growth on one node, no peer required.
- **`aiohttp` is a hard requirement.** The script `sys.exit()`s at import without it, so a missing dependency presents as a unit that fails *instantly* rather than one that quietly does nothing. That is exactly how it read on the Jetson before installing it.

It also records what actually stops the loop, which is not what the code comment implies: the bridge stamps its sends `bridge:<agent_id>`, but the local server overwrites the source with `broadcast:<agent_id>` on the peer hop — so the load-bearing filter is `broadcast:`, and the `bridge:` stamp only matters on the local-store path. Verified on the wire: a bridged memory arrives at the peer as `broadcast:loci`.

## Timer shape

Deliberately **not** `Persistent`. A missed window is not worth catching up, and a burst of back-to-back runs after downtime is the wrong shape for a mesh path. The state file means a skipped tick loses nothing — the next run picks up everything since the last success.

`RandomizedDelaySec=60` keeps it off the same instant as the other timers on the box.

## Verified before scheduling

- echo filter against real data: 24 eligible → 20 sent, 4 excluded, and the 4 are exactly the `context_broadcast` and `broadcast:oxalis-mrpink` rows. Zero leaked.
- one controlled cycle: memory bridged, landed on the peer once, **no local duplicate** (`store_local=False` held), zero `bridge:*` rows written locally.
- idempotent: runs 2 and 3 find nothing, state advances.
- the token reaches the unit through `EnvironmentFile` — proven by a send that actually landed, not by the absence of an error.

author: abdelmonemawad
body:
Closes #20.

I removed the wizard's port question because the desktop icon, the firewall entry and `INFO.sh` all hardcode 8760, so a custom port published the container on one port while the icon opened another and the firewall opened a third.

That was the wrong repair. The port was **required** to be configurable — the inconsistency was the defect, not the choice.

### DSM supports this; the reference implementation already uses it

`filamind-app/filamind-ai` ships to the same two devices and does exactly this:

```json
"port": "8181",
"allowAltPort": true
```

`allowAltPort` makes the DSM desktop icon follow the port the package reports rather than the one it was built with. The value also has to be a **string**, not a number — ours was a number.

### What the package still has to do itself

The firewall service definition is the part DSM does not carry automatically, since `conf/cadenza.sc` is read at install time. `postinst` now rewrites the installed copy when it can reach it — through a temp file, so a half-written `.sc` cannot leave DSM with an unparseable service definition. When it cannot, the install log names the port to open and where, rather than leaving the user to discover a blocked port with no explanation.

### Validation in both places

The wizard bounds the port to 1024–65535 in the UI, and `postinst` re-checks it, because UI validation is client-side and a command-line install sets the variable directly. Privileged, non-numeric or out-of-range values fall back to 8760.

### Verified against a simulated DSM

| Input | compose | firewall `.sc` | env file |
|---|---|---|---|
| `9123` | `9123:8760` | `dst.ports="9123/tcp"` | `CADENZA_HTTP_PORT=9123` |
| `80` (privileged) | `8760:8760` | unchanged | `8760` |
| `9123`, `.sc` unreachable | `9123:8760` | — | logs the exact manual firewall step |

Port-regex boundaries were checked too: 1024 and 65535 accepted, 1023 and 65536 rejected.

Part of the wider correction tracked in #19 (native SPK) and #21 (install-time guidance).

author: sommerville-ee-defra
body:
## Summary
The move to the Blankie CSP plugin changed where the `Content-Security-Policy` header is attached on error responses, which broke the dev-login-only CSP override on the check-details page.

On any error response from that page the override crashed with a "cannot read properties of undefined" error, taking down the local dev login journey. This fixes the override to read the header from the location the CSP plugin actually uses for error responses, and to no-op safely when no policy header is present. Dev-login only; no production or consumer-facing behaviour changes.

## What Changed
- The dev CSP override on the check-details page now reads the policy header from the correct store for both normal and error responses, and skips cleanly when no header is present rather than throwing.
- Added a unit test for the override covering the normal, error, and missing-header paths (it previously had none, which is why the regression slipped through).

## Why
Blankie attaches the CSP header to a different place on error responses than on normal ones. The dev override still assumed the single location the old hand-rolled header plugin always used, so it threw as soon as the check-details page returned an error. This restores the override across all response types while keeping the change confined to the dev-login path.

author: bergjs
body:
Conductor's run command is `npm run env:setup && npm run start`, so starting the dev server now leaves a working multilingual site rather than a WordPress with no plugin.

## What it does

`tools/setup-polylang.mjs` runs after the seed in `setup-env.mjs` and is idempotent:

1. Install + activate Polylang (dev environment only).
2. Create `en`, `de`, `nl`, `fr`, `it`; **English** default.
3. Register `wp_navigation` and the theme's CPTs as translatable.
4. Tag every untagged page, menu, activity and photo as English.
5. Create a German stub — `Startseite` and `Kontakt` linked as translations of Home and Contact, plus a German menu linking to both.

The actual work lives in `tools/polylang-setup.php` because Polylang's free build ships no WP-CLI commands. `tools/` is in `.distignore`, so none of this reaches a release zip.

## Two decisions worth knowing

**It runs after the seed, not before.** The seed creates pages, the navigation menu and CPT posts with no language attached, and untagged content is exactly what cost staging its header navigation. Tagging has to follow every seed rather than happen once.

**English is the default** so its URLs stay unprefixed — the e2e suite drives `/guide/`, `/ways-to-stay/` and the English header labels.

Polylang is installed by the script rather than listed in `.wp-env.json`, which only accepts paths, zip URLs or git repos — not wordpress.org slugs.

## Verification

- **Full e2e suite green with Polylang active: 52 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed, 0 flaky, 0 retries consumed** (run with `--retries=2` to match CI).
- Two consecutive `setup-polylang` runs produce no duplicate language, page or menu (`languages=5`, `startseite=1 kontakt=1 primary-de=1`).
- A clean run creates both German pages *before* the menu, so the menu links to `/de/startseite/` and `/de/kontakt/`.
- `/` renders its 13 English nav items; `/de/startseite/` renders `[Startseite, Kontakt]`.

Per-language menu binding needs **no theme change** — Polylang scopes the header's lookup itself on a front-end request. A `wp eval` probe suggests otherwise by returning menus in every language, but that is misleading: WP-CLI has no current language to scope to. This is recorded in the design note so it doesn't get re-diagnosed.

## Scope

No theme code changes — `inc/` and `tests/` are byte-identical to `main`. CI is unaffected either way, because its e2e job calls `env:start` + `wp theme activate` + `wp pediment-child seed` directly and never runs `env:setup`. That also means CI will not regression-test the multilingual path; adding a `npm run env:polylang` step there is a separate decision.

author: timveil
body:
Addresses the slow `build` job — 4m08 on a typical run.

## Where the time actually goes

Profiling [the run](https://github.com/timveil/bloviate/actions/runs/30281511575/job/90028776539?pr=574):

| Plugin | Seconds | |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| **surefire** | **178.1** | 72% of the job |
| spotbugs | 21.6 | already run by the `static-analysis` job |
| cyclonedx | 10.7 | |
| javadoc | 10.6 | |
| pmd | 9.6 | already run by the `static-analysis` job |
| compiler | 6.9 | |

`bloviate-core` alone is 3m11 of the 4m08. Inside surefire, the suite starts **39 containers** and spends **~99s — 58% of all test time — waiting for them to become healthy**:

| Image | Starts | Total | Avg |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `mysql:9.7` | 5 | 36.7s | 7.3s |
| `postgres:18-alpine` | 20 | 28.7s | 1.4s |
| `cockroachdb/cockroach:latest` | 8 | 18.1s | 2.3s |
| `mariadb:11.4` | 3 | 13.7s | 4.6s |

That is wait time, not compute. Overlapping it is the win.

## 1. Parallelise the core suite

Test classes run concurrently; methods within a class stay `same_thread`.

**This needed no test changes at all.** Every `fillDatabase(...)` already stands up its own container and tears it down, so no two tests share a database, schema or pool. The per-method container pattern that costs the time is precisely what makes parallelising it safe.

Measured locally on `bloviate-core`:

| | Wall clock |
| --- | --- |
| Sequential (baseline) | **1m59** |
| Parallel, 4 threads | **1m01** |
| Parallel, 4 threads (repeat) | **59.5s** |

266 tests passing in all three, no flakes across repeats.

> **Caveat:** this machine has 10 cores, GitHub's runner has 4. Expect a smaller gain in CI. Because the bottleneck is I/O wait rather than CPU most of it should carry, but treat the local 49% as an upper bound, not a promise — the real number will be on this PR's own run.

`parallelism` is `fixed` at 4 rather than dynamic: the ceiling is how many database containers fit at once, not how many cores are idle.

## 2. Stop running static analysis twice

The `build` job now passes `-Dspotbugs.skip -Dpmd.skip -Dcpd.skip`. The `static-analysis` job added in #574 already runs all three against the same commit, *concurrently with this job* — the second run cost ~31s and gated nothing extra.

They stay bound to `verify`, so local `./mvnw verify` remains one command that runs everything. Only the CI job with a sibling covering it skips them.

## Verification

Full `./mvnw verify` — BUILD SUCCESS, 266 tests, and **jacoco's per-package floors still pass**, so parallel execution doesn't disturb coverage collection.

## Considered and rejected

- **Container reuse across tests** would cut the 39 starts directly, but means sharing a container and creating a schema per test — removing the isolation that makes parallelism safe, for a win parallelism already gets more cheaply.
- **A CI matrix job per database** conflicts with the coverage gate: each job would see only a subset of tests, so `jacoco:check`'s per-package floors would fail unless exec files were merged across jobs.
- **`cockroachdb/cockroach:latest` is an unpinned tag** — a reproducibility concern in a repo with a seed-reproducibility invariant, and the only unpinned image here. Out of scope for a perf PR; worth its own issue.

Refs #570

author: ehky2882
body:
Finishes Rome. These seven arrived with the launch audio in [PR #450](https://github.com/ehky2882/TRAVEL-GUIDED-TOUR/pull/450) but couldn't ship: they were narrated *after* the image-staging session closed, so the delivery carried their MP3s and nothing else — no scripts, and no images for five of them. The owner supplied the scripts; images came through the pipeline or direct from the owner.

**Rome 30 → 37 tours. Catalog 978 → 985 tours / 1227 → 1234 stops.**

## The seven

| Tour | Category | Hero | Gallery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Piazza del Quirinale | history | sourced | 1 |
| Monti | culturalHeritage | **owner** | 1 |
| Santa Maria Maggiore | sacredSites | sourced | 1 |
| San Giovanni in Laterano | sacredSites | sourced | 1 |
| Trajan's Column | history | **owner** | 1 |
| Porta San Sebastiano | history | **owner** | 1 |
| Testaccio | culturalHeritage | sourced | 1 |

All single-stop, geofenced 30 m, under the existing **Atlas Studio ROM**. 1,041 s of narration. Their audio was already banked on gh-pages at launch, so nothing needed re-uploading.

## Image sourcing — two real defects found and fixed

The pipeline as documented let wrong content through to the owner twice, and both are now corrected:

1. **It asked "is this the right subject AND a usable photo" as one question**, and the model answered only the first half. That let a batch of Rijksmuseum 19th-century prints through as "photos" of the Quirinale and Santa Maria Maggiore. It is now **two independent gates** — a modern-photograph test, then a subject test.
2. **The subject test was too lenient on look-alikes.** It passed the **Column of Marcus Aurelius** as Trajan's Column, and **Porta Asinaria** (three arches) as Porta San Sebastiano (one arch). The subject prompt now names the distractors explicitly, which is what caught both.

Net effect across the batch: **375 candidates → 105 verified**, and every image here passed both gates or came from the owner.

Worth recording for future batches: under the CC0-only policy, public-domain imagery of famous Roman landmarks is overwhelmingly historical prints — modern photos are rarely PD. Unsplash and owner-supplied photos are the practical sources.

## Two gh-pages overwrites (deliberate)

`trajans-column_hero.webp` and `testaccio_hero.webp` already existed as walk-only images and are **replaced** with the owner's picks. They are shared with the *Ancient Rome* and *Aventine & Testaccio* walk stops, so those two stop images change too. Both are improvements — an owner-chosen photo for Trajan's Column, and for Testaccio a public-domain image replacing a CC BY 2.0 one, which removes an attribution obligation.

## Verification

- **Validator: 0 errors, 0 warnings** across all 985 tours.
- **Diff is additions-only** — 301 +, 0 −.
- Deterministic uuid5 ids (`atlas-{tour,stop}:rom:<slug>`); **0 collisions** against the live catalog.
- `transcriptText` = each display script minus its `[beat]` marker; no bracketed directions survive.
- **Caption bug fixed:** the sentence splitter broke on `St.`, so San Giovanni's caption came out a 41-character fragment. It now ignores common abbreviations and extends until it clears 60 characters — all seven now run 104–307. This would have recurred on Montreal and Berlin, which are full of `St.` place names.
- Asset URLs are being live-checked; the images are confirmed present on `origin/gh-pages` and awaiting Pages deployment. **I'll confirm all 21 return 200 before this merges.**

Content-only — no app code, no backend change.
