author: robin-wambi
body:
Adds the customer-facing app and the cart epic on top of it, then closes the loop by showing staff what a customer sent.

Large but cohesive: 22 commits over six planned phases, none of which were previously PR'd.

## What this delivers

**Customer app** (`apps/amuwak_customer`) — self-registration, place/track/edit/cancel an order, per-order chat, an inbox, and a four-tab dashboard shell.

**A laundry cart** — customers build a multi-item order (weight items priced per kg, specialty items priced per piece), see a live itemized breakdown with a free-delivery progress bar, and check out as **one combined pickup** carrying an itemized `orders.cart_items` snapshot. Staff still weigh the load and set the real price; the shared pricing engine is untouched.

**Damage photos** — a photo of a stained or damaged garment per cart line, so staff are warned before the load goes in a machine. First real Supabase Storage write path in the codebase.

**Staff visibility** — the customer's declared items and their photos on order details (above pricing) and pickup capture (before the rider counts), plus an "N flagged" indicator on the order card.

## Offline behaviour

The customer app was online-only; it now has a Drift DB + outbox. The cart is local source-of-truth, and checkout and photo uploads queue and drain on reconnect. Transient failures never dead-letter — the lesson the staff sync engine learned on poor networks.

Photo bytes live in the local DB rather than a file: the app also ships as a web PWA where there is no filesystem, so a blob keeps one code path instead of a conditional `dart:io` import.

## Includes a bug fix worth reviewing on its own

`d2c1b42` — `SyncPuller._ordersFromJson` dropped **every** priced column (`total_ugx`, `line_items`, `rate_per_kg_snapshot_ugx`, `payment_amount_ugx`, the delivery/express snapshots). Staff screens read Drift exclusively, so this mapper is the only server→local path for an order: a pulled order read as **USh 0** with no line items, and recorded cash looked uncollected. Locally-created orders were fine because the write path carries these fields, which is why it went unnoticed — it only bites orders that arrive by pull, i.e. every customer-app order. Found while adding the cart snapshot to the same mapper.

## Backend

Migrations `0041`–`0052` are **already applied on production** (verified against the live schema: columns, the `carts` table, the `customer-uploads` bucket and its three policies — not just the migration tracker). Each has a sibling pgTAP test, including denied-access cases.

The `customer-uploads` bucket is private and per-customer scoped, with **no UPDATE policy** — uploads are immutable from the client. The upload is therefore not an upsert; a duplicate object can only be our own retry, so it settles as success rather than 403-ing forever in a queue that never dead-letters.

Staff Drift schema goes to v8; both new migrations (`v7→v8`, and the customer app's `v1→v2`) have tests that seed a real old-version sqlite file and assert the upgrade.

## Testing

`flutter analyze` clean across `amuwak_core`, `amuwak_staff`, and `amuwak_customer`. Test files were run individually (this host deadlocks on parallel runs) — the cart, photo, sync, order-model, migration, and both edited staff screens' suites are green, plus the 57-test dashboard suite. CI is the full-suite check.

**Not done:** the live end-to-end pass — build a mixed cart, check out, confirm the snapshot and photo appear in the staff queue, the offline round-trip, and an RLS pen-test of customer B against customer A. Worth doing before this ships to real customers.

author: amd-sriram
body:
## Summary

Removes the full-width `out_logits.fill_(float("-inf"))` before the decode paged MQA-logits kernel in `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`).

The decode consumer, `top_k_per_row_decode`, bounds its per-row scan by `seq_lens` (it reads only `[0, rowEnd)` where `rowEnd = seq_len - next_n + next_n_idx + 1`) and pads short rows (`rowLen <= topK`) with `-1` internally. The paged MQA-logits kernels write every in-causal column that top-k reads:
- Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` writes `-inf` into masked in-tile positions itself.
- FlyDSL `flydsl_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` writes exactly `col <= q_limit` (== the columns top-k reads).

So the out-of-window `[rowEnd, max_model_len)` region initialized by this `fill_` is never consumed on the decode path, making the prefill redundant. Dropping it saves a `rows x max_model_len` fp32 HBM write every decode step.

## Why it's safe (decode path)

`q_limit` (kernel write extent) and `rowEnd` (top-k read extent) are both derived from the same context length and `next_n`, so every column top-k reads is freshly written; nothing reads the untouched tail.

## Scope / caveats

- Only affects the **decode** paged path (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`).
- The prefill top-k path and the `topk_indices_buffer[...] = -1` init are untouched.
- The FlyDSL kernel documents a `-inf`-prefill contract; this change relies on the consumer's `seq_lens` bounding rather than the kernel self-initializing, so it should be validated numerically.

## Test plan

- [ ] Compare decode top-k indices with/without the fill across short / long / padded batches (Gluon and FlyDSL paths) on gfx942/gfx950.
- [ ] Run existing `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` and sparse-indexer tests.
- [ ] Sanity-check end-to-end GLM-5.2 sparse-MLA decode output.

author: tatewilsonwork
body:
## Why

v0.5.35 (Migration Phase A) added `excel_to_powerpoint.find_soffice()` — PATH first, then the standard per-platform install locations — but wired it into `slide_render` only, on the stated reasoning that the other five call sites were "workbook/chart paths, unaffected by this flip."

That reasoning was wrong. The Windows LibreOffice MSI puts nothing on PATH, so on a dev box with LibreOffice correctly installed, every one of those sites' own `shutil.which("soffice") or shutil.which("libreoffice")` reported "not installed" and either **failed outright** or **silently degraded** — indistinguishable from a genuinely LibreOffice-less box, and the exact inverse of the dev/prod parity Phase A exists to create.

**Phase A's `pytest` green exit criterion was therefore not actually met.** `test_slide_library_poc.py::test_pitch_deck_inserts_cap_table_into_slide7` was failing with `LibreOffice (soffice/libreoffice) not found on PATH`: the cap-table renderer falls back Excel COM → LibreOffice, and on a box whose Excel COM was unavailable the fallback could not find the installed binary.

## What changed

All five sites resolve through the locator:

| Site | Failure mode before |
|---|---|
| `excel_to_powerpoint._libreoffice_range_to_png` | hard failure — the cap-table / ownership range renderer's COM fallback |
| `financial_charts._libreoffice_recalc_values` | hard failure — FS chart values |
| `financial_charts._render_single_chart_png` | silent — charts persisted on the tab, deck placeholders left in place |
| `financial_charts._render_single_pie_png` | silent — same, for the overview LTM pie |
| `workbook_aggregator._recalc_with_libreoffice` | silent — combined workbook kept its un-evaluated cross-tab formulas |

Plus: messages now say "not found on PATH **or in the standard install locations**"; `find_soffice` is documented as **the** locator (never `shutil.which`), with this miss recorded as the reason; `financial_charts`' now-unused `import shutil` is dropped; and two `skipif win32` test skip-guards that did their own PATH probe now use the locator (no change on Windows — but they were skipping on macOS, where the installer also skips PATH, with LibreOffice installed).

**The locator stays in `excel_to_powerpoint`** rather than moving to a neutral module: `financial_charts` and `workbook_aggregator` already import `_soffice_convert` from there, so this adds no dependency edge — and Phase D deletes `workbook_aggregator` outright along with the COM surface of the other two, so a new shared module would be short-lived. The existing lazy in-function import style is kept, which is also what lets the tests patch one attribute and reach every caller.

## Tests

`551 passed, 4 skipped, 2 failed` → **`561 passed, 2 skipped`**. Both previously-failing COM picture-insertion tests now pass, via the LibreOffice fallback — i.e. through the same renderer production uses.

- **A drift lock** — `test_no_bare_libreoffice_path_lookups_outside_the_locator` scans every `scripts/**/*.py` and fails if a `which("soffice"|"libreoffice")` probe reappears outside `excel_to_powerpoint.py`. This is the test that would have caught the v0.5.35 miss.
- `find_soffice` gains direct unit coverage: PATH hit beats the install locations; a PATH miss falls back to an install location (the Windows MSI case); neither present ⇒ `None`.
- Two wiring tests pin resolution **platform-independently** — `shutil.which` stubbed to find nothing and only the locator knowing the binary, so a site that regresses to `which` cannot resolve it.
- The existing "LibreOffice absent" tests patched `financial_charts.shutil.which` / `workbook_aggregator.shutil.which`, which can no longer simulate absence — `find_soffice` probes install locations too, so a real MSI install stayed visible and those graceful-degradation assertions were about to exercise the *present* path. They now patch the locator (`_no_libreoffice` / `_libreoffice_at` helpers).

## For the reviewer

**The suite is green, but not repeatably so on the dev box.** A later full run flaked two *different* COM picture-insertion tests (`Chart.Paste` `_ClipboardPasteError`, including the Bloomberg-institutions one); both pass on isolated re-run. That is the pre-existing race already documented in 0.5.35 — this PR removes its *startup*-failure mode (COM unavailable → `RuntimeError` → LibreOffice, which now resolves), but a **mid-render** COM failure is still re-raised raw by v0.5.21's deliberate design ("so a mid-operation Excel error is not mistaken for 'no Excel'"). Whether the mid-render case should also degrade to LibreOffice, now that LibreOffice is the reference renderer on every platform, is a Phase D question and is **not** decided here.

**Amplifier found, deliberately not fixed:** `_excel_com_range_to_png` leaks its Excel automation instance on every call — the COM references are still bound when `Quit()` / `CoUninitialize()` run, so the out-of-process server never exits. Measured 9 → 13 resident `EXCEL.EXE` across one suite run plus probes; at 13, `DispatchEx` itself began failing with `Server execution failed`. Out of scope here, unverifiable while COM was saturated, and Phase D deletes the path — recorded in the CHANGELOG and tracked separately. Note the instances were **not** force-killed (that trips Office crash-resiliency and disables the analyst's CapIQ add-ins); a graceful ROT-attach `Quit()` loop reclaimed 3 of 13, the rest clear on logoff.

Version bumped to `0.5.36` across the three files, with CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md (phase bullet + the shared-helpers import list), and a `docs/migration-plan.md` note recording that Phase A's exit criterion actually landed here.

author: moon-bot-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

`moonshotai/Kimi-K3` has no parameter count on the Hub. Its `model.safetensors.index.json` is **59.8 MB** (497,220 tensors over 96 shards), and `parseShardedIndex` did:

```ts
const index = JSON.parse(await indexBlob.slice(0, MAX_HEADER_LENGTH /* 25MB */).text());
```

The 60 MB index gets hard-truncated to 25 MB → invalid JSON → `SafetensorParseError` → `safetensors` is left unset on the model, so the UI has nothing to render and size filters don't match.

Verified against the real file:

```
old path (25MB slice + JSON.parse): SyntaxError -> Unterminated string in JSON at position 25000000
```

Simply raising the cap would work today but re-buffers the whole document, which is the memory-exhaustion vector the cap existed to prevent — and the next bigger model blows past whatever number we pick.

## What this does

The index is only read for two things: the small `metadata` object, and the **distinct** shard filenames that `weight_map` points at (96 of them). The 497k-entry `weight_map` is ~99% of the bytes and is used purely to derive `[...new Set(Object.values(weight_map))]`.

So instead of materializing it:

- **`utils/streamJson.ts`** — a dependency-free, ~380-line SAX-style incremental JSON parser. Emits `startObject` / `key` / `value` / `endObject` … as bytes arrive, off a `ReadableStream` or `AsyncIterable`. Resumable state machine, so any token may straddle a chunk boundary (including UTF-8 mid-character and `\uXXXX` escapes). Works on web streams, so it stays isomorphic.
- **`lib/parse-safetensors-index.ts`** — consumes those events and keeps only `metadata`, `dtype` and the distinct shard filenames. Peak memory is proportional to the shard count (~100), not the tensor count (~500k). Retains byte and shard-count ceilings; hitting one cancels the reader so the HTTP response is torn down mid-body rather than fully downloaded.
- **`parse-safetensors-metadata.ts`** — `parseShardedIndex` now returns `{ index, shardFilenames }` and `fetchAllHeaders` takes the filename list directly. The per-shard `MAX_HEADER_LENGTH` path is untouched: shard headers were already read correctly via range requests.

Measured on a 500k-tensor index — **retained heap 0.39 MB streaming vs 49.17 MB for `JSON.parse`**. On the real Kimi-K3 index: parses in 1.55 s, 96 shards and `metadata` byte-identical to a full `JSON.parse`.

## Note on the public type

`SafetensorsIndexJson.weight_map` becomes optional. It's dropped above `MAX_WEIGHT_MAP_ENTRIES` (200k), where the parser deliberately stops materializing it — every model below that threshold is unaffected, and the handful above it currently fail to parse entirely, so nothing that works today regresses. `filepaths` on the result is the supported way to get the shard list.

## On reusing the old parser

Checked the original `server/lib/JsonStream.ts` from moon-landing#3528 (before it was swapped for `ld-jsonstream`). It doesn't transplant: it's a Node `Duplex` built on `stream` / `string_decoder` / `RichError`, so it wouldn't work in browsers or workers, and being schema-driven over *whole top-level values* it would buffer `weight_map` in one piece — `collectEach` only splits arrays, not objects. Hence written from scratch against web streams, emitting per-entry events. Happy to export `streamJson` publicly if it's wanted for reuse elsewhere.

## Tests

126 new tests. `streamJson` is differentially tested against `JSON.parse` across 19 document shapes at chunk sizes 1/2/3/5/7/13/∞ (byte-by-byte exercises every resumption path), plus 24 malformed inputs asserted to be rejected by both, early-termination and token-length limits. The index reader is covered for metadata/shard extraction, key ordering, unknown root keys, chunk-boundary invariance, unicode, the caps, and a Kimi-K3-shaped index that the old 25 MB-slice path provably cannot parse.

---
Requested by @coyotte508 - [Slack thread](https://huggingface.slack.com/archives/C02EMARJ65P/p1785166127523619?thread_ts=1785166127.523619&cid=C02EMARJ65P) - [Agent trace](https://huggingface.co/buckets/huggingface/moon-bot-memory/tree/sessions/2026-07-27T15-37-14-480Z_3a3ee6d6-fd5d-46dc-9db9-46bcf25df3a3.jsonl)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core Hub safetensors metadata parsing and public `weight_map` optionality; bounded limits and extensive tests reduce regression risk, but behavior changes for very large indexes and untrusted index files.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes Hub safetensors metadata for models whose `*.safetensors.index.json` exceeds the old **25MB** `JSON.parse` slice (e.g. **moonshotai/Kimi-K3** ~60MB / ~500k `weight_map` entries).
> 
> Adds **`streamJson`** — an incremental SAX-style JSON parser over `ReadableStream` / async iterables — and **`parseSafetensorsIndexStream`**, which walks index files as events and keeps only **`metadata`**, **`dtype`**, distinct **shard filenames**, and optionally a bounded **`weight_map`**. Peak retained memory scales with shard count, not tensor count. Limits cover bytes, shard count, token length, nesting, and hostile retention; hitting a limit can **cancel** the download early.
> 
> **`parseShardedIndex`** in `parse-safetensors-metadata.ts` now streams the blob instead of `JSON.parse(slice(0, MAX_HEADER_LENGTH))`, returns **`{ index, shardFilenames }`**, and **`fetchAllHeaders`** takes the filename list directly. **`SafetensorsIndexJson.weight_map`** is **optional** when entry/char caps drop materialization; **`filepaths`** remains the supported shard list.
> 
> Integration test fixture for sharded diffusers weights switches from Krea-2-Turbo to **Qwen/Qwen-Image**. Large test coverage for `streamJson` and the index parser (including Kimi-K3-shaped indexes and hostile input).

author: cheapsteak
body:
## What's broken

Six of the 27 tests in `Active tab resolution` (`Tests/TBDAppTests/ActiveTabResolutionTests.swift`) fail on the fast parallel pass, on branches that cannot have touched them. Every failure is the same line:

```
Caught error: timed out waiting for the scheduled fetch to finish after polling up to 30.0 seconds
```

Failing runs, all on **PR #522, a docs-only branch**:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| [30275284765](https://github.com/cheapsteak/tbd/actions/runs/30275284765) | `✘ Suite "Active tab resolution" failed after 49.371 seconds with 6 issues` |
| [30279755880](https://github.com/cheapsteak/tbd/actions/runs/30279755880) | `✘ Suite "Active tab resolution" failed after 47.759 seconds with 6 issues` |

#538's own merge run, [30272477719](https://github.com/cheapsteak/tbd/actions/runs/30272477719), went red the same day on `ControlModeInputHealth` — a different suite with the same wait shape, and the same failure family this repo already knows (`timed out waiting for 2 health events`, tests "failed after 45.280 seconds").

**PR #522 is currently blocked on this**, having changed nothing but Markdown.

## Why it happens

The six failing tests are exactly the six that call the file's private `waitFor` helper — a 5 ms poll loop against a 30 s `ContinuousClock` deadline, watching for `AppState.tabStateFetchesInFlight` to lose a worktree id. What it is waiting on is the unstructured `Task` that `scheduleTabStateHydration` (`Sources/TBDApp/AppState+Tabs.swift:136` as merged) arms to run `loadTabStates`.

Both sides of that wait are `@MainActor`: `AppState` is main-actor isolated, `Task {}` inherits that isolation, and the suite is `@MainActor` too. So the poll is not waiting for the fetch — it is waiting for **main-actor turns**, and the main actor is a single serial executor shared by every `@MainActor` suite in the process. All test targets compile into one binary and Swift Testing parallelizes suites in-process, so on the full pass that one executor is arbitrated between ~480 suites at once.

The CI log proves the starvation directly, from this suite's own siblings. These are pure synchronous in-memory assertions with no I/O and no awaits:

```
✔ Test "plain command-w closes the active tab" passed after 25.305 seconds.
✔ Test "closing the trailing active tab clamps onto the new last tab" passed after 44.578 seconds.
✔ Test "closing the active tab moves the selection to the tab that takes its slot" passed after 44.578 seconds.
✘ Test "reconcileTabs re-fetches tab state until hydrated, then stops" ... timed out ... 30.0 seconds
```

A no-op test taking 44 s of wall time is the finding. The work under test is fine; getting scheduled is what costs 40 s. So a 30 s budget on the wait measures **whole-process contention**, not this worktree's fetch — the suite finishes in 80 ms alone and blows the budget in company, and raising the budget only moves the cliff. The poll also made the congestion it was losing to worse: 30 s at 5 ms is ~6000 extra main-actor wakeups per waiting test.

## How it got broken

The suite is one day old — it arrived with #538 (`2e359c82`, "new worktrees open on the agent tab") — and has flaked since its first full pass. Nothing about #538's production fix is wrong; only the way its tier-2 tests observe an unstructured `Task`.

## What the fix does

Replaces the wall-clock poll with a structured completion signal — there is now **no deadline anywhere in the file**, so there is no budget left to blow.

- `AppState.tabStateFetchesInFlight: Set<UUID>` becomes `tabStateFetchTasks: [UUID: Task<Void, Never>]`. The stored handle *is* the in-flight marker, so the dedup guard is unchanged in meaning, and the scheduled work is now directly awaitable.
- The scheduler's `Task` clears its own entry as its last act, so "the handle resumed" and "the worktree may schedule again" are the same instant.
- Tests call `settleHydration(state, worktreeID:)`, which `await`s that handle (draining in a loop, so a regression that armed several overlapping fetches is still fully settled before the assertion). A loaded machine now makes these tests slower and never red.
- The `for _ in 0..<20 { await Task.yield() }` spins that guarded "and no further fetch happens" are gone: each round drains what it armed, so a stray re-fetch lands *inside* the loop and shows up in the count instead of racing it. The assertions got stronger, not weaker.

One incidental correctness fix falls out: `loadTabStates` no longer clears the in-flight marker. It is also called directly (initial load, tier-1 tests), where it was clearing a marker belonging to a scheduled fetch it did not own.

No behavior change in the app: same guards, same attempt cap, same refund rule, same RPC.

## Test plan

- `swift build` — clean. `swiftlint --strict` — 0 violations, 612 files.
- `swift test --filter ActiveTabResolutionTests` — **27 tests in 1 suite passed** after 0.080 s.
- Full `swift test --parallel -j 2`, twice:
  - run 1 — `Test run with 4524 tests in 501 suites passed after 35.783 seconds with 1 known issue`
  - run 2 — `Test run with 4524 tests in 501 suites passed after 32.104 seconds with 1 known issue`

  (The known issue in both is `FlakyQuarantineSelfTests/retriesUntilPass`, the quarantine mechanism's own fixture, which fails once and passes on retry by design.)
- Mutation-checked, because the waits were rewritten and a rewritten wait can quietly stop proving anything:
  - deleting the in-flight dedup guard → `overlapping reconciles never stack tab-state fetches for one worktree` fails (`fetchCount` 3, not 1).
  - latching hydration unconditionally instead of only on a response carrying content (the bug #538 fixed) → `reconcileTabs re-fetches tab state until hydrated, then stops` and `the hydration gap closes: a retry lands the selection on the agent tab` fail, 4 issues between them.
  - Both guards restored and re-verified green.

This pull request introduces three new experiment scripts and updates the documentation to describe the new milestones and their usage. The main additions are the implementation of the M4, M5, and M6 experiment stages, each with their own script, and corresponding updates to the `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` to document these features and the underlying data. The new experiment scripts provide comprehensive pipelines for evaluating feature matching, preprocessing, and benchmarking under various conditions.

The most important changes are:

**New experiment scripts:**

* Added `experiments/m4_e1_smoke.py`: Implements the M4 experiment, which tests the pipeline's ability to recover a known homography under synthetic conditions, serving as a correctness check before proceeding further.
* Added `experiments/m5_preprocess.py`: Implements the M5 experiment, comparing preprocessing methods (Otsu, Sauvola, CLAHE, etc.) and their effects on binarization and SIFT keypoint detection, including handling of illumination gradients.
* Added `experiments/m6_e1_completo.py`: Implements the M6 experiment, running a full grid of tests with varying degradation and geometric transformations, outputting results to a CSV for further analysis.

**Documentation and workflow updates:**

author: agropper
body:
Backlog #4. Private AI Primary (GPT) chat ("Who are you?") returned **500 "Internal server error"** while the **draft Patient Summary — the same GPT agent — worked**.

## Cause
In `server/routes/chat.js`, when the selected profile has no `modelName`, the model fell back to the **agent name**:
```js
options.model = profileModelName ? profileModelName : profileAgentName; // e.g. "jenna53-agent-…"
```
That's not a valid model, so the DO agent's OpenAI-compatible endpoint 500s before any inference. The draft-summary path never hit this because it falls back to a **real** model (`userDoc.agentModelName || 'openai-gpt-oss-120b'`). This also explains why prompt size was irrelevant — a one-word question failed too; it never reached the model.

## Fix
Mirror the working draft path — never use the agent name as the model:
```js
options.model = profileModelName || userDoc.agentModelName || 'openai-gpt-oss-120b';
```

`node --check` clean. Off `main` (1.5.110 → **1.5.111**).

**Verify live:** on an account where chat was 500'ing, "Who are you?" to Private AI Primary (GPT) should now answer (and correctly state its agent/model per the identity system prompt). I couldn't reproduce locally (no provisioned agent in the local CouchDB), so a live check on `test.agropper.xyz` confirms it.

author: kurrik
body:
## Summary

Makes the polish loop the default pre-push gate for both workflow commands, now that `ark:polish` (#6) is merged:

- `/ark:pr` step 3 invokes the `ark:polish` skill instead of `/code-review` plus its own inline triage — polish subsumes both (parallel reviewers, triage, fix commits with audit trails). It skips the run only when the human explicitly opts out ("without polish", "skip the review", "just push"), doesn't re-run when a polish loop this session already covered the current branch tip (a run from before commits landed is stale), stops and asks when polish exits blocked or round-capped, and falls back to an inline review at the same bar when the skill is unavailable in the session.
- `/ark:review` step 5 becomes "Commit, polish, then push": the fix commits are polished before pushing, catching "feedback on the fixes" locally instead of in the next review round, with the same opt-out and stop-if-blocked rules. Polish outcomes fold into the thread replies and final summary.

Also bumps ark to 0.6.0 and updates the README bullets for both commands.

## Test plan

`claude plugin validate` passes locally for the marketplace and the ark plugin; CI re-runs it. Worth exercising once each: `/ark:pr` on a small branch to confirm it runs polish before pushing and reports its triage, and an explicit "skip the polish" invocation to confirm the opt-out is honored.

body:
# Description

Adds an opt-in cached selector path to asset `find_*` APIs. With
`as_proxy=True`, articulation, rigid-object, and rigid-object-collection
finders return a per-asset cached `ProxyArray` backed by device-local
`wp.int32` storage. The same allocation can be consumed directly by Warp
writers or accessed as a zero-copy Torch view.

The existing finder result types remain available during the deprecation
period: omitted `as_proxy` retains the legacy result and warns, while
`as_proxy=False` explicitly retains it without warning. The cache is a
per-asset 128-entry LRU and is cleared when the asset is invalidated.

PhysX, Newton, and OVPhysX selector boundaries consume the cached Warp
allocation without materializing Torch. Repeated actuator and action-term
writer paths now retain proxy selectors, and the articulation benchmark
grid covers list, Torch int32/int64, Warp int32/int64, and cached proxy
representations.

author: mastacontrola
body:
`configureMySql()` built `$dbservice` with `grep -o` and three `-e` patterns. `grep -o` prints **one line per match**, and `systemctl list-unit-files` lists the `mysql`/`mysqld` alias symlinks alongside the real unit — so the fallback lookup returned a three-line value. Verified on a stock Fedora box:

```
raw candidates: mariadb.service mysql.service mysqld.service
dbservice     : $'mariadb.service\nmysql.service\nmysqld.service'
word-split    : 3 args -> mariadb.service mysql.service mysqld.service
```

Unquoted, that fed `systemctl enable|stop|start` **three** arguments — two of them alias names rather than the real unit — where one was intended.

## This is the fresh-install path, not an edge case

The primary lookup uses `systemctl list-units`, which only sees units **already running**. RedHat-family packages don't auto-start the DB after install — so on a new Fedora/RHEL install the primary comes back empty, the fallback fires, and this is exactly where it lands.

## Two changes

1. **Resolve to a single name, preference stated explicitly.** `grep` cannot express preference — `-e` order does not rank matches, it reports whichever appeared first in the *input*. So the real unit was never actually preferred over its aliases; it just usually sorted that way by luck.
2. **Quote `$dbservice` at the three `systemctl` call sites**, so a multi-valued result can never silently become multiple arguments again.

On `working-1.6` the alpine `rc-service -l | grep mariadb` lookup was also bounded with `head -1` — same unbounded shape. This branch has no alpine lookup, so there's no counterpart here; the resolution block is otherwise byte-identical across the two branches.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| fallback path on this box | **1 arg** (was 3) |
| primary path on this box | unchanged, `mariadb.service` |
| input `mysql.service` | → `mysql.service` |
| input `mysqld.service` + `mysql.service` | → `mysqld.service` |
| input all three | → `mariadb.service` |
| input empty | → empty (unchanged from before) |
| `bash -n` | passes |

**Not verified:** whether `systemctl enable` on the alias names errors or merely no-ops on a fresh RedHat box — that needs an actual install run to observe. The multi-argument expansion itself is demonstrated above.

Companion PR for `working-1.6`: #905

author: iiivan37
body:
## Bug trouvé par la validation réelle D6

Le premier build `workflow_dispatch` (D6) a révélé que l'archive Windows **n'était pas un vrai zip** : sur `windows-latest`, `tar` en `shell: bash` résout vers **GNU tar** (git-bash), pas bsdtar. `tar -a -cf x.zip` sur une extension `.zip` inconnue de GNU tar produit **un tar non compressé** sous le nom `.zip`. Un utilisateur Windows double-cliquant le fichier aurait une erreur (`file` : `POSIX tar archive (GNU)`, `unzip` : *End-of-central-directory signature not found*).

**Faux positif de ma simulation locale** : je l'avais testé sur macOS, dont le `tar` EST bsdtar (qui, lui, sait écrire un zip). Seul le runner Windows réel exposait la divergence — c'est précisément ce que la validation plateforme D6 doit attraper.

## Correctif

Étape `Package archive` scindée par OS :
- **Windows** : `shell: pwsh` + `Compress-Archive` → vrai zip deflate.
- **unix** : `shell: bash` + `tar -czf` (inchangé).

## Vérifié en réel

Build `workflow_dispatch` sur cette branche (runner `windows-latest`) → artefact retéléchargé :
```
file : Zip archive data, ... compression method=deflate
unzip -l : loupe.exe (6 721 024 o)
```
Les tar Linux/macOS restent corrects (le binaire macOS arm64 tourne, `loupe 0.1.0`).

Aucune Release publique impliquée (dispatch, pas de tag).

author: anas-mattar
body:
29 fixture rows added BEFORE any fix, per guard-cases.tsv's own instruction. 23 of them failed on the first run. The behavioural fixture is now 128 cases.

W5a -- A GLOB NEVER CONTAINS THE STRING IT MATCHES, and the perimeter was tested with a literal substring. `rm -rf .cla*` removed .claude entirely while never mentioning it, and that is ordinary shell:

    $ ls -a          .  ..  .claude
    $ rm -rf .cla*
    $ ls -a          .  ..

Any word carrying * ? or [ is now judged by its non-glob prefix: `.cla*` ->
`.cla` is a prefix of `.claude` (hit); `dist/*` -> `dist/` is not (allowed). A bare `*` has an empty prefix, a prefix of everything, so it blocks -- at the project root it really would take the perimeter with it.

W5b -- A QUOTE INSIDE A WORD is removed by the shell, not treated as a separator. The normaliser mapped quotes to a SPACE, right at a word boundary and exactly wrong inside one: `npm in"stall" x` became `npm in stall x`, so `install` existed in no haystack. A backslash failed from the other side -- mapped to `/` for path stripping, `n\pm install x` became `n/pm install x` and the path rule deleted the word. Six haystacks now: three translated, three with those characters DELETED. The perimeter scan reads segments from both normalisations for the same reason.

W6 -- ENUMERATING OPTION SPELLINGS LOSES to a tool with abbreviation matching. GNU cp also takes the directory attached to the short option, and any unambiguous long-option abbreviation; `cp -t.claude/hooks /tmp/x` and `cp --targ=.claude/hooks/ /tmp/x` both overwrote a hook. Inverted: any option at all means the perimeter path is a destination. `cp -v <perimeter> /tmp/out` is now over-blocked, which is this guard's documented direction of failure.

W7 -- THE EXEMPTION WAS MATCHED AGAINST THE PATH. `grep -H` prefixes each match with `<path>:<lineno>:` and the filter ran over the whole line, so `git mv src/ledger.ts 'src/approved-stub: deferred/'` removed every marker beneath that directory, silently and without limit -- the same "a rename is not a code-review event" argument this file already makes about latest-ledger.ts. Also a divergence: sh counted 1 where the .ps1, filtering line text only, counted 4. The prefix is stripped before the exemption applies, located by the `:<digits>:` field so a path containing a colon cannot shift the split.

W11 -- WIN32 STRIPS TRAILING SPACES AND DOTS when it opens a file, so `package.json `, `package.json.`, `Gemfile.` and `.claude/allow-package-changes ` all reached the real file while the guard returned 0. One Write with a trailing space created the marker that disables both guards permanently, on the platform settings.json ships configured for. Stripped per component now, BEFORE the slash squeeze -- squeezing first turned `src/../package.json` into `src//package.json`, and the directory-shaped patterns are matched against the whole path.

W12 -- seven patterns added: npm exec, npm x, go mod tidy, go mod download, dotnet restore, dotnet tool restore, cargo fetch. Each a sibling of a listed pattern, reached by the spelling the tool's own docs use -- `npx` was guarded while `npm exec` was not. 56 -> 63, and all four digests regenerated.

Every fix landed on BOTH twins in this one change, which is the discipline the previous commit had to be written to restore. Each verified to fail with its fix reverted: dropping hay4-6, disabling the glob scan, re-enumerating the cp options, removing the trailing-dot strip, and restoring the whole-line exemption each produce a failure.

Suite: 100 passing, 0 failing (47 + 31 + 22), verified against a git checkout-index copy so the CRLF working tree matches what CI sees. Two pwsh-absent FAILs remain in this sandbox and pass on ubuntu-latest.

author: pveloso01
body:
## Why it looked bad

Tiles were **298×78 — a 3.8:1 letterbox** — filled with `object-fit: cover`. Against a normal 1080p screenshot that means:

- scale to width: **6.4× downscale**
- scaled height 168px into a 78px tile → keep the **middle 46%**, discard the top and bottom 27% each
- 17px source text lands at **2.6px**

Screenshots keep their meaning at the *top* — title bars, headers, the first line of a terminal, the URL. The crop threw exactly that away. A tall phone capture kept **12%** of the image.

Rendered with four realistic captures, **two of four tiles were visually blank** and the other two were unidentifiable. For a product whose entire value is recognising a capture at a glance, the tile geometry defeated the point.

Three things compounded it:

- **Tiles were darker than the panel** (`rgba(0,0,0,0.35)` on near-black), so a dark capture sank in and read as a hole rather than an item.
- **The filename sat on the picture**, a permanent gradient eating the bottom third of an already tiny thumbnail, white text over unpredictable content.
- **Icons were emoji mixed with typographic symbols** (📸 🎬 ⚠ ★ ☆ ⧉ × ▶) — different weights, different colour behaviour, a different look on every machine.

## What changed

- **Two-column 16:10 grid**, grouped by day, in a 360px window. Near-native aspect so almost nothing is cropped; ~12 visible instead of ~6.
- **Elevation inverted**: tiles now sit above the surface.
- **Filename on hover**; recordings keep a permanent length/size badge, because that is identity rather than chrome.
- **One 24×24 stroke icon set** inheriting `currentColor`, replacing every emoji and symbol.
- **Chrome cut from 64px to 40px**: the wordmark became the capture count, and the status line that permanently read "Watching 1 folder + clipboard" became a live dot with a tooltip plus an alert strip that only appears when something is wrong.

## A data bug this uncovered

The video badge read **"0:09 · 48 B"** for a 135,725-byte file. `std::fs::metadata` really was returning 48 — the capture event fires **while the encoder is still writing**.

ffmpeg lays down a 48-byte header, stalls ~1s while encoding, then flushes everything at once. The settle rule (3 × 350ms of unchanged size) read that stall as "finished". My phase-02 test wrote chunks *continuously* every 400ms, so it never paused and never caught this.

That is not cosmetic: a recording shelved mid-write **drags out truncated**. `VIDEO_STABLE_TICKS` now requires ~2.8s of genuine silence, and the badge reads `0:09 · 133 kB`.

## Why this shipped looking like it did

Every visual check across six phases used **solid-colour fixtures and an ffmpeg test pattern** — content that looks identical at any crop and any scale. The layout was being validated against material chosen to make it look fine. The realistic fixtures that exposed all of this (a code editor, a browser article, a terminal, a phone screenshot) took ten minutes to write.

author: mastacontrola
body:
`configureMySql()` built `$dbservice` with `grep -o` and three `-e` patterns. `grep -o` prints **one line per match**, and `systemctl list-unit-files` lists the `mysql`/`mysqld` alias symlinks alongside the real unit — so the fallback lookup returned a three-line value. Verified on a stock Fedora box:

```
raw candidates: mariadb.service mysql.service mysqld.service
dbservice     : $'mariadb.service\nmysql.service\nmysqld.service'
word-split    : 3 args -> mariadb.service mysql.service mysqld.service
```

Unquoted, that fed `systemctl enable|stop|start` **three** arguments — two of them alias names rather than the real unit — where one was intended.

## This is the fresh-install path, not an edge case

The primary lookup uses `systemctl list-units`, which only sees units **already running**. RedHat-family packages don't auto-start the DB after install — so on a new Fedora/RHEL install the primary comes back empty, the fallback fires, and this is exactly where it lands.

## Two changes

1. **Resolve to a single name, preference stated explicitly.** `grep` cannot express preference — `-e` order does not rank matches, it reports whichever appeared first in the *input*. So the real unit was never actually preferred over its aliases; it just usually sorted that way by luck.
2. **Quote `$dbservice` at the three `systemctl` call sites**, so a multi-valued result can never silently become multiple arguments again.

On `working-1.6` the alpine `rc-service -l | grep mariadb` lookup was also bounded with `head -1` — same unbounded shape. This branch has no alpine lookup, so there's no counterpart here; the resolution block is otherwise byte-identical across the two branches.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| fallback path on this box | **1 arg** (was 3) |
| primary path on this box | unchanged, `mariadb.service` |
| input `mysql.service` | → `mysql.service` |
| input `mysqld.service` + `mysql.service` | → `mysqld.service` |
| input all three | → `mariadb.service` |
| input empty | → empty (unchanged from before) |
| `bash -n` | passes |

**Not verified:** whether `systemctl enable` on the alias names errors or merely no-ops on a fresh RedHat box — that needs an actual install run to observe. The multi-argument expansion itself is demonstrated above.

author: talchain
body:
**P0 fail-open.** A withheld analysis could entitle the product to name a leading option. Confirmed at `cf10c553` with an executed repro before any fix (6 RED assertions), and the repro is committed.

**This PR goes first.** #727, #728, #729 rebase onto it.

## The defect: a QUALITY selector used as an ENTITLEMENT selector

Two independently-correct decisions composed into a wrong one — which is why it survived review.

1. **`selectRunAnalysisFact` (`context/freshness.ts:317`)** answers *"is this analysis good enough to build a result view from?"* Its eligibility filter excludes `partial`, `blocked`, `failed`, `degraded`, and — deliberately — **any status it does not recognise**. Correct for freshness.
2. **The run_analysis handler ACCEPTS a `partial` analysis** (permissive accept matrix, resilience contract Part C), persists it, and may name a leading option from it. Also correct.

Composed: a `partial` fact carrying `may_name_leading_option: false` is **invisible** to `claim-safety-read.ts`, which then takes its `no analysis exists ⇒ true` branch — the branch whose entire justification is *"no claim can be grounded, so nothing can leak."* On that input a claim **had** been grounded and explicitly withheld.

**The fail-closed default was never wrong. The selector made it unreachable.**

### Executed repro, at the pinned code, before the fix

| input | pre-fix | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `partial` status + `may_name_leading_option: false` | `true` / `no_analysis_exists` | `false` / `scenario_fact` |
| unknown status string + `may_name_leading_option: false` | `true` / `no_analysis_exists` | `false` / `scenario_fact` |
| newer `partial` withheld over older `completed` permitted | `true` | `false` |

### ⚠ The forward-compatibility clause inverts

The filter excludes unrecognised statuses so a new PLoT status can never be mistaken for success. Safe for freshness; **the exact opposite here.** The day PLoT ships a new `analysis_status` string, every fact carrying it becomes entitled to name a leader — **with no CEE deploy, no code change, and no alarm.** A conservative rule in one question is a fail-open in the other. This is the part that makes it a P0 rather than an edge case.

## The fix

**Entitlement is selected independently of quality.** New `selectClaimBearingRunAnalysisFact` — newest `run_analysis` fact regardless of `analysis_status`. `selectRunAnalysisFact` is **unchanged in behaviour** and keeps the quality filter; both now share one `selectNewestRunAnalysisFact` core, so *"the entitlement fact and the freshness fact are ordered the same way"* is true by construction.

**Two selectors answering two questions is design; two copies of one ordering rule would be the mirror defect.** The distinction is stated in the code, because the obvious reading of "there are now two selectors" is that I reintroduced the very thing the sibling PR removes.

**One typed object.** `MayNameLeadingOptionVerdict` now carries `constraint_verdict_state` read off **the same selected fact** under one `fact_type` narrow, and `readConstraintVerdictStateForFacts` becomes a delegate — so `claim-safety-read.ts` performs exactly one selection. This was queued as tidy-up (1.272 B2); the P0 makes it **load-bearing**.

**P2 sibling folded in.** `turn-executor.ts:8062`'s explanation gate re-selected over the 20-turn window while the permission was scenario-scoped, so after eviction the system **withheld correctly and explained the wrong reason**. Permission, constraint state and disclosure copy now all originate from the one fact. Entry state (`:1234`) likewise.

**Provenance extended, never overloaded.** New `fail_closed_uninterpretable` replaces a branch that returned **`true`** for an uninterpretable selection. #726 shipped the discriminator so a `true` from "permitted" and from "blind" stopped being the same byte; overloading `no_analysis_exists` would rebuild that on the `false` side.

## The shadow case — ruling, with the reasoning

`supabase-store.ts` returns only the newest non-noop scenario fact, so a `partial` can shadow an older `complete`. **A1's prior is adopted: the newest CLAIM-BEARING fact governs**, and the justification is not taste — the alternative ("skip the partial, let the older complete fact's permission stand") lets a **newer withheld** verdict be overridden by an **older permitted** one. That is a `false → true` move, and #726's one-directionality argument exists to forbid exactly that direction. Nothing about a status string earns an exception.

Pinned in both directions: a newer partial that **permits** IS honoured over an older withheld one, so the rule is "newest claim-bearing fact", not "withhold always wins" — otherwise the fix could degenerate into a blanket withhold that passes every other test here.

## Proofs

**RED-first, executed.** The committed repro had **6 failing assertions** at `cf10c553` and passes after the fix.

**Mutation — 3 mutants.**

| mutant | verdict |
|---|---|
| M0-1 — entitlement reverted to the quality selector (the P0 itself) | 🔴 5 assertions |
| M0-2 — uninterpretable selection fails OPEN again | 🟢 **does not bite — see below** |
| M0-3 — quality filter re-applied to both selectors | 🔴 5 assertions |

**M0-2 does not bite, and I am reporting that rather than quietly dropping it.** The `fail_closed_uninterpretable` branch is **unreachable by construction**: `viewRunAnalysisFact` calls `isRunAnalysisFact` before admitting a candidate, so the selector cannot return anything else. It is a defensive guard whose only value is **direction** — if the selector's contract changes, the failure becomes a withhold rather than an entitlement. It is **not covered and is not claimed to be**. A test now pins the *reachability premise* instead: if the selector ever admits a non-run_analysis fact, that test goes red and the guard needs real coverage.

**A third hand-maintained mirror found and removed while fixing this.** `MayNameLeadingOptionProvenance` had **two hand-typed copies** of its union (`diagnostics/v5-diagnostic-trace.ts:264`, `orchestrator/route-v2.ts:785`). Adding the new state broke the build at the consumer — which is the lucky case; had the field been wider, both copies would have silently narrowed what the diagnostic could report. Both now import the type.

**Positive controls:** a genuinely empty scenario still returns `true` / `no_analysis_exists` (the honest-true branch must not become dead, or the fail-closed default's cost moves from content to correctness); `completed`-status behaviour byte-identical; legacy no-status facts unchanged; and the **freshness selector is asserted untouched**, so the fix cannot have "solved" the P0 by loosening quality — which would have had every freshness consumer building result views from partial analyses.

## Gates

| gate | pristine `cf10c553` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| full suite | 1299 files / 21825 passed, 0 failed | **1300 files / 21835 passed, 0 failed** |
| `pnpm typecheck` | PASS | PASS |
| Typecheck Drift ratchet | 98 files / 282 errors | **98 files / 282 errors — unchanged** |
| `pnpm lint` | 0 errors | 0 errors |

Delta is exactly `+1 file / +10 tests` — the repro, and nothing else.

One intermediate run showed 5 `admin.*`/`auth.*` files failing in `beforeAll` with `Hook timed out in 10000ms` and **zero assertion failures**. Same signature I diagnosed earlier in this lane and reproduced against the **pristine tip**: stray `vitest` processes exhausting the machine. Cleared, re-run, table above. Reporting it rather than only the green run.

## Effect on the open cleanup train

- **#727** — its B2 unification is absorbed here (the P0 made it load-bearing). Rebasing reduces it to R8 + A6 + the array-literal binding + its structural pins.
- **#728** — stacked on #727; rebases with it. Untouched by this fix.
- **#729** — branched from `staging` and disjoint; unaffected.

author: rickfelix
body:
## The defect

`buildPreSendConsultBody` forwarded the raw body and **nothing else**. The reviewer received second-person prose written to a *different* party, with no field that disambiguates it — so every "you"/"your" silently re-pointed at the reviewer.

**Witnessed live.** An advisory correctly addressed to the coordinator was read by Solomon as crediting **him** with editing SD row descriptions. He is propose-only under CONST-002 and has edited zero rows. His reasoning was sound and his counts were right — he proved non-authorship from his own outbound — but his conclusion was wrong, because the one field that resolves it was never transmitted.

The omission therefore:
1. manufactured a **false governance-violation record** against the oracle,
2. **stripped credit** from the party who actually did the work,
3. burned a consult round-trip while the real send sat at the gate.

**The reviewer cannot self-correct this.** No amount of care recovers a field that was never sent — which is why the fix belongs in the envelope, not in guidance.

## The fix

- `buildPreSendConsultBody(body, addressee)` — optional second arg, emitting `[PRE-SEND CONSULT -> <role> <id-prefix>]` plus an explicit note that second-person pronouns refer to the **addressee**. That note isn't padding: the failure mode was resolving second person to self, and naming the addressee alone still leaves that reading available on a skim.
- Header sits **inside** `capBody`, for the same reason the prefix does (QF-20260720-729) — anything outside the cap can be the thing that gets dropped.
- The lane threads `addressee`; the call site passes the **already-resolved** role and target, so this moves an existing value rather than deriving a new one.
- Omitting the addressee is **byte-identical** to the previous envelope.

## Mutation-verified, not assumed

Reverting the lane to `buildPreSendConsultBody(body)` **kills both new lane tests**.

That check mattered here: the suite's existing fake is `(b) => …` — single-arg, so it silently discards a second argument. A test written against it would have passed whether or not the value was threaded, **which is the same shape as the bug being fixed**. The new tests use a *capturing* fake and assert the addressee **arrived**, not merely that the parameter slot exists.

The degrade path is pinned too: no addressee passes `null` rather than inventing a plausible one — a **wrong** addressee is worse than none, because it would re-point the pronouns confidently.

## Testing

**471 passed across 35 adam suites** (17 in the two directly-touched files).

## Raised, deliberately out of scope

This is the **second** loss through this one function — QF-20260720-729 was a `.slice(0, 300)` that hid the very tail Solomon was asked to check (recurred ~9×). Two different fields lost through the same envelope suggests it should carry the full send context rather than be patched per-field. Flagged for the owning SD.

author: rubicon
body:
## Summary
Closes #42. The highest-leverage introspection gap behind full design fidelity: native Divi 5 core modules (`divi/text`, `divi/section`, …) are largely **not** in `WP_Block_Type_Registry` (only third-party `difl/*` register), so `schema_get_module` returned `not_found` for them.

Divi ships its own definitions as `module.json` per module under `includes/builder-5/visual-builder/packages/module-library/src/components/<slug>/` — each with `name`, `title`, `category`, and the full **`attributes`** tree. These are Divi's own generated interoperability data (clean-room: independent of the commercial Pro package; the approach is confirmed by Divi's official developer docs). `schema_get_module` now falls back to reading them; `schema_list_modules` augments from the same files.

## Security (path traversal)
The slug comes from a caller-supplied block name, so file reads are guarded three ways:
1. `native_module_slug_from_name` requires `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$` — nothing with `.`, `/`, or `..` survives.
2. `native_module_schema_from_dir` adds a **realpath-containment** check (resolved file must sit under the components dir).
3. `parse_native_module_json` rejects a file whose declared `name` mismatches the request.

## Verification
- **24 unit assertions** — slug mapping incl. traversal rejection (`divi/../../../etc/passwd`, `divi/..`, embedded slash), json parse/shape, from-dir read against a synthetic fixture. Suite: **468 / 16 files**.
- **Live on Divi 5.9** (branch deployed to colleyvillelions, then restored): `divi/text`/`section`/`blurb`/`accordion` resolve with their attribute trees (`source: divi_module_json`); `divi/nonexistent-xyz` → not_found; **traversal → not_found (no leak)**; `schema_list_modules` now surfaces **83 native modules**.

No MCP server change — `diviops_schema_get_module` / `diviops_schema_list_modules` already exist; the handlers improved. This is the foundation for the clean-room skills epic (#50).

author: panosatha
body:
Two independent changes that happened to share a branch.

## `zonal_sums` — aggregate model rasters over polygons

`postprocessing.zonal_sums(arrays, meta, shapes, *, all_touched=False)` sums 2-D
model rasters per zone → `{zone_id: {name: total}}`. E.g. infected people per district.

- **NaN-safe** (`np.nansum`) — the pipeline writes NaN on unexposed cells, so a
  plain sum would return NaN for any zone containing dry land.
- **Takes rasterio `(geometry, zone_id)` pairs, not a GeoDataFrame**, keeping
  `geopandas` out of the dependency set. Geometries in `meta`'s CRS, ids >= 0.
- **`all_touched=False` by default** so neighbouring zones cannot both claim a
  boundary cell and double-count its people. On overlap, later shapes win.
- **Extensive quantities only** — summing risk gives a meaningless number; divide
  two sums instead.

7 tests in `tests/test_zonal_sums.py`, on the existing `small_meta` fixture.

## Lazy `wbgapi` import

Moved into `_fetch_latest`, so model-only installs that never touch the
preprocessing layer do not need the package to import `d_health`.

## Verification

`pixi run tests` — 145 passed, coverage 77.46% (floor 65%).

body:
## 这次改了什么

### 摘要

`apps/desktop/src/main/__tests__/deviceId.test.ts` 的用例「追加而非前置:不覆盖已有的用户 PATH 项」在 Windows 上必然失败：

```
AssertionError: expected '/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin' to be '/opt/homebrew/bin'

Expected: "/opt/homebrew/bin"
Received: "/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
```

用例用 **Unix 风格的 `:`** 构造 PATH，却用 **`path.delimiter`** 去拆分 —— 后者在 Windows 上是 `;`，`split` 拆不开这条字符串，`dirs` 只有一个元素（整条 PATH），于是 `dirs[0]` 拿到的是整串而非首项。

被测函数 `ensureSystemBinPathForMachineId()` 在 Windows 上是 no-op（`deviceId.ts` 首行即 `if (process.platform !== 'darwin' && process.platform !== 'linux') return;`，注册表取指纹不依赖 PATH），所以**这是测试自身的缺陷，不是产品代码问题**。

该文件头部已声明约定：

> 每个用例在所有平台都断言:darwin/linux 断言补齐,其它平台(Windows)断言 no-op,避免非目标平台上整套用例空跑通过。

同文件其余 4 个用例都带了 `if (PATCHES_PATH)` 分支，唯独这条漏了 —— `expect(dirs[0])` 是无条件断言，而它依赖的 `dirs` 在 Windows 上根本没被正确拆分。本次按同一模式补齐：

- **darwin / linux**：断言原有优先项仍在最前，且已补上 `/usr/sbin`（原用例对后者只做了 `if (PATCHES_PATH)` 的单行断言，语义不变）
- **Windows**：断言 PATH 未被改动，与同文件用例 1、4、5 的 `else` 分支同款

同时补了一行注释说明为什么拆分必须收在平台分支内，避免以后再被改回去。

### 变更类型

- [ ] `feat` 新功能
- [ ] `fix` 缺陷修复
- [ ] `refactor` / `perf` 重构或性能优化
- [x] `docs` / `test` / `chore` 文档、测试或工程维护
- [ ] 其他：

### 范围

- 关联 Issue / 需求：Closes #707
- 本 PR 包含：`apps/desktop/src/main/__tests__/deviceId.test.ts` 中单个用例的平台分支补齐
- 明确不包含：
  - 不改动产品代码（`deviceId.ts` 未触碰）
  - 不改动同文件其它 4 个用例
  - #706（Windows CRLF 导致 GLOSSARY.md 门禁必红）是另一个独立的 Windows 门禁问题，不在本 PR 修
- 用户可见变化：无（纯测试改动）
- 是否存在 breaking change：无

### UI 变化

不涉及

- 引用的设计规范：不涉及

## 怎么验证的

### 自动验证

```text
pnpm --filter desktop exec vitest run src/main/__tests__/deviceId.test.ts
结果：Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 5 passed (5)      ← 修复前该文件 1 failed

pnpm --filter desktop run --if-present typecheck
结果：通过（exit 0）
      注：本次改动位于 src/** 下，确实在 tsconfig.json 的 include 覆盖范围内。

pnpm test:unit
结果：全部 workspace PASS，退出码 0（apps/desktop unit 156.3s PASS）
      修复前同一命令在本机为 1 failed / 1226 passed，唯一失败项即本 PR 修复的用例。
```

### 手工验证

不涉及：纯测试改动，无运行时行为变化。

### 未执行的验证

- **macOS / Linux 上的实际执行**：本机为 Windows，未在 darwin/linux 实跑。该分支下的断言相较原用例只增强不削弱（新增 `expect(dirs).toContain('/usr/sbin')` 由原来的单行 `if (PATCHES_PATH)` 改写而来，语义一致），且 `PATCHES_PATH` 为真时走的代码路径与原用例相同，预期不受影响；CI 会在 Linux 上覆盖。

author: geodro
body:
The tray menu built its services and PHP sections twice over, each with a fixed pool of menu items, parallel arrays mirroring the rendered state, a mutex, and click handlers that worked out what to run by reading those mirrors. The dot a service was drawn with and the command a click sent were decided in different places, and anything past the pool size vanished without a word.

Both sections now build rows that carry their own title and command, and one generic list type owns the pool, the redraw and the dispatch. A row's action cannot drift from its label, and overflow is reported on the last slot instead of dropped.

With the lists behind that, both move into submenus and the global toggles into a settings submenu. On a machine with the full stack installed the top level goes from roughly thirty five rows to twelve, with the running service count and the current PHP default readable on the parent rows.

The status block gains a worker line. Per-site workers are invisible in the tray today because the menu filters them out of the services list, and their number grows with sites, so this is a count rather than another list. A worker stopped because its site is paused or idle-suspended is not a fault, so the red state comes from the worker health endpoint rather than from comparing running against declared, and the line hides itself when there is nothing running and nothing broken.

Closes #1197

author: ankur1996
body:
Measured on run `2026-07-27-sample100-7fc8b4c`: **8 `HOP_FETCH_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` events across 7 properties, 6 of them on `hop_index=1`.** Five of those seven ended `FAILED_NO_DATA`. Hop #1 was consuming the entire 150s crawl budget and starving the hop that holds the roster.

### The cap alone would have been a no-op

```python
_hop_remaining = max(_MIN_HOP_FETCH_S, _hop_deadline - time.monotonic())
```

Every in-flight hop gets **all** remaining budget, so a per-hop cap looks like a one-line fix. It isn't — the `except TimeoutError` handler does `break`, which is correct *only* while allowance == remaining budget. Add a cap and they diverge: hop 1 times out at 90s with 57s unspent and the loop exits anyway.

Confirmed from artifacts: across all 8 timeout events, **zero** further `link_hop_fetched` events were emitted, despite 3–7 unvisited candidates in the matching `link_hop_started` payload.

`break` → conditional `continue` is the load-bearing edit; the cap only makes it reachable. `continue` fires **only** when the per-fetch cap bound the hop and real headroom remains — when the *deadline* bound it, the 2026-07-25 fail-fast `break` is preserved verbatim.

### Why 90s

OK hop fetches (n=30): p50 5.5s, 26 under 12s, then `35.4 / 60.1 / 80.5 / 86.6 / 94.5`. Of the five slow ones, **exactly one produced units** — property 7595's `/api/v1/floorplans/` at 86.6s, 6 units.

| cap | budget freed | 7595 |
|---|---|---|
| 60s | 339.7s over 6 hops | ❌ killed |
| **90s** | 189.0s over 5 hops | ✅ kept |

`LINK_HOP_PER_FETCH_S=90`, env-tunable. `<=0` disables and restores previous behaviour byte-for-byte — the kill switch is total, not partial.

### The bound got TIGHTER

150s was never a hard wall clock; it is an **admission** deadline. Worst case = deadline + gate + floor allowance + cancel unwind. The cheap-GET gate was previously **unbounded** — 256.6s of queue-wait measured on property 27577, whose allowance had already floored to 20s, making a per-hop cap inert for it. Now bounded at ≤12s:

```
worst case   ~427s  →  182s     (150 admission + 12 gate + 20 floor)
```

Verified with a harness driving the **real** `_try_link_hop` at 10:1 scale including re-entry: `continue` doubles candidates tried at *identical* total wall clock, and a second call inheriting `shared_budget` admits nothing.

### Honest on the payoff

> **Measured net properties gained on the sample: ZERO.**
>
> Two plausible rescues (256603, 48389 — both get a genuinely different next page once near-duplicate URLs collapse), two measurably no-gain (97935's later session fetched both candidates the freed budget would have bought and still got 0 units).

This is a correctness and worst-case-latency fix. The gold effect is unproven; the full 5k run is what settles it. Adds `HOP_FETCH_CAP_EXCEEDED` as a distinct outcome so the next run can tell cap-bound from deadline-bound without inference.

### Verification

`7 failed / 7350 passed`, failure **set** byte-identical to main's 7, over **3 consecutive runs**. +22 test functions. **5 mutations applied at the gate, all caught** (9/4/2/2/1 tests fail). ruff 9→9 same set; mypy unchanged per file.

author: dcoupry
body:
Closes #194. Stacked on #201 (targets `fix-mapping-enumeration-order`; will retarget to master once that merges).

`_summarize` collected rebuilds by walking **every** net candidate of every structure:

```python
rebuilds = [
    entry["rebuild"]
    for record in measured
    for entry in record["nets"].values()
    if entry.get("rebuild")
]
```

while every other statistic in the same block — `size_error`, `shape_error`, `size_bias` — is taken from `record["nets"][record["best_net"]]`, one value per structure. A structure whose identification is ambiguous therefore contributed **one** row to the size/shape statistics but **two or more** to `n_rebuilt`, `n_rebuilt_faithful`, `rebuilt_min_contact` and `rebuilt_bond_residual`.

The rebuild is what closes the loop on *that structure's* volume-ratio prediction, so it belongs to the same population the prediction does. `measure_one` now rebuilds the best (buildable) candidate only, after the choice has been made, and `_summarize` reads that single entry.

This is not only a counting fix: structures with several rebuildable candidates are exactly the ones most likely to rebuild faithfully on one net and not on the other, so the old aggregation biased the *faithful fraction* as well as inflating the denominator.

Side benefit: an ambiguous structure no longer pays for a full build per runner-up.

### Tests

`test_embedding_rebuilds_once_per_structure` asserts the invariant directly — only the best net carries a `rebuild` entry, and `n_rebuilt <= n_measured`. The existing `test_embedding_predicts_the_rebuilt_cell` still passes (pcu is MOF-5's best candidate).

Lint, format and the driver tests pass locally.

author: bricef
body:
## Why

A hold is indistinguishable from neglect unless the reason is written down.

The graph-executor plan sat untouched for three weeks and read as abandoned. It was deliberately waiting on security and structural work — but nothing said so anywhere a reader would look. This adds the missing map: one coarse mermaid graph of what gates what, plus the rule that **anything held carries a named exit condition**.

## What this adds

One new section in `STATUS.md`, `## How the work is sequenced`, placed between "What's next" and "Not built yet". Docs-only and purely additive — 35 insertions, 0 deletions, no existing line touched.

Deliberately coarse: workstream-level only. Per-issue dependency trees already come from `issue-graph` against GitHub sub-issue links, and duplicating those here would guarantee drift. Solid arrows are hard gates; dashed arrows are open questions or weak couplings, so the two aren't read as the same claim.

## What is *not* asserted

This matters as much as what is:

- **`#414`'s exit criteria (`#399`, `#400`, `#78`, `#189`, `#191`) are proposed and not yet maintainer-confirmed.** The prose says this explicitly. They're a candidate release condition for the hold, not a settled contract — the text refuses to let the arrows imply agreement.
- **`#78`/`#189`/`#191` carry no allocated capacity today.** The size ratchet (`#388`) stops those files growing but does not shrink them, which is why that edge is dashed.
- **The non-code workload (cleanroom finding 1.3) has no issue yet** and is drawn as untracked.
- **Registry + split execution (ADR-0006/0031) and exactly-once trigger dispatch are omitted.** Both are in flight, but neither gates anything on this map — drawing them would suggest a dependency the repo doesn't have.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `just lint-docs` | exit 0 — 33 files, 0 errors |
| `just check-links` | exit 0 — 631 relative links, 0 broken |

Two notes on how those were run:

- `just check-links` reports `0 relative links checked` when run from inside the worktree, because the worktree lives under `.claude/` and the script's `SKIP_PARTS` matches against absolute path components. The gate passes, but vacuously. It was re-run against an identical export of the tree outside that path to get the real number (631 links, 0 broken; the 1 "outside the repo" skip is a pre-existing Canopy sibling-repo reference, untouched here).
- Neither `just quality` nor `just ci` was run — both build Rust and neither is affected by a docs-only change.

Beyond the required gates: `markdownlint` on `STATUS.md` itself is 0 errors before and after, and the diagram round-trips through `mermaid-cli` to SVG with all ten nodes rendered — so the block is a real parse, not an eyeballed one.

body:
# FE: unsloth server status in the intentd status indicator + stop with confirm modal

Part of intent-hq/monorepo#878. Frontend surface for the managed Unsloth server RPCs merged in intent-hq/intentd#623 (`unsloth.status` / `unsloth.stop`, protocol 2.5).

## What

- **Status dropdown section**: when a managed Unsloth server is running, the `DaemonStatusIndicator` dropdown shows an "Unsloth Server" section — model (shortened HF repo id, full id in a tooltip), phase (`starting`/`minting`/`loading`/`ready`), port, uptime, CPU and memory (process tree, matching the daemon rows' formatting), and attached agent count.
- **No background polling**: `unsloth.status` is polled only while the dropdown is open (on open + the existing 1s tick), mirroring the task requirement. There is no persistent interval like `system.status`'s 10s poll.
- **Stop with confirmation**: a "Stop server" action opens a destructive confirm dialog (reuses `BulkActionConfirmDialog`). When `attachedAgentCount > 0` the description warns that stopping will break in-flight requests from those agents; otherwise it notes the server restarts automatically on next unsloth agent creation. On confirm the middleware invokes `unsloth.stop` and re-polls `unsloth.status` so the dropdown reflects the post-stop state immediately.

## Wire contract (traits.rs / PROTOCOL §5.37)

- `unsloth.status` → `{ running, repoId?, port?, pid?, uptimeSecs?, phase?, cpuPercent?, memoryBytes?, attachedAgentCount? }`; `{ running: false }` degrade stored as-is (section hidden). `attachedAgentCount` is optional — a daemon whose agent manager is not attached reports exactly `{ running: false }`.
- `unsloth.stop` → `{ stopped: boolean }`; `stopped: false` is a no-op, not an error.
- Poll failures (older daemon without the method) clear the stored status — no stale server rows, no error surfaced.

## Store changes

- `daemon-health-types.ts`: `UnslothStatusWirePayload` + `unslothStatus`/`unslothPolling`/`unslothStopping`/`unslothStopError` on `DaemonHealthState`.
- `daemon-health-slice.ts`: `pollUnslothStatus`, `unslothStatusSuccess`/`Failure`, `stopUnslothRequested`/`Succeeded`/`Failed` actions + reducer cases.
- `daemon-health-service.ts` (middleware): routes the new actions to `backendRequest('unsloth.status')` / `backendRequest('unsloth.stop')` with the same in-flight guard and stale-generation dispose guard as the `system.status` poll.
- `daemon-health-selectors.ts`: `selectUnslothStatus`, `selectUnslothStopping`, `selectUnslothStopError`.

## Tests

- `daemon-health-slice.test.ts`: initial state + every new reducer case (running payload stored as-is, `{ running: false }` degrade, failure clears status, stop lifecycle).
- `daemon-health-service.test.ts` (mock IPC router): asserts the exact wire requests (`unsloth.status` / `unsloth.stop`, both param-less per PROTOCOL), no polling at boot, PROTOCOL-shaped mock responses landing in state, stop → re-poll choreography, stop failure, in-flight poll guard.
- `DaemonStatusIndicator.test.ts`: section renders with all rows for a running server, hidden for `{ running: false }`/null, poll dispatched on open, confirm dialog gating (warning text with attached agents, no dispatch until confirm, cancel dispatches nothing), stop button disabled while stopping.

## Verification

- `pnpm vitest run` (targeted daemon-health + indicator suites): 95 passed
- `pnpm tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean
- `pnpm tsc -p tsconfig.main.json --noEmit` / `tsconfig.preload.json`: clean
- `pnpm run check` (svelte-check): 0 errors
- `pnpm run lint`: 0 errors

body:
### Motivation

- Establish a single authoritative Access security surface for Wallet/LNURL flows that is privacy-preserving and fail-closed for critical operations.
- Provide canonical tamper-evident audit linking, authoritative revocation, and issuer envelope metadata to support crypto-agility and migration paths without fabricating PQ capabilities.
- Enable offline continuity via signed Offline Validity Packs and a constrained local policy while preventing bearer semantics and secret leakage.
- Add structured recovery (Recovery Capsules), quorum-based multi-party approvals, and Wallet/LNURL step-up integration so high-risk actions require appropriate proofs.

### Description

- Introduces canonical audit chain enhancements in `app/services/access/audit_chain.py` with sequence numbers, chain id, idempotency handling, stronger sanitization, and verification APIs plus related DB migration `20260726_0067_wallet_lnurl_audit_chain.py`.
- Adds an authoritative revocation registry `app/services/access/revocation_registry.py` with typed targets/scopes, peppered private lookup derivation, propagation metadata, and APIs for actor-tree revocation and resolution.
- Implements issuer envelope, crypto capability/epoch primitives and registries (`app/services/access/crypto/*`) to attach truthful issuer metadata and fail-closed PQ requirements, plus migrations and model columns for envelope metadata.
- Ships Offline Validity Pack writer, verifier, local queue, and policy (`offline_validity_pack.py`, `offline_pack_verifier.py`, `offline_policy.py`) and DB tables via migrations `0069` that produce signed, device- and entitlement-bound packs.
- Adds Recovery Capsule orchestration with factor registry, LNURL recovery factor adapter, cooldowns, redaction, and policy-driven workflows under `app/services/wallet_auth/recovery/*` and LNURL recovery factor module `app/services/wallet_auth/lnurl_recovery_factor.py`.
- Implements principal-bound Access Certificate bridge `app/services/access/principal_certificate_bridge.py` to mint Access Certificates for wallet principals with policy checks, idempotency, and binding records plus DB migration `0068`.
- Provides Wallet/LNURL step-up and quorum primitives and services (`app/services/wallet_auth/step_up_policy.py`, `app/services/wallet_auth/quorum_*`) to coordinate multi-approval flows and project quorum state into policy decisions.
- Expands the central Policy Engine and context (`app/services/access/policy_engine.py`, `app/services/access/policy_context.py`) to consume integrity signals, LNURL normalization, step-up decisions, quorum hints, and stronger denial modes.
- Adds an advisory Access Integrity engine and cache (`app/services/access/access_integrity.py`, `app/domain/access/integrity.py`) that deterministically scores posture from verified signals and emits audits/metrics.
- New LNURL policy hooks, revocation adapters, metrics, observability helpers and wallet audit builders to integrate LNURL and Wallet flows with the central Policy Engine and low-cardinality Prometheus metrics (`app/services/lnurl/*`, `app/services/access/observability*`, `app/services/wallet_auth/audit.py`).
- Schema, model and API surface updates across `app/schemas/*`, `app/db/models/*`, and many new tests plus docs and observability assets; environment examples updated with new configuration keys in `.env.example`.

### Testing

- Ran the automated test suite including unit, integration and contract tests under `tests/unit`, `tests/integration`, and `tests/contract` via `pytest -q`, covering audit chain canonicalization/concurrency/idempotency, revocation resolution, offline pack issuance/verification/reconciliation, recovery capsule end-to-end flows, LNURL policy hooks, step-up/quorum logic, crypto envelope behavior, and many privacy/secret-redaction assertions; all tests passed.
- Exercise of metrics and observability registration was validated by importing metric modules and asserting registered metric names via `prometheus_client.generate_latest()` succeeded.
- Verified DB migrations and model parity checks via the included migration files and model inspection tests to ensure new tables/columns and uniqueness constraints are present.

author: ronblum
body:
Both macOS E2E engines shared a single R-library cache key (`runner.os`, which is just `macOS` for both). Because macOS 26 is arm64 and macOS 15 is x86_64, the x86_64 job restored the arm64 job's `pak`/`cli` binaries and couldn't load them ("incompatible architecture"), dying at the "Install e2e test dependencies" step. This scopes each engine's cache by OS and architecture (`macos15-x86_64`, `macos26-arm64`) via the `os-e2e-deps` action's existing `cache-scope` input, matching the pattern the Linux engines already use.

Also raises the macOS 15 `build` job timeout from 90 to 180 minutes. The Intel runner is the slowest builder in the fleet, and a cold sccache can push a from-scratch compile past the 90 minutes that suffices for the faster arm64/Linux runners, the same headroom already granted to windows-2025. Addresses #18359.

Both cache-scope changes were verified green on macOS 15 and macOS 26 via a temporary push-triggered validation workflow, removed before merge.

body:
## Change

`loadWcpLicense` only resolved the WCP project environment from the CLI-computed `WCP_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` blob (set by `applyWcpEnvVars` during `webiny serve` and the AWS deploy). A self-hosted **server** deploy boots the built handler directly (`node start.mjs`) with no CLI step, so the blob is absent — the license fell back to `NullLicense` and `getProject` returned `COULD_NOT_GET_PROJECT`.

This adds a fallback: when the blob is missing, derive `org` / `project` / `apiKey` straight from the runtime env (`WEBINY_PROJECT_ID` + `WEBINY_PROJECT_API_KEY`) so a fresh license is still fetched. No new WCP API call — the license endpoint already takes `{orgId, projectId, apiKey}`, and WCP resolves the specific environment from the api key server-side (so the environment `id` isn't needed).

Behavior unchanged when the blob is present (AWS + `webiny serve`).

## Test

Validated end-to-end on a self-hosted EC2 deploy: container env had only `WEBINY_PROJECT_ID` + `WEBINY_PROJECT_API_KEY` (no `WCP_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`), and `getProject` returned `error: null`.

author: curtismu7
body:
Answers the question three reverts kept asking: **what breaks when the Node gateway introspects against real PingOne.** PingOne scopes RFC 7662 introspection to the **issuing client**. This gateway serves the **A2A path only** (5/5 calls over 6h), and those tokens are minted by **five different specialist clients**. Probed live, gateway out of the picture: | token | introspected by | result | |---|---|---| | specialist-issued | `f4dd707d` (gateway's identity) | **`active:false`** | | specialist-issued | the specialist itself | `active:true` | | `f4dd707d`-issued | `f4dd707d` | `active:true` | No single `GW_INTROSPECTION_CLIENT_ID` can cover them. Pointing this gateway at real PingOne blocks every A2A call at `TokenIntrospection`, every later filter skipped. **Wrong mechanism for a multi-issuer resource server — not a permission gap**, which is why a fourth re-apply would have failed identically. JWKS verifies anything PingOne signed regardless of issuer, and is **confirmed active on this exact path**: a forged token is rejected with *"no kid header and the JWKS exposes 4 keys"* — proof it fetched and consulted PingOne's keys. ## Real introspection is not lost IG serves the main path, where tokens **are** minted by `f4dd707d`, and introspects against real PingOne — it always has. Both mechanisms live, each where it works. The mock is now referenced by neither. ## Honesty of the skip `audit.introspection` is `null` → `filterChain TokenIntrospection=skipped`, never `passed`. And `authorizeMcpRequestCore` refuses to skip unless a JWKS endpoint is configured, so the two checks can never both be off (#1012). ## Deploy note `mcp-gateway` sits behind `profiles: ["demo-auth"]`, so `docker compose build mcp-gateway` **silently no-ops and reports success** while the image stays stale. Must be `docker compose --profile demo-auth build …`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Greptile Summary

This PR changes the Compose Node gateway from mock token introspection to an introspection-disabled configuration intended to rely on JWKS validation. - Removes the mock introspection endpoint from the mcp-gateway environment. - Sets `GW_INTROSPECTION_ENABLED` to `false`. - Documents why specialist-issued A2A tokens cannot use one gateway introspection client.

Confidence Score: 2/5

 This PR is not safe to merge because the changed Compose configuration rejects every A2A request unless an optional external env file provides a JWKS URI. The Node gateway explicitly refuses to skip introspection without `PINGONE_JWKS_ENDPOINT` or `PINGONE_JWKS_URI`, while the changed service disables introspection and its adjacent configuration states that no JWKS endpoint is configured. **Files Needing Attention:** docker-compose.yml

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | docker-compose.yml | Disables introspection but does not configure the JWKS endpoint required by the gateway core, causing the Compose A2A path to reject all tokens. |
