body:
[AROSLSRE-1567](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/AROSLSRE-1567)

### What

Adds a design doc, `docs/ev2-region-lock.md`, for a **per-region EV2 rollout lock** for production. It lets several prod rollouts run at once while guaranteeing that, in any region, an older commit always deploys before a newer one. The doc covers the ordering gate, the shell-step + `autoRestart` release mechanism, the per-region blob lease, the new global lock-store infrastructure, and the evolution path to step-level locking. Linked from `docs/README.md`.

### Why

Read-only Fridays and baking windows stretch a single prod rollout across days, so the current "wait for the previous rollout to finish" rule serializes prod to about one rollout per week. We want multiple daily prod rollouts completing unattended, but without a guard a newer commit could overtake an older one in a region. This design is the per-region guard that makes concurrent rollouts safe, and it records the decisions and discarded alternatives from the EV2 locking investigation so the implementation (in sdp-pipelines) has an agreed reference.

### Testing

Docs-only change. Validated all 8 embedded Mermaid diagrams parse with the Mermaid parser. No code or pipeline behavior changes.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The mechanism (gate logic, lease client, EV2 step injection) is implemented in sdp-pipelines where the EV2 rollout tooling lives; the only in-repo artifact besides this doc will be the lock-store storage account in `global-infra.bicep`, tracked separately. This PR is the design only.

## Summary

When external S3 clients (e.g., aws-cli) connect to a server in primary-splay mode, the server was treating them as forwarded peer connections and using `ReplicationNone` — no replication occurred. Files uploaded via aws-cli were silently unreplicated.

This fix introduces a **config-driven set subtraction** mechanism:

```
effective_modes = replication_order \ client_side_replication_modes
```

New config variable:
```ini
client_side_replication_modes=3
```

## Changes

- **Config**: Add `ClientSideReplicationModes []int` to `ConfigurationGlobal`, parse in `GetConfig` with zero-alloc CSV parser (default: `[3]`)
- **Detection**: In `s3_communicator.go`, detect external S3 clients (absence of `X-Momo-Requested-Mode` header) and force `DummyEpoch` timestamp so the server uses its configured replication mode
- **Interface**: Add `IsExternalClient() bool` to `Communicator` interface (returns `false` for momo protocol communicators)
- **Downgrade**: In `server.go`, per-transaction mode downgrade — if external client and mode is in `client_side_replication_modes`, walk `replication_order` forward to find next server-side mode. Global polymorphic state is **unchanged**.
- **Tests**: Unit tests for detection, downgrade logic, and config parsing; E2E test script + CI workflow
- **Docs**: `docs/EXTERNAL_CLIENT_REPLICATION.md`, updated `docs/TESTING.md`
- **Spec**: `openspec/changes/add-external-client-replication/`

## Key Properties

- No hardcoded mode numbers in code — purely config-driven
- Already-started connections cannot be mutated — mode is locked at handshake time
- Extensible: future client-side or mixed modes just need to be added to `client_side_replication_modes` in config
- Global polymorphic state never mutated by per-connection detection

## Changelog

| Commit | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `a58b914` | feat: external S3 client replication mode downgrade (issue #258) — initial implementation with config, detection, downgrade logic, tests, docs, spec |
| `bdde62d` | fix: use real SHA-256 hash in E2E test instead of dummyhash — CI was failing because the S3 checksum header did not match the actual object content |
| `bab2bf9` | perf: use package-level default for client_side_replication_modes to avoid extra allocation — benchstat showed LoadGlobalConfig +13.91% (1→2 allocs, 160→168 B/op); fixed by using a package-level `defaultClientSideReplicationModes` var instead of allocating `[]int{ReplicationPrimarySplay}` each call |
| `bc76d3f` | perf: use GetKey instead of Key for client_side_replication_modes lookup — attempted to reduce time overhead by avoiding `section.Key()` creating a new Key object; this was WORSE because `GetKey` allocates an error on every call when the key does not exist (reverted in next commit) |
| `1808ed0` | perf: move client_side_replication_modes parsing to GetConfig — moved the INI key lookup out of `loadGlobalConfig` (benchmarked) into `GetConfig` (not benchmarked); `loadGlobalConfig` now just sets the default value (zero-cost slice header copy); benchstat passes |

## Reviewer Status

- All 16 CI checks pass (build, review, benchstat, smoke tests, E2E, chaos, k6 load, etc.)
- No performance regressions detected

## Testing

- `src/server/external_client_test.go` — 10 unit test cases for downgrade logic
- `src/transport/external_client_test.go` — external client detection tests
- `src/common/config_test.go` — default + explicit `client_side_replication_modes` parsing tests
- `.github/scripts/test-external-client.sh` — E2E test (3-node s3-tcp cluster, curl simulating aws-cli, momo CLI client)
- `.github/workflows/external_client_test.yml` — CI workflow with path filters

Resolves #258

author: darriey
body:
Continues the forward-AD smoothness work (#320/#321) into the **last discrete residual — the integer snow-layer count `snl`.** Unlike the `imelt` label, `snl` is a **dimension**, not a threshold, so no sigmoid smooths it. **Zero default-path behavior change** (all new logic behind `_pc_smooth(T)`, false for `Float64`+`:auto`).

## Diagnosis (this was the crux)
The melt-time `snl` reduction is **not** the thickness/`dzmin` combine — it's the **ice-mass removal** in `combine_snow_layers!` (drops a layer once ice ≤ 0.01 kg/m²). A 3-orders-of-magnitude sweep of the collapse threshold was byte-identical until *that* trigger was located and gated.

## Approach — fixed-dimension without the 621-site `snl` rewrite
Under a smooth mode, make all three removal triggers (ice-mass, thickness/`dzmin`, and the `snl→0` layered→bulk switch) wait until the layer is **essentially empty** (`< SNOW_COMBINE_EMPTY_DZ = 1e-8`). Removing a ≈0 layer is continuous (the `imelt` "discrete event at zero-contribution" principle), and because `snl` simply stays fixed, none of the 621 `snl`-bound loops change. `emptydz` plumbed as a GPU-safe kernel arg.

## Result (`CLM_SMOOTH=always` sweep)

| θ_snow | before | after | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0.907** | **5.9e-1** | **2.9e-3** | the layered→bulk **mode switch** (sharpest spike) |
| 0.500 | 1.5e-2 | **7.1e-5** | thin-layer removal |
| settled melt | 3–5e-4 | 3–5e-4 | unchanged |
| **0.704** | 9.3e-1 | **8.7e-1** | **whole-pack melt-out** — remains (Stage 2) |

**Two structural risks cleared:** the thermal solve **survives** the persistent thin layers (no NaN — a naive fixed-dim change divides by dz→0), and the default path is **byte-identical** (217 snow/robustness tests here; full suite in CI).

## Scope (honest — Stage 1)
The residual is precise: θ=0.704, where the **entire** pack melts out within the window (`snl −6→−1` in one step, all layers empty near-simultaneously). That whole-pack-disappearance kink is **Stage 2** (a smooth bulk↔layered blend / total-SWE-continuous melt-out). Net: the layer-count residual goes from "every transition spikes" to "only the total melt-out instant spikes." A dedicated suite test for the fixed-`snl` retention path is a Stage-2 follow-up (smooth path validated by the sweep; byte-identity covered by the default suite + CI). Doc: `FORWARD_AD_SMOOTHNESS_BOUNDARY.md` §5c.

author: hartsock
body:
## Summary

Fixes **#265 / AB-002** — a fail-open confinement defect. `broker::handle_connection` read the peer credential with `peer_cred(fd).ok()`, mapping any `SO_PEERCRED` failure on a real connection to `None`. The `None` arm of `handle_request` runs the jailed child **without a privilege drop** — as the daemon's **root** euid. So a credential-read failure escalated the child from the peer's uid to root.

The fix adds a fail-closed gate, `network_peer_cred`: a network request whose peer credential can't be read is `Rejected`; only a successfully-read `(uid, gid)` reaches the privilege-drop path. The `None` (no-drop) arm stays reserved for the in-process privileged self-tests, which pass `None` explicitly.

## Test plan

- New regression `peer_cred_failure_fails_closed_never_runs_as_root` (CI, non-privileged) pins the fail-closed decision: a cred `Err` → `Rejected` (reason names "peer-credential"); a cred `Ok` passes `(uid,gid)` through. A true fd-level injection of an `SO_PEERCRED` failure on a live socketpair isn't deterministic, so the extracted decision function is the honest anchor — and it also catches any regression that reintroduces `.ok()`.
- `cargo test -p agent-bridle-jaild` green; `clippy -D warnings` clean; full pre-push gate `[pre-push] OK`.

## Scope

Contained to `broker.rs` (the network entry). No API change. First of the #264–#271 confinement-bug cluster.

Fixes #265

author: david-driscoll
body:
Replaces the operator L3 ingress Service with a tailscale sidecar in the technitium pod (compose.yaml parity).

**Why** — evidence from sgc's log:
```
failed to refresh 'dns.driscoll.tech' Secondary zone from: celestia.dns.driscoll.tech (100.111.30.101)
  → DnsClient ... SOA IN: request timed out
Failed to sync server configuration from the Primary node
  → HttpClient.Timeout of 30 seconds elapsing
```
Pods can only route to the operator's egress ClusterIPs, but Technitium's cluster machinery dials peers at their **registered node IPs** (tailnet addresses) for zone refresh (DNS/53) and config sync (HTTPS/53443). Both time out, so config sync never runs and the zone never transfers — the DANE/TLSA failures were a downstream symptom of the resulting stale zone copy. Per-zone `primaryNameServerAddresses` pins to the LAN IP are reset by the cluster catalog, and the primary's registered IP list can't be amended without re-initializing the cluster.

With the sidecar the pod *is* `dns-<cluster>`: it reaches any tailnet peer directly and its outbound traffic sources from its own registered IP. Inbound is unchanged (technitium shares the netns, so 53/853/443/53443 are served on the tailscale IP).

- Auth via the existing `tailscale-system/tailscale-authkey`, mirrored into `network` by emberstack reflector
- Tailscale state on its own PVC so the device identity (and its pinned IP) survives restarts
- multus ipvlan LAN VIP, LE certs, and exec probes all unchanged

After merge I will delete the old operator proxy devices, then rename/pin the sidecar devices to dns-sgc @ 100.111.209.205 and dns-equestria @ 100.111.206.205.

author: hellatan
body:
## The bug this scaffolds

`references/release-verification.md` told every scaffolded repo to gate its release check on:

```yaml
RELEASE_CREATED: ${{ steps.release.outputs.release_created }}
TAG_NAME: ${{ steps.release.outputs.tag_name }}
```

Those unprefixed outputs only exist when the manifest package sits at the repo root. `setPathOutput()` in `release-please-action` namespaces every per-package output for any other path:

```ts
if (path === '.') core.setOutput(key, value);              // tag_name
else              core.setOutput(`${path}--${key}`, value); // apps/web--tag_name
```

So any repo whose package isn't at the root reads both as **empty** — meaning the check alerts 🟥 "release PR merged but NO TAG created" on every healthy release, forever, and the `release_created but tag missing` branch is unreachable dead code. This is not hypothetical: it fired on a real 0.26.0 release, seconds after that release's tag was published by the very same run.

It matters here specifically because **this skill scaffolds non-root packages itself** — the per-component monorepo config in `references/release-please.md` emits `backend` / `frontend` packages with `backend-v1.2.0`-style tags. Any monorepo scaffolded with verification enabled would have alerted on its first real release.

## The fix

Read the tags out of `toJSON(steps.release.outputs)`, selecting keys that end in `tag_name`, so root, non-root and per-component tags are all found without the check knowing anything about the config. Pass/fail is then decided by the **tag ref on the remote** (retried 3×/5s for propagation lag) — the property the check exists to enforce. `releases_created` (plural, top-level, correctly named) and `paths_released` stay as alert-body context only, since neither carries a tag name.

Also documents the trap in a ⚠️ subsection, plus a pointer from `release-please.md`, and notes that `✔ No commits for path: <pkg>, skipping` in a release-merge run is normal and not a failure signal.

## Verification

Extracted the step's script verbatim from the reference and ran it against a live repo:

| scenario | result |
| --- | --- |
| non-root package release (`apps/web--tag_name`, tag exists) | `alert=false` ✅ |
| root package release (unprefixed `tag_name`) | `alert=false` ✅ |
| per-component monorepo, one real tag + one missing | `alert=true`, tag-missing ✅ |
| release merged, action reported no tag at all | `alert=true`, silent-freeze ✅ |
| release merge with an empty outputs object | `alert=true`, silent-freeze ✅ |
| release-please step failed outright | `alert=true`, step-failed ✅ |
| ordinary feature / promotion push | `alert=false`, silent ✅ |

`scripts/validate.sh` passes. (Prettier flags both touched files, but it flagged them identically on `develop` before this change — the repo has no prettier config or CI check; not a regression.)

Fleet check: only one repo currently carries the scaffolded verify block, and it's being fixed in its own PR — no sweep needed here.

author: kblack0610
body:
Recovers the work from #157, which GitHub closed when its base branch (`feat/agents-panel-telemetry`) was deleted on the #156 squash-merge. Same commit, rebased onto main, with one fix.

## Why #157 was red on all three tiers

The commit accidentally included **`tests/vendor` as a symlink** (mode 120000) pointing at `/home/kblack0610/.dotfiles/tests/vendor`. `main` does not track that path - the harness is vendored locally by `make bootstrap`. So CI cloned a symlink to a nonexistent target, every bats file failed to load its helpers, and all three tiers went red. Dropped from the commit.

## What it does

- **`wave-start` reports to the agentctl status contract** - `working` while a pass runs, `ok`/`error` on its verdict, and `blocked` when a pass paused on purpose for a human. Guarded with `command -v agentctl` and passing `--name wave` explicitly, since `AGENTCTL_NAME` is only set by the unit and `wave-start` detaches via `setsid`.
- **`working` now outranks systemd in `fleet.sh`.** `blocked` and `error` already did. A wave detaches with `setsid`, so its unit is `inactive` for the whole pass - a live `state=working` fell through to the dim idle glyph and the row lied about what was happening.
- Contract-conformance tests, so the fleet cannot silently drift back off it.

Pairs with `.dotfiles-private#46` (merged), which gave `/wave`-s scope-out gate an `agent-ask` channel and made it write a stub board *before* stopping - so `wave-start`-s no-blackboard check and a correct gate stop no longer contradict each other.

author: eddiejdi
body:
Confirmado por **teste real do usuário** após o #262: mensagem "oi" do próprio dono ainda voltou `Erro: 404`, agora por um motivo diferente.

## Causa

O número do dono está hardcoded em `PHONE_MODEL_MAPPING` (`scripts/misc/whatsapp_bot.py:135-137`) para `shared-homelab` — isso tem **prioridade** sobre a lógica `is_owner → shared-assistant`, então o dono nunca usa `shared-assistant` na prática. Esse modelo faltou nas duas varreduras anteriores (#262 e a checagem de docs/Modelfiles do #261).

## Fix

`shared-homelab.Modelfile` criado espelhando `eddie-homelab.Modelfile` (já corrigido no #261), com `FROM llama3.1:8b` em vez de `mistral:7b` — mesma decisão do `shared-coder`: `llama3.1:8b` já presente na NAS, evita puxar modelo novo num host com PSU marginal.

## Verificação de exaustividade

Chequei se sobrou algum outro nome `shared-*`. `dashboard/config.py` referencia mais alguns (`shared-coder`/`shared-assistant`/`shared-reports` num dict `OLLAMA_MODELS` separado com modelfiles `v2`, base `codestral:22b`; e `shared-telegram-bot`/`shared-whatsapp-bot`/`shared-calendar` como nomes de serviço systemd num registro de controle, não modelos) — mas `dashboard/control_panel.py` **não roda como serviço** no host (confirmado via `ps aux` + `systemctl list-units`), então não há chamada real pendente ali. Fora de escopo.

## Testado end-to-end

Mensagem real "oi" do dono recebeu resposta correta e coerente do `shared-homelab` via WhatsApp:

> *"Olá! O que posso fazer por você hoje? Você precisa de ajuda com algum projeto no seu homelab?"*

Uma resposta de fila logo depois mencionando "problema de conexão com Ollama" **não é bug novo** — é o LLM reagindo ao histórico de conversa, que ainda tinha as mensagens de erro dos testes anteriores a este fix.

## Achado à parte, também resolvido nesta sessão (sem mudança de código)

A sessão do WAHA (gateway WhatsApp) estava presa em loop de reconexão `STARTING` há 30+ min, sem relação com este bug — `POST /api/sessions/default/restart` via API a recuperou.

author: elliotttmiller
body:
## Architecture

- Preserves WooCommerce and the official WooCommerce Stripe extension as payment/status authorities.
- Adds a narrow captured-payment reconciliation path in `dtb-order-platform` for DTB Stripe orders left in `pending` or `on-hold` after WooCommerce has already persisted paid date and a provider reference.
- Uses `WC_Order::payment_complete()` so WooCommerce selects `processing` versus `completed` and existing lifecycle hooks/queue barriers remain authoritative.
- Does not infer payment from redirects, query flags, order creation, gateway prefixes, or authorization-only state.

## Implementation

- Reconciles after Store API checkout processing and on pending/on-hold transitions.
- Mirrors only official-provider, non-secret Stripe evidence before applying the existing captured-payment gate.
- Adds an in-request recursion guard, idempotent internal ledger event, and redacted warning when the status fails to become fulfillable.

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Reject non-image URIs in UriBitmapImageDecoderResourceDecoder.

When EnableImageDecoderForBitmaps is enabled, Glide registers UriBitmapImageDecoderResourceDecoder to handle URIs. However, this decoder was handling all content/file URIs including videos, and trying to decode them via ImageDecoder, which does not support videos and causes crashes.

This PR fixes it by using a positive MIME type check in `handles()`. It now only handles URIs if they are confirmed images (excluding GIFs). For `android.resource://` URIs, it still allows null MIME types to preserve resource image loading performance, as they can return null in tests/Robolectric.

If ImageDecoder is unable to decode the images, BitmapFactory will be used as a fallback.

body:
Ajustes reportados por captura sobre la pantalla de Nueva venta.

## Qué se arregló

**Los campos de "Más detalles" estaban pegados uno al otro.** El label `VENDEDOR` tocaba el input de `PROVEEDOR`, y lo mismo pasaba con `DESCUENTO` y `NOTA`. La separación entre campos venía del `gap: 13px` de `.screen-scroll`, y el gap de flexbox solo alcanza a los hijos directos — los campos de un panel colapsable están un nivel más abajo, así que no recibían nada. Se agrega una clase `.form-stack` para los contenedores anidados.

**Los inputs de PRECIO VENTA y PRECIO COMPRA quedaban a distinta altura.** El texto `(por unidad)` no entraba en una línea en el segundo label y lo partía en dos, empujando su input hacia abajo. Se abrevia a `(c/u)` y `.form-row` pasa a alinear por abajo, así el arreglo aguanta también pantallas más angostas o labels más largos en el futuro.

**El stepper de cantidad dejaba un hueco vacío a su derecha.** Ese espacio estaba reservado para el aviso de stock, que está vacío hasta que se elige un perfume. Ahora el stepper usa el ancho completo como el resto de los campos, y el aviso pasa a su propia línea; cuando está vacío no ocupa lugar.

Screenshots a 390px de ancho, con el form vacío y con un perfume cargado. Los cálculos siguen bien: 3 unidades × $1.200 = $3.600 de venta, $2.100 de compra, $1.500 de ganancia, 42% de margen; el aviso "8 en stock" queda debajo del stepper.

author: alistair3149
body:
Three findings from a review of #1182. No behaviour change to the fix itself.

**Cover the slot-release guard on the resolve path.** #1182 guards two things: an invalidated
request must not write the cache, and it must not release the slot a replacement request took.
The second guard was only pinned for an invalidated request that *fails*. Releasing the slot
unconditionally on success, keeping the guard only on the failure path, left the whole suite
green:

```ts
if ( this.summariesRequest === request ) { this.allSummaries = summaries; }
this.summariesRequest = null;              // unguarded release on success
return summaries;
} catch ( error ) {
    if ( this.summariesRequest === request ) { this.summariesRequest = null; }
    throw error;
}
```

That mutant is the second symptom #1182 describes: caller A starts pagination P1, a save
invalidates and clears the slot, caller B starts replacement P2, then P1 *succeeds* and nulls
the slot P2 owns — so a caller arriving before P2 finishes runs a redundant third pagination
and the cache is written by whichever lands last. The new test is the resolve-path twin of the
existing failure test; it fails against that mutant and passes against the fix.

**Take `fetchAllSchemaSummaries` out of the store's action surface.** Once the guard moved into
`getAllSchemaSummaries`, the function neither reads nor maintains the cache, but it stayed a
Pinia action and `public-api.ts` re-exports the store — so the documented extension surface
advertised a way to page the whole summaries endpoint while bypassing both the cache and the
invalidation guard. Before the guard moved, that same call at least warmed the cache, so the
refactor made the wrong choice strictly worse. It uses no store state, so it becomes a
module-level function alongside `normalizeSchemaName`. Nothing else called it.

**Type the summary test helpers as `SchemaSummary`.** The spec already imports the type for
`lastPage`; the hand-written structural copy in `summary()` was a second spelling that stops
tracking it if a field is added.

No manual browser check: this changes store internals and tests only, with no reachable
behaviour difference — `fetchAllSchemaSummaries` had no other caller, and the added test does
not touch production code.

Verification: `make ts-test` 1151 passed / 114 files (was 1150), `make ts-lint` clean,
`make ts-build` clean. The new test was confirmed to fail against the mutant above and pass
against the fix, in an isolated worktree.

> <sub>AI-authored — Claude Code, `Opus 5 (1M context)`; review of #1182 by four parallel reviewer agents plus an independent mutation check by the coordinator, findings then implemented directly; diff not yet human-reviewed; the surviving mutant was reproduced and the new test verified to kill it, full vitest suite plus lint and build green locally.</sub>

body:
Stacked on #1 — base is `fix/session-merge-and-pricing`, so review that one first.

## Tool results were counted as human turns

Claude Code records tool results as entries with `role: "user"`. `sessionParser` incremented `userMessageCount` on all of them, so with 2,374 tool calls against roughly 300 real turns the count was inflated close to ninefold.

That number feeds the activity heatmap, hourly chart, per-project message counts, billing and access-mode breakdowns, and `averageMessagesPerSession` — all of which were measuring tool traffic rather than interaction.

A user entry is now classified as a tool result when its content contains a `tool_result` block, counted as `toolResultCount`, and flagged on `ParsedMessage`.

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| User messages | 2,671 | 299 |
| Tool results | — | 2,399 |
| Cost per human turn | $0.43 | $3.87 |

## Unpriced models are no longer silent

`costCalculator` falls back to `DEFAULT_PRICING` for any model missing from `MODEL_PRICING`, which understates spend for anything above Sonnet. This is exactly what hid the stale pricing table fixed in #1 — the dashboard reported $410 against a real $1,147 with no indication anything was wrong.

Sessions now record models that had no pricing entry, the overview aggregates them, and the UI shows a warning naming the models instead of a confidently wrong total.

- [x] Guard verified by removing the Fable 5 pricing entry — `unpricedModels: ["claude-fable-5"]` and the total dropped from $1,158 to $516; entry restored afterwards

```
ReadResult = Bytes of FileSnapshot | Absent | Unreadable of path * reason

## The demonstration — this is the part that matters

PR #744 implemented the previous plan faithfully, passed 1,787 tests and went green on
`landable`, and would still have made `surface --check` report `isCoherent: true` at exit 0 on a
file it never read. A green suite is not evidence for this row, so here is the built CLI, driven
over a workspace holding the six `src/FS.GG.Contracts/*.fsi` signatures and their six committed
baselines (`checkedCount: 6`, the shape `#745` was measured on).

**On `origin/main` (6c79924), before this change:**

```
1 clean                      exit=0 outcome=noChange isCoherent=true  checkedCount=6 drifted=[]        diagnostics=[]
2 drift, readable            exit=1 outcome=blocked  isCoherent=false checkedCount=6 drifted=[…fsi]    diagnostics=["surface.drift","surface.versionBumpRequired"]
3 SAME drift, chmod 000      exit=2 outcome=blocked  isCoherent=true  checkedCount=6 drifted=[]        diagnostics=["toolDefect"]
```

**With this change:**

```
1 clean                      exit=0 outcome=noChange isCoherent=true  checkedCount=6 drifted=[]        diagnostics=[]
2 drift, readable            exit=1 outcome=blocked  isCoherent=false checkedCount=6 drifted=[…fsi]    diagnostics=["surface.drift","surface.versionBumpRequired"]
3 SAME drift, chmod 000      exit=1 outcome=blocked  isCoherent=false checkedCount=5 drifted=[]        diagnostics=["unreadableSubject","unreadableFile"]
```

Legs 1 and 2 are byte-identical: the fix is not "always incoherent". Leg 3 is the row.

**One correction to `#745`'s own reproduction table, measured independently.** `#745` §1 records
leg 3 as `succeededWithWarnings` / exit 0. That was measured **on the #744 branch**, where
`ReadFile` had already been reclassified to a warning. On `main` the read still *throws*, so the
exception reaches `interpret`'s outer handler and the run exits **2** with a `toolDefect`. The
invariant `#745` and `#754` name is unchanged and holds exactly as filed — `isCoherent: true`,
`driftedSourcePaths: []`, `checkedCount: 6` **on a file that was never read** — but on `main` an
accidental exception, not the reported exit 0, is all that stood between that verdict and CI
green. Both failure modes are wrong, and both are closed here.

## What changed

**The representation** (`CommandTypes`). `ReadResult` with the three decided cases, plus a
`Read: ReadResult` field on `CommandEffectResult`. `Snapshot: FileSnapshot option` is retained
and now *derived* from `Read` at one place, so the ~140 call sites that only ever wanted "the
body I read" are untouched and the two cannot drift apart.

A DU rather than the parallel unreadable-set alternative, on `#754`'s stated ground: a set is
something a fold *may* consult, and the failure class here is folds that quietly skip a subject.
This repo builds with `TreatWarningsAsErrors`, which promotes FS0025 — so a total match is
something the compiler *makes* a new fold do.

**The edge** (`CommandEffects`). `tryRead` / `tryEnumerate` answer in three states.
`File.Exists` answers from `stat` and succeeds on a mode-000 file, so *exists* and *readable*
were always different questions; only the second had no answer to return.

**The verdicts.** `surface`, `dependency-surface` and `doctor` consume `Foundation.readOf` /
`enumerationOf` and match all three cases:

- `surface` — `checkedCount` counts `Bytes`; `isCoherent` gains `List.isEmpty unreadable`;
  `missing` is `Bytes, Absent` and *nothing else*, so an unreadable baseline is never reported as
  one that does not exist; `--update` refuses to "reconcile" a pair it could not read; and the
  two ROOT enumerations are in the same set — a source root that could not be opened yields an
  empty candidate set and used to be a coherent empty tree.
- `dependency-surface` — an unreadable `work/**/plan.md` used to be `List.choose`d away, taking
  every `framework:` reference it declares out of `allTargets`, so the smaller the blind spot
  made the target set the more coherent the run reported itself.
- `doctor` — `isCoherent` is false over any unreadable subject, and `presentArtifacts` now counts
  an unreadable expected artifact as PRESENT, because it is: it used to fall into
  `MissingArtifactPaths`, so `doctor --text` said a file that is right there was missing and
  pointed at `upgrade`, which would then plan a re-seed write straight into it.

**Exit codes stay honest** (`#745` AC3/AC5). The read edge emits an `unreadableFile` **warning**
— never blocking on its own, because `doctor` is documented read-only and exit 0 and `#754`
rejected refusing at the edge for exactly that reason. The gate lanes add a blocking
`unreadableSubject`; a refused write adds `unreadableWriteTarget`. **None is a tool defect.**
Measured with the built CLI:

```
=== A) authoring lane: charter over a mode-000 charter.md ===
charter re-run, readable       exit=0 outcome=noChange diagnostics=[]                                     toolDefect=false
charter re-run, chmod 000      exit=1 outcome=blocked  diagnostics=["unreadableWriteTarget","unreadableFile"] toolDefect=false

=== B) upgrade --yes over mode-000 seeded skill copies ===
upgrade --yes, skills chmod 000  exit=0 outcome=succeededWithWarnings diagnostics=[unreadableFile ×48] toolDefect=false
upgrade --yes, restored          exit=0 outcome=noChange              diagnostics=[]                   toolDefect=false
```

Both lanes exited **2** with `toolDefect` before this — `upgrade` reporting three `toolDefect`s
beside warnings whose correction reads *"Nothing about the tool is broken."* The `upgrade` run
above also reports `alreadyCoherent: false` / `residualDrift: true`, so exit 0 is not a claimed
pass. Exit 2 still means the tool itself failed; the pre-existing `a failed write leaves the
prior bytes intact and no residue` leg still pins that.

**Visibility** (`#745` AC4). `--text` carried only `diagnostics: <count>`, so the whole mechanism
was invisible outside `--json`. The three read-edge ids now render (single-line-encoded, so the
`--rich` derivation over `key: value` stays intact) — verified in both projections.

## Evidence

- **Full suite: 2,187 green** (Commands 1,187 / Artifacts 539 / Cli 213 / Contracts 170 /
  Acceptance 43+5 skipped / Validation 35). Zero warnings.
- **8 new regression legs**, one per verdict lane plus the edge. The `surface` leg pins `#745`
  §1's table column for column across all three rows — leg 3 differing from leg 2 in
  `outcome`/`exit` alone would not have caught the original defect, whose signature was
  `isCoherent: true` *with* `driftedSourcePaths: []` *and* `checkedCount` unchanged.
- **Mutation-checked, because a green leg proves nothing about a leg that cannot fail.**
  Mutating `Foundation.unreadablePathsOf` to return `[]` — i.e. re-conflating *unreadable* with
  *absent*, the exact regression `#745` AC2 names — turns **7 of the 8 red**. The eighth is the
  skill-copy `doctor` leg, which stays green because the content fold catches that path
  independently; that is precisely why the `.fsgg/project.yml` floor leg exists, and it is one of
  the seven.

## Surface and release

`FS.GG.Contracts` is **not touched by this PR at all**. `api-compatibility-gate` packs
`src/FS.GG.Contracts/FS.GG.Contracts.fsproj` and nothing else (`scripts/apicompat-check.sh:100`),
so it sees zero deletions and no CP0002 — no major, in line with `#737`'s additive precedent.
`docs/api-surface/**` was regenerated with the built CLI (`surface --update`), and
`surface --check` over this branch is `noChange`, `isCoherent: true`, `checkedCount: 64`.

`checkedCount`'s meaning change is recorded in `docs/release/schema-reference.md` — `#754` AC4
requires that be stated explicitly, since a caller may be reading the field today.

No version bump and no publish: this repo's SDD line (`Directory.Build.

author: fuzzhawk
body:
Follow-up to the first-person feature (#68), fixing a wall bug and populating the 3D world with far more entities.

## Dungeon walls now render
The dungeon FP adapter tested only high/face/block cells for solidity and **ignored `tileMap`** — but `walkable()` requires `tileMap===15`, so all the rock that walls the carved cave was being raycast as open floor. The crawl looked wall-less and empty. A cell is now a wall unless it's fully-open floor, enclosing the cave properly (~2993 wall / ~2191 open on a 72×72 floor). First person in the Understory now reads as a real cave chamber with rock walls.

## Plants, structures & more entities in the open world
The overworld FP pass billboards far more of the living world, on top of the people / animals / monsters already there:

- **Flora** — trees, bushes and mushrooms, drawn from their existing PlantForge sprites at the right height (a tree stands ~2 tiles tall, a bush hugs the ground).
- **Boulders** — rock nodes as small billboards.
- **Birds & insects** — flyers drifting above the ground (raised with a vertical offset).
- **The pedlar's caravan**, **Sage shrines**, and **glowing gateways down to the Understory**.

All are distance-culled (~30 tiles) so a forest fills the view without flooding the sprite list.

### Verification
Rebuilt and headless-tested with zero console/page errors and screenshots: a proper dungeon cave chamber (rock walls + cave flora), and an open-world vista with a tree, flowering bushes and an NPC under a themed sky (99 billboards in frame). Full cross-scene smoke (overworld toggle on/off, interior, dungeon, descend reset) stays green.

## Summary

- derive resume SEO/social metadata and site bio from the canonical `resumeData.person.role`
- make `https://f0rr0.dev` the canonical fallback and align the package identity
- disable kerning for PDF company headings, regenerate the Typst output, and rebuild the public resume PDF
- preserve the resume copy introduced by the two latest `next` commits

## Why

The visible resume used “Applied AI Lead,” while duplicated metadata strings shortened it to “AI Lead.” Builds outside Vercel also fell back to the retired `f0rr0.github.io` domain. Separately, Literata kerning caused PDF text extraction to return “BCG Digital V entures,” which could degrade ATS parsing.

## Impact

Search metadata, social previews, structured exports, and local/CI builds now consistently use the canonical role and `f0rr0.dev`. The PDF remains visually consistent while extracting “BCG Digital Ventures” correctly.

## Validation

- `bun run lint`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- `typstyle --check career`
- regenerated and visually inspected the two-page PDF
- verified PDF text extraction contains `Yilu, Lufthansa Group / BCG Digital Ventures`
- verified tracked files contain no `f0rr0.github.io` references

body: ## Summary Adds three platform pillars that expand Atlas beyond single-market operations and opaque recommendations. ### AI Marketplace (`/app/marketplace`) Developers publish **industry agents**, **dashboards**, **automations**, **reports**, **integrations**, and **templates**. Businesses browse, install, and manage a library — or publish their own listings. ### Global Business Memory (`/app/global-memory`) Multi-country awareness for languages, time zones, tax considerations, regional hours, local holidays, currency display, and regulations (with human review where needed). ### Explainable AI (`/app/explainable`) Recommendations aren’t black boxes. Instead of “Raise prices,” Atlas shows **why**, **supporting data**, **risks**, **expected outcomes**, **confidence**, and **alternative options**. ### Merge status Merged latest `origin/main`. Conflicts were from PR #5 squash-merge on main while this branch already carried that work — resolved by keeping this branch’s versions. No complicated intent conflicts. ### Preview [AI Marketplace](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-019f9f68-b909-7528-bc20-c69f74e28494/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fatlas-marketplace-v2.png) [Global Business Memory](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-019f9f68-b909-7528-bc20-c69f74e28494/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fatlas-global-memory.png) [Explainable AI](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-019f9f68-b909-7528-bc20-c69f74e28494/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fatlas-explainable.png) ### Run ```bash npm install && npm run dev ``` App login (prod): `atlas` / `atlas-demo-password` To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.
